rules.detail: Absolute ban on limiting the economic risk of unvested entitlements under any equity-based remuneration scheme; no clearance route.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons are prohibited from entering into transactions or arrangements which limit the economic risk of participating in unvested entitlements under any equity based remuneration schemes.

rules.detail: Hedging of the person's security holding is expressly permitted with prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer under Section 7. The policy does not distinguish vested-but-locked shares; release from holding lock is an excluded dealing but hedging locked shares is not separately addressed.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward or similar is an agreement to dispose of securities (a trade) and, insofar as it limits economic risk or is secured on the shares, falls under the clearance regimes in Sections 9 and 10.
rules.evidence: To "trade" in securities means, whether as principal or agent, to apply for, acquire or dispose of securities; or enter into an agreement to apply for, acquire or dispose of securities.

rules.detail: Short selling is not named anywhere in the Policy.
Securities lending is not named and is not within the trade definition.
CFDs are not named but cash-settled derivatives and equity swaps over Company shares are Company Securities, so a CFD is a trade requiring prior written clearance.
rules.evidence: derivatives of any of the above (including equity swaps, futures, hedges and exchange-traded or over-the-counter options) whether settled by cash or otherwise

rules.detail: Margin loan agreements over Company Securities are permitted with prior written clearance from the Approving Officer. A disposal resulting from a secured lender exercising rights under a margin lending arrangement is excluded from the blackout restrictions.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must not enter into margin loan agreements or other secured lending arrangements in relation to Company Securities without first obtaining prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer in accordance with the procedure set out in Section 7.

rules.detail: Granting a charge, mortgage or pledge is not named as such, but any 'secured lending arrangement in relation to Company Securities' requires prior written clearance, which captures a security interest granted to a lender. A charge unconnected with lending is not addressed.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must not enter into margin loan agreements or other secured lending arrangements in relation to Company Securities without first obtaining prior written clearance

rules.detail: Any secured lending arrangement in relation to Company Securities is permitted with prior written clearance; no vesting-state carve-out is stated. A lender's enforcement disposal is an excluded trade for blackout purposes.

rules.detail: No short-term, speculative or minimum holding-period rule; the Approving Officer may consider reputational implications when clearing.

NST.summary: A funded collar over vested shares is possible for a Restricted Person under this policy, subject to clearance. Hedging of a person's security holding (Section 9) and margin loans or other secured lending arrangements over Company Securities (Section 10) are each expressly permitted with prior written clearance from the Approving Officer (Company Secretary for Senior Employees and consultants; Executive Chairman for non-director KMP; Executive Chairman and Lead Independent Director jointly for non-executive directors), who must take General Counsel advice and may withdraw clearance at any time; clearance is valid for 5 business days. Hedging of unvested equity-based remuneration entitlements is absolutely prohibited, and OTC options and cash-settled derivatives are expressly Company Securities so every entry, unwind or settlement is a trade needing fresh clearance and cannot occur in the half-year, full-year and quarterly Blackout Periods or a confidential Additional Period absent exceptional circumstances. A lender's enforcement disposal is an excluded trade for blackout purposes. There is no short-term dealing rule or minimum shareholding requirement, and no express disclosure obligation for the financing beyond directors' notification of holding changes.

rules.detail: The derivative definition expressly names options, forwards, swaps, caps and collars and any transaction limiting the economic risk of holding securities; derivatives (cash or physically settled, including third-party products) are QBE securities. rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward is a forward contract limiting economic risk (hedging, banned) and any structure secured on QBE securities is a prohibited secured financial arrangement.

QBE.summary: A funded collar is not possible under this policy for any director, executive or employee. Hedging of QBE securities, defined to include any transaction in financial products that limits the economic risk of holding them, is prohibited at all times for all Relevant Persons and their Closely Related Parties, and 'collars' are expressly named in the derivative definition, so the put and call legs are banned over vested and unvested shares alike. The loan leg is independently prohibited: paragraph 4.2(c) bars margin lending, transfers into margin accounts and any pledging, collateralisation or use of QBE securities as security for any financing arrangement, and granting a mortgage or other right over securities is a dealing. The paragraph 5 waiver power extends only to Closed Periods and the three-month short-term dealing rule, not to hedging or secured financing, and there is no other exemption authority. Paragraph 6 persons (directors, GEC members and their direct reports, divisional board directors and EMB members) need written clearance, valid for 5 business days, for any other dealing at any time.

COL.summary: A funded collar is not possible for a director or Executive Leadership Team member: section 6.3(a) absolutely prohibits them and their Connected Persons from hedging any exposure to Company securities, and section 6.2 bars all Restricted Persons from any secured financing arrangement in respect of Company securities, including margin loans, transfers into margin accounts and sales to meet margin calls, with no waiver authority. For Permitted Restricted Persons (General Manager level and above, nominated team members) the put and call legs over vested, unrestricted shares are permitted as a cleared dealing with written approval from the Company Secretary (confirmed with two Disclosure Committee members), executed within two clear trading days outside the 20 June, 20 December, 1 April and 1 October blackouts, but the loan secured on those shares remains prohibited, so only an unfunded collar is available to them. Plan securities can never be hedged before vesting or while under a holding lock, and forward contracts are named as short-term dealings so tenor should exceed three months. Team members below Restricted Person level are outside sections 5 and 6 and could enter a funded collar over vested unrestricted shares subject only to insider trading law.

Only 'margin loan arrangements' are named, but the ban extends to any such arrangement 'in relation to which Sigma Shares may be used as security against loan repayment' and the stated rationale (lender-compelled sale in a Closed Period) applies to any loan secured on Sigma Shares. Section 11 separately bars arrangements that could result in disposal within 12 months of acquisition. A non-margin secured loan over shares held more than 12 months is not expressly addressed.

SIG.summary: The collar legs are available but the loan leg is doubtful. Derivatives, with collars and OTC put and call options expressly named, may be used over vested Sigma Shares that are not under a holding lock, so a director or executive who is a Specified Person can enter the put and call with prior written clearance from the Chairman (CEO for the Chairman), valid for two business days, outside the 31 July, 31 January and pre-AGM Closed Periods, with post-trade confirmation within three business days. Derivatives over unvested shares are absolutely prohibited, stock lending and short selling are banned, and no arrangement that could result in disposal within 12 months of acquiring the shares is permitted, so the collar should cover shares held for at least 12 months (or LTI/SPP/ESP shares). The loan secured on the collared shares is caught by section 12 if it is a 'margin loan arrangement in relation to which Sigma Shares may be used as security'; the policy's stated concern is lender-compelled sales in Closed Periods, so a facility with LVR triggers or enforcement rights is likely prohibited, while a non-margin secured loan over shares held more than 12 months is not expressly addressed and would need the Chairman's clearance. Sections 11 and 12 are addressed to Team Members, leaving their application to non-executive Directors to their engagement terms.

EVN.ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Company reserves the right to impose a restriction on trading during any period, including one that would otherwise fall within a permitted trading window; the Company Secretary may also designate employees as subject to trading-window restrictions at his or her discretion. Any period in which a matter constituting inside information exists is a prohibited trading period. Confidentiality of ad hoc restrictions is not addressed.

rules.detail: No express derivatives rule. 'Securities' include financial products issued or created over securities by third parties, structured financial products, swaps, futures, CFDs, spread bets, options, warrants and other derivatives, with no venue limit; 'deal' includes entering into a contract with the purpose to secure a profit or avoid a loss by reference to price fluctuations. An OTC put/call with a bank is therefore a dealing requiring written clearance from the Company Secretary, inside a trading window, with no inside information. Designated employees are treated identically; employee insiders need clearance but are not window-bound.

EVN.exemption_authority: Company Secretary may permit dealing outside trading windows, ordinarily only in exceptional circumstances and only if the person has no price sensitive information. Under section 6, clearance in a prohibited trading period is for a sale only (not a purchase), the determination of severe financial difficulty or other exceptional circumstances can only be made by the Executive Chairman, and prior written clearance must come from the Executive Chairman (or the Chairperson of the Audit Committee if the Executive Chairman is the applicant), with the request also provided to the Company Secretary; the sale must occur within five business days. There is no authority to waive the absolute bans in section 2 (short-term trading, short selling, secured financing, hedging unvested entitlements).

bespoke_clauses.clause: Personnel are not permitted at any time to: ... enter into margin lending or other secured financing arrangements in respect of the Company's securities;
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar, secured on the collared shares, is an 'other secured financing arrangement' expressly prohibited for all personnel at any time, regardless of vesting state, with no approval or exemption route.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Deal ... Includes, in relation to securities: Any acquisition or disposal, or agreement to acquire or dispose: Entering into a contract with the purpose to secure a profit or avoid a loss by reference to price fluctuations
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A put/call collar is squarely a contract to avoid a loss by reference to price fluctuations, so entry, unwind, roll and settlement are each dealings requiring clearance and a trading window for Directors, Senior Executives and designated employees.

bespoke_clauses.clause: enter into transactions with securities (or any derivative thereof) which limit the economic risk of any unvested entitlements awarded under an equity-based remuneration scheme, or otherwise awarded, or which will be offered by the Company in the future (eg hedging).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The ban reaches entitlements 'otherwise awarded' and future offers, so the collar must be sized strictly to vested shares and a bank should confirm that no part of the hedged parcel is referable to unvested or prospective awards.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Clearance may be given for such a person to sell (but not purchase) Evolution securities in a prohibited trading period.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Closed-period relief cannot cover entry into a collar or a purchase to close a written call; only an outright sale in severe financial difficulty or under a court order can be cleared, and only by the Executive Chairman.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The trading windows for Directors, Senior Executives and designated employees are: (a) For a period of thirty days after the release of the Company's half yearly results; ... (g) For a period of fifteen days following the release of the Company's quarterly reports.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The policy uses narrow open windows (15 or 30 days after specified releases) rather than closed periods, so the collar must be documented and executed within one of those windows and within five business days of clearance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Company reserves the right to impose a restriction on trading during any period, including one that would otherwise fall within a permitted trading window.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A trading window can be closed without notice, which may block a scheduled unwind, roll or physical settlement of the collar.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A clearance to deal can be withdrawn if new information comes to light or there is a change in circumstances. The Company's decision to refuse clearance is final and binding on the person seeking clearance.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A cleared collar can become unexecutable between clearance and pricing, so the bank should price and sign promptly within the five-business-day validity.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and Senior Executives (or any family member or associate over whom they have influence) have additional dealing restrictions
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Routing the collar or the secured loan through a family member, trust or controlled entity does not escape the window, clearance or secured-financing rules.

bespoke_clauses.clause: engage in short-term trading (less than one month), or short selling of the Company's securities at any time;
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar or any related share purchase/sale that is opened and closed within one month risks characterisation as short-term trading; tenor should exceed one month.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Remedial action may include a requirement that the person who sold Evolution securities in breach of the Policy to donate any profits earned to charity.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any profit from a non-compliant collar or forced sale could be required to be disgorged to charity, in addition to disciplinary action.

EVN.summary: A funded collar is not possible under this policy. Section 2 prohibits all personnel, at any time, from entering into margin lending or any other secured financing arrangement in respect of the Company's securities, so a loan secured on the collared shares is banned outright with no clearance or exemption route. An unfunded collar (purchased put and written call) over vested shares is a dealing, because 'deal' includes any contract to secure a profit or avoid a loss by reference to price fluctuations and 'securities' include OTC options, swaps and other third-party derivatives; Directors, Senior Executives and designated employees may enter one only with prior written clearance from the Company Secretary, within a nominated trading window (15 or 30 days after specified releases), executed within five business days, and without price sensitive information. The collar must not limit the economic risk of any unvested entitlement, entitlement otherwise awarded or future offer, and tenor should exceed one month to avoid the short-term trading ban. Closed-period relief is available only for a sale in severe financial difficulty or under a court order, cleared by the Executive Chairman, and cannot cover collar entry or settlement.

rules.evidence: If you are an Executive Team Member, you are prohibited from Trading in a Blackout Period in Derivatives, financial products issued or created over or in respect of Amcor Securities. Examples of these financial products include swaps, caps and collars.

rules.detail: The express Blackout Period ban in 9(a) names only Executive Team Members, but Derivatives are Securities and Directors are prohibited from Trading in Amcor Securities in a Blackout Period under clause 8, so the outcome is the same. Outside a Blackout Period, clause 9(b) subjects Derivatives trading to the notification procedures, meaning notification to the Chairman of the Board (Chairman of the Audit & Compliance Committee for the Chairman) with a copy to the Company Secretary and confirmation received before trading.
rules.evidence: Trading in Derivatives outside a Blackout Period is subject to the notification procedures in this policy.

rules.detail: Co-workers are not listed in the clause 10 notification table, so the notification procedures referred to in 9(b) do not reach them. Derivatives are Securities, so co-workers may not trade them in a Blackout Period or while holding price sensitive information, but outside those constraints no clearance is required.
rules.evidence: “Securities” means shares and other instruments considered to be a security for the purposes of the Corporations Act. The definition of a Security is complex and includes not only ordinary shares but also Derivatives, and any other financial products that are able to be traded on a financial market.

rules.detail: Absolute ban, extended to Associates, on hedging arrangements over unvested Securities issued under any employee or director option or share plan. Put and call options are expressly named as examples, so a collar over unvested plan securities is squarely prohibited with no consent route.
rules.evidence: You and your Associates must not engage in hedging arrangements (including, for example, the use of put and call options or other derivative instruments) over unvested Securities issued pursuant to any employee or director option or share plan.

rules.detail: Hedging over vested Securities is expressly contemplated and permitted, but must comply with this Policy (Blackout Periods, notification and confirmation, short-term trading ban, insider trading law) and, where applicable, with Amcor's Minimum Shareholding Policy. The clause 10 notification must confirm the Executive Team Member will be in compliance with the minimum shareholding policy after the trade, so a collar that takes the effective holding below the minimum is the binding constraint on size.
rules.evidence: In addition, any hedging over vested Securities must comply with this Policy and if applicable to you, Amcor’s Minimum Shareholding Policy.

rules.detail: Hedging over vested Securities is permitted provided it complies with the Policy, which for a Director means outside a Blackout Period, after notification to the Chairman of the Board (copied to the Company Secretary) and receipt of confirmation, no inside information, and no short-term trading. The Minimum Shareholding Policy applies only 'if applicable to you'; the express minimum shareholding confirmation in clause 10(a)(i) is drafted for Executive Team Members.
rules.evidence: In addition, any hedging over vested Securities must comply with this Policy and if applicable to you, Amcor’s Minimum Shareholding Policy.

rules.detail: The policy draws the line at vesting rather than at release from plan restrictions, but Appendix 1 item 6 makes clear that plan securities remain governed by the plan until they cease to be held under its terms. Securities that have not vested, including those still subject to plan holding conditions before vesting, cannot be hedged; the policy does not separately address shares that have vested but remain locked under a holding lock.
rules.evidence: Amcor Securities issued under an employee share plan provided that where securities granted under that plan cease to be held under the terms of the plan, any subsequent Trading of those Securities must be in accordance with the Amcor Share Trading Policy;

rules.detail: Monetisation, prepaid forwards and similar structures are not named. A structure that transfers the beneficial or legal interest in Amcor Securities is Trading, and a cash-settled structure over Amcor Securities is a Derivative or a financial product created over Amcor Securities, so either way it requires the clause 10 notification and confirmation for Directors and Executive Team Members and is barred in Blackout Periods. If the structure is secured on Amcor Securities it additionally needs the Company Secretary's prior consent under clause 17.
rules.evidence: “Trade” and “Trading” includes subscribing for, buying, selling or otherwise transferring the beneficial or legal interest in Securities of Amcor.

rules.detail: Outright ban on short selling for all persons covered and their Associates, defined narrowly as borrow-and-sell. A covered written call or a put purchased against shares actually held is not a borrow-and-sell and so is outside this definition, but a naked short position would be caught.
rules.evidence: You and your Associates must not engage in short selling. Short selling refers to the technique where a person borrows the security for the purpose of selling it in the hope that they will be able to buy the security back for a lower price at a point in the future and close out their position at a profit.

rules.detail: Securities lending as a lender is not named and is not within the definition of Trade, which turns on subscribing, buying, selling or transferring the beneficial or legal interest. Borrowing securities is mentioned only as an element of the short selling definition.

Contracts for differences are expressly inside the definition of Derivatives, so they follow the derivatives regime: banned for Executive Team Members in a Blackout Period, and subject to the clause 10 notification and confirmation outside it for Directors and Executive Team Members. A CFD closed within three months would also breach the short-term trading ban.
rules.evidence: “Derivatives” includes warrants, exchange traded and over the counter options and contracts for differences.

rules.detail: Margin lending over Amcor Securities is not banned. It is permitted for all covered persons and their Associates with the prior consent of the Company Secretary. No criteria, form, timing or conditions for that consent are stated, and no tier is excluded.
rules.evidence: You and your Associates are not permitted to enter into margin lending or other secured financing arrangements in respect of Amcor Securities without the prior consent of the Company Secretary.

rules.detail: Granting security over Amcor Securities as part of a margin loan or other secured financing arrangement requires the Company Secretary's prior consent. A charge, lien or pledge unconnected with a financing is not named, and the definition of Trade does not expressly capture the grant of security, although an outright transfer of the legal interest to a security trustee would be Trading.
rules.evidence: You and your Associates are not permitted to enter into margin lending or other secured financing arrangements in respect of Amcor Securities without the prior consent of the Company Secretary.

rules.detail: The clause reaches beyond margin loans to 'other secured financing arrangements in respect of Amcor Securities', which captures the loan leg of a funded collar secured on the collared shares. It is a consent regime, not a prohibition, and the sole gatekeeper is the Company Secretary. The policy is silent on whether consent may be conditioned, how long it lasts and whether it can be withdrawn.
rules.evidence: You and your Associates are not permitted to enter into margin lending or other secured financing arrangements in respect of Amcor Securities without the prior consent of the Company Secretary.

rules.detail: The secured financing consent requirement is not limited by security state and there is no express ban on pledging unvested plan securities. In practice unvested plan securities are typically not transferable and any economic protection over them would be a prohibited hedge under clause 16, so the useful collateral is vested shares.
rules.evidence: You and your Associates must not engage in hedging arrangements (including, for example, the use of put and call options or other derivative instruments) over unvested Securities issued pursuant to any employee or director option or share plan.

rules.detail: A buy-sell window test rather than an intention test: trading in and out of Securities within a consecutive three month period is prohibited. Because Securities include Derivatives, an option position opened and closed inside three months is caught, so a collar and any unwind, roll or early termination must be spaced more than three months apart. No carve-outs are stated.

bespoke_clauses.topic: secured financing is consent-based, not banned
bespoke_clauses.clause: You and your Associates are not permitted to enter into margin lending or other secured financing arrangements in respect of Amcor Securities without the prior consent of the Company Secretary.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar, secured on the collared shares, is available to Directors, Executive Team Members and co-workers on a single consent from the Company Secretary, making Amcor one of the policies under which the structure is achievable.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If you are an Executive Team Member, you are prohibited from Trading in a Blackout Period in Derivatives, financial products issued or created over or in respect of Amcor Securities. Examples of these financial products include swaps, caps and collars.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Collars are named and are prohibited only during Blackout Periods, which confirms by implication that a collar entered outside a Blackout Period with the required notification is contemplated by the policy.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Amcor Share Trading Policy does not apply to ... an involuntary disposal of Amcor Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bank enforcing its security or a margin call sale during a Blackout Period falls outside the policy entirely, so the lender's enforcement rights do not put the executive in breach - a materially better position than policies that treat forced sales as a breach.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Short-term Trading refers to Trading in and out of Securities within a consecutive three month period.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Because Securities include Derivatives, the collar's tenor and any unwind, roll, restrike or early termination must be more than three months apart, ruling out short-dated or frequently rolled structures.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The notification must confirm the Executive Team Member will be in compliance with the minimum shareholding policy after the trade, (if applicable).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The confirmer must be satisfied the Executive Team Member still meets the minimum shareholding after the collar, so the collared parcel must be sized to leave the minimum holding unhedged unless the Minimum Shareholding Policy says otherwise.

bespoke_clauses.topic: two week trading window in the notification
bespoke_clauses.clause: specify the proposed dates of the trade which should be no more than two weeks
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Pricing, documentation and execution of the collar and the secured loan must all be completed inside the two-week window nominated in the notification, or a fresh notification and confirmation is needed.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A clearance to trade can be withdrawn if new information comes to light or there is a change in circumstances; ... A decision to refuse clearance is final and binding ... the person seeking the clearance must keep that information confidential and not disclose it to anyone.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank cannot be told why a trade was blocked and confirmation can be withdrawn between pricing and settlement, so the trade documentation needs a condition precedent for subsisting clearance at execution.

bespoke_clauses.clause: IF YOU DO COME INTO POSSESSION OF INSIDE INFORMATION AFTER RECEIVING A CLEARANCE TO TRADE, YOU MUST NOT TRADE DESPITE HAVING RECEIVED THE CLEARANCE.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A cleared collar can become unexecutable at any point before signing, so the bank should expect a walk-away right on the executive's side.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A person is an “Associate” if a Director or co-worker is acting in concert with that person or if a Director or co-worker has, or can be regarded as having, investment control or influence over that person. Examples ... a trust of which the Director or co-worker ... are the trustee or beneficiary; ... a company which the Director or co-worker or their family controls.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Booking the collar or the loan through a family trust or controlled company does not avoid the consent, notification and Blackout Period requirements.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Following the end of each financial year, all Directors and Executive Team Members must certify to the Company Secretary that they and their Associates are in compliance with this policy (or advise of any breaches of this policy).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An outstanding collar and secured loan must remain compliant for its whole life and is re-attested annually, so a structure that drifts out of the minimum shareholding or is rolled inside three months surfaces at certification.

bespoke_clauses.clause: “Derivatives” includes warrants, exchange traded and over the counter options and contracts for differences.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no venue limitation, so an OTC put and call written with a bank is inside the derivatives regime rather than outside an exchange-limited ban.

bespoke_clauses.clause: any other period that the Board specifies from time to time. If the Board specifies any other period, communications will be sent to you.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Additional blackouts are notified rather than kept confidential, so an executive can tell the bank a window is closed without breaching confidentiality, though the reason may not be disclosable.

AMC.summary: A funded collar is achievable under this policy, which is unusually permissive on the financing leg. Margin lending and other secured financing arrangements in respect of Amcor Securities are not prohibited but simply require the prior consent of the Company Secretary, and no criteria for that consent are stated, so the loan secured on the collared shares turns on a single internal approval. The put and call legs are Derivatives and Securities, so for Directors and Executive Team Members they require the clause 10 pre-trade notification to the Chairman of the Board or the CEO respectively, copied to the Company Secretary, with confirmation received before trading, execution within the nominated window of no more than two weeks, outside the 31 December and 30 June Blackout Periods and any Board-specified period, and with no inside information at signing. Hedging is absolutely prohibited over unvested plan securities, so only vested shares can be collared, and an Executive Team Member must confirm continued compliance with Amcor's Minimum Shareholding Policy after the trade, which caps the collared parcel. Tenor must exceed three months to avoid the short-term trading ban, and the structure benefits from Appendix 1 item 5, under which an involuntary disposal resulting from a secured lender exercising its rights falls outside the policy altogether, so enforcement or a margin call sale during a Blackout Period is not a breach.

tiers.name: Directors, executives and employees
tiers.description: The general population to whom the policy is addressed. Bound by the insider trading prohibition, the section 5 hedging ban on unvested and locked securities, the front page test and the obligation to ensure their Connected Persons comply. Not subject to Trading Windows, clearance, the short-term dealing ban or the margin lending ban unless they are also a Designated Person; for other employees the margin lending clause is cautionary only.

rules.detail: There is no express derivatives rule. A Designated Person may therefore write or buy an option only inside a Trading Window with prior written clearance, and the front page test must be satisfied.

STO.exemption_authority: Section 4.6 allows a written application to the Company Secretary to deal outside a Trading Window due to severe financial difficulty or other exceptional circumstances, cleared by the Chairman for Directors and by the Company Secretary or CEO for other Designated Personnel. That authority relieves only the Trading Window restriction in section 4.1; there is no waiver power over the section 4.9 margin lending and security ban, the section 4.8 short-term and speculative dealing ban, or the section 5 hedging ban.

bespoke_clauses.topic: any form of security is banned
bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons must not enter into margin lending or any other arrangements where any form of security is granted over Santos securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is broader than a margin lending ban and kills the funded leg outright: a loan secured on the collared shares, and any charge, pledge or security trust over them, is prohibited for every Designated Person with no consent route.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Short-term or speculative dealing includes buying and selling securities on market within a 3 month period, forward contracts and short selling.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Naming forward contracts as speculative dealing blocks prepaid forward and forward sale alternatives to a collar, and invites the same characterisation of a tightly struck zero-cost collar that is economically a forward sale.

bespoke_clauses.topic: no waiver over the financing and hedging bans
bespoke_clauses.clause: A written application to deal with Santos securities outside a Trading Window due to severe financial difficulty or other exceptional circumstances may be made to the Company Secretary.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The only discretionary relief in the policy is from the Trading Window restriction, so the sections 4.8, 4.9 and 5 prohibitions cannot be waived even in hardship.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If the market was aware of all the current circumstances, could the proposed dealing be perceived to be inappropriate for someone in my position? ... Clearance to deal under this Policy will not be granted where the person providing clearance does not consider that the ‘front page test’ is satisfied.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even an unfunded collar over vested unrestricted shares can be refused on perception grounds alone, with no reasons given and no appeal, so the bank cannot rely on the technical permissibility of the derivative legs.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons may not assume that a Trading Window is open, even after the relevant ASX announcement or Annual General Meeting. ... A Trading Window may be varied, suspended or withdrawn by the Board or the CEO at any time.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Execution windows are discretionary and can be withdrawn mid-window, so any collar entry, roll or unwind must be documented as conditional on a subsisting open window at the moment of dealing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any clearance given under section 4.3 or 4.6 will be provided in writing and lasts for 5 business days or such other period specified in the notice of clearance. ... Any clearance may be revoked or withdrawn or the clearance period shortened or lengthened and may include conditions at the company's absolute discretion.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Pricing and execution of the derivative legs must complete within 5 business days and can be conditioned or revoked at any point before dealing, and a refusal must be kept confidential from the bank.

bespoke_clauses.clause: In the case of an on-market trade, the dealing occurs at execution (but not settlement) of the trade. In the case of an off-market trade, the dealing occurs at settlement of the trade.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: For an OTC collar the dealing is timed at settlement rather than trade date, so physical settlement or delivery must itself fall inside an open window with subsisting clearance, not merely the trade date.

bespoke_clauses.clause: “securities” include ... financial products relating to a company's securities (for example, warrants and other derivative products), irrespective of whether the financial products are created by the company or by third parties.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bank-written OTC put and call are securities in their own right, so the Trading Window, clearance, short-term dealing and front page test rules all attach to the option legs, not just to the shares.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons must ... ensure that their Connected Persons do not engage in any short-term or speculative dealing or margin lending arrangements.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Routing the collar or the secured loan through a spouse, family trust or controlled company does not escape the section 4.9 ban.

bespoke_clauses.clause: margin lending and other such arrangements could result in a forced sale of securities in breach of insider trading laws or this policy, such as during a period when you are in possession of or could be perceived to be in possession of inside information.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Santos treats lender enforcement as capable of breaching the policy rather than excluding it, so even for non-Designated employees a secured structure carries policy risk on enforcement.

STO.summary: A funded collar is not possible for any Designated Person, which covers all Non-Executive Directors, the CEO, the Executive Committee, their direct reports and every employee at Job Grade 13 or above. Section 4.9 bans not only margin lending but 'any other arrangements where any form of security is granted over Santos securities', so the loan secured on the collared shares is prohibited outright, and the only discretionary relief in the policy, section 4.6, reaches the Trading Window restriction alone and cannot waive it. The derivative legs on their own would be workable over vested, unrestricted shares, because the section 5 hedging ban stops at vesting and release from a holding lock, but they are dealings requiring prior written clearance inside a Board-notified Trading Window, valid 5 business days, revocable and conditionable at absolute discretion, and refusable on the front page test with no reasons. Tenor is also constrained: forward contracts are expressly branded speculative dealing and on-market round trips inside 3 months are prohibited, and for an off-market trade the dealing is timed at settlement, so physical settlement of a collar must itself fall in an open window. Only employees who are not Designated Persons sit outside the financing ban, and for them the policy still warns that a forced sale under a secured facility could itself breach the policy.

The Board of Directors or the General Counsel may modify the Policy or grant an exception where circumstances make it appropriate.

rules.section: 2.A (No Investments in Derivatives of the Company's Securities)
rules.detail: Flat ban on investing in Company-based derivative securities, expressly including put and call option contracts and straddles. No venue limitation, so OTC puts and calls written or bought with a bank are caught as squarely as listed ones, and the ban applies to every Covered Person and their family members and controlled entities regardless of whether the underlying shares are vested. The only carve-out is holding and exercising options, RSUs or other derivative securities granted under the Company's own equity compensation plans.
rules.evidence: No Covered Person shall invest in Company-based derivative securities. “Derivative Securities” are options, warrants, stock appreciation rights or similar rights whose value is derived from the value of an equity security, such as the Company’s common stock. This prohibition includes, but is not limited to, trading in Company-based put or call option contracts, trading in straddles and the like.

rules.detail: The single express permission: holding and exercising Company-granted options, RSUs and other plan derivative securities is not prohibited, and the grant, award, vesting and settlement of those instruments is not a 'transaction' at all. This is a carve-out for the Company's own instruments only and does not extend to third-party derivatives over the resulting shares.
rules.evidence: However, holding and exercising stock options, restricted stock units or other derivative securities granted under the Company’s equity compensation plans is not prohibited by this Policy.

rules.detail: One-sentence absolute ban on hedging any equity compensation or Company securities held directly. No definition of 'hedging' is given, no clearance or exception route is offered within the clause, and no distinction is drawn between unvested, vested-locked and vested-unrestricted holdings. A collar is the paradigm hedge and is prohibited on this clause alone, independently of the derivatives ban.
rules.evidence: No Hedging or Pledging. Covered Persons are prohibited from hedging or pledging any equity compensation or Company securities that they hold directly.

rules.section: 2.A (No Hedging or Pledging); Appendix A cl.4
rules.detail: Vesting does not release the hedging ban: it reaches 'Company securities that they hold directly', not merely unvested equity compensation. Appendix A reinforces the position for anyone using a Rule 10b5-1 plan, requiring that no corresponding or hedging transaction has been entered into or altered over the plan securities and that none be entered into while the plan is in effect.
rules.evidence: No Hedging. Covered Persons may not have entered into or altered a corresponding or hedging transaction or position with respect to the securities subject to the Rule 10b5-1 Trading Plan and must agree not to enter into any such transaction while the Rule 10b5-1 Trading Plan is in effect.

rules.section: 2.A (No Hedging or Pledging; No Investments in Derivatives)
rules.detail: Monetisation, prepaid forwards, variable prepaid forwards and zero-cost collars are not named. Each is caught twice over: as a hedge of Company securities held directly, and as an investment in a Company-based derivative security. A monetisation that instead borrows against the shares is caught by the pledging limb. There is no clearance path that cures a prohibited transaction; only the Board or General Counsel exception power in section 2.B could.
rules.evidence: Covered Persons are prohibited from hedging or pledging any equity compensation or Company securities that they hold directly.

rules.detail: Outright ban, with a definition wide enough to catch a sale of owned shares that is not settled by delivery within twenty days ('short against the box'). Relevant to any physically settled forward or delayed-delivery leg of a collar structure.
rules.evidence: No Covered Person shall engage in the short sale of the Company’s securities. A short sale is a sale of securities not owned by the seller or, if owned, not delivered against such sale within twenty (20) days thereafter (a “short against the box”).

rules.detail: Securities lending and rehypothecation are nowhere named, and the Policy has no general 'dealing' definition that sweeps them in. In practice a lend that enabled non-delivery against a sale would engage the twenty-day short-against-the-box limb, and for a Restricted Person any transaction, direct or indirect, in Company securities requires pre-clearance.

rules.section: 2.A (No Investments in Derivatives of the Company's Securities)
rules.detail: CFDs, swaps and total return swaps are not named, but the derivative-securities definition is open-ended ('or similar rights whose value is derived from the value of an equity security') and the prohibition is expressed as non-exhaustive, so a cash-settled contract for difference over News Corp stock or CDIs falls within it. A short CFD would also engage the short sale ban.
rules.evidence: “Derivative Securities” are options, warrants, stock appreciation rights or similar rights whose value is derived from the value of an equity security, such as the Company’s common stock. This prohibition includes, but is not limited to, trading in Company-based put or call option contracts, trading in straddles and the like.

rules.section: 2.A (No Margin Purchases; No Hedging or Pledging)
rules.detail: Two overlapping bans. Borrowing from a brokerage firm, bank or other entity in order to purchase Company securities is prohibited outright, with a narrow carve-out for cashless option exercises under the Company's equity plans. Borrowing against Company securities already held is prohibited under the pledging limb. Neither has a clearance or hardship route.
rules.evidence: No Covered Person shall purchase the Company’s securities on margin. This means such persons are prohibited from borrowing from a brokerage firm, bank or other entity in order to purchase the Company’s securities (other than in connection with “cashless” exercises of stock options under the Company’s equity compensation plans).

rules.detail: Pledging any equity compensation or directly held Company securities is banned in the same sentence as hedging. The ban is on the act of pledging, not on the underlying loan, so it bites on the security interest a lender would take over the collared shares. It is expressed by reference to securities 'that they hold directly', which leaves indirectly held securities textually unaddressed even though family members and controlled entities are themselves Covered Persons.
rules.evidence: No Hedging or Pledging. Covered Persons are prohibited from hedging or pledging any equity compensation or Company securities that they hold directly.

rules.section: 2.A (No Hedging or Pledging; No Margin Purchases)
rules.detail: The Policy never uses the phrase 'secured financing', but any loan secured on News Corp shares or CDIs requires a pledge, and pledging is prohibited for all Covered Persons and their family members and controlled entities without regard to vesting, tier or amount. There is no margin-loan-only qualifier, no threshold, no notification alternative and no disclosure regime; the only relief is the general Board or General Counsel exception power.
rules.evidence: Covered Persons are prohibited from hedging or pledging any equity compensation or Company securities that they hold directly.

rules.section: 2.B (No Trading in the Company's Securities on a Short-Term Basis)
rules.detail: Hard six-month minimum holding period for any Company securities purchased on the open market by a Restricted Person, reinforced by the Section 16 short-swing profit disgorgement rule. Same-day cashless option exercises are excluded provided there were no open-market purchases in the preceding six months. Any collar whose put leg could be exercised, or whose shares could be delivered, within six months of an open-market purchase would breach this.
rules.evidence: Any Company securities purchased on the open market by a Restricted Person must be held for a minimum of six (6) months.

rules.detail: The six-month holding period sits in section 2.B, which applies only to Restricted Persons. Covered Persons who are neither Section 16 Reporting Persons nor Designated Individuals have no holding period or speculative-trading restriction beyond the MNPI, short sale, derivatives, hedging, pledging and margin bans.

Restricted Persons inherit the outright derivatives ban and, even for permitted transactions, are additionally barred during quarterly and special black-out periods and must pre-clear with the General Counsel. Derivative securities including put and call options are expressly within the definition of the Company's securities to which section 2 applies, so nothing in the pre-clearance machinery converts a prohibited derivative into a permitted one.
rules.evidence: the following policies apply to all transactions (including gifts), direct or indirect, in all of the Company’s securities, including, but not limited to, the Company’s Class A Common Stock and Class B Common Stock ... CHESS Depositary Interests representing the Class A Common Stock and Class B Common Stock and derivative securities (including stock options, put or call options and other similar securities).

rules.detail: Family members and controlled entities (trusts and corporations managed by, or over whose investment decisions control is held or shared by, the Covered Person or their family members) are themselves Covered Persons, so the hedging, pledging, derivatives, short sale and margin bans apply to them directly. Routing a collar or a secured loan through a family trust or holding company therefore does not escape the prohibitions, and the Covered Person is made responsible for their compliance.
rules.evidence: This Policy applies to ... (i) such persons’ “family members” and (ii) entities (such as trusts and corporations) which such foregoing persons or their family members manage or over which they or their family members have or share control over investment decisions (“controlled entities”). You are responsible for ensuring that your family members and controlled entities comply with this policy.

For the avoidance of doubt, transactions pursuant to Rule 10b5-1 Trading Plans that are effected in accordance with this Policy may occur notwithstanding the other prohibitions included herein.

NWS.exemption_authority: The Company's Board of Directors or the Company's General Counsel may modify the Policy or grant an exception where the circumstances make it appropriate and it is in compliance with applicable law (section 2.B). This is the only relief valve; there is no hardship, financial-need or court-order exception, and the clause is stated in the context of black-out periods but is drafted at Policy level. The General Counsel and the Legal Department also administer pre-clearance and the Rule 10b5-1 guidelines.

bespoke_clauses.clause: No Hedging or Pledging. Covered Persons are prohibited from hedging or pledging any equity compensation or Company securities that they hold directly.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This single sentence kills both legs of a funded collar at once: the put and call are a hedge and the loan security is a pledge, for every Covered Person and their family members and controlled entities, with no vesting, tier or size qualifier and no clearance route.

bespoke_clauses.clause: prohibited from hedging or pledging any equity compensation or Company securities that they hold directly
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The only textual soft spot in the ban is the words 'hold directly', but the Scope section makes family members and controlled entities Covered Persons in their own right, so an indirect holding structure does not create a workable exemption and any attempt would need General Counsel confirmation.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This prohibition includes, but is not limited to, trading in Company-based put or call option contracts, trading in straddles and the like.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An OTC bilateral put and call with a bank is caught exactly as a listed option would be, and a two-leg collar is closer to a 'straddle and the like' than a plain option, so there is no exchange/OTC arbitrage.

bespoke_clauses.clause: all of the Company's securities, including ... CHESS Depositary Interests representing the Class A Common Stock and Class B Common Stock and derivative securities (including stock options, put or call options and other similar securities)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar written over ASX-quoted CDIs rather than Nasdaq-listed common stock is inside the Policy, so the ASX line offers no separate route.

bespoke_clauses.clause: For the avoidance of doubt, transactions pursuant to Rule 10b5-1 Trading Plans that are effected in accordance with this Policy may occur notwithstanding the other prohibitions included herein.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is the widest permission in the document and could in principle cover disposals inside a black-out, but Appendix A clause 4 expressly forbids any corresponding or hedging position over the plan securities, so a 10b5-1 plan is an alternative to a collar, not a wrapper for one.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This Policy may be modified or an exception granted with approval of the Company's Board of Directors or the Company's General Counsel, where the circumstances make such modification or exception appropriate, in compliance with applicable law.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The only conceivable path to a funded collar is a bespoke Board or General Counsel exception, which would sit against a proxy-disclosed anti-hedging commitment and would still have to survive Section 16, Rule 144 and short-swing profit analysis.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A short sale is a sale of securities not owned by the seller or, if owned, not delivered against such sale within twenty (20) days thereafter (a 'short against the box').
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any physically settled forward or delayed-delivery leg where shares are not delivered within twenty days is a prohibited short sale, which forecloses prepaid variable forward structures as well as collars.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Additional black-out periods may be implemented from time to time ... Any person made aware of any such additional black-out period shall not disclose the existence of the black-out to anyone else inside or outside the Company.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Undisclosed event-driven black-outs can freeze entry, roll, unwind or settlement at any time and cannot be flagged to a counterparty bank, so any structure would need documentation permitting silent suspension.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the transaction must be executed within five Trading Days after the approval is obtained, but regardless may not be executed if the Restricted Person acquires material, non-public information concerning the Company or its securities during that time.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even for permitted transactions the pricing window is five Trading Days and clearance falls away automatically on receipt of inside information, so a bank must accept a short, revocable execution window.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any Company securities purchased on the open market by a Restricted Person must be held for a minimum of six (6) months.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Combined with Section 16 short-swing profit disgorgement, this rules out any collar tenor or early unwind that could put a disposal within six months of an open-market purchase by a director or Section 16 officer.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The prohibition against trading during the Black-Out Period also prohibits the fulfillment of 'limit orders' by any broker for Restricted Persons, and the brokers with whom any such 'limit order' is placed must be informed of such prohibition at the time such 'limit order' is placed.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Automatic third-party execution is treated as the executive's own trading, so a lender's or counterparty's price-triggered sale or delivery during a black-out would be a Policy breach attributed to the executive.

bespoke_clauses.clause: transferring shares to an entity that does not involve a change in the beneficial ownership of the shares (for example, transferring shares from one brokerage account to another brokerage account that a Covered Person controls)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Moving shares into a collateral or custody account is not itself a 'transaction' needing clearance, but the security interest granted over them is still a prohibited pledge, so the transfer carve-out gives no help.

bespoke_clauses.clause: After termination of employment or other service, any Covered Person who is aware of material, non-public information regarding the Company or its securities is prohibited from trading in Company securities until that information has become public or is no longer material.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A departing executive cannot assume that leaving releases the restrictions in time to unwind or settle a structure.

NWS.summary: A funded collar is not available to a News Corp director or executive under this Policy. Both legs fail independently: section 2.A bans investing in Company-based derivative securities, expressly including put and call option contracts and straddles, with no venue limit so OTC options with a bank are caught, and the same section prohibits Covered Persons from hedging or pledging any equity compensation or Company securities they hold directly, which defeats the loan security as well as the hedge. The bans apply to every Covered Person and, through the Scope section, to family members and controlled entities, so a trust or holding company does not help, and the only carve-out is holding and exercising Company-granted options and RSUs. Layered on top for Section 16 Reporting Persons and Designated Individuals are quarterly black-outs running from fourteen days before quarter end until one Trading Day after results, General Counsel pre-clearance valid for five Trading Days, and a six-month minimum holding period on open-market purchases reinforced by short-swing profit disgorgement. The only conceivable route is a bespoke modification or exception approved by the Board of Directors or the General Counsel under section 2.B; absent that, the realistic alternative is a pre-cleared Rule 10b5-1 sale plan, which may trade notwithstanding the other prohibitions but whose Appendix A conditions expressly forbid any corresponding or hedging position over the plan securities.

NWSLV.ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Company may implement additional black-out periods from time to time with regard to certain Covered Persons or groups who are aware of non-public information regarding potentially significant matters. rules.section: 2.A (No Investments in Derivatives of the Company's Securities)
rules.detail: Flat ban on investing in Company-based derivative securities, expressly including put and call option contracts and straddles. No venue limitation, so OTC puts and calls written or bought with a bank are caught as squarely as listed ones, and the ban applies to every Covered Person and their family members and controlled entities regardless of whether the underlying shares are vested. The only carve-out is holding and exercising options, RSUs or other derivative securities granted under the Company's own equity compensation plans.
rules.evidence: No Covered Person shall invest in Company-based derivative securities. “Derivative Securities” are options, warrants, stock appreciation rights or similar rights whose value is derived from the value of an equity security, such as the Company’s common stock. This prohibition includes, but is not limited to, trading in Company-based put or call option contracts, trading in straddles and the like.

rules.detail: The single express permission: holding and exercising Company-granted options, RSUs and other plan derivative securities is not prohibited, and the grant, award, vesting and settlement of those instruments is not a 'transaction' at all. This is a carve-out for the Company's own instruments only and does not extend to third-party derivatives over the resulting shares.
rules.evidence: However, holding and exercising stock options, restricted stock units or other derivative securities granted under the Company’s equity compensation plans is not prohibited by this Policy.

rules.detail: One-sentence absolute ban on hedging any equity compensation or Company securities held directly. No definition of 'hedging' is given, no clearance or exception route is offered within the clause, and no distinction is drawn between unvested, vested-locked and vested-unrestricted holdings. A collar is the paradigm hedge and is prohibited on this clause alone, independently of the derivatives ban.
rules.evidence: No Hedging or Pledging. Covered Persons are prohibited from hedging or pledging any equity compensation or Company securities that they hold directly.

rules.section: 2.A (No Hedging or Pledging); Appendix A cl.4
rules.detail: Vesting does not release the hedging ban: it reaches 'Company securities that they hold directly', not merely unvested equity compensation. Appendix A reinforces the position for anyone using a Rule 10b5-1 plan, requiring that no corresponding or hedging transaction has been entered into or altered over the plan securities and that none be entered into while the plan is in effect.
rules.evidence: No Hedging. Covered Persons may not have entered into or altered a corresponding or hedging transaction or position with respect to the securities subject to the Rule 10b5-1 Trading Plan and must agree not to enter into any such transaction while the Rule 10b5-1 Trading Plan is in effect.

rules.section: 2.A (No Hedging or Pledging; No Investments in Derivatives)
rules.detail: Monetisation, prepaid forwards, variable prepaid forwards and zero-cost collars are not named. Each is caught twice over: as a hedge of Company securities held directly, and as an investment in a Company-based derivative security. A monetisation that instead borrows against the shares is caught by the pledging limb. There is no clearance path that cures a prohibited transaction; only the Board or General Counsel exception power in section 2.B could.
rules.evidence: Covered Persons are prohibited from hedging or pledging any equity compensation or Company securities that they hold directly.

rules.detail: Outright ban, with a definition wide enough to catch a sale of owned shares that is not settled by delivery within twenty days ('short against the box'). Relevant to any physically settled forward or delayed-delivery leg of a collar structure.
rules.evidence: No Covered Person shall engage in the short sale of the Company’s securities. A short sale is a sale of securities not owned by the seller or, if owned, not delivered against such sale within twenty (20) days thereafter (a “short against the box”).

rules.detail: Securities lending and rehypothecation are nowhere named, and the Policy has no general 'dealing' definition that sweeps them in. In practice a lend that enabled non-delivery against a sale would engage the twenty-day short-against-the-box limb, and for a Restricted Person any transaction, direct or indirect, in Company securities requires pre-clearance.

rules.section: 2.A (No Investments in Derivatives of the Company's Securities)
rules.detail: CFDs, swaps and total return swaps are not named, but the derivative-securities definition is open-ended ('or similar rights whose value is derived from the value of an equity security') and the prohibition is expressed as non-exhaustive, so a cash-settled contract for difference over News Corp stock or CDIs falls within it. A short CFD would also engage the short sale ban.
rules.evidence: “Derivative Securities” are options, warrants, stock appreciation rights or similar rights whose value is derived from the value of an equity security, such as the Company’s common stock. This prohibition includes, but is not limited to, trading in Company-based put or call option contracts, trading in straddles and the like.

rules.section: 2.A (No Margin Purchases; No Hedging or Pledging)
rules.detail: Two overlapping bans. Borrowing from a brokerage firm, bank or other entity in order to purchase Company securities is prohibited outright, with a narrow carve-out for cashless option exercises under the Company's equity plans. Borrowing against Company securities already held is prohibited under the pledging limb. Neither has a clearance or hardship route.
rules.evidence: No Covered Person shall purchase the Company’s securities on margin. This means such persons are prohibited from borrowing from a brokerage firm, bank or other entity in order to purchase the Company’s securities (other than in connection with “cashless” exercises of stock options under the Company’s equity compensation plans).

rules.detail: Pledging any equity compensation or directly held Company securities is banned in the same sentence as hedging. The ban is on the act of pledging, not on the underlying loan, so it bites on the security interest a lender would take over the collared shares. It is expressed by reference to securities 'that they hold directly', which leaves indirectly held securities textually unaddressed even though family members and controlled entities are themselves Covered Persons.
rules.evidence: No Hedging or Pledging. Covered Persons are prohibited from hedging or pledging any equity compensation or Company securities that they hold directly.

rules.section: 2.A (No Hedging or Pledging; No Margin Purchases)
rules.detail: The Policy never uses the phrase 'secured financing', but any loan secured on News Corp shares or CDIs requires a pledge, and pledging is prohibited for all Covered Persons and their family members and controlled entities without regard to vesting, tier or amount. There is no margin-loan-only qualifier, no threshold, no notification alternative and no disclosure regime; the only relief is the general Board or General Counsel exception power.
rules.evidence: Covered Persons are prohibited from hedging or pledging any equity compensation or Company securities that they hold directly.

rules.section: 2.B (No Trading in the Company's Securities on a Short-Term Basis)
rules.detail: Hard six-month minimum holding period for any Company securities purchased on the open market by a Restricted Person, reinforced by the Section 16 short-swing profit disgorgement rule. Same-day cashless option exercises are excluded provided there were no open-market purchases in the preceding six months. Any collar whose put leg could be exercised, or whose shares could be delivered, within six months of an open-market purchase would breach this.
rules.evidence: Any Company securities purchased on the open market by a Restricted Person must be held for a minimum of six (6) months.

rules.detail: The six-month holding period sits in section 2.B, which applies only to Restricted Persons. Covered Persons who are neither Section 16 Reporting Persons nor Designated Individuals have no holding period or speculative-trading restriction beyond the MNPI, short sale, derivatives, hedging, pledging and margin bans.

Restricted Persons inherit the outright derivatives ban and, even for permitted transactions, are additionally barred during quarterly and special black-out periods and must pre-clear with the General Counsel. Derivative securities including put and call options are expressly within the definition of the Company's securities to which section 2 applies, so nothing in the pre-clearance machinery converts a prohibited derivative into a permitted one.
rules.evidence: the following policies apply to all transactions (including gifts), direct or indirect, in all of the Company’s securities, including, but not limited to, the Company’s Class A Common Stock and Class B Common Stock ... CHESS Depositary Interests representing the Class A Common Stock and Class B Common Stock and derivative securities (including stock options, put or call options and other similar securities).

rules.detail: Family members and controlled entities (trusts and corporations managed by, or over whose investment decisions control is held or shared by, the Covered Person or their family members) are themselves Covered Persons, so the hedging, pledging, derivatives, short sale and margin bans apply to them directly. Routing a collar or a secured loan through a family trust or holding company therefore does not escape the prohibitions, and the Covered Person is made responsible for their compliance.
rules.evidence: This Policy applies to ... (i) such persons’ “family members” and (ii) entities (such as trusts and corporations) which such foregoing persons or their family members manage or over which they or their family members have or share control over investment decisions (“controlled entities”). You are responsible for ensuring that your family members and controlled entities comply with this policy.

If the transaction or stock option exercise is cleared to proceed, the transaction must be executed within five Trading Days after the approval is obtained, but regardless may not be executed if the Restricted Person acquires material, non-public information concerning the Company or its securities during that time.

NWSLV.exemption_authority: The Company's Board of Directors or the Company's General Counsel may modify the Policy or grant an exception where the circumstances make it appropriate and it is in compliance with applicable law (section 2.B). This is the only relief valve; there is no hardship, financial-need or court-order exception, and the clause is stated in the context of black-out periods but is drafted at Policy level. The General Counsel and the Legal Department also administer pre-clearance and the Rule 10b5-1 guidelines.

bespoke_clauses.clause: No Hedging or Pledging. Covered Persons are prohibited from hedging or pledging any equity compensation or Company securities that they hold directly.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This single sentence kills both legs of a funded collar at once: the put and call are a hedge and the loan security is a pledge, for every Covered Person and their family members and controlled entities, with no vesting, tier or size qualifier and no clearance route.

bespoke_clauses.clause: prohibited from hedging or pledging any equity compensation or Company securities that they hold directly
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The only textual soft spot in the ban is the words 'hold directly', but the Scope section makes family members and controlled entities Covered Persons in their own right, so an indirect holding structure does not create a workable exemption and any attempt would need General Counsel confirmation.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This prohibition includes, but is not limited to, trading in Company-based put or call option contracts, trading in straddles and the like.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An OTC bilateral put and call with a bank is caught exactly as a listed option would be, and a two-leg collar is closer to a 'straddle and the like' than a plain option, so there is no exchange/OTC arbitrage.

bespoke_clauses.clause: all of the Company's securities, including ... CHESS Depositary Interests representing the Class A Common Stock and Class B Common Stock and derivative securities (including stock options, put or call options and other similar securities)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar written over ASX-quoted CDIs rather than Nasdaq-listed common stock is inside the Policy, so the ASX line offers no separate route.

bespoke_clauses.clause: For the avoidance of doubt, transactions pursuant to Rule 10b5-1 Trading Plans that are effected in accordance with this Policy may occur notwithstanding the other prohibitions included herein.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is the widest permission in the document and could in principle cover disposals inside a black-out, but Appendix A clause 4 expressly forbids any corresponding or hedging position over the plan securities, so a 10b5-1 plan is an alternative to a collar, not a wrapper for one.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This Policy may be modified or an exception granted with approval of the Company's Board of Directors or the Company's General Counsel, where the circumstances make such modification or exception appropriate, in compliance with applicable law.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The only conceivable path to a funded collar is a bespoke Board or General Counsel exception, which would sit against a proxy-disclosed anti-hedging commitment and would still have to survive Section 16, Rule 144 and short-swing profit analysis.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A short sale is a sale of securities not owned by the seller or, if owned, not delivered against such sale within twenty (20) days thereafter (a 'short against the box').
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any physically settled forward or delayed-delivery leg where shares are not delivered within twenty days is a prohibited short sale, which forecloses prepaid variable forward structures as well as collars.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Additional black-out periods may be implemented from time to time ... Any person made aware of any such additional black-out period shall not disclose the existence of the black-out to anyone else inside or outside the Company.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Undisclosed event-driven black-outs can freeze entry, roll, unwind or settlement at any time and cannot be flagged to a counterparty bank, so any structure would need documentation permitting silent suspension.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the transaction must be executed within five Trading Days after the approval is obtained, but regardless may not be executed if the Restricted Person acquires material, non-public information concerning the Company or its securities during that time.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even for permitted transactions the pricing window is five Trading Days and clearance falls away automatically on receipt of inside information, so a bank must accept a short, revocable execution window.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any Company securities purchased on the open market by a Restricted Person must be held for a minimum of six (6) months.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Combined with Section 16 short-swing profit disgorgement, this rules out any collar tenor or early unwind that could put a disposal within six months of an open-market purchase by a director or Section 16 officer.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The prohibition against trading during the Black-Out Period also prohibits the fulfillment of 'limit orders' by any broker for Restricted Persons, and the brokers with whom any such 'limit order' is placed must be informed of such prohibition at the time such 'limit order' is placed.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Automatic third-party execution is treated as the executive's own trading, so a lender's or counterparty's price-triggered sale or delivery during a black-out would be a Policy breach attributed to the executive.

bespoke_clauses.clause: transferring shares to an entity that does not involve a change in the beneficial ownership of the shares (for example, transferring shares from one brokerage account to another brokerage account that a Covered Person controls)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Moving shares into a collateral or custody account is not itself a 'transaction' needing clearance, but the security interest granted over them is still a prohibited pledge, so the transfer carve-out gives no help.

bespoke_clauses.clause: After termination of employment or other service, any Covered Person who is aware of material, non-public information regarding the Company or its securities is prohibited from trading in Company securities until that information has become public or is no longer material.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A departing executive cannot assume that leaving releases the restrictions in time to unwind or settle a structure.

NWSLV.summary: A funded collar is not available to a News Corp director or executive under this Policy. Both legs fail independently: section 2.A bans investing in Company-based derivative securities, expressly including put and call option contracts and straddles, with no venue limit so OTC options with a bank are caught, and the same section prohibits Covered Persons from hedging or pledging any equity compensation or Company securities they hold directly, which defeats the loan security as well as the hedge. The bans apply to every Covered Person and, through the Scope section, to family members and controlled entities, so a trust or holding company does not help, and the only carve-out is holding and exercising Company-granted options and RSUs. Layered on top for Section 16 Reporting Persons and Designated Individuals are quarterly black-outs running from fourteen days before quarter end until one Trading Day after results, General Counsel pre-clearance valid for five Trading Days, and a six-month minimum holding period on open-market purchases reinforced by short-swing profit disgorgement. The only conceivable route is a bespoke modification or exception approved by the Board of Directors or the General Counsel under section 2.B; absent that, the realistic alternative is a pre-cleared Rule 10b5-1 sale plan, which may trade notwithstanding the other prohibitions but whose Appendix A conditions expressly forbid any corresponding or hedging position over the plan securities.
