tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: Any Director of Orica Limited, executives who are members of the Executive Committee, and any other employee who has regular access to inside information or has been advised by Company Secretariat that they are subject to the additional dealing restrictions. This tier carries the approval requirement, the blackout periods and the prohibited dealings list.

tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: A family member who may be expected to influence, or be influenced by, your dealings in Securities (including spouse or partner and their child or dependant), or a company or other entity which you have an ability to control or significantly influence. Associates are subject to the same dealing restrictions as the individual they are associated with.

windows.start_anchor: 1 April
windows.end_anchor: one trading day following the release of the Company's half year results to the ASX

windows.start_anchor: 1 October
windows.end_anchor: one trading day following the release of the Company's annual results to the ASX

ORI.ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Company may specify 'any other period' as a blackout period for Restricted Persons, and may also formally notify any individual (Restricted Person or not) that they are restricted from dealing. No criteria, duration or announcement obligation is stated, and no confidentiality rule is stated for the notification itself.

rules.section: Additional Dealing Restrictions - Prohibited dealings; Glossary (Deal or dealing, Securities)
rules.detail: Securities expressly include 'any other financial product relating to securities whether or not the product is created by Orica or by a third party', and dealing includes 'entering into a contract or arrangement to secure profit or avoid a loss by reference to price fluctuations', so an OTC put or call over Orica shares is a dealing in Securities. Because the put and call legs of a collar are hedging, they fall squarely within the express prohibited dealings list for Restricted Persons. A non-hedging derivative would instead require written approval and fall outside blackout periods.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must not enter into, create or deal in the following in respect of Securities: - margin loans; - hedging;

rules.section: General Dealing Restrictions; Glossary (Deal or dealing, Securities)
rules.detail: For employees and contractors who are not Restricted Persons the prohibited dealings list does not apply. A derivative over Orica Securities is a dealing, so it is barred only while the person holds inside information or has been formally notified that they are restricted; no approval, blackout or notification applies. Employees are told to consider perception issues and consult the Company Secretary if necessary.
rules.evidence: You may deal in Securities unless you have inside information or are a Restricted Person.

rules.detail: Hedging is listed as a flatly prohibited dealing for Restricted Persons. The word is undefined and unqualified: there is no distinction between unvested, locked and vested unrestricted Securities, no venue limit, no approval route and no exceptional-circumstances relief (the exceptional circumstances power reaches only dealing during a blackout period).
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must not enter into, create or deal in the following in respect of Securities: - margin loans; - hedging;

rules.section: General Dealing Restrictions; Additional Dealing Restrictions - Prohibited dealings
rules.detail: The hedging prohibition is expressed only as an 'additional dealing restriction' applying to Restricted Persons, so employees and contractors outside that tier are not prohibited from hedging; the only constraints are inside information, a formal restriction notice, and the general perception warning.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons have more exposure to inside information and therefore additional dealing restrictions apply.

rules.section: Additional Dealing Restrictions - Prohibited dealings; Glossary (Deal or dealing)
rules.detail: Monetisation, prepaid forwards and similar structures are not named. A prepaid forward or collar-plus-loan is an arrangement to secure profit or avoid a loss by reference to price fluctuations and is therefore a dealing; in substance it is hedging, which is prohibited for Restricted Persons, and if funded by a loan against the shares it also engages the margin loan prohibition.
rules.evidence: entering into a contract or arrangement to secure profit or avoid a loss by reference to price fluctuations

rules.detail: Short selling is an express prohibited dealing for Restricted Persons at all times, with no approval route. It is not prohibited for employees and contractors outside that tier.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must not enter into, create or deal in the following in respect of Securities: ... - short selling.

rules.detail: Securities lending is not named anywhere in the policy and the glossary definition of 'Deal or dealing' does not refer to it.

rules.section: Glossary (Deal or dealing); Additional Dealing Restrictions - Prohibited dealings
rules.detail: CFDs are not named but fall precisely within the dealing limb 'entering into a contract or arrangement to secure profit or avoid a loss by reference to price fluctuations'. For Restricted Persons a CFD is in substance hedging, a short position, or short-term dealing, all of which are prohibited dealings.
rules.evidence: entering into a contract or arrangement to secure profit or avoid a loss by reference to price fluctuations

rules.detail: Margin loans in respect of Orica Securities are an express prohibited dealing for Restricted Persons at all times, with no approval route, no vesting carve-out and no grandfathering language. Employees and contractors outside the tier are not prohibited.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must not enter into, create or deal in the following in respect of Securities: - margin loans;

rules.detail: Granting security, a charge, mortgage, lien or pledge over Orica Securities is not named as a prohibited dealing and does not appear in the glossary definition of 'Deal or dealing'. Only margin loans are expressly caught, so a security interest is regulated only to the extent it forms part of a margin loan.

The financing prohibition is drafted narrowly as 'margin loans' rather than as secured financing generally, so a bank loan secured on Orica Securities is not expressly named. Whether a limited-recourse loan advanced against collared shares is a 'margin loan' in substance is untested and the policy contains no anti-avoidance or substance-over-form clause.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must not enter into, create or deal in the following in respect of Securities: - margin loans;

rules.detail: Short-term dealing is prohibited for Restricted Persons, with on-market buying and selling within three months given as an inclusive example, so the ban is not confined to on-market round trips. No carve-out for plan securities and no stated matching basis.
rules.evidence: short-term dealing, including buying and selling Securities on market within a three month period;

clearance.approver: Directors (other than the Chairman): the Chairman. Chairman: Chair of the Board Audit & Risk Committee. Any other Restricted Person: the Company Secretary. Company Secretary: Managing Director & CEO.
clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary (Directors only), for ASX Listing Rule disclosure
clearance.post_trade_deadline: within two business days of the trade
clearance.section: Additional Dealing Restrictions - Approval to deal
clearance.evidence: A Restricted Person approved to deal must deal no later than two business days commencing on the day after approval is received, otherwise new approval must be sought. Any approval to deal may be withdrawn at any time if there is a change in circumstance, and any decision to refuse approval is final and binding and must be kept confidential.

clearance.approver: The relevant approver for the Restricted Person with whom the associate is connected
clearance.evidence: Restricted Persons must obtain written approval to deal in Securities on behalf of their associates from the relevant approver.
You may deal in Securities unless you have inside information or are a Restricted Person.

short_term.basis: on market buying and selling, given as an inclusive example of short-term dealing
short_term.evidence: short-term dealing, including buying and selling Securities on market within a three month period;

exceptions.approver: Chairman for Directors; Chair of the Board Audit & Risk Committee for the Chairman; Company Secretary for any other Restricted Person; Managing Director & CEO for the Company Secretary
exceptions.evidence: Restricted Persons that need to deal in Securities during a blackout period due to exceptional circumstances (such as demonstrated and severe financial hardship), must obtain written approval to deal in Securities during a blackout period
The acquisition of Securities through: - a dividend reinvestment plan or share purchase plan available to all retail shareholders; or - a rights issue.

Applying for or acquiring Securities under an employee incentive scheme; however, for clarity, any subsequent dealing of Securities which cease to be held under the terms of a scheme remains subject to the provisions of this Policy.
The disposal of Securities through the acceptance of a takeover offer, scheme of arrangement or equal access buy-back.

Any dealing that results in no effective change to the beneficial interest (e.g. transfer of Securities already held into a superannuation fund or trust of which you or your associate is a beneficiary).
Any dealing under a pre-approved non-discretionary trading plan, provided the plan is not entered into or amended during a blackout period (e.g. a regular share acquisition plan).

ORI.exemption_authority: Only the 'exceptional circumstances' power, which permits a Restricted Person to deal during a blackout period with written approval from the Chairman (Directors), the Chair of the Board Audit & Risk Committee (Chairman), the Company Secretary (any other Restricted Person) or the Managing Director & CEO (Company Secretary), on grounds such as demonstrated and severe financial hardship. There is no power to waive the prohibited dealings list (margin loans, hedging, short-term dealing, short selling).

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons must not enter into, create or deal in the following in respect of Securities: - margin loans; - hedging; - short-term dealing, including buying and selling Securities on market within a three month period; and - short selling.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: 'Hedging' is undefined and unlimited by vesting state or venue, so a collar over fully vested unrestricted shares is prohibited for every Director and Executive Committee member, with no approval or hardship route.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons must not enter into, create or deal in the following in respect of Securities: - margin loans.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The financing prohibition names only margin loans rather than secured financing generally, so the loan leg is not expressly banned; but with the hedge itself prohibited the point is academic, and a loan advanced against collared shares may still be characterised as a margin loan.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Securities Includes, in relation to Orica Limited: ... any other financial product relating to securities whether or not the product is created by Orica or by a third party.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bank-written OTC put and call are expressly Securities, so every leg of a collar and every roll or unwind is a dealing subject to the policy rather than sitting outside it.

bespoke_clauses.topic: profit or loss arrangements are dealings
bespoke_clauses.clause: Deal or dealing Includes: ... entering into a contract or arrangement to secure profit or avoid a loss by reference to price fluctuations.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This limb catches economically synthetic structures (collars, CFDs, prepaid forwards) even when no share changes hands, so no cash-settled variant escapes the policy.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Do not deal in Securities if the Company has formally notified you that you are restricted from dealing.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even an employee outside the Restricted Persons tier can be individually blocked at any time without notice or criteria, so a counterparty cannot rely on a person's tier remaining unrestricted for the life of a collar.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any approval to deal may be withdrawn at any time if there is a change in circumstance, and any decision to refuse approval is final and binding and must be kept confidential.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Approval can be pulled after it is given and before execution, and the executive cannot explain a refusal to the bank, so there is execution risk between pricing and signing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A Restricted Person approved to deal must deal no later than two business days commencing on the day after approval is received, otherwise new approval must be sought.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any permitted dealing must be documented and executed inside a two business day window, which is tight for negotiating and signing OTC derivative and loan documentation.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Associates of Directors, employees and contractors are subject to the same dealing restrictions that apply to that individual. ... a company or any other entity which you have an ability to control or significantly influence.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Routing a collar through a family trust or controlled company does not avoid the hedging prohibition, and the Restricted Person must obtain written approval for dealings on the associate's behalf.

bespoke_clauses.topic: plan shares remain in scope after release
bespoke_clauses.clause: Applying for or acquiring Securities under an employee incentive scheme; however, for clarity, any subsequent dealing of Securities which cease to be held under the terms of a scheme remains subject to the provisions of this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Shares released from an incentive plan do not become policy-free, so vested shares held by a Restricted Person remain subject to the hedging prohibition.

ORI.summary: A funded collar is not available to Orica Directors or Executive Committee members. They are Restricted Persons, and the policy flatly prohibits 'hedging' in respect of Securities with no definition, no vesting distinction, no venue limit, no approval route and no exceptional-circumstances relief, so the purchased put and written call are barred over vested unrestricted shares as much as over unvested ones. The financing leg is drafted more narrowly, catching only 'margin loans' rather than secured financing generally, so a bank loan secured on the shares is not expressly named, but that does not rescue the structure and such a loan may itself be characterised as a margin loan. Employees and contractors who are not Restricted Persons are not subject to the prohibited dealings list and could in principle hedge, but they would rarely be the intended clients and can be made subject to a formal restriction notice at any time. If Orica were ever to permit a structure, it would still need written approval valid for only two business days, would have to avoid the 1 April and 1 October blackouts, would be disclosed by Directors to the Company Secretary within two business days, and would have to exceed three months to avoid the short-term dealing ban.

ALD.title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Caltex staff
tiers.description: Directors, full-time, part-time and casual employees, consultants, secondees, contractors of, and persons seconded to, the Caltex Group. Staff who are not Designated Caltex Personnel may trade at any time provided they hold no inside information; none of the closed periods, clearance requirements or trading restrictions (derivatives, short-term, short selling, hedging, margin lending and secured financing) apply to them.

tiers.name: Designated Caltex Personnel
tiers.description: Caltex Australia Limited Directors (including alternate Directors), Caltex Australia Limited Leadership Team (CLT) members, and Caltex staff who have been notified that they are Designated Caltex Personnel. This tier carries the closed periods, the trading clearance regime, the post-trade notification duty and all of the substantive trading restrictions. The only differentiation within the tier is the identity of the clearance approver.

tiers.name: closely connected persons
tiers.description: Immediate family members, companies and businesses in which Caltex staff hold a controlling interest and/or are a Director or Trustee where Caltex staff are beneficiaries. Designated Caltex Personnel must take reasonable steps, including notifying them of closed periods, to prevent them trading in any way prohibited by the policy.

definitions.hedging_definition: any arrangements that would have the effect of limiting their risk exposure relating to Caltex securities, including vested Caltex securities or unvested entitlements to Caltex securities under Caltex employee incentive schemes

windows.start_anchor: 1 July
windows.end_anchor: the day after Caltex's half year results are released to ASX

windows.start_anchor: 1 January

ALD.ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Caltex Board may designate any other period as a black-out period; it must be advised to the Designated Caltex Personnel, so it is notified to those affected but not necessarily announced to the market. Separately, clearance may be withheld for perception reasons without reasons being given, and a refusal must be kept confidential by the applicant.

rules.section: Trading Restrictions - Trading in Derivatives; Definitions
rules.detail: The policy expressly extends to derivative markets and derivative products, naming warrants, exchange traded options, over-the-counter options and contracts for differences, over both vested securities and unvested entitlements, and Caltex securities are defined to include third-party issued options and swaps. A derivative is therefore a trade requiring clearance, outside closed periods, with post-trade notification. This does not rescue collar legs: any derivative that limits risk exposure is separately prohibited by the hedging ban.
rules.evidence: This policy applies to transactions in derivative markets and trading involving derivative products (including warrants, exchange traded options, over-the-counter options and contracts for differences) issued over or in respect of vested Caltex securities and unvested entitlements to Caltex securities.

rules.detail: Staff who are not Designated Caltex Personnel are outside the closed periods, the clearance regime and the Trading Restrictions section, so a derivative over Caltex securities is limited only by the insider trading prohibition.
rules.evidence: Caltex staff who are not Designated Caltex Personnel may trade in Caltex securities at any time provided they do not have or possess any inside information.

rules.detail: An effects-based ban on any arrangement limiting risk exposure to Caltex securities, expressly extended to vested securities. There is no approval route, no de minimis and no venue limit; the exceptional circumstances discretion relieves only against the closed period prohibition, not against this restriction.
rules.evidence: Designated Caltex Personnel are prohibited from entering into any arrangements that would have the effect of limiting their risk exposure relating to Caltex securities, including vested Caltex securities or unvested entitlements to Caltex securities under Caltex employee incentive schemes.

rules.detail: The same ban expressly reaches unvested entitlements under Caltex employee incentive schemes, so unvested rights cannot be hedged or used as the reference asset for a derivative.
rules.evidence: including vested Caltex securities or unvested entitlements to Caltex securities under Caltex employee incentive schemes.

rules.section: Trading Restrictions - Hedging Transactions; Insider Trading Prohibition
rules.detail: The hedging prohibition is expressed to bind Designated Caltex Personnel only, so staff outside that tier are not prohibited from hedging; the insider trading prohibition still applies at all times.
rules.evidence: Caltex staff who are not Designated Caltex Personnel may trade in Caltex securities at any time provided they do not have or possess any inside information.

rules.section: Trading Restrictions - Hedging Transactions; Margin Lending and other secured financing arrangements
rules.detail: Monetisation, prepaid forwards and collar-plus-loan structures are not named. Each has the effect of limiting risk exposure to Caltex securities and so falls within the hedging ban, and if the advance is secured on the shares it is separately caught by the secured financing prohibition.
rules.evidence: prohibited from entering into any arrangements that would have the effect of limiting their risk exposure relating to Caltex securities

rules.detail: Flat ban on entering into any arrangements for short selling Caltex securities, with no approval route or security-state carve-out. The reference to 'any arrangements' would reach synthetic short exposure as well as physical short sales.
rules.evidence: Designated Caltex Personnel are prohibited from entering into any arrangements for short selling Caltex securities.

rules.detail: Securities lending is not named. A stock loan transfers the legal interest in the security and is therefore a 'trade', so it would need clearance, fall outside closed periods and be notified within three days; it is not separately prohibited unless it forms part of a short selling or risk-limiting arrangement.
rules.evidence: "trade" includes subscribing for, buying, selling or otherwise transferring the beneficial or legal interest in a security.

rules.section: Trading Restrictions - Trading in Derivatives, Short-term Trading, Short Selling, Hedging Transactions
rules.detail: Contracts for differences are expressly brought within the policy, so they are trades requiring clearance rather than being outside it. In practice most CFD positions are separately prohibited: a short CFD by the short selling ban, a risk-limiting CFD by the hedging ban, and any CFD closed out within six months by the short-term trading ban.
rules.evidence: This policy applies to transactions in derivative markets and trading involving derivative products (including warrants, exchange traded options, over-the-counter options and contracts for differences)

rules.section: Trading Restrictions - Margin Lending and other secured financing arrangements
rules.detail: Margin lending in respect of Caltex securities is expressly prohibited at all times for all Designated Caltex Personnel, with no approval route, no vesting carve-out and no grandfathering.
rules.evidence: Designated Caltex Personnel are prohibited from entering into any margin lending and other secured financing arrangements in respect of Caltex securities.

rules.section: Trading Restrictions - Margin Lending and other secured financing arrangements
rules.detail: Granting security over Caltex securities to support financing is prohibited as a secured financing arrangement. A charge, lien or pledge unconnected with any financing is not named, and the definition of 'trade' does not expressly sweep in the creation of a security interest.
rules.evidence: prohibited from entering into any margin lending and other secured financing arrangements in respect of Caltex securities.

rules.section: Trading Restrictions - Margin Lending and other secured financing arrangements
rules.detail: The prohibition is deliberately wider than margin loans, extending to 'other secured financing arrangements in respect of Caltex securities'. It binds every Director and CLT member regardless of security state, has no clearance or waiver route, and the exceptional circumstances discretion is confined to closed period trading.
rules.evidence: Designated Caltex Personnel are prohibited from entering into any margin lending and other secured financing arrangements in respect of Caltex securities.

rules.detail: Six month ban on short-term or speculative trading, expressly extended to derivative products issued over or in respect of Caltex securities, with purchase and sale of the same securities within six months given as an inclusive example. No stated matching basis and no carve-out for plan securities.
rules.evidence: Designated Caltex Personnel are prohibited from engaging in short term or speculative trading in Caltex securities or derivative products issued over or in respect of Caltex securities, including purchasing and selling the same Caltex securities within a six month period.

clearance.approver: Company Secretary for all Designated Caltex Personnel except Directors; Chairman of the Board for Directors (excluding the Chairman); Chairman of the Audit Committee for the Chairman of the Board. Requests go by email to secretariat@caltex.com.au and the Company Secretary follows an Internal Approval Process before confirming.
clearance.post_trade_to: Caltex Secretariat (contract note, or an email with holder name, SRN/HIN, number or dollar value, price, date and nature of trade); Directors should also notify the Company Secretary as soon as practical after any Permitted Trading
clearance.post_trade_deadline: no later than three days after the date of the trade
clearance.evidence: Clearance for trading in Caltex securities is only valid for trading notified in the request for clearance and will lapse 14 calendar days after the date the clearance was granted. ... The Caltex Secretariat will respond to requests for clearance to trade in Caltex securities within one business day of receipt of the request.
Caltex staff who are not Designated Caltex Personnel may trade in Caltex securities at any time provided they do not have or possess any inside information.

clearance.section: Trading Restrictions - Trading by Connected Persons
clearance.evidence: Designated Caltex Personnel must take reasonable steps, including notifying their closely connected persons of closed periods, to prevent any closely connected persons from trading in Caltex securities in any way that is prohibited under this policy.

short_term.basis: purchasing and selling the same Caltex securities, given as an inclusive example of short term or speculative trading; expressly extends to derivative products over Caltex securities
short_term.evidence: including purchasing and selling the same Caltex securities within a six month period.

exceptions.approver: Chairman of the Board for Directors and CLT; Chairman of the Audit Committee for the Chairman of the Board
exceptions.evidence: severe financial hardship if, in the opinion of the person exercising the discretion, they are only able to meet their financial commitments by selling their securities ... and the proposed disposal of Caltex securities is the only reasonable course of action to overcome these circumstances.

exceptions.approver: Chairman of the Board for Directors and CLT; Chairman of the Audit Committee for the Chairman of the Board
exceptions.evidence: to give effect to a court order, court enforceable undertaking or other legal or regulatory requirement.

exceptions.approver: Chairman of the Board for Directors and CLT; Chairman of the Audit Committee for the Chairman of the Board
exceptions.evidence: exceptional personal circumstances;

acquisition of securities under an offer or invitation made to all or most of the security holders in Caltex, such as a rights issue, a security purchase plan, a dividend or distribution reinvestment plan or an equal access buy-back, where the timing and structure of the offer has been approved by the Caltex Board;
disposal of securities arising from the acceptance of a takeover offer, scheme or arrangement or equal access buy-back;
transfers of Caltex securities where there is no change in the person's underlying beneficial interest in the securities;
transfers of securities between someone closely related such as a spouse, minor child, family company or family trust or to their superannuation fund;

indirect or incidental trading that occurs as a consequence of Designated Caltex Personnel dealing in securities issued by a managed investment scheme, listed investment company, exchange traded fund or similar investment vehicle that is managed by a third party and that happens to hold as part of its portfolio securities in Caltex;

The restrictions on trading during closed periods do not apply to: offers made to Caltex staff to participate in Caltex short and long term incentive plans and share plans (together, Plans); acceptance by Caltex staff of offers referred to above ... and transfers of unrestricted Caltex securities from the Trustee of any of the Plans to Caltex staff

external_documents: Internal Approval Process followed by the Company Secretary before confirming clearance to trade
ALD.exemption_authority: The Chairman of the Board (for Directors and CLT) and the Chairman of the Audit Committee (for the Chairman of the Board) have a discretion to exempt from the closed period prohibition only, and only for severe financial hardship, exceptional personal circumstances, or to give effect to a court order, court enforceable undertaking or other legal or regulatory requirement, where disposal is the only reasonable course of action. No person has authority to waive the hedging, short selling, short-term trading, margin lending or secured financing prohibitions.

bespoke_clauses.topic: effects-based hedging ban over vested shares
bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Caltex Personnel are prohibited from entering into any arrangements that would have the effect of limiting their risk exposure relating to Caltex securities, including vested Caltex securities or unvested entitlements to Caltex securities under Caltex employee incentive schemes.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is drafted by economic effect and expressly reaches vested shares, so the purchased put and written call of a collar are prohibited outright for every Director and CLT member with no approval or hardship route.

bespoke_clauses.topic: secured financing wider than margin lending
bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Caltex Personnel are prohibited from entering into any margin lending and other secured financing arrangements in respect of Caltex securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg secured on the collared shares is independently prohibited, so the funded element fails even before the hedging ban is considered.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This policy applies to transactions in derivative markets and trading involving derivative products (including warrants, exchange traded options, over-the-counter options and contracts for differences) issued over or in respect of vested Caltex securities and unvested entitlements to Caltex securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no argument that a bilateral OTC collar sits outside the policy; it is expressly captured, over both vested and unvested exposure.

bespoke_clauses.clause: "Caltex securities" includes ordinary shares of Caltex and any structured financial product, swap, futures contract, option, warrant, or other derivative over an ordinary share of Caltex, whether issued by Caltex or a third party, and any other interest in an ordinary share of Caltex.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank-written put and call are themselves Caltex securities, so the six month short-term trading ban and the closed period restrictions apply to the derivative legs and to any roll or unwind, not just to the underlying shares.

bespoke_clauses.topic: six month short-term ban including derivatives
bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Caltex Personnel are prohibited from engaging in short term or speculative trading in Caltex securities or derivative products issued over or in respect of Caltex securities, including purchasing and selling the same Caltex securities within a six month period.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even if hedging were permitted, any collar with a tenor, roll or early unwind inside six months would be separately prohibited as short-term or speculative trading.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Clearance ... will lapse 14 calendar days after the date the clearance was granted ... Clearance to trade can be given or refused without giving any reasons and may be withdrawn if new information comes to light or there is a change in circumstances. If clearance to trade is refused, the person seeking the clearance must keep that information confidential and not disclose it to anyone.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any permitted transaction must be executed inside 14 calendar days, can be revoked between grant and execution, and the executive cannot tell the bank why a refusal occurred.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any clearance to trade may be withheld for perception reasons.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even a technically compliant transaction can be blocked on reputational grounds alone, which is precisely the ground on which a director's collar would be scrutinised.

bespoke_clauses.topic: transfer to a third party holding is a trade
bespoke_clauses.clause: Nature of proposed trade (i.e. on market purchase, on-market transfer or sale, transfer to super fund).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The clearance form treats a transfer to another holding vehicle as a notifiable trade, so moving collared shares into a bank custody or security account would require clearance and post-trade notification, even though transfers with no change in beneficial interest are listed as Permitted Trading.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Caltex Personnel must notify the Caltex Secretariat of details of any trading in Caltex securities by submitting a contract note to secretariat@caltex.com.au no later than three days after the date of the trade.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any collar entry, roll or unwind by a Director or CLT member is reported to the Secretariat within three days and, for Directors, flows into ASX disclosure.

bespoke_clauses.clause: "closely connected persons" of Caltex staff include immediate family members, companies and businesses in which Caltex staff hold a controlling interest and/or are a Director or Trustee where Caltex staff are beneficiaries.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Holding the shares through a family company or trust does not escape the hedging and secured financing prohibitions.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Caltex staff who are not Designated Caltex Personnel may trade in Caltex securities at any time provided they do not have or possess any inside information.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: All of the collar-relevant prohibitions bind only Designated Caltex Personnel, but any employee can be notified into that tier at any time, so a counterparty cannot rely on a client remaining outside it for the life of the trade.

ALD.summary: A funded collar is not possible for any Ampol (Caltex) Director or Leadership Team member. Both legs of the structure are separately and expressly prohibited: the hedging restriction bans 'any arrangements that would have the effect of limiting their risk exposure relating to Caltex securities, including vested Caltex securities', and the financing restriction bans 'any margin lending and other secured financing arrangements in respect of Caltex securities'. Neither prohibition has an approval route, and the only discretion in the policy, exercisable by the Chairman of the Board or the Chairman of the Audit Committee, relieves solely against the closed period restriction on grounds of severe hardship, exceptional personal circumstances or a court order. The policy expressly captures over-the-counter options and contracts for differences, and defines third-party derivatives over Caltex shares as Caltex securities, so no cash-settled or offshore variant escapes it, and the six month short-term trading ban would independently bar a short-dated collar. Only Caltex staff outside the Designated Caltex Personnel tier fall outside these restrictions, and any employee can be notified into that tier at any time.

REH.title: Securities Dealing Policy

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: All executive and non-executive directors of Reece Limited and its subsidiaries. Subject to black-out periods, the three month short-term dealing ban, prior written clearance from the Chair or Company Secretary (Chair of the Board from the Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee), immediate notification of buys and sells to the Company Secretary for ASX disclosure, and the section 6.2 hedging regime.

tiers.name: Executives
tiers.description: Employees who are members of the Executive Leadership Teams, and/or receive equity awards or any form of equity under any Group Long Term Incentive Plan, and/or hold a position which makes them a Director or Officer of any Group company under the Corporations Act. Subject to the same additional restrictions as Directors, with clearance from the MD and Group CEO or Company Secretary, plus a specific bar on hedging Plan equity awards before exercise or while subject to a transfer restriction.

tiers.name: Employees
tiers.description: All employees of the Company and its subsidiaries. Outside black-out periods, Employees other than Directors and Executives may deal without clearance provided they hold no inside information. The three month short-term dealing ban still applies to them; the section 6 clearance and hedging provisions do not.

tiers.name: Related Parties
tiers.description: A spouse, domestic partner, child (under 18) or dependent of the person, a child or dependent of their spouse or domestic partner, any other family member who may be expected to influence or be influenced by the person, or a company, trust, partnership or other entity that the person or those persons control or significantly influence. For clause 6.1 purposes a reference to Directors and Executives is also a reference to their Related Parties.

REH.ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may designate any other period as a black-out period; it must be advised to Employees, and Employees are notified of black-out periods through a notification posted to the Company intranet, so ad hoc blackouts are communicated internally rather than kept confidential. Separately, the Company may notify a person in writing that certain company securities cannot be traded for a specified period.

rules.detail: The policy expressly contemplates derivatives over Reece shares by permitting Directors to hedge their shareholdings, with equity swaps and contracts for differences named as examples of hedging instruments. Entry, renewal, alteration and close-out each require compliance with clause 6.1: advance written notice, written clearance acknowledgement from the Chair or Company Secretary, outside a black-out period, and no price sensitive information. There is no venue restriction, so an over-the-counter put and call with a bank are within the permission.
rules.evidence: Directors and Executives are only permitted to hedge their shareholdings: In compliance with section 6.1 above; and Providing the hedge transaction is not entered into, renewed, altered or closed out when the Director or Executive is in possession of price sensitive information.

rules.detail: Same position as Directors for shares that have been acquired on exercise and are free of any transfer restriction, except clearance comes from the MD and Group CEO or Company Secretary.
rules.evidence: Executives must give advance notice and receive clearance acknowledgement (e.g. by way of exchange of emails) from the MD and Group CEO or Company Secretary before commencing to deal in Company Securities

rules.detail: Employees who are not Directors or Executives are outside the section 6 clearance and hedging provisions. They may deal outside black-out periods without inside information and without clearance; the three month short-term dealing ban in 5.3 still binds them, and forward contracts are named there as prohibited short-term dealings.
rules.evidence: At any time other than during a black-out period, Employees (other than Directors and Executives) may deal in securities in the Company but only if you do not have inside information.

rules.detail: Hedging of a Director's shareholding is expressly permitted, subject only to clause 6.1 clearance and to the requirement that entry, renewal, alteration and close-out do not occur while holding price sensitive information. The bar on hedging Plan equity awards is directed at Executives; a Director who receives Plan equity would also meet the 'Executives' definition and be caught by it. There is no absolute hedging prohibition anywhere in the policy.
rules.evidence: Directors and Executives are only permitted to hedge their shareholdings: In compliance with section 6.1 above; and Providing the hedge transaction is not entered into, renewed, altered or closed out when the Director or Executive is in possession of price sensitive information.

rules.detail: Absolute bar on hedging equity awards granted under a Plan before the rights are exercised. No clearance route and no exceptional circumstances relief.
rules.evidence: However, Executives are not permitted to hedge equity awards granted under a Plan prior to exercising those rights or, once exercised, while the securities are subject to a transfer restriction.

rules.detail: The bar continues after exercise for as long as the resulting securities are subject to a transfer restriction, so shares still inside a holding lock cannot be collared.
rules.evidence: or, once exercised, while the securities are subject to a transfer restriction.

rules.detail: Once Plan awards have been exercised and the resulting securities are free of any transfer restriction, the specific bar falls away and the general permission applies: hedging is allowed with clearance from the MD and Group CEO or Company Secretary, outside black-out periods and with no price sensitive information at entry, renewal, alteration or close-out.
rules.evidence: Directors and Executives are only permitted to hedge their shareholdings: In compliance with section 6.1 above

rules.detail: Section 6.2 regulates hedging only by Directors and Executives. The policy says nothing about hedging by other Employees, who are otherwise free to deal outside black-out periods without inside information.

Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward, collar or similar is a transaction, arrangement or financial product operating to limit the economic risk of a Reece shareholding and so is hedging, permitted with clause 6.1 clearance. The counterweight is clause 5.3, which gives forward contracts as an example of prohibited short-term dealings, so a short-dated monetisation is at risk of being characterised as prohibited short-term dealing.
rules.evidence: hedging includes the entry into any transaction, arrangement or financial product which operates to limit the economic risk of a security holding in the Company

rules.detail: Short selling is not mentioned anywhere in the policy and there is no prohibited dealings list. Only the three month short-term dealing ban and the insider trading prohibition would apply.
Securities lending is not named and is not caught by the section 4.1 description of trading or dealing, which is confined to buying, selling, subscribing and agreements to do so.

Contracts for differences are expressly named as an example of a hedging instrument, so a CFD over a Director's or Executive's shareholding is permitted with clause 6.1 clearance. A CFD closed out within three months would engage the short-term dealing ban, and an Executive may not use one over unvested or transfer-restricted Plan securities.
rules.evidence: includes financial instruments such as equity swaps and contracts for differences.

rules.detail: Margin lending is not mentioned anywhere in the policy, for any tier or security state, and there is no requirement to notify or obtain approval for it.

Granting security, a charge, mortgage, lien or pledge over Company securities is not mentioned, and the section 4.1 description of trading or dealing (buy, sell, subscribe, or agree to do so) does not sweep it in.
The policy contains no secured financing provision of any kind: no ban, no clearance requirement, no disclosure obligation and no guidance on forced sales by a lender during a black-out period.

Directors and Employees must not round-trip Company securities within three months in either direction, and must not enter into any other short-term dealings, with forward contracts given as an express example. No stated matching basis and no carve-out for Plan securities or for the exercise of equity awards.
rules.evidence: Directors and Employees must not buy and sell or sell and buy securities in the Company within a three-month period or enter into any other short-term dealings in Company securities (for example, forward contracts).

REH.exemption_authority: The Company Secretary may, on written application, approve the disposal (but not the acquisition) of Company securities during a black-out period where the person holds no price sensitive information and there are exceptional circumstances such as severe financial difficulties or passive trades such as sales compelled by law; such approvals are valid for three business days. The Company Secretary may also give written permission for the sale during a black-out period of securities acquired on exercise of equity awards. No one is given authority to waive the three month short-term dealing ban or the bar on Executives hedging unvested or transfer-restricted Plan securities.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and Executives are only permitted to hedge their shareholdings: In compliance with section 6.1 above; and Providing the hedge transaction is not entered into, renewed, altered or closed out when the Director or Executive is in possession of price sensitive information.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is a permission rather than a prohibition, so the derivative legs of a collar over a Director's or Executive's shareholding are allowed provided each of entry, renewal, alteration and close-out is separately cleared and clean of price sensitive information.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The policy contains no reference to margin lending, secured financing, charges, pledges or encumbrances over Company securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg secured on the collared shares is neither prohibited nor made subject to clearance or disclosure, so the funded element of the structure is not blocked by the policy, though the bank should still confirm the position with the Company Secretary.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The policy is silent on sales of Company securities effected by a third party such as a secured lender, and there is no excluded dealing for them.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A lender enforcement sale or physical settlement falling inside a black-out period has no safe harbour, and the only relief route is a discretionary Company Secretary approval for a disposal on exceptional circumstances grounds.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and Employees must not buy and sell or sell and buy securities in the Company within a three-month period or enter into any other short-term dealings in Company securities (for example, forward contracts).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Forward-style monetisation is expressly given as an example of a prohibited short-term dealing, so the collar tenor and any roll or unwind should comfortably exceed three months and the structure should be documented as a hedge rather than a forward sale.

bespoke_clauses.clause: However, Executives are not permitted to hedge equity awards granted under a Plan prior to exercising those rights or, once exercised, while the securities are subject to a transfer restriction.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The collar can only reference shares acquired on exercise that are free of any transfer restriction, so the eligible parcel must be verified against Plan records before pricing.

bespoke_clauses.topic: close-out is a separate cleared event
bespoke_clauses.clause: Providing the hedge transaction is not entered into, renewed, altered or closed out when the Director or Executive is in possession of price sensitive information.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Renewal, amendment and termination of the collar each require the person to be clean of price sensitive information and, under clause 6.1, to be cleared and outside a black-out period, so the documentation should avoid automatic or counterparty-triggered close-outs.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Can be given or refused by Reece in its discretion, without giving any reasons; Can be withdrawn if new information comes to light or there is a change in circumstances; Reece's discretion to refuse clearance is final and binding.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Clearance can be revoked between grant and execution and a refusal cannot be explained to the bank, so there is execution risk in the five business day window.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A clearance under this clause is not an endorsement of proposed trading and it is the Directors and Executives whom are ultimately responsible for ensuring their dealings in securities comply with the applicable laws and as applicable, the Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A clearance acknowledgement should not be treated by the bank as a company confirmation that the collar is compliant; the risk stays with the individual.

bespoke_clauses.clause: For the purpose of this clause 6.1, a reference to 'Directors' and 'Executives' is also a reference to their Related Parties. ... A company, trust, partnership or another entity that the person or any of the persons referred to in the above bullet points controls or significantly influences.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar entered through a family trust or controlled company still requires clearance, and the Director or Executive must communicate with the approver on that entity's behalf.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If you possess price sensitive information in relation to an entity you cannot 'trade' or 'deal' in the following ways: Buy or sell securities in that entity or subscribe for new securities; or Enter into an agreement to subscribe for, buy or sell securities in that entity.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The general dealing definition does not sweep in derivatives, encumbrances or stock lending; derivatives are regulated only through the separate section 6.2 hedging regime, which is a permission, so the policy's restrictive reach over an OTC collar is narrow.

bespoke_clauses.clause: you may apply in writing to the Company Secretary for approval to dispose of (but not to acquire) Company securities during a black-out period.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The exceptional circumstances relief is disposal-only, so a collar entry (which involves acquiring a put) cannot be cleared inside a black-out period on hardship grounds.

REH.summary: A funded collar is available to Reece Directors and Executives, on conditions, and this policy is unusually permissive. Section 6.2 expressly permits Directors and Executives to hedge their shareholdings, defining hedging to include any transaction, arrangement or financial product limiting the economic risk of a Reece holding and naming equity swaps and contracts for differences, with no venue restriction, so an over-the-counter put and call with a bank are contemplated. The conditions are prior written clearance under clause 6.1 (Chair or Company Secretary for Directors, Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee for the Chair of the Board, MD and Group CEO or Company Secretary for Executives), execution within five business days, dealing outside the 1 January, 1 July and 1 October black-out periods, no price sensitive information at entry, renewal, alteration or close-out, and immediate notification by Directors to the Company Secretary for ASX disclosure. The loan leg is not obstructed: the policy says nothing at all about margin lending, secured financing, charges or pledges over Company securities, and imposes no related disclosure, although it equally gives no safe harbour for a lender's forced sale during a black-out period. The collar must reference shares that are not unvested Plan awards or subject to a transfer restriction, and its tenor, roll and unwind should exceed three months because clause 5.3 bans short-term dealings and gives forward contracts as an example.

NXT.title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: Directors and Senior Executives, Senior Executives being the Managing Director, other key management personnel as defined under the Corporations Act who hold executive roles, direct reports to the Managing Director who are not KMP, and others selected by the Board. This tier carries the Blackout Periods, the 12 month short-term trading ban, the prior consent requirement for dealing and for Hedging, and the post-trade confirmation duty.

tiers.name: Employees
tiers.description: All directors, Senior Executives and employees of the Company and its subsidiaries. Employees who are not Restricted Persons may deal at any time provided they notify the Company Secretary before and after the transaction and hold no inside information; they are only 'strongly advised' not to deal during Blackout Periods and are not subject to the 12 month short-term trading ban.

tiers.name: Connected Persons
tiers.description: Associates of Restricted Persons, including a company or trust controlled by the Restricted Person, a spouse, dependent children, a close relative and a person acting in concert with the Restricted Person. Connected Persons are subject to the same Blackout Periods, short-term trading ban, consent requirement and Hedging rules, and Restricted Persons must take appropriate steps to ensure they do not breach the policy.

definitions.hedging_definition: transactions or arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk of their holdings of Company securities (known as Hedging)

NXT.ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may specify any other period as a Blackout Period from time to time. No criteria, notification method, duration or confidentiality rule is stated. Separately, the Board may in its discretion determine that persons other than Restricted Persons are prohibited from Hedging.

rules.detail: The definition of Company securities is confined to Company-issued instruments (shares, debentures, units of shares and rights or options to acquire or subscribe for shares), and 'deal' is confined to subscribing, purchasing, selling and agreements to do so, so a bank-written option is not itself a Company security. Paragraph 15 nonetheless regulates derivatives economically by requiring prior consent for any transaction or arrangement which operates to limit the economic risk of a holding, with no venue limit, so an over-the-counter put and call over vested unrestricted shares require the prior consent of the Managing Director (or the Chairman of the Board for the Managing Director) and post-trade confirmation.
rules.evidence: A Restricted Person or Connected Person may not deal in Company securities or enter into transactions or arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk of their holdings of Company securities (known as Hedging) without the prior consent of the Managing Director or Chairman of the Board in the case of the Managing Director before commencing the transaction.

rules.detail: Employees who are not Restricted Persons need only notify the Company Secretary before and after a transaction; the paragraph 15 consent requirement binds Restricted Persons and Connected Persons only, and the Board would have to make a specific determination to prohibit Hedging by anyone else.
rules.evidence: Employees other than Restricted Persons may deal in Company securities at any time if the employee notifies the Company Secretary before commencing the transaction and after the transaction has occurred, providing confirmation of the trading.

rules.detail: Hedging is not banned outright for ordinary shareholdings: it requires the prior consent of the Managing Director (or the Chairman of the Board where the Managing Director is hedging), and subsequent confirmation of the trading, including trading by a Connected Person. The policy records that Hedging is 'generally speaking discouraged', so consent is discretionary and may be refused or made conditional without reasons.
rules.evidence: Generally speaking Hedging is discouraged and is explicitly prohibited in relation to participation in any securities-based remuneration plan or scheme operated by the Company.

rules.detail: Hedging is explicitly prohibited in relation to participation in any securities-based remuneration plan or scheme operated by the Company, which covers unvested options and rights held under those plans. The only route around it would be the paragraph 14 exceptional circumstances discretion.
rules.evidence: Hedging ... is explicitly prohibited in relation to participation in any securities-based remuneration plan or scheme operated by the Company.

rules.detail: The same explicit prohibition applies while securities remain part of participation in a securities-based remuneration plan or scheme. Shares received on exercise may not be sold other than in accordance with the policy's procedures, so shares still held under plan arrangements should be treated as outside the collar.
rules.evidence: explicitly prohibited in relation to participation in any securities-based remuneration plan or scheme operated by the Company.

rules.detail: Paragraph 15 binds Restricted Persons and Connected Persons. Employees outside those tiers may hedge subject only to the paragraph 18 notification duty and the insider trading prohibition, unless and until the Board exercises its discretion to prohibit them.
rules.evidence: The Board may, in its discretion, determine that other persons are prohibited from Hedging.

rules.detail: Monetisation, prepaid forwards and collar-plus-loan structures are not named. Each is an arrangement operating to limit the economic risk of a holding and so falls within Hedging, requiring prior consent and post-trade confirmation. A structure that in substance sells the shares within 12 months would also engage the short-term trading ban.
rules.evidence: enter into transactions or arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk of their holdings of Company securities (known as Hedging) without the prior consent of the Managing Director

rules.detail: Short selling is not mentioned anywhere in the policy. A short position would in practice be caught by the 12 month short-term trading ban for Restricted Persons and by the Front Page Test general principle.
Securities lending is not named, and the definition of 'deal' is confined to subscribing for, purchasing or selling Company securities or agreeing to do those things.

CFDs are not named. A CFD written against an existing holding is an arrangement limiting economic risk and so is Hedging requiring prior consent; a speculative CFD closed out within 12 months would breach the short-term trading ban and would be difficult to reconcile with the Front Page Test.
rules.evidence: transactions or arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk of their holdings of Company securities (known as Hedging)

rules.detail: There is no margin lending clause. The nearest provision is the general principle that personal trading must not use broker credit and must settle on relevant exchange settlement terms and industry standards, which bars buying Company securities on credit extended by a broker. It is directed at settlement of trades rather than at a third party lender taking security over an existing holding, and the accompanying principle that trading be on a scale reflecting the individual's ability to fund and maintain the portfolio points the same way.
rules.evidence: do not utilise broker credit - relevant exchange settlement terms must apply on all occasions and all transactions must be settled according to industry standards;

rules.detail: Granting security, a charge, mortgage, lien or pledge over Company securities is not mentioned, is not within the definition of 'deal', and triggers no notification or consent obligation.

The policy contains no secured financing provision: no prohibition, no consent requirement, no disclosure obligation and no treatment of a lender's forced sale during a Blackout Period. Only the broker credit principle in paragraph 11(f) and the perception-based Front Page Test bear on the question.

An unusually long 12 month intention test binding Restricted Persons and Connected Persons at all times, catching both a purchase with a view to resale and a sale with a view to repurchase within 12 months. The only carve-out is the sale of shares acquired on conversion of a security where the combined holding periods of the security and the resulting shares exceed 12 months. Paragraph 14 allows the Managing Director or Chairman to approve dealings that would otherwise be prohibited, so this ban is in principle waivable.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons and Connected Persons may never engage in short term trading of any Company securities. In general, the purchase of securities with a view to resale within a 12 month period and the sale of securities with a view to repurchase within a 12 month period would be considered to be transactions of a "short term" nature.

clearance.approver: Paragraphs 11(h) and 15 require the prior approval or consent of the Managing Director, or the Chairman of the Board in the case of the Managing Director. Paragraph 16 instead routes the request through the Company Secretary, who seeks consent from the Chairman of the Board as Authorising Officer, or from the Chairman of the Audit & Risk Management Committee where the Chairman of the Board is the person dealing.

NXT.exemption_authority: Paragraph 14: in exceptional circumstances the Managing Director, or the Chairman of the Board in the case of the Managing Director, has discretion to approve dealings during a Blackout Period 'or other dealings that would otherwise be prohibited by this policy'. This is a broad waiver power that on its face can relieve against the short-term trading ban and the prohibition on Hedging plan securities, assessed case by case in the absolute discretion of the Board, and it may include severe financial hardship or a court order or court enforceable undertaking. Any such approval must be provided by electronic delivery via email and the paragraph 16 notification and procedural requirements still apply.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A Restricted Person or Connected Person may not deal in Company securities or enter into transactions or arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk of their holdings of Company securities (known as Hedging) without the prior consent of the Managing Director or Chairman of the Board in the case of the Managing Director before commencing the transaction.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Hedging is a consent-gated activity rather than a prohibition, so the derivative legs of a collar over ordinary vested shares can be approved; the consent is discretionary and the policy adds that Hedging is 'generally speaking discouraged'.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The policy contains no provision on margin lending, secured financing, charges, mortgages or pledges over Company securities, and no related disclosure obligation.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg secured on the collared shares is not prohibited or made subject to consent, so the funded element turns on the general principles and on whatever conditions the approver imposes rather than on an express bar.

bespoke_clauses.clause: do not utilise broker credit - relevant exchange settlement terms must apply on all occasions and all transactions must be settled according to industry standards.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The only leverage-related principle in the policy bars trading on broker credit, so the bank should structure the facility as a third party loan secured on an existing holding rather than as credit used to acquire or settle Company securities.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons and Connected Persons may never engage in short term trading of any Company securities. In general, the purchase of securities with a view to resale within a 12 month period and the sale of securities with a view to repurchase within a 12 month period would be considered to be transactions of a "short term" nature.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The tenor of the collar, and any roll, early termination or physical settlement, should exceed 12 months, since a written call that is exercised inside that period looks like a sale with a view to a repurchase or a short-dated disposal.

bespoke_clauses.clause: in exceptional circumstances the Managing Director or Chairman of the Board in the case of the Managing Director, has discretion to approve dealings in Company securities during a Blackout Period, or other dealings that would otherwise be prohibited by this policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike most ASX policies, the waiver power extends beyond blackout relief to any dealing otherwise prohibited, so even the plan-securities hedging bar and the 12 month rule are in principle waivable on a case-by-case basis.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Paragraphs 11(h) and 15 require consent from the Managing Director (or the Chairman for the Managing Director), while paragraph 16 requires the Company Secretary to seek consent from the Chairman of the Board as Authorising Officer (or the Chairman of the Audit & Risk Management Committee for the Chairman of the Board).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The policy names two different approval routes for the same dealing, so consent for a collar should be obtained from both the Managing Director and the Chairman of the Board through the Company Secretary to be safe.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Authorising Officer may refuse to consent to the proposed dealing or impose conditions on the dealing at their discretion, and is not obliged to provide reasons for any refusal or condition.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The company can attach conditions to a collar approval, for example on size, tenor or disclosure, and those conditions must be reflected in the derivative and loan documentation before pricing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: In all cases, the dealing consented to must occur within 5 business days following approval, otherwise the consent is no longer effective and fresh consent must be sought.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The collar and loan documentation must be ready to sign before consent is sought, since the approval expires five business days after it is granted.

bespoke_clauses.clause: "Company securities" includes any shares in the Company, debentures (including convertible notes) issued by the Company, units of shares in the Company and rights or options to acquire or subscribe for shares in the Company.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Third party derivatives are not themselves Company securities, so a bank-written put and call are caught by the paragraph 15 Hedging test rather than by the dealing and Blackout provisions, and the analysis turns on economic effect rather than on instrument type.

bespoke_clauses.clause: avoid personal trading that would not satisfy the Front Page Test, being: If the market was aware of all the current circumstances, could the proposed dealing be perceived by the market as the individual taking advantage of his or her position in an inappropriate way? How would it look if the transaction were reported on the front page of the newspaper?
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A director's funded collar is exactly the kind of transaction that attracts perception scrutiny, so the approver may refuse consent on this ground alone even though nothing in the policy prohibits it.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A Restricted Person must also provide the Managing Director or Chairman of the Board ... with subsequent confirmation of the trading that has occurred (including trading by one of their Connected Persons). ... a director must notify the ASX within 5 days after any change in the director's relevant interest in securities of the Company.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Hedging by a Restricted Person must be confirmed to the company after the event and a director's change in relevant interest reaches the ASX within five days, so the collar will not stay private.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This policy also applies to Connected Persons of all Restricted Persons, being each of their respective associates (including a company or trust controlled by the Restricted Person, a spouse, dependent children, a close relative, a person acting in concert with the Restricted Person, etc).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Holding the collared shares through a controlled company or trust does not avoid the consent, short-term trading or confirmation requirements.

NXT.summary: A funded collar is possible for a NEXTDC director or Senior Executive, but only with discretionary consent and over ordinary vested shares. Hedging is defined by economic effect and is consent-gated rather than banned: a Restricted Person may not enter into transactions or arrangements limiting the economic risk of their holdings without the prior consent of the Managing Director (the Chairman of the Board where the Managing Director is hedging), must confirm the trading afterwards, and the policy records that Hedging is 'generally speaking discouraged' and is explicitly prohibited in relation to participation in any securities-based remuneration plan or scheme, so the collar must reference shares held outside those plan arrangements. The loan leg is not obstructed, since the policy says nothing about margin lending, secured financing or encumbrances; the only leverage-related principle bars the use of broker credit in settling trades, which a third party facility secured on an existing holding does not engage. The main practical constraints are the 12 month short-term trading ban, which argues for a tenor and unwind window comfortably beyond 12 months, the Blackout Periods running from 31 December and 30 June until the morning after results, the five business day life of a consent, the approver's unreviewable power to refuse or impose conditions without reasons, and the Front Page Test perception standard. Unusually, paragraph 14 gives the Managing Director or Chairman a discretion to approve not only blackout dealings but 'other dealings that would otherwise be prohibited by this policy', so even the plan-securities hedging bar and the 12 month rule are in principle waivable.

LNW.title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Employees
tiers.description: All of Light & Wonder's Directors, employees, consultants and independent contractors engaged by Light & Wonder. Section 3 restrictions (inside information, front page test, no speculative dealing/short selling, publicly traded options, hedging and monetisation, standing orders, margin accounts and pledging) apply to this whole tier.

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: Directors, Senior Executives (other key management personnel including the CEO and any direct reports to the CEO), Section 16 Officers and Nominated Employees. Only this tier is subject to the section 4 blackout periods and prior approval requirement.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Directors of the Company; a component of Restricted Persons, separately subject to prompt post-trade notification to the Chief Legal Officer and to US Section 16 and Rule 144 obligations.

tiers.name: Senior Executives

tiers.name: Section 16 Officers
tiers.description: Officers subject to Section 16 of the US Securities Exchange Act of 1934; a component of Restricted Persons, separately subject to post-trade notification, Form 4 filing, short-swing profit disgorgement and the statutory short sale ban.

The same restrictions apply to them as to the Employee.
