DNL.exemption_authority: Section 4.5: an Employee who needs to deal during a blackout period because of exceptional circumstances, likely severe financial hardship or compulsion by court order, and who holds no Inside Information, may apply for approval through the section 6 process; approval is granted only on sufficient evidence, in the clearer's opinion, that the dealing is the most reasonable course of action available. Approval will never be granted where the dealing fails the Front Page Test (s4.2). There is no power to exempt anyone from the margin lending prohibition or the hedging prohibitions in section 5.4.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons are not permitted to enter into margin lending arrangements in relation to the Company's securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg is the problem: if the facility secured on the collared shares is characterised as a margin lending arrangement it is flatly prohibited for Directors, Senior Executives and Nominated Employees, with no approval route.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Company will take a substance over form approach and will have regard to the intent and spirit of this Policy when applying and enforcing it.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A facility documented as a term loan rather than a margin loan will still be assessed on its substance, so LVR tests, top-up rights and enforcement over the shares make the section 5.2 ban likely to bite.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Short-term trading includes buying and selling securities on market within a 90 day period, and entering into other short term dealings (for example, forward contracts).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A short-dated collar or forward leg can itself be a prohibited short-term dealing, so tenor should comfortably exceed 90 days and early termination rights should be limited.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Company securities held by a Restricted Person must never be hedged while they are subject to a holding lock or restriction on dealing under the terms of an employee, executive or director equity plan.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Vesting alone is not enough: shares still under a plan holding lock cannot be collared, so the bank must diligence lock status as well as vesting.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Sections 4.3, 4.4 and 5.1 of this Policy do not apply to ... a disposal of securities of the Company that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If a compliant secured facility could be put in place, enforcement sales sit outside the blackout and approval rules, though this carve-out cannot cure the margin lending prohibition itself.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where any approval is required for a dealing under this Policy, approval will not be granted where the dealing would not satisfy the Front Page Test.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even an otherwise compliant collar over vested shares can be refused on perception grounds alone, and the approver need not give reasons.

bespoke_clauses.clause: During any period that is not a trading blackout period under section 4.4, Restricted Persons must, prior to any proposed dealing, seek approval for the proposed dealing in the Company's securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no free trading window: entry, roll, partial unwind and physical settlement each need fresh written approval, valid only 5 business days.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The approver is not obliged to provide reasons for any aspect of their decision, and may revoke their approval at any time. If a request is not approved or an approval is revoked, that fact must be kept confidential.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Approval can be withdrawn after pricing is agreed and the client cannot explain why, so the documentation must tolerate silent withdrawal before settlement.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Employees must not deal in Company securities: from the close of trading on the ASX on 30 September each year until the day after the announcement to ASX of the full year results ... from the close of trading on the ASX on 31 March each year until the day after the announcement to ASX of the half-year results.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The blackouts follow a 30 September financial year end, and approval is described as more likely only in the 4 weeks after each results release, so execution should be scheduled into those windows.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons must take appropriate steps to ensure that their Connected Persons only deal in securities in circumstances where the Restricted Person to whom they are connected would be permitted to deal under this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Booking the structure through a spouse, family trust or controlled entity does not escape the margin lending ban or the clearance requirement.

DNL.summary: The derivative legs of a collar are achievable for a Restricted Person, but the funding leg is the obstacle. Hedging is defined as any arrangement limiting the economic risk of holding Company securities and is prohibited only over unvested plan securities and securities under a plan holding lock, so a put and call over vested, unrestricted shares is permitted subject to prior written approval on the Clearance to Trade Request Form (Chairman for Directors, Company Secretary for Senior Executives), execution within 5 business days, the 30 September and 31 March blackouts and the Front Page Test. However, section 5.2 flatly prohibits Restricted Persons from entering into margin lending arrangements in relation to the Company's securities, with no approval route, and the express substance over form principle means a bank facility secured on the collared shares with LVR or margin call mechanics is likely to be treated as such, so a funded structure would need to be demonstrably not a margin lending arrangement. Tenor is a further constraint: forward contracts are expressly given as an example of a prohibited short term dealing and buying and selling within 90 days is banned, so the collar should run well beyond 90 days. If a compliant facility could be structured, section 7(g) helpfully excludes a secured lender's enforcement sale from the blackout and approval rules.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The windows trading policy means that trading in both securities and derivatives of Atlas Arteria can only occur at the discretion of the ATLAX and ATLIX Boards during the four week window commencing after: the release of annual and half yearly results; the Annual General Meeting; and lodgement with ASIC or ASX of a disclosure document or a cleansing statement for a capital raising.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no default open period: every leg of a collar (entry, roll, unwind, physical settlement) must be executed inside a Board-opened four week window that may be withheld or shut without notice.

bespoke_clauses.clause: ATLAX and ATLIX directors along with the CEO and direct reports to the CEO, must not enter into margin loans or other secured financing arrangements over their Atlas Arteria Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar secured on the collared shares is expressly prohibited for directors, the CEO and CEO direct reports, but the ban does not reach Staff below that level.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and Staff must not engage in short term or speculative trading in Atlas Arteria securities, or in derivative or other financial products issued over or in respect of Atlas Arteria securities. Short term means a term of less than a six month period.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar must have a term of at least six months and must not be structured with early unwind or knock-out features that make it short term or speculative in substance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: In the case of ATLAX and ATLIX directors, the CEO and direct reports to the CEO, they are expected to not actively trade in Atlas Arteria securities and if they wish to sell must also pre-clear these trades through the ATLAX or ATLIX Chair (as relevant).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even where a structure is technically permitted, the senior group is expected to be inactive, so a bank should assume any derivative programme for them attracts Chair-level scrutiny.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If pre-clearance is given for a specific transaction, then the order must be placed and executed within three trading days following the granting of the pre-clearance. Any part of the order that is not actioned within this time must be pre-cleared again or cancelled.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Pricing, documentation and execution of both collar legs must complete inside three trading days of clearance or the clearance must be sought again.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A pre-clearance can be withdrawn if new information comes to light or there is a change in circumstances. Any pre-clearance to trade can be given or refused by the clearer in their discretion, without giving any reasons. A decision to refuse pre-clearance is final and binding.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bank cannot rely on a granted clearance surviving to settlement, and there is no appeal if clearance for an unwind or settlement is refused.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Staff who hold unvested or restricted Atlas Arteria securities must ... not enter into any transaction that limits the economic risk of holding unvested or restricted securities. This includes not entering any transaction to manage the risk of the timing, likelihood or manner of vesting, or unrestricted vesting.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The hedging ban is limited to unvested or restricted securities, so a collar over vested unrestricted shares is not caught by it; but the collar must not be sized so that it economically covers unvested awards as well.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Trades in Atlas Arteria ... are prohibited for Atlas Arteria Staff and their Associates, as defined above, outside of the designated trading windows.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Booking the collar through a family trust, SMSF, controlled company or spouse does not escape the windows, pre-clearance or (for directors and the CEO group) the secured financing ban.

bespoke_clauses.clause: ATLAX and ATLIX directors are required to acquire and maintain a minimum holding of Atlas Arteria Securities which equates to one year of the base non-executive director fee.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Directors must keep an unencumbered-equivalent holding, and the policy is silent on whether collared or pledged shares count towards it, so the bank should assume shares delivered under the collar reduce compliance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The policy contains no provision dealing with sales by a third party (such as a lender) outside the holder's control, and no exemption other than exceptional circumstances.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If a financier ever sold collared shares outside a window there is no excluded-dealing safe harbour, and the holder would need a written exceptional-circumstances exemption from the Company Secretary and CEO (and Chairs).

ALX.summary: A funded collar is blocked for directors, the CEO and the CEO's direct reports, because they must not enter into margin loans or other secured financing arrangements over their Atlas Arteria Securities, and the only relief is a written exceptional-circumstances exemption drafted around forced sales and unforeseeable hardship. For Staff below that level the secured loan leg is not restricted, and a collar over vested unrestricted shares is possible in principle: the hedging ban reaches only unvested or restricted securities, and the derivative legs are simply trading in derivatives of Atlas Arteria. Any such structure must be entered inside a Board-opened four week window following results, the AGM or a capital raising, with prior written pre-clearance from the ATLAX Company Secretary (Chair as well for a sale by the senior group) and execution within three trading days, and the clearance can be withdrawn at any time before dealing. The tenor must be at least six months, because short term or speculative trading in derivatives or other financial products over ALX securities is expressly banned. Every later step, including roll, unwind and physical settlement, is a fresh trade needing its own window and pre-clearance, and there is no safe harbour for a lender's sale outside a window.

tiers.name: Designated Persons
tiers.description: All directors and other key management personnel of Steadfast, and any other person designated by the Managing Director & CEO from time to time, in relation to which the Company Secretary maintains a list. Parts 3 to 6 (trading windows, prior notification, clearance, notification of dealing, records, exceptional circumstances, permitted dealings, margin lending, short term trading, short selling, stock lending and hedging) apply only to this tier and their Associates.

tiers.name: Directors and alternate directors of Steadfast (other than the Chair)
tiers.description: Board directors and alternate directors other than the Chair; the Company Secretary is grouped with them for clearance. They clear through the Chair. Their off-market transfers with no change in beneficial ownership are expressly carved out of the permitted-dealings exclusion, so such transfers remain subject to windows and clearance for them.

tiers.name: Chair
tiers.description: The chair of the Board. Clears through the Chair of the Audit & Risk Committee or another non-executive director nominated by that Chair; exceptional circumstances involving the Chair are determined by the Chair of the Audit & Risk Committee.

tiers.name: key management personnel
tiers.description: Steadfast's key management personnel. Automatically Designated Persons, and the hedging prohibition is extended beyond them to their closely related parties as defined in the Corporations Act.

tiers.name: all directors, employees and contractors of Steadfast

rules.detail: Steadfast's Securities expressly include options, derivatives and other financial products of Steadfast that are able to be traded on a financial market, and dealing includes applying for, granting, exercising or transferring options. Exchange-traded options over SDF are therefore dealings requiring an open 30 day window and clearance from the Notification Officer.
rules.evidence: this policy summarises the law relating to insider trading and sets out Steadfast's policy on dealing in securities of Steadfast including shares, options, derivatives and any other financial products of Steadfast that are able to be traded on a financial market ("Steadfast's Securities").

rules.detail: The definition of Steadfast's Securities is qualified by 'that are able to be traded on a financial market', so a bilateral OTC put and call written by a bank is arguably outside part 3 and needs no window or clearance. The separately defined 'financial products' (which expressly includes swaps, forward contracts and contracts for difference issued or created over or associated with Steadfast's Securities by third parties) is used only in the short term trading prohibition in 6.2, not in the clearance regime. Prudent practice would still be to clear.
rules.evidence: financial products includes derivatives, options, warrants, futures, forward contracts, swaps and contracts for difference issued or created over or associated with Steadfast's Securities by third parties;

rules.detail: Absolute ban, with no clearance route, on any transaction or arrangement with anyone that could have the effect of limiting exposure to risk relating to an unvested element of remuneration. Only a disposal, not a hedge, can be relieved under the exceptional circumstances provision in part 4.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons (and, in relation to Steadfast's key management personnel, their closely related parties) must not enter into transactions or arrangements with anyone which could have the effect of limiting their exposure to risk relating to an element of their remuneration that: a) has not vested

rules.detail: The ban extends expressly to remuneration that has vested but remains subject to a holding lock, so shares still in a disposal restriction period cannot be collared.
rules.evidence: b) has vested but remains subject to a holding lock.

rules.detail: The hedging ban is confined to unvested remuneration and vested remuneration under a holding lock, so hedging vested unrestricted shares (whether plan-sourced or bought on market) is not prohibited. Any hedge implemented through Steadfast's Securities still needs an open window and prior clearance, and must not amount to short term trading within 3 months.
rules.evidence: must not enter into transactions or arrangements with anyone which could have the effect of limiting their exposure to risk relating to an element of their remuneration that: a) has not vested; or b) has vested but remains subject to a holding lock.

rules.detail: For KMP the hedging ban reaches beyond Associates to closely related parties as defined in the Corporations Act, so hedges booked by a KMP's spouse, dependant or controlled entity over unvested or holding-locked remuneration are equally banned.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons (and, in relation to Steadfast's key management personnel, their closely related parties) must not enter into transactions or arrangements with anyone which could have the effect of limiting their exposure to risk

rules.tier: all directors, employees and contractors of Steadfast
rules.detail: Parts 3 to 6 apply only to Designated Persons, so employees and contractors who are not directors, KMP or designated by the MD & CEO are not subject to the hedging, margin lending, short term trading, short selling or stock lending restrictions at all; only the insider trading prohibitions bind them.
rules.evidence: parts 3 to 6 (trading policy) apply to all directors and other key management personnel of Steadfast, and any other person designated by the Managing Director & CEO from time to time

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward, collar-plus-loan or similar monetisation that is secured on SDF securities is caught by the flat ban on margin lending or other secured financing arrangements in relation to Steadfast's Securities. An unsecured monetisation implemented through tradable Steadfast Securities would instead be a dealing requiring window and clearance.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons and their Associates are not permitted to enter into margin lending or other secured financing arrangements in relation to Steadfast's Securities.

rules.detail: Flat ban on short selling SDF securities by Designated Persons and their Associates, with no clearance route.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons and their Associates are not permitted to engage in short selling or stock lending of Steadfast's Securities.

rules.detail: Stock lending of SDF securities is expressly prohibited alongside short selling, which rules out any collar structure in which the shares are lent to the bank or on to the hedging desk.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons and their Associates are not permitted to engage in short selling or stock lending of Steadfast's Securities.

rules.detail: Contracts for difference are not separately prohibited but are named in the definition of 'financial products', which is the subject of the short term trading ban; a CFD entered and closed within 3 months is therefore prohibited, and a short CFD would also breach the short selling ban.
rules.evidence: financial products includes derivatives, options, warrants, futures, forward contracts, swaps and contracts for difference issued or created over or associated with Steadfast's Securities by third parties;

rules.detail: Flat ban on margin lending for Designated Persons and their Associates, with the stated rationale that the terms may force a sale outside a window or while holding Inside Information. Uncertain cases are to be referred to the Company Secretary.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons and their Associates are not permitted to enter into margin lending or other secured financing arrangements in relation to Steadfast's Securities. This is on the grounds that the terms may require Steadfast's Securities to be sold outside a trading window or when the Designated Person possesses Inside Information.

rules.detail: Granting security over SDF securities to support any financing is prohibited as an 'other secured financing arrangement in relation to Steadfast's Securities'. A charge or pledge unconnected with a financing is not addressed and is not within the definition of dealing.
rules.evidence: not permitted to enter into margin lending or other secured financing arrangements in relation to Steadfast's Securities.

rules.detail: The prohibition is not limited to margin loans: any secured financing arrangement in relation to Steadfast's Securities is banned for Designated Persons and Associates regardless of vesting state or loan-to-value ratio. There is no clearance route; the only conceivable relief is the Board's general power to adjust or exclude a requirement of the policy case by case.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons and their Associates are not permitted to enter into margin lending or other secured financing arrangements in relation to Steadfast's Securities.

rules.tier: all directors, employees and contractors of Steadfast
rules.detail: Employees and contractors who are not directors, KMP or otherwise designated are outside parts 3 to 6 entirely, so the secured financing ban does not reach them.

Buying and selling within a 3 month period is short term trading and is banned, and the ban expressly extends to financial products associated with Steadfast's Securities, so a collar with a tenor under 3 months, or one opened and unwound within 3 months, is prohibited. Only the exercise of plan options or rights and the subsequent sale of the resulting shares is carved out.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons and their Associates must not engage in short term trading in Steadfast's Securities or in financial products associated with Steadfast's Securities. Buying and selling Steadfast's Securities within a 3 month period is considered short term trading.

clearance.post_trade_to: Notification Officer
clearance.post_trade_deadline: 3 business days from when the dealing occurred
clearance.evidence: Chair | Chair of the Audit & Risk Committee or another non-executive director nominated by the Chair of the Audit & Risk Committee

clearance.approver: Managing Director & CEO and the Company Secretary, and if unavailable the Chair, or if the Chair is unavailable the Chair of the Audit & Risk Committee
clearance.post_trade_to: Notification Officer
clearance.post_trade_deadline: 3 business days from when the dealing occurred
clearance.evidence: If a Designated Person proposes to deal in Steadfast's Securities (including entering into an agreement to deal) at any time they must first provide: a) written notice of their intention to the "Notification Officer" ... b) written confirmation that the Designated Person is not in possession of Inside Information.

clearance.tier: all directors, employees and contractors of Steadfast
clearance.evidence: part 2 (insider trading laws) and part 9 (breaches of this policy) apply to all directors, employees and contractors of Steadfast, and their Associates;

short_term.basis: buying and selling within a 3 month period; extended to financial products associated with Steadfast's Securities
carve_outs: exercising options or rights under Steadfast incentive schemes and subsequently selling the Steadfast Securities acquired
short_term.evidence: Buying and selling Steadfast's Securities within a 3 month period is considered short term trading. This does not prohibit exercising options or rights under Steadfast incentive schemes and subsequently selling Steadfast's Securities acquired.

exceptions.approver: Notification Officer (consulting the Chair, or the Chair of the Audit & Risk Committee where the Chair is involved)
exceptions.evidence: severe financial hardship, for example, a pressing financial commitment that cannot be satisfied otherwise than by selling Steadfast's Securities;

exceptions.approver: Notification Officer
exceptions.evidence: requirements under a court order or court enforceable undertakings or other legal or regulatory requirements;

exceptions.approver: Chair (or Chair of the Audit & Risk Committee where the Chair is involved)
exceptions.evidence: A Designated Person may request, and the Notification Officer may give, prior confirmation for the Designated Person or their Associate to: a) deal in Steadfast's Securities outside a trading window; or b) dispose of Steadfast's Securities even if otherwise prohibited under part 6, if there are exceptional circumstances

(lender disposals) disposals of Steadfast's Securities that are the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, however, this does not extend to disposals under any margin lending agreement where such agreements are prohibited by this policy;

(off market) off-market transfers of Steadfast Securities, other than those by the Board Directors and their Associates, where there is no change in beneficial ownership (e.g. transferring between two of your own accounts, such as from your employee holding to a personal holding in your name).

(superannuation) dealings in Steadfast's Securities between a superannuation fund, custodian or other saving scheme in which the Designated Person is a beneficiary and the Designated Person or their Associate, provided that any such dealings are notified immediately to the Notification Officer;

(third parties) investments in, or dealings in units of, a fund or other scheme (other than a scheme only investing in Steadfast's Securities) where the assets of the fund or other scheme are invested at the discretion of a third party and the Designated Person or Associate has no ability to exercise any influence or discretion in relation to such dealing
(schemes and takeovers) disposals, or undertakings to dispose, of Steadfast's Securities arising from a scheme of arrangement or acceptance of a takeover offer;

(DRPs and SPPs) acquisitions of Steadfast's Securities under a dividend or distribution reinvestment plan or security purchase plan, provided that the Designated Person or their Associate did not join or vary their participation in the plan while in possession of Inside Information;

(incentive scheme) exercises (but not the sale of Steadfast's Securities following exercise) of an option or right under an employee incentive scheme, or the conversion of a convertible security, where the final date for the exercise of the option or right, or the conversion of the security, falls outside a trading window and it has been an exceptionally long time since the last trading window
(deceased estates) dealings in Steadfast's Securities arising from the administration of a deceased estate;

exceptions.approver: Board (timing and structure of the offer approved by the Board)
exceptions.evidence: (rights offers, bonus issues and buy-backs) dealings in Steadfast's Securities under an offer or invitation made to all or most of Steadfast's security holders, such as a rights issue, a bonus issue and an equal access buy-back, where the timing and structure of the offer has been approved by the Board.

financing.price_trigger_guidance: The stated rationale for the margin lending ban is the forced-sale risk itself: 'This is on the grounds that the terms may require Steadfast's Securities to be sold outside a trading window or when the Designated Person possesses Inside Information.' A collar structure that can force delivery or sale on a price trigger therefore offends the policy's underlying concern even where the drafting is arguably narrower.

external_documents: The list of Designated Persons maintained by the Company Secretary
Steadfast employee incentive scheme rules (referenced for option and right exercises and holding locks)
SDF.exemption_authority: Two routes. (1) Part 4: a Notification Officer may give prior confirmation for a Designated Person or Associate to deal outside a trading window, or to dispose of Steadfast's Securities even if otherwise prohibited under part 6, in exceptional circumstances (severe financial hardship, court order or legal or regulatory requirement, or other exceptional circumstances determined by the Chair or, where the Chair is involved, the Chair of the Audit & Risk Committee); prior notification, clearance and post-trade notification still apply. This route covers only disposals, not entry into a hedge or a secured financing. (2) Part 8: 'The Board may, in its discretion, adjust or exclude a specific requirement of this policy from time to time, either generally or on a case by case basis.'
jurisdiction_overlays: For those parts of Steadfast impacted by laws, regulatory requirements or contractual obligations that conflict with the policy, the more stringent standard applies

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons and their Associates are not permitted to enter into margin lending or other secured financing arrangements in relation to Steadfast's Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar, secured on the collared shares, is expressly prohibited for every director, KMP and designated person and their Associates, with no clearance route.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons and their Associates are not permitted to engage in short selling or stock lending of Steadfast's Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Structures in which the executive lends the collared shares to the bank to support its hedge, or the bank borrows them back, are separately prohibited.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A Designated Person may request, and the Notification Officer may give, prior confirmation for the Designated Person or their Associate to: a) deal in Steadfast's Securities outside a trading window; or b) dispose of Steadfast's Securities even if otherwise prohibited under part 6.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The only relief from part 6 is to dispose of shares, so it cannot be used to authorise entering into a secured loan, a hedge, stock lending or a short-dated collar.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Board may, in its discretion, adjust or exclude a specific requirement of this policy from time to time, either generally or on a case by case basis.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is the only realistic route to a funded collar: the Board would have to disapply the margin lending and stock lending prohibitions for the specific transaction.

bespoke_clauses.clause: (lender disposals) disposals of Steadfast's Securities that are the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, however, this does not extend to disposals under any margin lending agreement where such agreements are prohibited by this policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A secured lender's enforcement sale is a permitted dealing in principle, but the carve-back withdraws that protection for any facility the policy itself prohibits, so a bank enforcing against a Designated Person's collared shares gets no safe harbour.

bespoke_clauses.topic: OTC derivatives arguably outside the clearance regime
bespoke_clauses.clause: shares, options, derivatives and any other financial products of Steadfast that are able to be traded on a financial market ("Steadfast's Securities") ... financial products includes derivatives, options, warrants, futures, forward contracts, swaps and contracts for difference issued or created over or associated with Steadfast's Securities by third parties.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The window and clearance machinery bites on 'Steadfast's Securities', which is qualified by tradability on a financial market, while the wider 'financial products' definition that plainly captures an OTC collar is used only in the short term trading ban; the gap is arguable rather than reliable, so a bank should still require clearance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: (off market) off-market transfers of Steadfast Securities, other than those by the Board Directors and their Associates, where there is no change in beneficial ownership.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: For directors, moving collateral shares into a lender's nominee or custodian account is not an excluded dealing even if beneficial ownership is unchanged, so it needs an open window and clearance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons and their Associates must not engage in short term trading in Steadfast's Securities or in financial products associated with Steadfast's Securities. Buying and selling Steadfast's Securities within a 3 month period is considered short term trading.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The tenor of any collar must exceed three months and it must not be unwound early, because the ban expressly reaches associated financial products.

bespoke_clauses.clause: must not enter into transactions or arrangements with anyone which could have the effect of limiting their exposure to risk relating to an element of their remuneration that: a) has not vested; or b) has vested but remains subject to a holding lock.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The 'with anyone' and 'could have the effect' wording is broad but the ban is limited to unvested or holding-locked remuneration, leaving vested unrestricted shares hedgeable.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons will be notified of trading windows by email prior to the opening of a trading window. Designated Persons must not assume that a trading window is open in the absence of notification, as the Board may vary, suspend or terminate (conditionally or unconditionally) trading window arrangements at any time.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Execution certainty is low: a window can be suspended between pricing and signing, and there is no default open period.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons must keep for 12 months and make available to the Company Secretary on request, a record of all dealings in Steadfast's Securities by themselves and their Associates, in the form of a record of every trade, including any supporting materials.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Collar documentation and confirmations would be discoverable by the Company Secretary for at least 12 months.

SDF.summary: A funded collar is not available to any Steadfast director, KMP or other Designated Person: part 6.1 bans margin lending and any other secured financing arrangement in relation to Steadfast's Securities for them and their Associates, and part 6.2 separately bans stock lending, so both the loan leg and any borrow-based hedge are prohibited. The exceptional circumstances relief in part 4 only permits a disposal notwithstanding part 6, not entry into a financing or a hedge, so the only route would be the Board exercising its power under part 8 to adjust or exclude a requirement of the policy case by case. The unfunded collar legs are more workable: the hedging ban reaches only remuneration that is unvested or vested but under a holding lock, so vested unrestricted shares can be hedged, subject to an open 30 day window, prior written notice and clearance from the Notification Officer (Chair for directors, MD & CEO with the Company Secretary for others) valid for 5 business days, and written post-trade confirmation within 3 business days. Any structure must run longer than three months because short term trading expressly extends to financial products associated with Steadfast's Securities. Employees and contractors who are not directors, KMP or MD & CEO designees fall outside parts 3 to 6 entirely and are constrained only by the insider trading laws.

CGF.title: Challenger Staff Trading Policy (Version 10)
CGF.date_approved: November 2018 (Authorised by the Group Risk Committee)

tiers.name: staff
tiers.description: All employees of the Challenger Group including its Key Management Personnel, regardless of Division, and the consultants, directors (including non-executive directors), officers, agents and contractors that act for or on behalf of Challenger Group entities. All specific rules for trading Challenger Securities (Prohibited Periods, pre-trade approval, short term gain, margin lending, net short positions, derivatives and hedging) apply to this whole tier.

tiers.name: Key Management Personnel
tiers.description: Persons with authority and responsibility for planning, directing and controlling Challenger's activities directly or indirectly, per AASB 124, including all directors of Challenger, the CEO and certain of the CEO's direct reports. Distinguished only in that their pre-approval to trade Challenger Securities must be granted by the Committee rather than through the ordinary online process.

tiers.name: Designated Staff
tiers.description: The CEO, CEO Direct Reports and staff nominated by a CEO Direct Report or who by virtue of their role have or may have access to sensitive information about Challenger Securities or products, or about Challenger's trading positions (researchers, those aware of Challenger positions or M&A activity, those making recommendations or decisions on Securities Challenger trades, and those involved in fund management). Distinguished by needing pre-trade approval for Third Party Securities as well, and must sign a Designated Person Form - Acknowledgement and Undertaking.

tiers.name: Non-Executive Directors
tiers.description: Non-executive directors of Challenger Group companies. They are within 'staff' and, as Challenger directors, within KMP for Challenger Securities (so Committee pre-approval applies), but are expressly treated as non-Designated Staff for trading in Third Party Securities.

tiers.name: closely connected persons and entities
tiers.description: Related parties or controlled entities such as an immediate family member, or companies and trusts including self-managed superannuation funds, through which a staff member's ownership of or power over Securities may be acquired. Holdings and powers held through them count as the staff member's personal trading.

definitions.hedging_definition: the hedging of or taking out of derivatives over Challenger Securities are not permitted to be used in relation to any unvested Challenger Securities. For the purposes of this Policy, Challenger Securities are considered vested once the Challenger imposed time and performance hurdles have been satisfied, irrespective of whether a Challenger staff member has opted for a longer period of restriction.

CGF.ad_hoc_blackout_authority: Challenger imposes 'additional periods' from time to time when it is considering matters which may include price sensitive information and/or matters subject to ASX Listing Rule 3.1A; the Company Secretary manages the commencement and end dates and staff communications. The Boards of entities issuing the relevant Challenger Securities may vary the timing of closed periods at any time, and the Board and CEO may require temporary changes to the procedures. Refusal of an approval to trade is final and binding and must be kept confidential.

rules.detail: Derivatives and hedges over unvested Challenger Securities are flatly prohibited because they would distort performance and time hurdles. No venue limit and no approval route within 7.6; only the exceptional circumstances process in part 9 could conceivably reach it.
rules.evidence: Accordingly, the hedging of or taking out of derivatives over Challenger Securities are not permitted to be used in relation to any unvested Challenger Securities.

rules.detail: Securities count as vested once Challenger-imposed time and performance hurdles are met, even if the staff member has elected a longer restriction period, so a self-elected holding lock does not push the shares back into the unvested prohibition; the 7.6.2 gateways and criteria apply.
rules.evidence: For the purposes of this Policy, Challenger Securities are considered vested once the Challenger imposed time and performance hurdles have been satisfied, irrespective of whether a Challenger staff member has opted for a longer period of restriction.

rules.detail: OTC derivatives are expressly within Securities ('derivatives (both over the counter (OTC) and exchange traded)') and Challenger Securities expressly include security specific derivatives, options, CFDs and warrants issued by third parties over CGF. Over vested securities, derivatives are permitted only in three defined circumstances, must not mature in a closed prohibited period, must not have any Challenger Group entity as counterparty, and must go through the pre-trade approval process (Committee approval for KMP).
rules.evidence: once Challenger Securities have vested, derivatives or hedging may be used in relation to those vested Securities in the following circumstances: to protect the value of an asset supporting a loan taken out for the exercise price of options granted by Challenger; to protect the value of the security where the staff member had paid or is required to pay a tax liability in relation to the vested Securities; on a case by case basis with approval from the Committee.

rules.detail: Hedging is banned over any unvested Challenger Securities, with no tier or approval carve-out.
rules.evidence: The use of derivatives over unvested Challenger Securities could distort the proper functioning of these hurdles and reduce the intended alignment between management and shareholder interests. Accordingly, the hedging of or taking out of derivatives over Challenger Securities are not permitted to be used in relation to any unvested Challenger Securities.

rules.detail: Unusually permissive: hedging vested securities is endorsed as encouraging longer term holding. It is allowed only (a) to protect the value of an asset supporting a loan taken out for the exercise price of Challenger options, (b) to protect value where the staff member has paid or must pay a tax liability on the vested securities, or (c) case by case with Committee approval. Two mandatory criteria apply on top: no maturity date falling within a closed prohibited period, and no Challenger Group entity as counterparty. The hedge must also comply with the law and the pre-trade approval process.
rules.evidence: Further, any use of derivatives or hedging over vested Challenger Securities must meet both of the following criteria: the derivative or hedge must not have a maturity date that falls within a closed prohibited period; and neither Challenger nor any member of the Challenger Group can be a counter party to the derivative.

rules.detail: For KMP (all Challenger directors, the CEO and certain direct reports) the pre-approval for any trade in Challenger Securities, including entry into a hedge, must be granted by the Committee (Chair of the Board, CEO and General Counsel and Company Secretary for directors; CEO and General Counsel and Company Secretary for other staff), with the requesting member excluded.
rules.evidence: Key Management Personnel will require pre-approval to trade in Challenger Securities to be granted by the Committee.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward or collar-and-loan is a trade in Challenger Securities (Securities expressly include OTC derivatives and third party derivatives referencing CGF) requiring pre-trade approval outside a Prohibited Period, must not create a net short position, and over plan securities must fit one of the 7.6.2 gateways.
rules.evidence: Trading includes the following: applying for, acquiring or disposing of (or entering into an agreement to do so) any Securities;

rules.detail: The ban is on holding net short positions in Challenger Securities through derivatives or otherwise, framed as a general principle. A conventional collar over shares actually held (long stock, long put, short call) is net long and so is not caught; a naked written call or a put purchased over shares not held would be.
rules.evidence: As a general principle, staff are prohibited from holding net short positions in Challenger Securities through derivative instruments or otherwise.

rules.detail: Securities lending or borrowing is not mentioned anywhere and is not within the definition of trading, which is limited to applying for, acquiring or disposing of Securities and procuring others to do so.

rules.section: Key Terms (Challenger Securities; Securities or Division 3 Financial Products); 7.3; 7.6
rules.detail: CFDs are expressly named in both the Challenger Securities and the Securities definitions, so trading a CFD over CGF requires pre-trade approval outside a Prohibited Period. A short CFD would breach the net short position prohibition, and a CFD held less than three months would breach the short term gain rule.
rules.evidence: It also includes security specific derivatives, options, Contracts for Difference (CFDs) and warrants that may be issued by third parties where the underlying or referenced security is Securities issued by Challenger or any other subsidiary entity.

rules.detail: Margin lending over Challenger Securities is prohibited by default but is expressly approvable by the Challenger Board. This is the only board-level financing consent in the policy and is the gateway for the loan leg of a funded structure. No conditions, process or timeframe for that Board approval are stated.
rules.evidence: Challenger prohibits margin lending over Challenger Securities other than as approved by the Challenger Board.

rules.detail: Granting security, a charge, lien or pledge over Challenger Securities is not addressed except through the margin lending prohibition in 7.5. The definition of trading does not sweep in encumbrances, so a pledge that is not part of a margin loan is not itself a trade requiring approval.

There is no general prohibition on secured financing; only margin lending over Challenger Securities is restricted, and even that is subject to Board approval. A term loan secured on CGF shares without margin call mechanics is arguably outside 7.5, but the general rule that 'You must not do indirectly what you are prohibited from doing directly' means a bank should assume the Board consent route applies. Notably 7.6.2 positively contemplates a hedge protecting an asset supporting a loan.

Symmetric three month rule in both directions (sell after buy, buy after sell) applied to parcels of Challenger Securities, which by definition include derivatives over CGF. Carve-out only for vesting or exercise of performance rights or options and the subsequent sale of those shares; expressly captures shares taken as short term incentive payment.
rules.evidence: Accordingly, selling a parcel of Challenger Securities after buying within a 3 month period is prohibited as is buying a parcel of Challenger Securities after selling within a 3 month period.

CGF.exemption_authority: Part 9 (Exceptional Circumstances): a staff member not in possession of inside information who wishes to trade in Challenger Securities or Third Party Securities in a way that would otherwise breach the Policy (including trading during a Prohibited Period) needs specific prior written approval. The written request goes to the General Counsel and Company Secretary or the General Manager, Risk and Compliance, with supporting evidence, and is decided by the Committee, which may impose conditions in its absolute discretion including execution and settlement time limits and post-trade reporting. Separately, the Challenger Board may approve margin lending over Challenger Securities (7.5), and the Board and CEO may require temporary changes to the procedures (1).

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedging over vested securities expressly permitted
bespoke_clauses.clause: once Challenger Securities have vested, derivatives or hedging may be used in relation to those vested Securities in the following circumstances: to protect the value of an asset supporting a loan taken out for the exercise price of options granted by Challenger; to protect the value of the security where the staff member had paid or is required to pay a tax liability in relation to the vested Securities; on a case by case basis with approval from the Committee.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is one of the few ASX policies that positively contemplates hedging vested shares, and the first limb even contemplates a hedge protecting an asset that supports a loan; a collar over vested shares can therefore be approved on a case by case basis by the Committee.

bespoke_clauses.clause: neither Challenger nor any member of the Challenger Group can be a counter party to the derivative.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank writing the collar must not be a Challenger Group entity, which is straightforward for a third party bank but excludes any Challenger-issued structured product.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the derivative or hedge must not have a maturity date that falls within a closed prohibited period.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The collar's expiry must be scheduled outside the 30 June to results and 31 December to results closed periods, and rolling or early termination must be planned around dates that can shift when the Boards vary closed period timing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Challenger prohibits margin lending over Challenger Securities other than as approved by the Challenger Board.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg is not an absolute bar as it is in most ASX policies: the Challenger Board can approve margin lending over CGF securities, so a funded collar turns on obtaining that Board approval alongside Committee approval of the hedge.

bespoke_clauses.clause: As a general principle, staff are prohibited from holding net short positions in Challenger Securities through derivative instruments or otherwise.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The collar must be sized no larger than the shares actually held, since an over-hedged position or a written call in excess of the holding would create a net short position.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Shares, securities, interests in a managed investment scheme including mFund units, options, stock specific derivatives, derivatives (both over the counter (OTC) and exchange traded), warrants, contracts for difference (CFDs) ... It also includes security specific derivatives, options, Contracts for Difference (CFDs) and warrants that may be issued by third parties where the underlying or referenced security is Securities issued by Challenger.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no venue limitation, so both collar legs written by a bank are Challenger Securities requiring pre-trade approval and subject to the Prohibited Periods.

bespoke_clauses.topic: prohibited periods framed around quoted securities
bespoke_clauses.clause: There are periods throughout the year during which Challenger staff are not permitted to trade in Challenger Securities which are quoted on a relevant stock exchange irrespective of whether or not they are in possession of inside information.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The Prohibited Period wording is expressed by reference to quoted securities, but 7.6.2 assumes derivatives are subject to closed periods, so a bank should not rely on an argument that OTC legs escape the blackout.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Approved trades must be placed within 1 business day and complete within 7 days, unless otherwise informed by the Company Secretary. Once the approval lapses, re-approval to trade will be required.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The collar must be placed within one business day of approval and completed within seven days, though the Company Secretary can vary this, which is likely necessary for a negotiated OTC structure.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any approval to trade can be granted or refused in the Company's absolute discretion, without providing any reasons. An approval to trade may be withdrawn if new information comes to light or there is a change in circumstances. Any refusal to trade is final and binding on you, and you must keep that information confidential.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Approval to enter, roll or unwind the collar can be withdrawn between pricing and execution, with no appeal and no reasons given.

bespoke_clauses.clause: You must not do indirectly what you are prohibited from doing directly.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A term loan secured on CGF shares that is economically a margin loan, or a synthetic short achieved through combined legs, will be treated as caught even if the label differs.

bespoke_clauses.topic: forced sale carve-out sits in the third party rules
bespoke_clauses.clause: Forced sales or acquisitions as a result of margin lending calls or corporate actions ... which do not accommodate personal discretion are not subject to pre-trade approval for Designated Staff.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The only forced-sale relief appears in section 8 (Third Party Securities) and is expressed for Designated Staff, so it is unclear whether a lender's enforcement sale of CGF shares in a Prohibited Period is protected.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A staff member's ownership or power in Securities may be acquired through closely connected persons and entities including a related party or controlled entity such as an immediate family member or companies and trusts including self-managed superannuation funds.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Booking the collar through a family trust, SMSF or controlled company is treated as the staff member's own personal trading and needs the same approvals.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Version 10, Date of Version November 2018, Review of Policy Due by November 2019.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The lodged policy is dated November 2018 and was due for review in November 2019, so the bank should confirm no more recent version has superseded these unusually permissive hedging provisions.

CGF.summary: Challenger is unusually accommodating and a funded collar over vested shares is genuinely possible, but only with two separate consents. Section 7.6.2 expressly permits derivatives and hedging over vested Challenger Securities, including to protect the value of an asset supporting a loan, and otherwise on a case by case basis with approval from the Committee (Chair, CEO and General Counsel and Company Secretary for directors; CEO and General Counsel and Company Secretary for other staff), while section 7.5 prohibits margin lending over Challenger Securities 'other than as approved by the Challenger Board', so the loan leg requires Board approval. The structure must satisfy the two mandatory criteria that no Challenger Group entity is a counterparty and that the hedge does not mature within a closed prohibited period, must not create a net short position, must be entered outside the 30 June and 31 December closed periods and any additional period, and must go through pre-trade approval with the trade placed within one business day and completed within seven days. Nothing may be hedged while unvested, though securities count as vested once Challenger's own hurdles are met even if the executive has elected a longer restriction. The three month short term gain rule and the anti-avoidance principle that staff must not do indirectly what they cannot do directly mean the tenor must exceed three months and a loan structured to avoid the margin lending label would still be treated as caught.

tiers.name: Personnel
tiers.description: All directors, full-time, part-time and casual employees, contractors, consultants and advisers of the Group, and their Associates. Subject to the insider trading prohibition, the Front Page Test, the hedging ban over unvested and holding-locked entitlements, the 3% funding security cap, and the bans on short term dealing, forward contracts and short selling. Personnel who are not Restricted Persons do not need written clearance to deal.

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: Directors, senior managers and other employees and their Associates, as determined by the Managing Director and Company Secretary from time to time, on a list maintained by the Company Secretary and notified to them by email. They may not deal in IGO securities at any time without prior written clearance and are barred from dealing during the prescribed blackout periods.

tiers.name: directors and senior management
tiers.description: Directors and senior managers. Uniquely subject to the requirement to obtain prior approval before entering into agreements that give lenders rights over their interests in IGO securities, and the only tier for whom a secured lender's enforcement disposal is an excluded dealing (and only where the original financing was pre-cleared).

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Directors of IGO. In addition to the Restricted Person regime, they must notify the Company Secretary within two business days of any dealing by themselves or an Associate, and their clearances are given by the Chair of the Board (or, for the Chair, the Chair of the Audit Committee).

tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: A family member who may be expected to influence, or be influenced by, the Personnel in dealings with the Company and its securities (spouse, partner, children or dependants, and the children or dependants of the partner); and a company or any other entity the Personnel can control, including a family trust or superannuation fund, including pursuant to standing orders to trade. Where the Standard requires an act such as obtaining written clearance, the Personnel must do it in respect of the Associate.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a disposal that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, where the director or senior manager has already received prior written clearance for the original financing arrangement in accordance with this Standard.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Enforcement or physical settlement by the bank is an excluded dealing even in a blackout period, provided the facility itself was pre-cleared in writing, which gives the bank certainty it lacks under most other policies.

bespoke_clauses.clause: or entering into forward contracts, or short selling at any time, except in circumstances of special hardship, with the Chair's prior written approval (email suffices).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A prepaid variable forward or any forward-sale leg is prohibited outright, so the structure must be built from a purchased put and a written call rather than a forward.

IGO.summary: IGO is one of the more workable policies for a funded collar. There is no ban on margin lending or secured financing: directors and senior management simply need prior approval before entering an agreement that gives a lender rights over their IGO securities, and a disposal by a secured lender exercising those rights is an excluded dealing provided the original financing arrangement received prior written clearance, which gives the bank a clean enforcement path even during a blackout. The two real limits on the loan leg are the size cap, since no Personnel may enter a funding arrangement where the funding security would affect 3% or more of IGO's listed shares, and the Front Page Test, under which approval will not be granted for anything that looks like an executive taking advantage of position. On the derivative legs, the collar may only cover vested entitlements free of any plan holding lock, must not be a forward contract or create a short sale (both banned at any time absent special hardship approved by the Chair), must have a tenor beyond the three month short term dealing rule, and for a Restricted Person needs prior written clearance on the Appendix 1 form, valid five business days, outside the September and March quarter, half year and full year blackouts and any confidential Additional Period. Directors must also notify the Company Secretary of each dealing within two business days.

RRL.title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: all directors and employees of Regis Resources and its subsidiaries
tiers.description: Every director and employee of Regis Resources and its subsidiaries, plus contractors who are Restricted Persons. Bound by the insider trading prohibition, the ban on short-term trading, discretionary restricted trading periods notified by the Company, and the prohibition on trading in other companies' securities while holding price sensitive information about them. Not subject to the closed periods, the funding arrangements cap or any notification obligation unless they are also a Restricted Person, director or Key Management Personnel.

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: All directors and their spouses and related parties (as defined in the Corporations Act 2001); contractors notified in writing by the Managing Director or Company Secretary; and any person designated by the Managing Director as Key Management Personnel. Restricted Persons are the only tier barred from buying or selling Company securities in the closed periods, and the only tier that can seek a Chairman's waiver in exceptional circumstances.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Directors of the Company. Automatically Restricted Persons together with their spouses and related parties. Must lodge a Trading Notification form with the Company Secretary within 2 days of buying or selling, and must promptly disclose to the Company Secretary the information the Company needs for its ASX notification within 5 business days of any change in their relevant interests. Subject to the 3% funding arrangements cap.

tiers.name: Key Management Personnel
tiers.description: Any person designated by the Managing Director as key management personnel from time to time and notified in writing by the Company Secretary, and who may be de-designated on notice. Likely to include those with authority and responsibility for planning, directing and controlling the Company's activities and those involved in key financial, corporate or technical activities. Restricted Persons, subject to the Trading Notification form and to the 3% funding arrangements cap.

tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: Nominees, agents or other associates of directors and employees, such as family members, family trusts and family companies. Directors' spouses and related parties as defined in the Corporations Act are expressly within the definition of Restricted Persons.

RRL.ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Company may at its discretion notify all directors and employees that a restricted trading period is in effect and they must refrain from trading during that period. The policy does not say whether the reason is disclosed or whether the existence of the period is confidential. Key Management Personnel are identified by the Managing Director as necessary and notified in writing by the Company Secretary as being affected by the closed period. Restricted Persons are also separately barred whenever they know results are likely to differ materially from guidance, a confidential incomplete price sensitive proposal exempt under Listing Rule 3.1A is on foot, or there is information about definition drilling, resource or reserve upgrades, new discoveries or the award of a major contract.

rules.detail: The policy never mentions derivatives, options over the Company written by third parties, warrants or any equivalent. Its operative restrictions are framed as 'buying or selling Company securities' and 'trading in the Company's securities', with the only references to options being Company-issued employee options and, in the funding arrangements clause, 'their interests in the Company's shares or options'. There is no definition of trading, dealing or securities, so an OTC put or call written by a bank is not clearly caught by the closed periods.

There is no hedging clause of any kind. The policy pre-dates the hedging restrictions now standard in ASX policies and says nothing about limiting the economic risk of unvested plan securities or performance rights. Any hedging restriction would have to come from the Employee Share Option Plan rules or remuneration documents, which are not part of this policy.

Hedging vested unrestricted shares is likewise unaddressed. The only constraints that could bite are the insider trading prohibition, the undefined short-term trading ban, the closed periods (which are framed as buying or selling securities) and, for directors and Key Management Personnel, the 3% funding arrangements cap.

Monetisation, prepaid forwards and equivalent structures are not mentioned. A monetisation that is funded and secured on Company shares would engage the funding arrangements cap in 4.12 for directors and Key Management Personnel if the security reached 3% or more of the Company's listed shares.
Short selling is not mentioned anywhere. Only the general short-term trading exhortation and the insider trading laws would apply.
Securities lending or borrowing is not mentioned and there is no definition of trading that would capture it.
Contracts for difference are not mentioned and there is no definition of securities or financial products that would sweep them in.

Margin lending is not banned as such. The only restriction is a size test: a funding arrangement relating to a director's interests in Company shares or options is prohibited where the funding security would affect the equivalent of 3% or more of the Company's listed shares. Below that threshold no approval, notification or condition is imposed on the loan itself.
rules.evidence: All directors and Key Management Personnel are prohibited from entering into funding arrangements relating to their interests in the Company's shares or options where the funding security would affect the equivalent of 3% or more of the Company's listed shares.

rules.detail: Identical 3% funding security cap for Key Management Personnel designated by the Managing Director. Employees who are neither directors nor designated Key Management Personnel are not caught by 4.12 at all.

rules.detail: Granting security over Company shares or options is regulated only through 4.12, and only by reference to the size of the funding security relative to the Company's listed shares. A charge or pledge is not otherwise a dealing and needs no clearance; there is no requirement to disclose the arrangement to the Company.
rules.evidence: All directors and Key Management Personnel are prohibited from entering into funding arrangements relating to their interests in the Company's shares or options where the funding security would affect the equivalent of 3% or more of the Company's listed shares.

There is no prohibition below the threshold, no approval gateway, no distinction by vesting state and no forced-sale provision.

financing.price_trigger_guidance: No price-trigger guidance. The single financing control is a size cap measured against the Company's whole issued capital: 'funding arrangements relating to their interests in the Company's shares or options where the funding security would affect the equivalent of 3% or more of the Company's listed shares'. The policy does not say how or when the 3% is measured, whether facilities or associates aggregate, or what happens if the threshold is crossed after inception through a fall in the share count.

RRL.exemption_authority: The Chairman may waive the closed period restrictions in 4.3 and the discretionary restricted trading periods in 4.4 in specific circumstances such as severe financial hardship or other exceptional circumstances (including a transfer of shares required by family court order or other legal requirement), conditional on the Restricted Person demonstrating they hold no price sensitive information and satisfying the Chairman that the proposed sale or disposal is the only reasonable course of action available. A Trading Exemption Request form goes to the Company Secretary and clearance is given in writing including by email. There is no authority to waive the short-term trading ban in 4.5 or the funding arrangements cap in 4.12.

bespoke_clauses.clause: All directors and Key Management Personnel are prohibited from entering into funding arrangements relating to their interests in the Company's shares or options where the funding security would affect the equivalent of 3% or more of the Company's listed shares.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is the only financing control in the policy: a funded collar is permissible for directors and KMP provided the security package stays below 3% of Regis's listed shares, with no approval, disclosure or condition otherwise imposed.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The policy contains no hedging clause, no derivatives clause, no short selling clause and no definition of dealing, trading or securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Neither collar leg is expressly restricted, but the absence of drafting also means there is no clearance mechanism through which a bank can obtain company comfort that the structure is compliant.

bespoke_clauses.topic: restrictions framed as buying or selling
bespoke_clauses.clause: All Restricted Persons are prohibited from buying or selling Company securities: in the 14 day period prior to the release of the half yearly results announcement to ASX ...
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The closed periods are expressed as a bar on buying or selling Company securities, so on a literal reading entering an OTC option with a bank is not caught, though physical settlement or a collateral transfer plainly would be.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Company Secretary will endeavour to notify all Directors, employees and any other Restricted Persons of the times when they are permitted to buy or sell the Company's securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no pre-clearance requirement for ordinary dealing, only notification of permitted times, so a bank cannot rely on a company approval as evidence the structure was sanctioned.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The notification must also specify whether the trading took place during a closed period, where prior written clearance was required, and if so, when that was provided.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The ASX notification clause assumes a prior written clearance process that the policy never establishes outside the exceptional circumstances route, so the practical process should be confirmed with the Company Secretary.

bespoke_clauses.clause: All directors and Key Management Personnel must complete a Trading Notification form and provide it to the Company Secretary within 2 days after that person buys or sells securities in the Company. The Trading Notification form must be completed in full, including details of the number of securities traded, the date the trading took place and whether the trading occurred inside a closed period.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any physical delivery or on-market leg of the collar triggers a two day notification and, for directors, a Company ASX filing within five business days if relevant interests change.

bespoke_clauses.clause: there exists information regarding definition drilling, resource or reserve upgrades or new discoveries or the awarding of any major contract or relating to other activities such as those set out in clause 3.5 of this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Exploration and resource news flow creates frequent open-ended trading bars for Restricted Persons that are not tied to a calendar, so execution dates cannot be planned reliably.

bespoke_clauses.topic: spouses and related parties are Restricted Persons
bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons means: all directors and their spouses and related parties (as defined in the Corporations Act 2001);
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Booking a collar through a director's spouse, family trust or related party does not escape the closed periods.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and employees should never engage in short-term trading of the Company's securities except for the exercise of options where the shares will be sold shortly thereafter.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no stated period, so the tenor risk is unquantifiable and a bank should assume a conservative minimum such as twelve months and avoid early unwind features.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Securities Trading Policy (applicable from 31 December 2010). Last updated: 23 December 2010.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This policy is from 2010, pre-dates the hedging and margin lending provisions now standard in ASX policies, and no review cycle is stated, so the bank must verify whether a current version exists before relying on the silences.

RRL.summary: On its face a funded collar is available to Regis directors and executives, because this 2010 policy is silent on hedging, derivatives, short selling and stock lending, and its only financing control is a size cap: directors and Key Management Personnel must not enter funding arrangements relating to their interests in Company shares or options where the funding security would affect 3% or more of the Company's listed shares. The derivative legs are not expressly regulated at all, and the closed periods (14 days before half year, full year and disclosure document announcements, 7 days before quarterlies, plus discretionary restricted trading periods and open-ended bars tied to drilling, resource upgrades or major contracts) are drafted as a bar on buying or selling Company securities, so entry into an OTC option is arguably outside them while physical settlement or a collateral transfer clearly is not. The practical obstacles are the absence of any pre-clearance mechanism through which the company could bless the structure, the undefined 'should never engage in short-term trading' ban, and the two day Trading Notification and five business day ASX disclosure obligations for directors and KMP on any purchase or sale. Because the policy is silent rather than permissive, the bank should not treat the silences as consent: any hedging restriction is more likely to sit in the Employee Share Option Plan and remuneration documents, which are outside this policy. Given the policy dates from December 2010 with no stated review cycle, its currency should be confirmed before relying on it.
