DXS.ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The CEO may cancel any trading window at any time, effective immediately on notification, and notification is communicated to all Employees (so cancellation itself is not confidential). The CEO in consultation with the Chair may also identify additional trading windows, and may in exceptional circumstances restrict trading by Listed Securities Funds. Restrictions on trading in other financial products may also be imposed and notified to relevant Employees. Separately, the reasons for refusing an individual approval may be withheld and the Employee must keep the refusal confidential.

rules.detail: The Policy never mentions derivatives, options, futures or synthetic positions, and there is no defined term 'Dealing' beyond the insider trading gloss ('apply for, acquire, dispose of or enter into an agreement to do so' in respect of the relevant financial product). Section 10 requires approval for 'All trades by Employees in listed and unlisted financial products managed by Dexus' - an OTC put or call written by a bank is not a product managed by Dexus, so it is doubtful the approval machinery reaches it at all. The safe reading for a bank is that the put and call legs are unregulated by the express words but would be tested against the Media Test and, for un-vested securities, the hedging ban.

A put/call collar over un-vested securities is a 'transaction or arrangement for the purpose of hedging exposure to movements in the price of un-vested securities' and is therefore banned outright, with no approval route.
rules.evidence: Employees must not undertake the following types of personal trading activity: ... entering into a transaction or arrangement for the purpose of hedging exposure to movements in the price of un-vested securities

rules.detail: Absolute ban on any transaction or arrangement whose purpose is hedging price exposure to un-vested securities. No exemption, hardship route or approval route is offered for this prohibition.
rules.evidence: entering into a transaction or arrangement for the purpose of hedging exposure to movements in the price of un-vested securities

rules.detail: The hedging prohibition is expressly limited to un-vested securities; the Policy is silent on hedging vested holdings. Section 8 states that once securities cease to be held under the terms of an equity plan, 'any dealings in those securities must only occur in accordance with this Policy', which brings vested plan shares back under the trading-window and approval regime but adds no hedging ban.

Where securities have vested but remain held under the terms of the Dexus equity plan, section 8 keeps the plan holding outside the Policy; where they cease to be held under the plan they are treated as vested. The Policy draws only the vested/un-vested line, so shares still subject to a plan holding lock that have not vested remain caught by the un-vested hedging ban.
rules.evidence: where securities granted under an employee, executive or director equity plan cease to be held under the terms of that plan, any dealings in those securities must only occur in accordance with this Policy

rules.detail: Prepaid forwards, exchangeable notes, zero-cost collars and similar monetisation structures are not named. Any structure that is in substance a sale of Dexus securities would need to occur inside a trading window with prior approval; any structure involving borrowing against the securities risks being characterised as 'margin lending activities' under section 7.
Short selling is not mentioned anywhere in the Policy. A short position would in practice be constrained by the 30-day short-term gain prohibition and the Media Test.
Securities lending is not named and there is no dealing definition that would sweep it in.

Contracts for difference are not named. A CFD over Dexus securities would in practice be caught by the 30-day short-term gain prohibition and by the general ban on trading that may cause a conflict or the appearance of conflict.

Trading in Dexus securities as part of margin lending activities is one of the listed prohibited personal trading activities, applying to Directors, all Employees, contractors and Associates, and to vested as well as un-vested holdings. There is no approval route: the section 9 hardship exemption relieves only the trading-window restriction and the section 11 approval table only authorises trades.
rules.evidence: Employees must not undertake the following types of personal trading activity: ... trading in Dexus securities as part of margin lending activities

rules.detail: Granting a mortgage, charge, lien or pledge over Dexus securities is not named and there is no dealing definition that treats an encumbrance as a dealing. Only encumbrance in the course of 'margin lending activities' is caught.

There is no general prohibition on secured financing in respect of Dexus securities; the only financing prohibition is the margin lending limb. Whether a bank loan secured on the collared securities is 'margin lending activities' is undefined in the Policy - the term is not defined and, given that the ban attaches to 'trading in Dexus securities as part of' such activities, a lender should treat a loan collateralised by Dexus securities with mark-to-market or enforcement rights as within the intended reach.
rules.evidence: trading in Dexus securities as part of margin lending activities

rules.detail: Trading for short term gain is prohibited and defined mechanically as a purchase and sale within 30 days. No carve-outs are stated for plan securities, although section 8 removes participation in Dexus equity plans from the Policy entirely.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A clearance to trade may be withdrawn if circumstances change. The Employee will be contacted directly in this situation and must keep this fact confidential.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Approval for the collar is revocable up to execution and the executive cannot tell the bank why, so the bank must accept unexplained withdrawal of the trade within the 5-business-day validity period.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Employees must not undertake the following types of personal trading activity: ... trading in Dexus securities as part of margin lending activities
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar secured on Dexus securities is at serious risk of being characterised as margin lending activity, which is prohibited outright with no approval or hardship route.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where any approval is required for a dealing under this Policy, approval will not be granted where the dealing would not satisfy the Media Test.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even where the black-letter prohibitions do not bite, approvers have an express reputational veto over a director hedging or borrowing against Dexus securities, and no reasons need be given.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Employees must not undertake ... trading that may cause a conflict (or appearance of conflict) of interest with Dexus or its clients.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A written call over Dexus securities held by a Dexus funds-management executive could be treated as an appearance of conflict independently of the hedging and margin lending limbs.

bespoke_clauses.clause: reference to Dexus Securities includes reference to Dexus (ASX:DXS), Dexus Industria REIT (ASX:ADI) and Dexus Convenience Retail REIT (ASX:DXC).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The Policy reaches the two managed REITs as well as DXS, so a collar over any of the three is caught by the same windows, approvals and margin lending ban.

bespoke_clauses.clause: All trades by Employees in listed and unlisted financial products managed by Dexus require prior approval in accordance with the Business Approval Table.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The approval trigger is drafted around products managed by Dexus rather than derivatives referencing them, leaving it unclear whether an OTC put and call with a bank needs approval at all; a bank should require the executive to seek approval anyway and obtain written confirmation.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Compliance team must be provided with a copy of contract notes or transaction advices of approved trades once they have been executed.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Confirmations for the collar legs would have to be handed to Dexus Compliance, so the structure cannot be kept confidential from the issuer.

DXS.summary: A funded collar is at best doubtful for a Dexus director or executive and is likely blocked on the funding leg. The derivative legs over vested securities are not expressly regulated - the Policy names no derivatives, short selling, CFDs, stock lending or encumbrance, and the hedging prohibition is confined to un-vested securities - but any trade in Dexus securities must be pre-approved under the Business Approval Table, executed within 5 business days, and confined to the two open windows (28 days after half and full year results, 14 days after the AGM), with approval refusable without reasons under the Media Test and withdrawable up to execution. The loan leg is the problem: section 7 prohibits 'trading in Dexus securities as part of margin lending activities' for every Director, Employee and Associate, with no approval, hardship or exemption route, and a bank loan secured on the collared securities with enforcement rights is squarely within the mischief that limb addresses. Nothing in the Policy addresses forced sales by a secured lender, disclosure of financing arrangements, or a minimum shareholding, so the practical position is that Dexus consent would have to be sought in writing on the specific structure. Tenor should also exceed 30 days to avoid the short-term gain prohibition, and the collar must not extend to any un-vested plan securities.

AZJ.exemption_authority: Section 4.2: the Company Secretary may approve disposals (but not acquisitions) of Company securities during a black-out period where the applicant has no price sensitive information and there are exceptional circumstances such as severe financial difficulties or passive trades; approvals are valid for three business days. Section 4.4: the MD & CEO or Company Secretary may give written permission for a sale of shares acquired on exercise of performance rights during a black-out period. There is no authority to waive the margin lending prohibition or the ban on hedging unexercised performance rights.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and Executives are only permitted to hedge their shareholdings: in compliance with section 5.1 above; and providing the hedge transaction is not entered into, renewed, altered or closed out when the Director or Executive is in possession of price sensitive information.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unusually for an ASX policy, the collar's derivative legs over vested unrestricted shares are affirmatively permitted rather than banned, subject only to clearance and the inside information test.

bespoke_clauses.clause: not entered into, renewed, altered or closed out when the Director or Executive is in possession of price sensitive information
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Every roll, restrike, partial unwind and termination of the collar is a separate compliance event, so the bank cannot rely on unilateral adjustment rights and must build in the executive's ability to stand still while in possession of price sensitive information.

bespoke_clauses.clause: hedging includes the entry into any transaction, arrangement or financial product which operates to limit the economic risk of a security holding in the Company and includes financial instruments such as equity swaps and contracts for differences.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The definition is drafted by economic effect rather than instrument or venue, so an OTC put and call package with a bank is plainly within it and cannot be structured around.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and Executives must not enter into a margin lending arrangement in relation to Company Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The funding leg is the only real obstacle: 'margin lending arrangement' is not defined, so a loan secured on the collared shares should be documented as a fixed-term facility without margin calls or collateral top-up, and written confirmation obtained from the Company Secretary that it is not caught.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Executives are not permitted to hedge performance rights granted under a Plan prior to exercising those rights or, once exercised, while the securities are subject to a transfer restriction.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The collateral pool must be limited to shares that have been exercised and released from any transfer restriction; the bank should require evidence of that status at trade date.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A clearance under this clause is not an endorsement of proposed trading and it is the Directors and Executives whom are ultimately responsible for ensuring their dealings in securities comply with the applicable laws and as applicable, the Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Clearance for the collar gives the bank no comfort that the Company has assessed the structure against the margin lending or short-term dealing prohibitions.

bespoke_clauses.clause: or enter into any other short-term dealings in Company securities (for example, forward contracts)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Naming forward contracts as an example of prohibited short-term dealing means the collar and any associated funding should have a tenor comfortably beyond three months and no early-termination triggers within it.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This policy applies to all executive and non-executive directors (Directors) and all employees (Employees) of the Company and its subsidiaries (the Group).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The Policy has no associates or connected persons clause, so on its face a collar entered by a family trust or controlled entity is not directly caught, although the executive's own conduct in procuring the dealing remains subject to the insider trading provisions.

bespoke_clauses.clause: for any other period designated as a black-out period by the Board and advised to the Employees.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Ad hoc black-outs are communicated by Company-wide email and intranet rather than kept confidential, so the executive can at least tell the bank that a dealing window is unavailable.

AZJ.summary: Aurizon is one of the more permissive ASX policies for the derivative legs of a collar: section 5.2 expressly permits Directors and Executives to hedge their shareholdings, and the hedging definition reaches any transaction, arrangement or financial product limiting the economic risk of a Company holding, including OTC instruments such as equity swaps and CFDs. The conditions are section 5.1 advance written notice and written clearance acknowledgement (Chairman or Company Secretary for Directors, the Audit Governance and Risk Management Committee Chairman for the Chairman, the MD & CEO or Company Secretary for Executives), dealing within 5 business days of clearance, outside the 1 January and 1 July black-out periods and any Board-designated black-out, and no price sensitive information at entry, renewal, alteration or close-out. The collar cannot cover unexercised performance rights or shares still subject to a transfer restriction, and its tenor should exceed three months given the short-term dealing ban that expressly names forward contracts. The funding leg is the pinch point: section 5.3 prohibits Directors and Executives entering any margin lending arrangement in relation to Company Securities, but there is no general secured financing, encumbrance or pledge prohibition and no definition of margin lending, so a fixed-term loan secured on the collared shares without margin calls or collateral maintenance is arguably outside the ban and should be confirmed in writing with the Company Secretary before documentation. The Policy is silent on forced sales, financing disclosure and any minimum shareholding, so those risks must be managed contractually rather than by reference to the Policy.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons may not, directly or indirectly, grant any form of security (whether by way of charge, mortgage, pledge or otherwise) over any Company Securities, to secure any obligation of that Designated Person or any third party or enter into any margin lending arrangement involving Company Securities, except with prior written consent under section 5.3.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unusually, the loan leg of a funded collar is expressly contemplated and available over vested unlocked shares with prior written consent, rather than banned outright.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons may not, at any time, directly or indirectly, grant any form of security ... over any Company Securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock ... or enter into any margin lending arrangement involving Company Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The margin lending limb of the first paragraph of section 6.3 is not on its face confined to unvested securities and appears to contradict the consent route in the second paragraph, so the facility should be documented as a secured term loan rather than a margin loan and the Company's written position on the inconsistency obtained.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons may, at any time: ... a disposal of Company Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights under a loan or security agreement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Lender enforcement is an express exemption available at any time, including during a Blackout Period, which removes the usual objection that a bank cannot realise its collateral without putting the executive in breach; the Designated Person must still advise the Authorising Officer.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Company Securities means all securities issued by the Company and includes shares, share rights, performance rights, options and derivatives of any of the above (including, equity swaps, futures, hedges and exchange-traded or over-the-counter options) whether settled by cash or otherwise.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Both legs of an OTC collar are Company Securities in their own right, so entering, amending or unwinding them are Dealings requiring authorisation and are barred in Blackout Periods absent exceptional circumstances.

bespoke_clauses.clause: including Company Securities held beneficially (for example, in trust or under an incentive plan) on that Designated Person's behalf
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Shares held through an employee share trust cannot be collared while unvested or locked, so the collateral pool must be limited to fully vested, released holdings.

bespoke_clauses.clause: from close of trading on the ASX on 31 March and 30 September, until commencement of trading on the ASX trading day immediately following the announcement of Westgold's quarterly reports
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Quarterly as well as half and full year blackouts leave narrow open windows, so entry, roll and unwind of the collar must be tightly scheduled or brought within the section 5.4 exceptional circumstances discretion.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Board may impose, without notice and in its sole and absolute discretion, additional restrictions on Dealing ... Any restriction communicated by the Board ... must be kept strictly confidential as the restriction itself may be considered Inside Information.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The executive may be unable to tell the bank why a scheduled roll or unwind cannot proceed, so the trade documentation must tolerate unexplained delay.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Written authorisation under this Policy may be withdrawn by the Authorising Officer in writing at any time during the clearance period ... having regard to the broader reputational, governance and other implications of the proposed Dealing.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Authorisation for the collar is revocable on reputational grounds at any point in the five business day window, so pricing should not be locked before execution.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Reporting insiders must also file an insider trading report within five (5) days if the reporting insider enters into, materially amends, or terminates an agreement, arrangement or understanding that (i) has the effect of altering, directly or indirectly, the reporting insider's economic exposure to the Company
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The collar and any material amendment or termination must be publicly disclosed on SEDI within five days, so the structure cannot be kept confidential and the parties should agree disclosure wording in advance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Under no circumstances should Designated Persons engage in short-term or speculative trading in Company Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The prohibition is undefined and absolute, so a short-dated or highly geared collar risks being characterised as speculative even where consent for the protection arrangement is available.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any authorisation to trade by the Authorising Officer under this section 5.4 is not an endorsement to trade.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Consent to the collar carries no representation by Westgold that the structure complies with the Policy or the law, so the bank should not treat the Form FM201 as a compliance opinion.

WGX.summary: Westgold is one of the few ASX policies under which a funded collar is affirmatively available, but only over fully vested Company Securities that are not subject to a holding lock, and only with prior written consent. Section 6.2 treats the put and call legs as a 'protection arrangement', prohibited absolutely over unvested or holding-locked securities and otherwise permitted with consent under section 5.3; section 6.3 does the same for the loan leg, prohibiting any charge, mortgage or pledge over Company Securities to secure any obligation except with prior written consent, so the bank's security is contemplated rather than banned. Consent is given by the relevant Authorising Officer on Form FM201, is valid five business days, may be withdrawn on reputational grounds and may be refused in absolute discretion without reasons; Dealings are otherwise barred in four Blackout Periods a year and during confidential Board-imposed ad-hoc restrictions, subject to the section 5.4 exceptional circumstances discretion which can approve 'other Dealings that would otherwise be prohibited'. Critically, section 8.0 expressly exempts a disposal resulting from a secured lender exercising rights under a loan or security agreement, so enforcement of the bank's collateral does not itself breach the Policy. Two cautions: the first paragraph of section 6.3 contains an unqualified margin lending prohibition that sits awkwardly with the consent route, so the facility should be documented as a secured term loan and the Company's position confirmed in writing; and as a TSX-listed issuer, entering into, materially amending or terminating the collar triggers SEDI insider reports within five days for reporting insiders.

rules.detail: BEN Securities include 'any derivatives relating to BEN Group securities', with no venue limitation, and Trading is 'any action taken to buy, sell, transfer, or otherwise deal in securities'. A purchased put and written call over a BEN holding are hedging transactions limiting economic risk and are therefore prohibited outright for Designated Officers, whether the underlying entitlements are vested or unvested; a derivative that was not a hedge would still require prior written clearance and could not be short-term or speculative.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Enter into hedging transactions to limit the economic risk of their holdings in BEN securities. This applies to both unvested and vested entitlements.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The derivative legs of a collar are prohibited outright for every Designated Officer over fully vested shares, with no clearance or exemption route, which defeats the structure at the first step.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Use BEN securities as security for entering into margin loans or similar financing arrangements.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The words 'or similar financing arrangements' extend past classic margin lending to any loan secured on BEN securities, so the funding leg is prohibited independently of the hedging ban.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Officers and close connections may apply to trade during blackout periods only in exceptional circumstances
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The only discretionary relief in the Policy is permission to trade during a blackout period; nothing empowers the Board Chair, CEO or Company Secretary to waive the hedging or secured financing prohibitions.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The following close connections of Designated Officers are also subject to restrictions: Family members - Parents, spouse/partner and dependent children. Entities controlled by the Designated Officer or their family. Trusts where the Designated Officer or family are beneficiaries.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar written on shares held by a family trust or controlled entity is caught, and the Designated Officer is obliged to take reasonable steps to ensure the entity complies.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Trading: Any action taken to buy, sell, transfer, or otherwise deal in securities. Transfer: Administrative transfers of securities between own accounts or to personal superannuation funds.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no carve-out for dealings with no change in beneficial interest, so even moving the collateral parcel into a custody or security trustee account is Trading requiring prior written clearance inside a Trading Window.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Hold BEN securities for less than 30 days.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any physically settled leg of a collar must not result in shares being acquired and disposed of within 30 days, which constrains cash-settled substitution and early unwind mechanics.

bespoke_clauses.clause: BEN Securities: Includes shares, options, rights, debentures or any derivatives relating to BEN Group securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Every leg of an OTC collar is itself a BEN Security, so entering, amending or closing it is Trading and is caught by the clearance regime as well as the hedging ban.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Share Registry Provider (MUFG): Monitor controls and provide alerts placed on Designated Officers in the share registry. ... Flagged Holdings Reports when Designated Officers trade.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Registry alerts are placed on Designated Officer holdings, so any transfer of the collateral parcel to a bank nominee would be detected and reported to the Company Secretary.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The decision to grant or refuse clearance is at the Approving Officer's absolute discretion. If clearance is refused, that decision must be kept confidential.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even for permitted trades the executive cannot explain a refusal to the bank, so no timetable dependent on clearance can be contractually guaranteed.

BEN.summary: A funded collar is not available to any BEN Designated Officer. Section 1.2 prohibits Designated Officers from entering into hedging transactions to limit the economic risk of their holdings in BEN securities and states expressly that this applies to vested as well as unvested entitlements, so the put and call legs are banned outright with no clearance route; short selling is separately prohibited. The funding leg is independently blocked, because Designated Officers must not use BEN securities as security for margin loans 'or similar financing arrangements', wording that reaches a bank facility secured on the collared parcel. The prohibitions extend to close connections, including family trusts and controlled entities, and the only discretionary relief in the Policy is permission to trade during a blackout period in cases of severe financial hardship or court order, which cannot waive the hedging or financing bans. Even ordinary dealing is tightly controlled: written clearance from the designated approving officer, valid five business days and revocable, trading only in the roughly 30-day window after each results announcement, and a 30-day minimum holding period.

rules.detail: Monetisation structures are not named, but a prepaid forward, collar or exchangeable is a transaction in financial products that operates to limit the economic risk associated with holding HUB24 Securities, so it is a hedge permitted over vested unrestricted holdings with prior written approval and outside Restricted Periods.
rules.evidence: A hedge includes entering into transactions in financial products that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding HUB24 Securities.

rules.detail: Short selling is not mentioned. A short position taken to limit the economic risk of a holding would be a hedge and so would fall within the section 5.2 permission for vested unrestricted securities; a naked short is not addressed.
Securities lending is not named and there is no dealing definition that would sweep it in.

CFDs are not named. A CFD over HUB24 shares is a derivative in respect of HUB24 shares and therefore a HUB24 Security; where it limits the economic risk of a holding it is a hedge permitted over vested unrestricted securities with approval, and it is prohibited over unvested or holding-locked plan securities.
rules.evidence: derivative in respect of HUB24 shares

rules.detail: Margin loans holding interests in HUB24 Securities are expressly permitted for our People and their Associates, including meeting a margin call. The condition is that sufficient liquidity or alternative securities be maintained in the facility so that HUB24 Securities are not dealt with under a margin call until prior written approval to deal is obtained; dealings under margin lending arrangements are listed as a Restricted Period item and failure to obtain prior approval is a breach. HUB24 warns that no special consideration will be given to the urgency of a margin call and that a request to trade during a Restricted Period will most likely be rejected.
rules.evidence: Our People and their Associates are permitted to have margin loans that have interests in HUB24 Securities under their margin lending arrangement, this includes meeting a 'margin call'.

rules.detail: Granting a charge, mortgage, pledge or lien over HUB24 Securities is not named. The only financing provision is section 6, which permits margin lending arrangements and regulates dealings under them; taking security over HUB24 Securities is not itself treated as a dealing requiring approval.

The Policy addresses only margin lending arrangements and, far from prohibiting them, permits them. There is no general prohibition on secured financing over HUB24 Securities, so a bank loan secured on the collared parcel is not prohibited; but if the facility operates like a margin lending arrangement, section 6 requires prior written approval before any HUB24 Securities are dealt with under it.
rules.evidence: Our People and their Associates are permitted to have margin loans that have interests in HUB24 Securities under their margin lending arrangement

rules.detail: The Policy contains no minimum holding period and no prohibition on short-term or speculative trading; the only timing constraints are the Restricted Periods and the five business day expiry of an approval.

HUB.exemption_authority: Section 8: our People and their Associates who hold no Inside Information may trade during a Restricted Period only where an Exceptional Circumstance applies and the prior written approval of the Chair of the HUB24 Board or the Chair of the ARCC (where the Managing Director regards that as appropriate) is obtained. Exceptional Circumstances, on the recommendation of the Managing Director or delegate, are financial hardship that cannot be addressed otherwise than by dealing, a court order directing the dealing, and such other situations as the Managing Director or delegate determines. Approval must be in writing and identify an expiry date; an application from someone known to hold Inside Information should prima facie be declined.

bespoke_clauses.clause: For clarity, our People and their Associates are permitted to hedge their vested and unrestricted HUB24 Securities outside of designated restricted periods provided that the hedge transaction is treated as trading in HUB24 Securities for the purpose of this policy and the relevant approvals have been obtained.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The derivative legs of a collar over vested unrestricted shares are affirmatively permitted, including for Associates such as a family trust, subject only to timing and approval.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Our People and their Associates are permitted to have margin loans that have interests in HUB24 Securities under their margin lending arrangement, this includes meeting a 'margin call'.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unusually, borrowing against HUB24 Securities is expressly allowed rather than banned, so the funding leg of a collar is available in principle.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Our People and their Associates must maintain sufficient liquidity or alternative securities in the margin lending arrangement to ensure that HUB24 Securities are not dealt with under a 'margin call' until prior written approval is obtained to deal in HUB24 Securities. ... regardless of the urgency of a margin call, a margin call that includes a request to trade HUB24 Securities, will only be considered in accordance with this policy and no special consideration is likely to be provided nor approval given.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is the central obstacle: the bank cannot realise the collared shares on short notice, because any sale under the facility needs prior written HUB24 approval that will most likely be refused during a Restricted Period, so the facility must be sized and documented so that enforcement over HUB24 shares is never needed.

bespoke_clauses.topic: margin dealings are a restricted period item
bespoke_clauses.clause: Our People and their Associates may not deal in HUB24 Securities during the following Restricted Periods: ... Dealings in HUB24 Securities under margin lending arrangements - refer to Section 6.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Dealings under a financing arrangement are drafted into the Restricted Period list itself, so they are treated as permanently restricted and always require an approval decision.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Failure by our People or their Associates to obtain prior written approval to deal in HUB24 Securities under a margin lending arrangement is considered a breach of this policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A lender's unilateral sale exposes the executive to disciplinary action up to dismissal, so the security documents should require notice and a standstill while approval is sought.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Enter into, renew, alter or close out a hedge transaction when they are in possession of Inside Information.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Rolls, restrikes, partial unwinds and terminations are each separately regulated, so the bank cannot rely on unilateral adjustment or early termination rights.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Hedge prior to vesting of any unvested HUB24 Securities acquired under the employee share plan operated by HUB24; Hedge HUB24 Securities subject to a holding lock or restriction on dealing under the terms of the employee share plan
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The collateral pool must be limited to shares that have vested and are free of any holding lock or plan dealing restriction.

bespoke_clauses.clause: from the balance date (i.e. 30 June or 31 December) until 24 hours after the release of HUB24's annual or half-yearly results to ASX
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Roughly four months of each year are closed, plus a month before any prospectus and each Market Sensitive announcement day, so entry, roll and unwind must be scheduled into the open periods.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any approval expires: within five (5) business days of the date of the approval; or such other period as is agreed by the Company Secretary ... any approved but incomplete trades will lapse at the expiry and new approval to must be sought.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The five business day window can be extended by agreement, which is useful for a negotiated OTC trade that cannot be executed as quickly as an on-market order.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Approvals can be withheld where it's reasonable to believe that the person seeking approval is in possession of Inside Information or for reasons of good corporate governance or for other reasons taking into account matters such HUB24's trading activities and proposed transactions.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Approval for a collar can be refused on general corporate governance grounds without reasons, and any refusal must be kept confidential from the bank.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Approval requests will generally be answered within one business day after their receipt, provided those requests are received prior to 3pm on a business day and all relevant information is provided.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A one business day service standard makes it practical to obtain approval close to pricing, reducing market risk between approval and execution.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Person includes any of our People who by virtue of their position and or duties are identified by management and Risk and Compliance as requiring additional securities trading requirements to be applied to them.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Additional, unpublished trading restrictions may be imposed in writing on a particular executive, so the bank should ask for confirmation of whether the client is a Designated Person and what extra requirements apply.

HUB.summary: HUB24 is among the most permissive ASX policies for this structure: section 5.2 expressly permits our People and their Associates to hedge vested and unrestricted HUB24 Securities outside Restricted Periods with the relevant approvals, and section 6 expressly permits margin loans holding interests in HUB24 Securities, so both the derivative and the funded legs of a collar are contemplated rather than banned. The conditions are prior written approval on the Annexure A Trade Approval Form (Chair of the Board or ARCC Chair for Directors, the Managing Director for executive KMP, the Company Secretary for everyone else), generally answered within one business day and expiring after five business days unless a longer period is agreed, execution outside the Restricted Periods (balance date to 24 hours after results, one month before a prospectus, each Market Sensitive announcement day, and any ad hoc period), and no Inside Information at entry, renewal, alteration or close-out. Unvested plan securities and shares subject to a holding lock or plan dealing restriction cannot be hedged, so the collateral must be fully released stock; there is no short-term trading ban or minimum holding period. The main structuring constraint is enforcement: HUB24 Securities must not be dealt with under a margin call until prior written approval is obtained, HUB24 warns that no special consideration will be given to the urgency of a margin call and that requests during a Restricted Period will most likely be rejected, and an unapproved dealing is a breach of the Policy. A funded collar should therefore be documented with conservative leverage, non-HUB24 substitute collateral or cash liquidity, and a contractual standstill while HUB24 approval is sought before any enforcement sale.

APE.title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: Any Director, the CEO, any KMP member, and any Employee nominated from time to time by the Chair or CEO to be a Restricted Person (which may include any Employee who reports directly to the CEO, has access to monthly management reports, or any other Employee whatsoever). This is the tier carrying the notice and Closed Period approval regime.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Directors of APE. A subset of Restricted Persons, additionally subject to the 3 business day relevant-interest notification, the minimum shareholding requirement and the Margin Loan Board approval and disclosure regime.

tiers.name: KMP
tiers.description: Key management personnel as defined in the ASX Listing Rules. Restricted Persons, and subject to the minimum shareholding requirement alongside Directors.

tiers.name: Senior Executive
tiers.description: Any Employee nominated from time to time by the Chair or CEO to be a Senior Executive for the purpose of section 8 (Margin Loans). Relevant only to the Margin Loan approval and disclosure regime.

tiers.name: Employees
tiers.description: Any employee of APE or its subsidiaries. Bound by the insider trading prohibition, the improper use of position clause and, if a participant in an employee equity or incentive plan, the hedging restriction on unvested or trading-restricted plan Securities.

tiers.name: Related Party
tiers.description: Any person, company or other entity under the direct or indirect control of a Director or Senior Executive. Named only in the Margin Loan clause, which bars taking out a Margin Loan 'either personally or through a Related Party'. The dealing, notice and approval clauses are not expressly extended to associates.

definitions.hedging_definition: hedge or otherwise reduce or eliminate the risk associated with the plan by Dealing in derivatives, hedging or similar arrangements in relation to Securities that have not vested or are subject to trading restrictions under the plan

windows.start_anchor: 30th June (described in the policy as the end of APE's half year)
windows.end_anchor: announcement of results for that period or the giving of market guidance on the results

windows.start_anchor: 31st December (described in the policy as the end of APE's full year)
windows.end_anchor: announcement of results for that period or the giving of market guidance on the results

APE.ad_hoc_blackout_authority: No express power to impose additional or ad hoc blackouts. The Chair or CEO may, however, nominate any Employee to be a Restricted Person 'from time to time' and 'for the purpose of any provision of this policy', which can extend the notice and Closed Period approval regime to a person at any time; the policy does not say whether such nominations are confidential.

rules.detail: There is no express derivatives rule for vested unrestricted holdings. Securities is defined to include options, rights, warrants, forward contracts or tradeable financial products in respect of shares, with no venue limitation, and Deal means buy, sell, transfer, hedge or otherwise trade. An OTC put and written call are therefore a Dealing: outside Closed Periods it requires only prior notice to the Chair or Company Secretary, and during a Closed Period prior written approval of the Chair (or a non-executive Director for a Dealing by the Chair).
rules.evidence: Securities means shares or options, rights, warrants, forward contracts or tradeable financial products in respect of shares. ... Deal means buy, sell, transfer, hedge or otherwise trade.

rules.detail: Exchange-traded options over APE shares are treated identically to OTC derivatives; the definition of Securities draws no distinction by venue and the policy contains no separate exchange-traded carve-out.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must not Deal in APE Securities outside Closed Periods without prior notice to the Chair or Company Secretary (or in their absence, to a non-executive Director).

rules.detail: Dealing in derivatives over unvested plan Securities in order to reduce or eliminate plan risk is expressly caught, but is subject to the Chair's approval rather than being an absolute ban. Breach triggers forfeiture or lapsing of the unvested Securities, or the imposition of additional performance hurdles or trading restrictions, at the Board's discretion.
rules.evidence: Any Employee who participates in an employee equity or incentive plan must not hedge or otherwise reduce or eliminate the risk associated with the plan by Dealing in derivatives, hedging or similar arrangements in relation to Securities that have not vested or are subject to trading restrictions under the plan, without the Chair's approval.

rules.detail: The same clause expressly extends to plan Securities that are vested but 'subject to trading restrictions under the plan', so a collar over holding-locked shares needs the Chair's approval in addition to the Restricted Person notice or Closed Period approval.
rules.evidence: in relation to Securities that have not vested or are subject to trading restrictions under the plan, without the Chair's approval.

rules.detail: Hedging of unvested plan Securities is not banned outright: it is prohibited only 'without the Chair's approval'. The test is functional, capturing any arrangement that reduces or eliminates the risk associated with the plan.
rules.evidence: must not hedge or otherwise reduce or eliminate the risk associated with the plan by Dealing in derivatives, hedging or similar arrangements in relation to Securities that have not vested ... without the Chair's approval.

rules.detail: Plan Securities that have vested but remain subject to plan trading restrictions are expressly within the hedging clause and may be hedged only with the Chair's approval.
rules.evidence: or are subject to trading restrictions under the plan, without the Chair's approval.

rules.detail: Hedging of vested, unrestricted shares (whether acquired on-market or delivered out of a plan free of restrictions) is not separately regulated. It is a Dealing because Deal expressly includes 'hedge', so it needs prior notice outside Closed Periods and prior written approval during a Closed Period, and must not occur while the person has Inside Information.
rules.evidence: Deal means buy, sell, transfer, hedge or otherwise trade.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward or similar structure is a Dealing in Securities because Securities expressly includes forward contracts in respect of shares, so it requires prior notice outside Closed Periods and prior written approval during a Closed Period. If the structure is funded by a loan secured against APE Securities it must also clear the Margin Loan gate in section 8.
rules.evidence: Securities means shares or options, rights, warrants, forward contracts or tradeable financial products in respect of shares.

rules.detail: The policy contains no short selling prohibition and does not use the term. A short sale would still be a Dealing requiring notice or approval.
Securities lending is not mentioned and is not listed in the definition of Deal, although a lending transfer would arguably fall within 'transfer'.

CFDs are not named. A CFD over APE shares is a tradeable financial product in respect of shares and so a Dealing in Securities, requiring prior notice outside Closed Periods and prior written approval during a Closed Period.
rules.evidence: Securities means shares or options, rights, warrants, forward contracts or tradeable financial products in respect of shares.

rules.detail: Margin Loans are permitted with prior Board approval, personally or through a Related Party. A Margin Loan is defined broadly as any loan secured against APE Securities where the lender is protected from falls in the value of the Securities by a call right over those Securities. Any Margin Loan actually taken out, approved or not, must be notified to the Chair immediately, with irrevocable consent to any public disclosure the Board considers necessary.
rules.evidence: Any person who is a Director or Senior Executive must not, either personally or through a Related Party, take out a Margin Loan without the prior approval of the Board.

rules.detail: Identical regime to Directors: prior Board approval, immediate notice to the Chair on taking out the loan, and irrevocable consent to public disclosure. Senior Executive means any Employee nominated from time to time by the Chair or CEO for the purpose of section 8, so the population is discretionary.
rules.evidence: Any Director or Senior Executive who takes out a Margin Loan, whether or not in contravention of the foregoing provision, must give immediate notice of the Margin Loan to the Chair and irrevocably consents to any public disclosure in relation to the Margin Loan which the Board may deem necessary or appropriate from time to time.

rules.detail: Section 8 applies only to Directors and Senior Executives. An employee who is neither is not restricted from margin lending by this policy.

Granting security over APE Securities is not itself a Dealing (Deal means buy, sell, transfer, hedge or otherwise trade) and there is no general encumbrance clause. An encumbrance is regulated only where it forms part of a Margin Loan as defined, in which case prior Board approval and immediate notice to the Chair apply. Security granted to a lender that is not protected from falls in value by a call right over the Securities falls outside the definition and is not addressed.
rules.evidence: Margin Loan means any loan secured against APE Securities where the lender is protected from falls in the value of the Securities by a call right over those Securities.

rules.detail: No encumbrance, pledge or charge restriction applies to Employees who are not Directors or Senior Executives.

There is no general ban on secured financing. Only a Margin Loan as defined is caught, and it is permitted with prior Board approval plus immediate notice to the Chair and consent to public disclosure. The policy does not distinguish vested from unvested Securities as collateral and does not address forced sales by a lender.
rules.evidence: must not, either personally or through a Related Party, take out a Margin Loan without the prior approval of the Board.

rules.detail: Same Board approval and Chair notification regime as Directors; no other form of secured financing over APE Securities is restricted.
rules.evidence: Any person who is a Director or Senior Executive must not, either personally or through a Related Party, take out a Margin Loan without the prior approval of the Board.

rules.detail: The policy imposes no minimum holding period, no buy/sell window and no prohibition on short-term or speculative dealing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Margin Loan means any loan secured against APE Securities where the lender is protected from falls in the value of the Securities by a call right over those Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar is secured against APE Securities and the bank takes a call right over them, so it should be treated as a Margin Loan requiring prior Board approval, immediate notice to the Chair and consent to public disclosure, even though it is not a margin loan in the conventional sense.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Section 8 restricts only Margin Loans, and only for Directors and Senior Executives; there is no general prohibition on secured financing, encumbrance or hedging of vested shares anywhere in the policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike most ASX policies this one leaves a funded collar over vested unrestricted shares available, subject to Board approval of the loan and the ordinary notice or Closed Period approval for the derivative legs.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any Employee who participates in an employee equity or incentive plan must not hedge ... Securities that have not vested or are subject to trading restrictions under the plan, without the Chair's approval.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even unvested and holding-locked plan shares can in principle be collared with the Chair's approval, which is unusual; without approval the sanction is forfeiture or lapsing of the unvested Securities.

bespoke_clauses.topic: notice not approval outside closed periods
bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons must not Deal in APE Securities outside Closed Periods without prior notice to the Chair or Company Secretary (or in their absence, to a non-executive Director).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Entering, rolling or unwinding the collar outside a Closed Period needs only prior notice, with no stated approval, validity period or response deadline, so execution timing is far more flexible than under a preclearance regime.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The approval may include conditions include the period in which the Dealing may occur.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A Closed Period approval for collar entry or settlement can be time-boxed or otherwise conditioned, so the bank should treat the approval terms as execution constraints.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The prohibitions on Dealing in Securities under clauses 3.1 and 3.2 will not apply to any Dealing ... in respect of which the Restricted Person has no control or influence over the Dealing decision.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A lender's enforcement sale or a bank's physical settlement of the collar during a Closed Period is arguably outside the executive's control and so within this exception, but the policy nowhere addresses forced sales expressly and the point is untested.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Each Director and/or KMP member must hold a relevant interest in APE shares to a value of at least equal to the Company's annual base fee for non-executive Directors, subject to a transitional period to acquire the initial holding of 3 years.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Shares pledged under the collar still give a relevant interest, but the policy is silent on whether hedged shares count towards the MSR, so the size of the collar relative to the required holding should be raised with the Chair.

bespoke_clauses.clause: irrevocably consents to any public disclosure in relation to the Margin Loan which the Board may deem necessary or appropriate from time to time.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The existence and terms of the collar loan may be publicly disclosed at the Board's discretion, which the executive cannot withdraw consent to, so confidentiality cannot be assured to the bank.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Closed Period means any period from: (i) 30th June (ie. the end of APE's half year) until either results for that half year are announced ... or (ii) 31st December (ie. the end of APE's full year) until ...
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The half year and full year labels are transposed relative to APE's actual reporting calendar, but the operative dates are clear: 30 June and 31 December to results or guidance, and all collar entry, roll and unwind should be scheduled outside those two periods.

bespoke_clauses.clause: any Employee who is nominated from time to time by the Chair or CEO to be a Restricted Person for the purpose of any provision of this policy ... or any other Employee whatsoever.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A counterparty cannot rely on an executive's current status; the Chair or CEO can bring any employee into the Restricted Person or Senior Executive regime at any time, changing the approvals needed to unwind an existing collar.

APE.summary: A funded collar is realistically achievable at Eagers Automotive, making this one of the more permissive ASX policies for this structure. Over vested, unrestricted shares the put and call legs are a Dealing (Deal expressly includes 'hedge' and Securities includes options and forward contracts in respect of shares), so a Restricted Person needs only prior notice to the Chair or Company Secretary outside the two Closed Periods (30 June and 31 December until results or guidance), or prior written and potentially conditioned approval of the Chair if entered inside one. The loan leg is the gating item: a loan secured against APE Securities where the lender is protected by a call right is a Margin Loan, which a Director or Senior Executive may take out only with prior Board approval, must notify to the Chair immediately, and is subject to irrevocable consent to public disclosure. Plan shares that are unvested or still subject to plan trading restrictions can be collared only with the Chair's approval, with forfeiture as the sanction for breach, so the cleanest structure uses vested unrestricted shares. There is no short-term trading ban, no short selling or stock lending prohibition and no general secured financing ban, but the Director and KMP minimum shareholding requirement and the silence on lender forced sales should be resolved with the Chair before execution.

AMP.title: Trading Policy
AMP.date_approved: Approved by the AMP Limited Board

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: A director of any AMP Group Company. AMP Limited directors (other than the CEO) are Designated Persons under section 2.1.1, and directors of each main subsidiary under 2.1.4. Directors of AMP Limited are additionally subject to the absolute margin lending ban in 2.7, notification of their trading intention to the Chairman of the Board, and notification of changes in notifiable interests within 3 business days.

tiers.name: members of the Executive Committee
tiers.description: Members of the AMP Executive Committee. Their direct reports are Designated Persons under section 2.1.3, and each ExCo member may nominate additional Employees as Designated Persons. ExCo members share the Directors' absolute prohibition on margin lending arrangements over or in respect of AMP Securities.

tiers.name: Designated Persons
tiers.description: AMP Limited directors (other than the CEO); the CEO and their direct reports; the direct reports of each Executive Committee member; the directors of each main subsidiary (AMP Bank Limited, N.M. Superannuation Proprietary Limited and any other so designated); the company secretaries of AMP Limited and of each main subsidiary; and any other Employee specifically nominated by an Executive Committee member. Subject to black-out periods, prior notification, short term trading and short selling bans.

tiers.name: Employees
tiers.description: Any full time, part time or casual employee of any AMP Group Company and any contractor of, or secondee to, an AMP Group member. Bound by the insider trading rules and the section 1.7 Share Plan hedging ban, but not by black-out periods, notification, short term trading or short selling restrictions unless also a Designated Person.

tiers.name: Key Management Personnel
tiers.description: As defined in AASB 124. Named only in section 1.7, which records the Corporations Act prohibition on KMP and their closely related parties hedging unvested equity remuneration or vested equity subject to holding locks.

tiers.name: Close Associates
tiers.description: A family member who may be expected to influence, or be influenced by, the Designated Person (spouse, partner, dependent children, dependents), and a company, trust, investment account or other vehicle the Designated Person or their Close Associate controls or has significant influence over. Designated Persons must take appropriate steps to ensure Close Associates only Trade where the Designated Person could. Carve-out where the Close Associate trades in the ordinary course of their professional capacity and not for the benefit of themselves or the Designated Person.

definitions.hedging_definition: Directors and Employees must not use any hedging arrangements in relation to shares, options, share rights and performance rights (whether vested or unvested) (Equity Instrument) held in a Share Plan. This prohibition ceases to apply in respect of any Equity Instrument acquired through a Share Plan from the time it is withdrawn from the plan, converted to an ordinary AMP share or converted to cash (whichever is the earliest).

AMP.ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The AMP Limited Board or AMP Limited's Market Disclosure Committee may specify any other black-out period from time to time. Not confidential to the affected population: AMP will provide Directors and Employees covered by section 2.1 with email notification of any additional black-out periods.

rules.detail: Entering into any derivative instrument over AMP shares is expressly an example of Trading, and AMP Securities expressly include derivatives entered into with a third party over or in relation to AMP shares, so OTC puts and calls with a bank are squarely covered. A Designated Person must notify the Head of Corporate Governance in writing at least 2 business days before, effect the trade on the second to fifth business day after notification, stay outside black-out periods and hold no Inside Information.
rules.evidence: entering into any derivative instrument over AMP shares ... derivatives entered into with a third party over or in relation to any of the above Securities.

rules.detail: No venue distinction is drawn; exchange-traded options over AMP shares are treated identically to OTC derivatives, subject to the same notification, black-out, short selling and 30 day short term trading rules.
rules.evidence: entering into any derivative instrument over AMP shares, and ... agreeing to do any of the above things.

rules.detail: A derivative used to hedge an Equity Instrument held in a Share Plan is caught by the absolute hedging prohibition in 1.7, which applies to all Directors and Employees regardless of Designated Person status and regardless of vesting.
rules.evidence: Directors and Employees must not use any hedging arrangements in relation to shares, options, share rights and performance rights (whether vested or unvested) (Equity Instrument) held in a Share Plan.

rules.detail: Vested Equity Instruments that remain held in a Share Plan (for example subject to a holding lock) cannot be hedged with derivatives until they are withdrawn from the plan, converted to an ordinary AMP share or converted to cash. For KMP the Corporations Act imposes the same result independently.
rules.evidence: In addition, the Corporations Act prohibits Key Management Personnel (and their closely related parties) from hedging unvested equity remuneration or vested equity subject to holding locks.

rules.detail: Absolute ban on any hedging arrangement over unvested shares, options, share rights and performance rights held in a Share Plan, applying to every Director and Employee. Breach may lead to forfeiture of Equity Instruments and, in serious cases, termination.
rules.evidence: Directors and Employees must not use any hedging arrangements in relation to shares, options, share rights and performance rights (whether vested or unvested) (Equity Instrument) held in a Share Plan.

rules.detail: The ban runs on vested Equity Instruments for as long as they are held in a Share Plan; it lifts only on the earliest of withdrawal from the plan, conversion to an ordinary AMP share, or conversion to cash.
rules.evidence: This prohibition ceases to apply in respect of any Equity Instrument acquired through a Share Plan from the time it is withdrawn from the plan, converted to an ordinary AMP share or converted to cash (whichever is the earliest).

rules.detail: Once shares are withdrawn from the Share Plan or converted to ordinary AMP shares, the hedging prohibition expressly ceases. Hedging those shares is then an ordinary Trade in AMP Securities: outside a black-out period, with prior written notification to the Head of Corporate Governance, no Inside Information, and subject to the direction and conditions power in 2.4.
rules.evidence: This prohibition ceases to apply in respect of any Equity Instrument acquired through a Share Plan from the time it is withdrawn from the plan, converted to an ordinary AMP share or converted to cash (whichever is the earliest).

rules.detail: An Employee who is not a Designated Person and holds AMP shares outside a Share Plan is not restricted from hedging by this policy; only the insider trading prohibition and the 'can we / should we' reputational test in 1.4 apply.
rules.evidence: This prohibition ceases to apply in respect of any Equity Instrument acquired through a Share Plan from the time it is withdrawn from the plan, converted to an ordinary AMP share or converted to cash (whichever is the earliest).

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward or similar structure is Trading because it involves granting or disposing of a beneficial interest in AMP shares or a right to dispose of them, and because AMP Securities include derivatives entered into with a third party, so the 2.4 notification and black-out rules apply. If it is held in a Share Plan the 1.7 hedging ban bites first.
rules.evidence: granting, acquiring or disposing of any beneficial interest in AMP shares (or any option or other right to acquire or dispose of AMP shares)

rules.detail: Outright ban, defined narrowly as selling borrowed financial products with a view to repurchasing them later at a lower price. A cash-settled short derivative position is not obviously within that definition, but would still be Trading requiring notification.
rules.evidence: Short selling of AMP Securities by Designated Persons is prohibited.

rules.detail: Section 2.9 is confined to Designated Persons; the policy is silent on short selling by other Employees.

Securities lending is not addressed. Borrowing is mentioned only in the descriptive definition of short selling in 2.9; lending out AMP shares is not prohibited or named, though a transfer of beneficial interest would be Trading.

CFDs are not named but are derivatives entered into with a third party in relation to AMP shares and so AMP Securities; trading them requires 2.4 notification and falls outside black-out periods, and in practice the 30 day short term trading ban in 2.8 would prevent most CFD activity.
rules.evidence: derivatives entered into with a third party over or in relation to any of the above Securities.

rules.detail: Absolute ban for AMP Limited directors on entering into or maintaining any margin lending arrangement over or in respect of AMP Securities. The ban is on maintaining as well as entering, so pre-existing arrangements must be unwound, and there is no approval or exceptional circumstances route out of 2.7.
rules.evidence: Directors of AMP Limited and members of the Executive Committee are prohibited from entering into or maintaining any margin lending arrangement over or in respect of AMP Securities.

rules.detail: Same absolute ban as for AMP Limited directors, covering entering into and maintaining any margin lending arrangement over or in respect of AMP Securities.
rules.evidence: Directors of AMP Limited and members of the Executive Committee are prohibited from entering into or maintaining any margin lending arrangement over or in respect of AMP Securities.

rules.detail: Designated Persons who are not AMP Limited directors or Executive Committee members are warned against, but not prohibited from, margin lending over or in respect of AMP Securities. The warning is grounded in forced sale risk during a black-out period, and the policy states clearance to sell in a black-out period to meet a margin lending arrangement would not likely be granted.
rules.evidence: AMP warns all other Designated Persons against entering into or maintaining any margin lending arrangement over or in respect of AMP Securities due to the risk of forced sale of those Securities during a black out period, in breach of this policy.

rules.detail: Section 2.7 sits within the additional restrictions for Designated Persons; Employees who are not Designated Persons are not addressed.

Granting security over AMP shares is not named, but granting a beneficial interest in AMP shares, or a right to dispose of them, is an express example of Trading, so a share mortgage or charge in favour of a bank should be notified under 2.4 and taken outside a black-out period. For AMP Limited directors and ExCo members an encumbrance that forms part of a margin lending arrangement is prohibited outright by 2.7.
rules.evidence: granting, acquiring or disposing of any beneficial interest in AMP shares (or any option or other right to acquire or dispose of AMP shares)

rules.detail: The policy does not address the use of unvested Share Plan entitlements as collateral; in practice they are unable to be dealt with while held in the plan and any risk-reducing arrangement over them is caught by the 1.7 hedging ban.

Only margin lending arrangements are expressly banned, but the wording 'over or in respect of AMP Securities' is broad enough to capture a bank loan secured on AMP shares with lender protection against price falls. Other forms of secured financing are not separately addressed and there is no general secured financing clause.
rules.evidence: prohibited from entering into or maintaining any margin lending arrangement over or in respect of AMP Securities.

rules.detail: Identical prohibition to AMP Limited directors; no waiver mechanism is provided and section 3 exceptional circumstances relief is directed at black-out period trading, not at 2.7.
rules.evidence: Directors of AMP Limited and members of the Executive Committee are prohibited from entering into or maintaining any margin lending arrangement over or in respect of AMP Securities.

rules.detail: For other Designated Persons the policy contains only a warning, not a prohibition, on margin lending, and says nothing about other secured financing over AMP Securities.
rules.evidence: AMP warns all other Designated Persons against entering into or maintaining any margin lending arrangement over or in respect of AMP Securities

rules.detail: A hard 30 day buy to sell (or sell to buy) window measured from the last buy until a sell of a Security of that class or type. Successive buys or successive sells within 30 days are unrestricted. Carve-out for trading shares acquired on the exercise of options or the exercise or vesting of performance or share rights under a Share Plan.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons must not engage in short term trading (ie 30 days or less) in AMP Securities. The 30 days applies from the last time an AMP Security is bought until an AMP Security of that class or type is sold (or vice versa).

rules.detail: The 30 day rule applies only to Designated Persons.

clearance.approver: Head of Corporate Governance (or their delegate); the Group General Counsel for a notification by the Head of Corporate Governance
clearance.post_trade_to: Head of Corporate Governance (or their delegate), written confirmation of the Trade

clearance.evidence: The notification must be provided at least 2 business days prior to the proposed Trade being effected. Further, any proposed Trade so notified to the Head of Corporate Governance must be effected (even if not settled) within 5 business days of the date of notification. ... The Head of Corporate Governance (or their delegate) may direct the Designated Person who is proposing to Trade not to do so, or to impose conditions on the Trade in their discretion, and is not obliged to provide reasons.

clearance.evidence: Any approval will be effective for 5 business days from the date on which it is given (or any other period specified) ... If a request is not approved or an approval is revoked, that fact must be kept confidential.

clearance.post_trade_to: AMP, notice of all changes in notifiable interests under the separate agreements between AMP and each Director (ASX Listing Rule 3.19A, s205G)

clearance.evidence: Directors of AMP Limited must give AMP notice of all such changes as soon as reasonably possible and in any event within 3 business days of the trade being undertaken.
Additional restrictions apply to Trading by Designated Persons as set out in section 2 of this policy.

Trades in shares acquired on the exercise or vesting of performance rights

the acquisition of AMP Securities through a dividend reinvestment plan
the acquisition of AMP Securities through a share purchase plan available to any retail shareholders

Trades that result in no effective change to the beneficial interest in the AMP Securities (for example, transfers of AMP Securities already held into a superannuation fund or trust of which the Designated Person is a beneficiary)
