AMP.exemption_authority: Section 3: a Designated Person may apply in writing to the Head of Corporate Governance (or the Group General Counsel for the Head of Corporate Governance) to Trade during a black-out period in exceptional circumstances, decided by the relevant Clearance Officer within 5 business days on evidence that trading is the most reasonable course of action and a declaration of no Inside Information. The relief is expressly limited to exempting the person from section 2.2 black-out restrictions; it does not lift the section 1.7 hedging ban or the section 2.7 margin lending prohibition.
jurisdiction_overlays: Section 1.8: Directors and Employees working outside Australia or Trading in Securities in another jurisdiction must also comply with the laws of that jurisdiction
Corporations Act prohibition on Key Management Personnel and their closely related parties hedging unvested equity remuneration or vested equity subject to holding locks (recorded in section 1.7)

bespoke_clauses.clause: This prohibition ceases to apply in respect of any Equity Instrument acquired through a Share Plan from the time it is withdrawn from the plan, converted to an ordinary AMP share or converted to cash (whichever is the earliest).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The hedging ban is defined by plan custody rather than by vesting, so a collar becomes available over exactly the shares that have been withdrawn from the Share Plan and are held as ordinary AMP shares; the bank should evidence withdrawal or conversion before pricing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors of AMP Limited and members of the Executive Committee are prohibited from entering into or maintaining any margin lending arrangement over or in respect of AMP Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: For the two most likely client groups the loan leg of a funded collar, secured over AMP shares, is very likely a margin lending arrangement 'in respect of AMP Securities' and is banned outright, with no clearance or exceptional circumstances route.

bespoke_clauses.clause: prohibited from entering into or maintaining any margin lending arrangement
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A person who becomes an AMP Limited director or ExCo member while a funded collar loan is outstanding must unwind it, so promotion or board appointment is an unwind trigger the facility documents must anticipate.

bespoke_clauses.clause: subject to section 2.7, a disposal of AMP Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement [is excepted from the black-out prohibition]
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: For a Designated Person who is not a Director or ExCo member, lender enforcement or physical settlement during a black-out period is an excepted Trade and does not breach the policy, which is unusually accommodating of secured lending mechanics.

bespoke_clauses.topic: no clearance for margin call sales
bespoke_clauses.clause: Clearance would not likely be granted under section 3 of this policy to sell AMP Securities during a black-out period to allow a Designated Person to comply with the terms of a margin lending arrangement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The executive cannot rely on being allowed to sell into a black-out period to top up collateral, so any funded collar should be sized and margined so no discretionary top-up sale is ever required.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Head of Corporate Governance (or their delegate) may direct the Designated Person who is proposing to Trade not to do so, or to impose conditions on the Trade in their discretion, and is not obliged to provide reasons for any direction or condition.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Although 2.4 is framed as notification rather than approval, AMP retains an unreasoned veto, so collar entry, roll and unwind carry execution risk right up to the trade date.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a proposed Trade may only be effected on the second, third, fourth or fifth business day after notification.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Pricing and execution of the collar legs must be scheduled inside a four business day window opening two business days after notification, which constrains fixing dates and roll mechanics.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons must not engage in short term trading (ie 30 days or less) in AMP Securities. The 30 days applies from the last time an AMP Security is bought until an AMP Security of that class or type is sold (or vice versa).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Because AMP Securities include derivatives over AMP shares, entering and unwinding or rolling collar legs within 30 days risks breaching 2.8; tenor and roll dates should exceed 30 days.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons must also take appropriate steps to ensure that their Close Associates only Trade in Securities in circumstances where the Designated Person themselves would be permitted to Trade under this policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Routing the collar through a controlled trust, company or investment account does not avoid the black-out, notification, short selling or hedging restrictions.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This policy may also be specifically extended in writing by the CEO by specifying that Designated Persons are restricted from Trading in the Securities of other specified entities with which an AMP Group Company may have a relationship.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The restricted universe is not fixed to AMP Securities and can be broadened by CEO direction, which matters where the collar references a basket or a related listed entity.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and Employees should ask themselves not only 'can we?', but 'should we?' ... How would it look if the transaction were reported on the front page of the newspaper?
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A funded collar by a senior executive is precisely the kind of transaction this test targets, so expect scrutiny and possible informal discouragement even where each leg is technically compliant.

AMP.summary: A funded collar is available only to a narrow group and only over shares that have left the Share Plan. Section 1.7 bans any hedging arrangement over shares, options, share rights and performance rights held in a Share Plan, vested or unvested, and lifts only once the instrument is withdrawn from the plan, converted to an ordinary AMP share or converted to cash, so the derivative legs can be written only over ordinary AMP shares held outside the plan. For those shares the put and call are expressly Trading in AMP Securities: a Designated Person must notify the Head of Corporate Governance in writing at least 2 business days ahead, execute on the second to fifth business day after notification, stay outside the 15 June and 15 December black-out periods and any Board or Market Disclosure Committee blackout, avoid the 30 day short term trading rule, and accept that the Head of Corporate Governance can veto or condition the trade without reasons. The loan leg is the blocker for the target clients: AMP Limited directors and Executive Committee members are absolutely prohibited from entering into or maintaining any margin lending arrangement over or in respect of AMP Securities, with no clearance or exceptional circumstances route, so a funded collar is not possible for them. For other Designated Persons the policy only warns against margin lending and expressly excepts a secured lender's enforcement sale from the black-out prohibition, so a funded collar is workable, subject to the caveat that clearance to sell into a black-out period to meet a margin obligation would not likely be granted.

AGL.title: AGL Securities Dealing Policy
AGL.date_next_review: Biennial review by AGL's Audit and Risk Management Committee, with changes approved by the AGL Board; no fixed date stated

tiers.name: AGL Employees
tiers.description: Each director, officer and employee of the Group, and each contractor and consultant to the Group who are contractually bound to comply with the Policy. All of the substantive prohibitions (blackout periods, short-term dealing, short selling, stock lending, unvested derivatives, margin loans and other secured financing) apply at this level.

tiers.name: Designated Persons
tiers.description: An AGL Employee who is an AGL Director, a member of AGL's Executive Team, a member of AGL's Enterprise Leadership Team, an executive assistant of an Executive Team member, or is designated as such by the Company Secretary from time to time. Must obtain written approval before any dealing in AGL Securities at any time, expressly including dealings in Derivatives over fully vested AGL Shares.

tiers.name: AGL Directors
tiers.description: Directors of AGL. Designated Persons whose dealings are approved by the Chair of the AGL Board (or the Chair of the Audit & Risk Management Committee for the Chair's own dealing), and who must notify the Company Secretary of dealings for ASX Appendix 3Y purposes.

tiers.name: Connected Persons
tiers.description: In relation to a Designated Person: close family members including a spouse or partner and dependent children, and companies, partnerships, trusts and other entities (such as family trusts or self-managed superannuation funds) controlled by the Designated Person or any close family member. The Policy is read as if references to Designated Person were references to Connected Persons.

definitions.hedging_definition: any other arrangement which operates to limit the economic risk of an unvested holding in AGL Securities or which itself or in combination with one or more other Derivatives would have the effect of providing an AGL Employee with a greater benefit than would otherwise have been realised in respect of the unvested AGL Securities

AGL.ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may specify any other blackout period from time to time. These are confidential: to protect confidentiality there may not be any internal notification that a prohibition on dealing is in place, and the Company Secretary may advise that a prohibition exists when an approval request is received but may not be in a position to explain why or how long it will be in place.

rules.detail: Flat prohibition on using Derivatives in relation to any unvested AGL Securities, on the stated rationale that they would allow value to be realised even if performance hurdles are not met. Derivatives takes its section 761D meaning and expressly extends to any arrangement that limits the economic risk of an unvested holding.
rules.evidence: AGL Employees are not permitted to use Derivatives in relation to any unvested AGL Securities.

rules.detail: The permission for Derivatives over vested AGL Securities is conditional on the Securities not being subject to a holding lock, so vested but holding-locked shares (for example under AGL's Employee Share Plan) cannot be collared.
rules.evidence: AGL Employees may use Derivatives in relation to AGL Securities which have vested, provided any dealing in those Derivatives complies with the other requirements of this Policy (including approval requirements) and the AGL Securities are not subject to a holding lock.

rules.detail: Derivatives over vested, unlocked AGL Securities are expressly permitted subject to the Policy's approval requirements, and paragraph 4.2 puts the point beyond doubt for Designated Persons. Securities includes Derivatives as defined in section 761D and financial products under section 1042A with no venue limitation, so an OTC put and call with a bank is within scope. Approval is discretionary, withdrawable without reason and valid for one week.
rules.evidence: For the avoidance of doubt, this requirement includes any proposed dealing in Derivatives in respect of fully vested AGL Shares.

rules.detail: Exchange traded options and warrants are expressly identified as Securities in the Purpose section, and are treated no differently from OTC derivatives: prior written approval, outside blackout periods, no inside information, no holding lock and compliance with the short-term dealing ban.
rules.evidence: The definition of Securities is complex but includes shares in a company and derivative instruments such as exchange traded options and warrants.

rules.detail: An AGL Employee who is not a Designated Person needs no approval to deal in Derivatives over vested, unlocked AGL Securities, but must still stay outside blackout periods, hold no inside information, satisfy the Front Page Test and comply with the short-term dealing, short selling and secured financing prohibitions.
rules.evidence: AGL Employees may use Derivatives in relation to AGL Securities which have vested, provided any dealing in those Derivatives complies with the other requirements of this Policy

rules.detail: Hedging of unvested holdings is caught both by the ban on Derivatives over unvested AGL Securities and by the anti-avoidance limb of the Derivatives definition, which sweeps in any other arrangement operating to limit the economic risk of an unvested holding or that in combination would confer a greater benefit than would otherwise have been realised.
rules.evidence: any other arrangement which operates to limit the economic risk of an unvested holding in AGL Securities

rules.detail: Vested AGL Securities subject to a holding lock fall outside the permission in 3.6 and so cannot be hedged with Derivatives; the exceptional circumstances route in 5.1 is also expressly unavailable for Securities subject to a restriction on disposal.
rules.evidence: the AGL Securities are not subject to a holding lock.

rules.detail: Hedging vested, unlocked AGL Securities with Derivatives is expressly permitted for Designated Persons with prior written approval from the person set out in the 4.2 matrix, executed within the one week approval validity and outside blackout periods.
rules.evidence: AGL Employees may use Derivatives in relation to AGL Securities which have vested, provided any dealing in those Derivatives complies with the other requirements of this Policy (including approval requirements)

rules.detail: Non-Designated employees may hedge vested, unlocked holdings without approval, subject to the blackout periods, insider trading rules, Front Page Test and the 3.4 short-term dealing ban.
rules.evidence: AGL Employees may use Derivatives in relation to AGL Securities which have vested

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward or similar is a dealing because it acquires or disposes of an economic interest and involves granting a right or obligation to dispose of Securities, so it requires prior written approval. Any monetisation funded by a loan for which AGL Securities may be used as security is separately prohibited by 3.7.
rules.evidence: granting, accepting, acquiring, disposing, exercising, or discharging an option or other right or obligation to acquire or dispose of the Securities.

rules.detail: Absolute ban on short selling for all AGL Employees, described as borrowing a security and selling it in the hope of buying it back at a lower price to close out the short position.
rules.evidence: AGL Employees are prohibited from entering into short selling or stock lending arrangements in relation to AGL Securities.

rules.detail: Stock lending arrangements in relation to AGL Securities are banned outright for all AGL Employees, with no approval route. This removes the ability to lend the collared shares to the bank or to support any borrow-based structure.
rules.evidence: AGL Employees are prohibited from entering into short selling or stock lending arrangements in relation to AGL Securities.

rules.detail: CFDs are not named but are Derivatives within section 761D and so Securities. Over vested unlocked shares a Designated Person would need prior written approval, but in practice a CFD would be difficult to reconcile with the ban on dealing as a short-term trader or on a speculative basis, and a short CFD would engage the short selling ban.
rules.evidence: AGL Employees must not deal in AGL Securities as a short-term trader or on a speculative basis.

rules.detail: A CFD referencing unvested AGL Securities is a Derivative in relation to unvested AGL Securities and so within the flat 3.6 prohibition.
rules.evidence: AGL Employees are not permitted to use Derivatives in relation to any unvested AGL Securities.

rules.detail: Margin loan arrangements are prohibited for every AGL Employee, both where they fund the acquisition of AGL Securities and where AGL Securities may be used as security against repayment. There is no approval, exceptional circumstances or grandfathering carve-out. Arrangements such as margin loans that could result in disposal within 3 months of acquisition are separately banned by 3.4.
rules.evidence: AGL Employees are prohibited from entering into margin loan arrangements (and other secured financing arrangements) to fund the acquisition of AGL Securities or in relation to which AGL Securities may be used as a security against repayment of the loan.

rules.detail: Granting security is not itself defined as a dealing, but 3.7 prohibits any arrangement in relation to which AGL Securities may be used as security against repayment of a loan. The prohibition is drafted at the level of possible use as security, so even a facility under which the shares merely may be charged is caught. An encumbrance unconnected with any loan is not addressed.
rules.evidence: or in relation to which AGL Securities may be used as a security against repayment of the loan.

rules.detail: The ban extends beyond margin loans to 'other secured financing arrangements', applies to all AGL Employees and their Connected Persons where practicable, and is not limited by vesting state, tier or amount. No approver is given power to waive it and the exceptional circumstances regime in 5.1 addresses only disposals during blackout periods.
rules.evidence: AGL Employees are prohibited from entering into margin loan arrangements (and other secured financing arrangements) to fund the acquisition of AGL Securities or in relation to which AGL Securities may be used as a security against repayment of the loan.

rules.detail: Two limbs: a general ban on dealing as a short-term trader or on a speculative basis, and a hard 3 month holding period from acquisition that also catches entering into arrangements (margin loans are the stated example) which could result in the Securities being disposed of within 3 months. Carve-outs for securities from options or rights held at least 3 months, shares acquired under an AGL employee equity plan, and share rights under a pro rata entitlement offer.
rules.evidence: AGL Employees who acquire AGL Securities must not dispose of those Securities, or enter into arrangements (such as margin loans) which could result in those Securities being disposed of, within 3 months of acquisition.

clearance.approver: Company Secretary for all other Designated Persons; CEO for Executive Team members and the Company Secretary; Chair of the AGL Board for non-executive Directors, the CEO and the CFO; Chair of the Audit & Risk Management Committee for the Chair of the AGL Board; a nominated alternate if the approver is unavailable
clearance.evidence: Any approval to trade can be given, withdrawn, or refused by the applicable approver in his or her absolute discretion without giving reason. ... Any approval to undertake the proposed dealing will be valid for one week unless it is withdrawn.

clearance.approver: Chair of the AGL Board (Chair of the Audit & Risk Management Committee for a dealing by the Chair of the AGL Board)
clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary (who lodges Appendix 3Y with the ASX)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: as soon as practicable and in any case no later than close of business on the second day after the dealing is entered into
clearance.evidence: AGL Directors must notify the Company Secretary as soon as practicable (and, in any case, no later than close of business on the second day after the dealing is entered into).

clearance.approver: Company Secretary (or, for a Designated Person, the approver specified in paragraph 4.2 or their nominated alternate). Required only for a disposal during a blackout period in exceptional circumstances; no routine clearance applies to non-Designated employees.
clearance.evidence: In addition, all AGL Employees (not just Designated Persons) must seek approval to deal in AGL Securities during a blackout period (i.e. due to exceptional circumstances).

clearance.approver: The approver applicable to the associated Designated Person under the paragraph 4.2 matrix
clearance.evidence: a Designated Person must take appropriate steps for Connected Persons to ... seek approval for any proposed dealings in AGL Securities

short_term.basis: from acquisition; also catches entering into arrangements (such as margin loans) which could result in disposal within that period

AGL shares acquired under an AGL employee equity plan, including AGL's Long Term Incentive Plan, AGL's Share Purchase Plan, or AGL's Employee Share Reward Plan

short_term.evidence: AGL Employees must not deal in AGL Securities as a short-term trader or on a speculative basis.

exceptions.evidence: the acquisition of AGL Securities under an AGL employee equity plan, including AGL's Long Term Incentive Plan, AGL's Employee Share Plan or AGL's Share Purchase Plan
the acquisition of AGL Securities under AGL's Dividend Reinvestment Plan

exceptions.approver: The approver specified in paragraph 4.2 (or their nominated alternate) for Designated Persons, otherwise the Company Secretary
exceptions.evidence: the AGL Employee is experiencing severe financial hardship and can only meet their financial commitments by selling their Securities

exceptions.approver: The approver specified in paragraph 4.2 (or their nominated alternate) for Designated Persons, otherwise the Company Secretary

AGL.exemption_authority: Paragraph 5.1 only, and only for disposals: the paragraph 4.2 approver (or nominated alternate) for Designated Persons, otherwise the Company Secretary, may approve a disposal during a blackout period where the employee is in severe financial hardship and can only meet financial commitments by selling, is compelled by court order, or there are other exceptional circumstances, provided they hold no inside information, the Securities are not subject to a restriction on disposal, and the application is supported by sufficient evidence that the dealing is the most reasonable course of action. The Company Secretary keeps a record and must promptly inform the Board. No authority exists to waive the paragraph 3.7 margin loan and secured financing prohibition, the 3.5 short selling and stock lending bans, or the 3.6 unvested derivatives ban.

bespoke_clauses.clause: AGL Employees are prohibited from entering into margin loan arrangements (and other secured financing arrangements) to fund the acquisition of AGL Securities or in relation to which AGL Securities may be used as a security against repayment of the loan.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar is a secured financing arrangement in relation to which AGL Securities would be used as security against repayment, so it is prohibited outright for every AGL Employee with no approval route.

bespoke_clauses.clause: or in relation to which AGL Securities may be used as a security against repayment of the loan
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The trigger is the possibility of the shares being used as security, not actual granting of the charge, so even a negative pledge structure or a facility with an optional security mechanic over AGL shares is caught.

bespoke_clauses.topic: derivatives over vested shares expressly allowed
bespoke_clauses.clause: For the avoidance of doubt, this requirement includes any proposed dealing in Derivatives in respect of fully vested AGL Shares.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The unfunded legs of a collar over fully vested, unlocked shares are contemplated and approvable, so the structure fails only on the financing leg; a cash-settled or unfunded collar could still be presented for approval.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Derivatives ... includes options, forward contracts, swaps, futures contracts and warrants and any combination of one or more of these things or any other arrangement which operates to limit the economic risk of an unvested holding in AGL Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A synthetic or combination structure over unvested entitlements cannot be engineered around the 3.6 ban, since the definition is drafted by economic effect rather than instrument type.

bespoke_clauses.clause: AGL Employees may use Derivatives in relation to AGL Securities which have vested, provided ... the AGL Securities are not subject to a holding lock.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank must verify not only vesting but the absence of any holding lock on the specific parcel before the collar legs may be written.

bespoke_clauses.clause: AGL Employees who acquire AGL Securities must not dispose of those Securities, or enter into arrangements (such as margin loans) which could result in those Securities being disposed of, within 3 months of acquisition.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Independently of 3.7, a collar with physical settlement or lender enforcement rights over recently acquired shares is an arrangement that could result in disposal within 3 months, so tenor and share selection matter.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where the Board imposes additional blackout periods from time to time, to protect confidentiality there may not be any internal notification by AGL that a prohibition on dealing is in place.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Undisclosed blackouts can block entry, roll or unwind at any time, and the executive may only learn of one when an approval request is refused without explanation.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any approval to trade can be given, withdrawn, or refused by the applicable approver in his or her absolute discretion without giving reason. ... Any approval to undertake the proposed dealing will be valid for one week unless it is withdrawn.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Approval for the derivative legs is revocable up to execution and lapses after one week, so pricing must be completed inside a short window and the bank carries the risk of late withdrawal.

bespoke_clauses.clause: There are certain times during the year when approval under this Policy is more likely to be granted. These are the four-week periods immediately following each blackout period.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Practical execution should be scheduled in the four weeks after each results announcement, which effectively narrows the collar entry and roll calendar to two short windows a year.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where any approval is required for a dealing under this Policy, approval will not be granted where the dealing would not satisfy the Front Page Test.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An express substantive ground for refusal: a senior executive hedging a large stake is exactly the transaction likely to fail a reputational perception test, independently of technical compliance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This Policy extends to Connected Persons of Designated Persons in relation to dealing in AGL Securities ... (which will be read as if references to 'Designated Person' throughout the Policy was a reference to Connected Persons).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Holding the shares or the borrowing through a family trust, controlled company or SMSF does not escape the secured financing ban or the approval requirement.

AGL.summary: A funded collar is not possible at AGL. The derivative legs themselves are workable in principle: paragraph 3.6 expressly permits Derivatives over AGL Securities that have vested and are not subject to a holding lock, and paragraph 4.2 confirms that a Designated Person may seek approval for a dealing in Derivatives over fully vested AGL Shares, with written approval from the Chair, CEO or Company Secretary according to the 4.2 matrix, valid for one week, outside the 1 July and 1 January blackout periods and any confidential Board blackout, and subject to the Front Page Test. The financing leg is fatal: paragraph 3.7 prohibits every AGL Employee from entering into margin loans or other secured financing arrangements in relation to which AGL Securities may be used as security against repayment, with no approval, hardship or grandfathering route, and the exceptional circumstances power in 5.1 extends only to disposals during blackout periods. Stock lending and short selling are also banned outright, and no Derivative may be used over unvested or holding-locked securities. Even an unfunded collar must clear the 3 month holding rule, which expressly catches arrangements that could result in disposal within 3 months of acquisition.

ANN.title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Designated Persons
tiers.description: All directors of Ansell; senior management, being all members of the executive leadership team and all employees with Vice President designation; and any employee with access to the monthly consolidated financial information or otherwise likely to receive price sensitive or Inside Information who is notified as such by the Company Secretary. Subject to Trading Windows, Clearance, the short-term dealing ban, the margin loan prohibition and ad-hoc restrictions.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: All directors of Ansell. Clearance is given by the Chairman of the Board (or the Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee for the Chair of the Board's own dealing), and directors must notify the Company of changes in their security interests for Listing Rule purposes.

tiers.name: ELT Members
tiers.description: All members of the executive leadership team. Designated Persons whose Clearance, and that of the Company Secretary, is given by the Managing Director/CEO.

tiers.name: Vice Presidents
tiers.description: All employees with Vice President designation. Designated Persons cleared by the Company Secretary.

tiers.name: Designated Employees
tiers.description: Any employee with access to the monthly consolidated financial information and any other employees likely to receive price sensitive or Inside Information in the course of their positions who are notified as such by the Company Secretary. Cleared by the Company Secretary.

tiers.name: employees
tiers.description: All directors, senior executives and employees (and their associates) to whom the Policy applies. Those who are not Designated Persons are bound by the insider trading rules, the front page test and, if plan participants, the clause 5.3 hedging prohibition, but not by Trading Windows, Clearance or the margin loan prohibition.

tiers.name: Closely Related Parties
tiers.description: Spouse, partner or dependent child (including adult and step-children); a relative residing with the Designated Person; another family member the Designated Person may be expected to influence or be influenced by in relation to Dealings in Ansell Securities; and companies, trusts, partnerships and other entities that the Designated Person or any of those persons control or significantly influence. Trading Windows and Clearance apply to them, and the Designated Person must do any required act on their behalf.

definitions.hedging_definition: any conduct that seeks to secure the economic value attaching to a security granted under the relevant plan and remove the element of price risk inherent in the value of those Securities, while the Securities remain unvested. Prohibited conduct includes, but is not limited to, writing put or call options over the underlying Securities, Dealing in derivative products or entering into other arrangements intended to hedge a 'profit' in those Securities.

ANN.ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Company, in its sole and absolute discretion, may impose additional restrictions on Dealing by all or any Designated Persons, expressly including where a Trading Window is otherwise open. Any such restriction communicated to Designated Persons must be kept strictly confidential. The Trading Windows themselves also operate only 'unless the Company advises otherwise'.

rules.detail: No express derivatives rule for vested holdings. Dealing expressly extends to forward contracts, granting options and hedging Securities, and to agreements to do any of those things, so an OTC put and written call are Dealings. A Designated Person may therefore enter them only inside a 30-day Trading Window, with written Clearance from the relevant Authorising Officer valid for five trading days, and only if not in possession of Inside Information.
rules.evidence: Dealing in Securities is a broad concept and covers more than simply buying or selling Securities. It extends to subscribing for the Company's Securities, forward contracts, granting options and hedging Securities.

rules.detail: Exchange-traded options over Ansell shares are Securities (the definition expressly includes options and any other financial product able to be traded on a financial market) and are treated identically to OTC derivatives: Trading Window plus five trading day Clearance.
rules.evidence: The definition of securities in the Corporations Act is very broad, and includes shares, options, debentures, convertible notes and any other financial product able to be traded on a financial market.

rules.detail: Writing put or call options over the underlying Securities and Dealing in derivative products are expressly named as prohibited conduct for all participants in an approved share or equity plan while the plan Securities remain unvested. The ban applies to every plan participant, not only Designated Persons.
rules.evidence: Prohibited conduct includes, but is not limited to, writing put or call options over the underlying Securities, Dealing in derivative products or entering into other arrangements intended to hedge a 'profit' in those Securities.

rules.detail: Purpose-based prohibition on any conduct that seeks to secure the economic value of a plan security and remove the element of price risk while it remains unvested. The list of prohibited conduct is expressly non-exhaustive, so economically equivalent structures are caught.
rules.evidence: All participants in an approved share or equity plan of the Company are prohibited from engaging in any conduct that seeks to secure the economic value attaching to a security granted under the relevant plan and remove the element of price risk inherent in the value of those Securities, while the Securities remain unvested.

rules.detail: Clause 5.3 is keyed to Securities that 'remain unvested' and clause 5.2 separately refers to 'the end of applicable vesting or restriction periods', so plan shares that have vested but are still within a restriction period are not expressly covered by the hedging ban. The underlying plan rules, which are not part of this Policy, would need to be checked.

The clause 5.3 hedging prohibition stops at vesting, and hedging Securities is expressly a Dealing. Hedging vested, unrestricted shares is therefore permitted for a Designated Person inside a Trading Window with Clearance from the relevant Authorising Officer, subject to the front page test which is an express ground for refusing approval.
rules.evidence: It extends to subscribing for the Company's Securities, forward contracts, granting options and hedging Securities.

rules.detail: An employee who is not a Designated Person and whose plan securities have vested is not restricted by clause 5.3 and is not subject to Trading Windows or Clearance; only the insider trading prohibition and the front page test apply.
rules.evidence: while the Securities remain unvested.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named, but forward contracts are expressly within the definition of Dealing, so a prepaid forward or similar requires a Trading Window and Clearance. If the monetisation is funded by a loan or similar funding arrangement in respect of Ansell Securities, clause 4.8 says a Designated Person should not enter into it.
rules.evidence: It extends to subscribing for the Company's Securities, forward contracts, granting options and hedging Securities. It also extends to entering into an agreement to do any of the above.

rules.detail: The Policy contains no short selling prohibition and does not use the term; a short sale would still be a Dealing requiring a Trading Window and Clearance for a Designated Person, and would sit uneasily with the short-term dealing ban.
Securities lending is not mentioned anywhere and is not listed in the definition of Dealing.

CFDs are not named. They are derivative products over Ansell Securities and so a Dealing requiring a Trading Window and Clearance, but the clause 4.6 prohibition on short-term trading, including within 3 months of receiving Securities, would in practice preclude typical CFD activity.
rules.evidence: No Designated Person should Deal in Ansell Securities on a short-term trading basis, including trading in Ansell Securities within a 3 month period of receiving the Securities

rules.detail: A CFD over unvested plan securities is Dealing in a derivative product that removes price risk and is expressly prohibited conduct under clause 5.3.
rules.evidence: Prohibited conduct includes, but is not limited to, writing put or call options over the underlying Securities, Dealing in derivative products

rules.detail: A one-line prohibition covering margin loans and 'similar funding arrangements' in respect of Ansell Securities, with no vesting-state or amount qualification. It is expressed as 'should' rather than 'must', and clause 4.5 gives Authorising Officers discretion to approve Dealings that would otherwise be prohibited by the policy, so a waiver route is arguably available.
rules.evidence: No Designated Person should enter into a margin loan or similar funding arrangement in respect to Securities in the Company.

rules.detail: Clause 4.8 sits within the additional restrictions for Designated Persons and does not apply to other employees.

Granting security over Ansell Securities is not named and is not listed in the definition of Dealing. The Policy nevertheless contemplates that security agreements over Ansell Securities exist, since clause 4.4(a)(v) treats a disposal resulting from a secured lender exercising rights under a loan or security agreement as an Excluded Dealing. An encumbrance forming part of a margin loan or similar funding arrangement is caught by clause 4.8.

Clause 4.8 reaches beyond margin loans to any 'similar funding arrangement in respect to Securities in the Company', which on its face captures a bank loan drawn against and secured on Ansell shares as part of a collar. There is no dedicated waiver in clause 4.8 itself, but clause 4.5 permits an Authorising Officer to approve Dealings otherwise prohibited by the Policy.
rules.evidence: No Designated Person should enter into a margin loan or similar funding arrangement in respect to Securities in the Company.

rules.detail: No secured financing restriction applies to employees who are not Designated Persons.

No short-term trading, including trading within 3 months of receiving the Securities, except in limited circumstances (severe financial hardship, dealings of long term incentive Securities upon vesting, or a legal obligation to sell or transfer) and with the approval of the Company Secretary.

jurisdiction_overlays: Clause 3.6 requires compliance with insider trading rules or law globally in relation to Securities of other listed entities

bespoke_clauses.topic: margin loan and similar funding ban
bespoke_clauses.clause: No Designated Person should enter into a margin loan or similar funding arrangement in respect to Securities in the Company.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar is a funding arrangement in respect of Ansell Securities and so within clause 4.8, which is the principal obstacle; note the hortatory 'should' rather than 'must not'.

bespoke_clauses.clause: In exceptional circumstances the Authorising Officers listed in clause 4.3(d) have discretion to approve Dealings by the respective Designated Person in Ansell Securities outside a Trading Window, or to approve Dealings in Ansell Securities that would otherwise be prohibited by this policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unusually, an Authorising Officer can approve dealings that the policy otherwise prohibits, so the funded collar is not structurally impossible; the whole structure would need Board Chair or CEO level sign-off as an exceptional circumstance.

bespoke_clauses.topic: lender enforcement is an excluded dealing
bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons may at any time, without seeking Clearance ... dispose of Ansell Securities that are the result of a secured lender exercising their rights under a loan or security agreement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The policy expressly contemplates secured lending over Ansell shares and protects the executive if the bank enforces or takes delivery outside a Trading Window, requiring only after-the-event notice to the Authorising Officer.

bespoke_clauses.clause: All participants in an approved share or equity plan of the Company are prohibited from engaging in any conduct that seeks to secure the economic value ... while the Securities remain unvested.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The hedging prohibition is bounded by vesting rather than by any holding lock, so vested plan shares are available for a collar, subject to the Trading Window and Clearance regime.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons and their Closely Related Parties may, unless the Company advises otherwise, Deal in Ansell Securities during the 30-day period beginning ... on the second trading day after [half-yearly results / annual results / the AGM]. ... Designated Persons may not Deal in Ansell Securities outside the Trading Windows.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is a positive-window policy: entry, roll and unwind of the collar must each fall inside one of only three 30-day windows a year, which constrains tenor selection and expiry dates.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the clearance will be confirmed in writing and will be valid for a period of five trading days (inclusive of the approval date) unless otherwise stated. No Dealing ... may be executed beyond the five day period ... without having sought and received further Clearance.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Pricing and signing of the derivative legs must complete within five trading days of Clearance, and a staged or averaged execution beyond that needs fresh Clearance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Company, in its sole and absolute discretion, may impose additional restrictions on Dealing ... even where the proposed Dealing would otherwise take place when a Trading Window is open. Any restriction ... must be kept strictly confidential.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An open window is never a guarantee; a confidential ad-hoc restriction can block collar entry or unwind without the bank being told why.

bespoke_clauses.topic: front page test as a refusal ground
bespoke_clauses.clause: Where any approval under this Policy is required for a Dealing, approval will not be granted where the dealing would not satisfy the 'front page' test.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An express mandatory ground for refusing Clearance, and a senior executive hedging a stake with bank funding is squarely the kind of transaction it targets.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons must take all reasonable steps to ensure that their Closely Related Parties are aware of, and comply with, this Policy. Where this Policy requires a Closely Related Party to do an act ... you must do that act on behalf of your Closely Related Party.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Holding the shares or the borrowing through a controlled trust or company does not avoid clause 4.8 or the Clearance requirement, and the Designated Person must obtain Clearance on the entity's behalf.

bespoke_clauses.clause: No Designated Person should Deal in Ansell Securities on a short-term trading basis, including trading in Ansell Securities within a 3 month period of receiving the Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Collaring shares within three months of vesting or acquisition risks breaching clause 4.6 unless the Company Secretary approves, so the parcel selection should favour older holdings.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any sale of Ansell shares acquired by a Designated Person under any Ansell share or equity plan (at the end of applicable vesting or restriction periods or upon exercise of options) must only occur during a Trading Window ... and with Clearance.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Physical settlement of the call leg over plan-sourced shares is a sale that must itself fall inside a Trading Window with fresh Clearance, so expiry dates should be aligned to the windows or the collar cash settled.

ANN.summary: A funded collar is possible at Ansell only as an approved exception, not as of right. The derivative legs over vested, unrestricted shares are permissible in principle: the clause 5.3 hedging prohibition stops at vesting, and hedging, granting options and forward contracts are expressly Dealings, so a Designated Person needs written Clearance from the relevant Authorising Officer, valid five trading days, executed inside one of the three 30-day Trading Windows that open on the second trading day after the half-yearly results, the annual results and the AGM, with no inside information and subject to the mandatory front page test. The loan leg runs into clause 4.8, under which no Designated Person should enter into a margin loan or similar funding arrangement in respect of Ansell Securities, which on its face captures a loan drawn against the collared shares. The saving feature is clause 4.5: in exceptional circumstances an Authorising Officer may approve Dealings outside a Trading Window or Dealings that would otherwise be prohibited by the policy, so a Chair or CEO level approval could in principle sanction the structure, and clause 4.4(a)(v) already treats a disposal resulting from a secured lender exercising rights under a loan or security agreement as an Excluded Dealing needing no Clearance. Practical constraints remain: confidential ad-hoc restrictions can override an open window, the 3 month rule after receiving Securities, and physical settlement of the call over plan-sourced shares must itself fall inside a Trading Window with fresh Clearance.

EDV.ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The policy is window-based rather than blackout-based, so any period that is not a Trading Window is a closed period. The Board may determine additional Trading Window periods, and the Board Chair may determine variations to any of the window periods on the recommendation of the Chief Legal Officer and Company Secretary. Windows are effective only when notified: the opening of Trading Windows will be notified to Designated Persons by email and Designated Persons must not assume a Trading Window is open in the absence of such notification.

rules.detail: A flat prohibition on Designated Persons and their Associates entering into Hedging arrangements in relation to any Endeavour Securities, not just plan securities and regardless of vesting. Hedging arrangement is defined by economic effect, capturing any transaction designed to limit exposure to economic risk in securities. Paragraph 16 provides an exemption route only for dealing outside a Trading Window in Exceptional Circumstances and for a prohibited dealing under paragraph 11b (collateral), not for 11d, so there is no approval pathway for hedging.
rules.evidence: Additionally, Designated Persons and their Associates must not: ... enter into Hedging arrangements in relation to Endeavour Securities, including those specified in paragraph 9 (no hedging).

rules.detail: Non-executive directors and the CEO are Designated Persons, so the flat 11d hedging ban applies to them and to their Associates over any Endeavour Securities, including shares acquired on market outside any plan. No exemption route exists: paragraph 16 reaches only trading window exemptions and prohibited dealings under 11b.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons are: non-executive directors, the CEO and the Company Secretary of Endeavour ... Additionally, Designated Persons and their Associates must not: ... enter into Hedging arrangements in relation to Endeavour Securities

rules.detail: Executive Committee members and their direct reports are Designated Persons and are therefore subject to the same flat prohibition on Hedging arrangements in relation to any Endeavour Securities, with no approval pathway.
rules.evidence: Executives Committee members and their direct reports; ... Designated Persons and their Associates must not: ... enter into Hedging arrangements in relation to Endeavour Securities

rules.detail: The 11d hedging ban applies directly to Associates of Designated Persons, and the Designated Person is responsible for making them aware of it and taking reasonable steps to ensure compliance, so a collar cannot be routed through a spouse, controlled entity or trust.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons and their Associates must not: ... enter into Hedging arrangements in relation to Endeavour Securities, including those specified in paragraph 9 (no hedging).

rules.detail: Plan participants and their Associates must not hedge unvested Endeavour Securities allocated under an equity-based remuneration plan. This applies to every participant, whether or not they are a Designated Person.
rules.evidence: If you participate in an Endeavour equity-based remuneration plan you (or your Associate) must not enter into any Hedging arrangement in respect to any unvested Endeavour Securities or vested Endeavour Securities which are subject to a dealing restriction, allocated to you under that plan.

rules.detail: The paragraph 9 ban expressly extends to vested plan securities that remain subject to a dealing restriction, so a holding lock keeps the shares out of reach of any collar.
rules.evidence: must not enter into any Hedging arrangement in respect to any unvested Endeavour Securities or vested Endeavour Securities which are subject to a dealing restriction, allocated to you under that plan.

rules.detail: Paragraph 9 stops at vested securities that are free of any dealing restriction, so a plan participant who is not a Designated Person may hedge vested unrestricted plan shares, subject only to the insider trading prohibition and the market perception obligation.
rules.evidence: any unvested Endeavour Securities or vested Endeavour Securities which are subject to a dealing restriction, allocated to you under that plan.

rules.detail: A team member who is neither a Designated Person nor an equity plan participant is not caught by either hedging prohibition; only the insider trading prohibition and the market perception obligation apply, and there is no Trading Window or clearance requirement.
rules.evidence: There are additional obligations which apply to Designated Persons and their Associates and to participants in Endeavour's equity-based remuneration plans.

rules.detail: The definition of derivative expressly names collars, together with options, forward contracts, swaps, futures, warrants, caps and contracts for difference, and defines them by their function of limiting the economic risk of holding securities. A purchased put plus written call over Endeavour shares is therefore a Hedging arrangement banned by 11d for Designated Persons and their Associates, with no venue limitation and no approval route.
rules.evidence: Any product (such as options, forward contracts, swaps, futures, warrants, caps, collars and contracts for difference) or transaction that operates to limit the economic risk associated with holding securities.

rules.detail: Exchange-traded options and warrants over Endeavour Securities are treated identically; in addition paragraph 11c separately bans dealing in derivatives issued over Endeavour Securities within a six month period.
rules.evidence: deal in the same Endeavour Securities, or in derivatives issued over Endeavour Securities, within a six month period (no short term gain).

rules.detail: The derivative and hedging restrictions in paragraph 11 apply only to Designated Persons and their Associates, and paragraph 9 only to equity plan participants, so an ordinary team member dealing in derivatives over their own vested unrestricted shares is not restricted by this policy.
rules.evidence: There are obligations in this policy that apply to Endeavour Group and to all team members. There are additional obligations which apply to Designated Persons and their Associates and to participants in Endeavour's equity-based remuneration plans.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named, but a prepaid forward or similar structure is a forward contract and a transaction that operates to limit economic risk, so it is a Hedging arrangement prohibited by 11d. If it also uses Endeavour Securities as collateral it engages the 11b collateral ban, for which an approval route does exist under paragraph 16b.
rules.evidence: Any product (such as options, forward contracts, swaps, futures, warrants, caps, collars and contracts for difference) or transaction that operates to limit the economic risk associated with holding securities.

rules.detail: Short selling is not named anywhere in the policy. A short sale by a Designated Person would still be a dealing requiring a Trading Window and clearance, would engage the six month rule, and a synthetic short would be caught by the hedging ban.

Stock lending is expressly within the definition of deal, so it is not prohibited as such but must occur inside a Trading Window with written clearance from the relevant approver, executed within three business days. There is no separate stock lending prohibition.
rules.evidence: Deal includes to: ... margin lend, stock lend or make other financing arrangements for securities

rules.detail: Contracts for difference are expressly named in the definition of derivative, which is framed as a product or transaction operating to limit economic risk, so CFDs over Endeavour Securities are Hedging arrangements banned by 11d, and are separately caught by the six month rule in 11c.
rules.evidence: Any product (such as options, forward contracts, swaps, futures, warrants, caps, collars and contracts for difference) or transaction that operates to limit the economic risk associated with holding securities.

rules.detail: Margin lending using Endeavour Securities as collateral is a prohibited dealing under 11b, but the December 2022 revision added an express clearance process: under 16b a Designated Person or Associate may seek approval for a prohibited dealing under 11b, submitting written details of the securitisation arrangement concurrently to the CLO and Company Secretary as endorsers and the Board Chair and the Chair of the Audit, Risk & Compliance Management Committee as approvers, who may grant, refuse or make it conditional in absolute discretion without reasons.
rules.evidence: use Endeavour Securities as collateral in any financial transaction, including any margin lending arrangements (no security or margin lending), unless otherwise permitted under this policy

rules.detail: Paragraph 11 applies only to Designated Persons and their Associates; the policy is silent on margin lending by other team members.

Using Endeavour Securities as collateral in any financial transaction is expressly prohibited unless otherwise permitted under the policy, and paragraph 16b supplies that permission route. The ban is drafted at the level of collateral use in any financial transaction, so it captures a charge, mortgage or pledge over the shares however the financing is characterised. Making financing arrangements for securities is also itself a dealing.
rules.evidence: use Endeavour Securities as collateral in any financial transaction, including any margin lending arrangements (no security or margin lending), unless otherwise permitted under this policy

rules.detail: The collateral prohibition extends beyond margin loans to any financial transaction in which Endeavour Securities are used as collateral, so the loan leg of a funded collar is squarely within it. Unusually the policy provides a dedicated approval process for exactly this, requiring written details of the securitisation arrangement, dual endorsement and dual approval at Board Chair and ARCMC Chair level.
rules.evidence: an approval for a prohibited dealing under paragraph 16b then you must provide written details of the securitisation arrangement and any other information requested by Endeavour.

rules.detail: The collateral ban and its clearance process sit within the Designated Persons obligations and do not reach other team members.

A six month buy/sell window applying both to the same Endeavour Securities and to derivatives issued over Endeavour Securities. The only carve-out is the exercise of rights under an equity-based remuneration plan and the subsequent dealing of those securities in accordance with the policy.
rules.evidence: deal in the same Endeavour Securities, or in derivatives issued over Endeavour Securities, within a six month period (no short term gain). EDV.exemption_authority: The Board is the policy's Exception Authority. Operationally, paragraph 16 allows a Designated Person or Associate to request either a trading window exemption to deal outside a Trading Window in Exceptional Circumstances, or approval for a prohibited dealing under paragraph 11b (use of Endeavour Securities as collateral), the latter decided by the Board Chair and the Chair of the Audit, Risk & Compliance Management Committee on the endorsement of the CLO and Company Secretary. Neither route is available where there would be a breach of the insider trading prohibition or market perception obligation, and neither extends to the paragraph 11d hedging prohibition or the paragraph 11c six month rule.
jurisdiction_overlays: Paragraph 4: the insider trading prohibition applies to acts in Australia as well as outside Australia

bespoke_clauses.topic: collars named in the derivative definition
bespoke_clauses.clause: derivative: Any product (such as options, forward contracts, swaps, futures, warrants, caps, collars and contracts for difference) or transaction that operates to limit the economic risk associated with holding securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The policy names collars specifically and defines derivatives by economic function, so there is no argument that a put plus call structure falls outside the hedging prohibition.

bespoke_clauses.topic: flat hedging ban for Designated Persons
bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons and their Associates must not ... enter into Hedging arrangements in relation to Endeavour Securities, including those specified in paragraph 9 (no hedging).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The ban is not limited to plan securities or to unvested holdings, so a Designated Person cannot collar even shares bought on market with their own money, and paragraph 16 offers no exemption route for it.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A Designated Person or their Associate may request to ... seek an approval for a prohibited dealing under paragraph 11b ... you must provide written details of the securitisation arrangement and any other information requested by Endeavour. The request should be submitted concurrently to the CLO and Company Secretary (Endorsers) and the Chair and the Board Chair of the Audit, Risk & Compliance Management Committee (Approvers).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Endeavour is one of the few ASX policies with an express pathway to approve pledging shares as loan collateral, so the financing leg of a funded structure is negotiable at Board Chair level even though the hedging leg is not.

bespoke_clauses.clause: use Endeavour Securities as collateral in any financial transaction, including any margin lending arrangements (no security or margin lending), unless otherwise permitted under this policy
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The prohibition is drafted at the level of collateral in any financial transaction, so it catches any bank facility secured on the shares regardless of how the loan is documented, and approval must be obtained before the security is granted.

bespoke_clauses.clause: deal in the same Endeavour Securities, or in derivatives issued over Endeavour Securities, within a six month period (no short term gain).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even a permitted derivative programme could not be entered, rolled or unwound within six months, so short-dated or frequently rolled collars are unavailable to Designated Persons.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The opening of Trading Windows will be notified to Designated Persons by email. Designated Persons must not assume that a Trading Window is open in the absence of such notification.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Windows are not self-executing from the results calendar; the bank should require evidence of the notification email before scheduling execution.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the Designated Person or Associate must undertake the dealing within three business days of obtaining the clearance ... A dealing must be placed within a Trading Window (not prior) and executed by 4.00pm on the last day of the relevant Trading Window. A dealing may settle after the close of the Trading Window.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any approved leg must be placed and executed inside the window and within three business days of clearance, though settlement may fall outside, which is helpful for a structure with a delayed settlement date.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Deal includes to: ... margin lend, stock lend or make other financing arrangements for securities; ... transfer ownership between accounts, brokers or sponsors.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Moving the collared shares into a custody or collateral account, and the financing arrangement itself, are each dealings needing a Trading Window and clearance, not just administrative steps.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Associates ... includes ... a company, trust, partnership or other entity that the Relevant Person, or any of the persons mentioned above, control or significantly influence; or the trustee of a trust or fiduciary arrangements of which the Relevant Person ... is a beneficiary.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Structuring the collar through a family trust, controlled company or the trustee of a fund in which the executive is a beneficiary does not escape the hedging ban or the collateral clearance requirement.

bespoke_clauses.clause: You must not deal in Endeavour Securities (or securities of another company) if the proposed dealing could be perceived by the market as you taking advantage of your position in an inappropriate way.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An independent, self-executing obligation that applies to every team member at all times and cannot be waived by any exemption, so even an approved collateral arrangement remains vulnerable to a perception challenge.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A liability to pay tax does not normally constitute severe financial difficulty.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Funding a tax bill on vesting is expressly not an exceptional circumstance, closing off the most common justification for an out-of-window monetisation.

EDV.summary: A funded collar is not possible for an Endeavour Designated Person, and the obstacle is the hedging leg rather than the financing leg. Paragraph 11d prohibits Designated Persons and their Associates from entering into Hedging arrangements in relation to any Endeavour Securities, vested or not and however acquired, and the definitions put the point beyond argument by defining derivative to include collars and by defining a Hedging arrangement as any transaction designed to limit exposure to economic risk in securities. Paragraph 16 provides exemption routes only for dealing outside a Trading Window in Exceptional Circumstances and for the paragraph 11b collateral prohibition, so there is no approval pathway for hedging, and paragraph 11c would independently bar entering and unwinding derivative positions within six months. The financing leg, by contrast, is expressly negotiable: the December 2022 revision added a clearance process under which a Designated Person may seek approval to use Endeavour Securities as collateral in a financial transaction, supported by written details of the securitisation arrangement, endorsed by the CLO and Company Secretary and approved by the Board Chair and the Chair of the Audit, Risk & Compliance Management Committee. Only an equity plan participant who is not a Designated Person retains room to hedge, and then only over vested plan securities that are free of any dealing restriction.

CWY.ad_hoc_blackout_authority: No express power to declare additional blackout periods; the Board's declaration power only opens extra Trading Windows. In substance CWY can block any dealing at any time: any request for approval can be refused by CWY in its absolute discretion, a granted approval may be revoked by the Company at any time at its absolute discretion, and Directors and Executives will not be given approval where price sensitive non-public information exists 'even though they may not be aware of it'. A refusal must be kept confidential.

rules.detail: Flat prohibition on trading in CWY derivatives by Directors and Employees, expressed to apply to all CWY securities and not limited by venue, so an OTC put or call written or bought with a bank over CWY shares is caught. The following sentence explains the ban by reference to hedging products over unvested performance rights, which creates a drafting tension, but the operative sentence is unqualified.
rules.evidence: Directors and Employees must not trade in CWY derivatives.  This applies to all CWY securities including performance rights issued under CWYs incentive schemes.

rules.detail: Collars are named in terms: equity swaps, caps and collars or other hedging products over unvested performance rights that reduce or limit exposure to the market value of CWY securities are prohibited outright, with no approval route.
rules.evidence: It means that you cannot enter into any hedging arrangements or acquire financial products (such as equity swaps, caps and collars or other hedging products) over unvested performance rights which have the effect of reducing or limiting exposure to risks associated with the market value of CWY securities.

rules.detail: Hedging vested shares is not separately addressed, but a hedge is executed through derivatives and the derivatives ban is expressed to apply to 'all CWY securities', so a collar over vested unrestricted shares is prohibited. The only textual argument the other way is that the explanatory sentence limits itself to unvested performance rights; the policy has no clearance route that could cure the point.
rules.evidence: Directors and Employees must not trade in CWY derivatives.  This applies to all CWY securities including performance rights issued under CWYs incentive schemes.

rules.detail: Monetisation, prepaid forwards and zero-cost collars are not named as such. Any structure that monetises CWY securities through a derivative is caught by the ban on trading in CWY derivatives and, where it reduces or limits market-value exposure, by the hedging prohibition. Monetisation by outright sale remains possible inside a Trading Window with approval.
rules.evidence: Directors and Employees must not trade in CWY derivatives.  This applies to all CWY securities including performance rights issued under CWYs incentive schemes.

rules.detail: Short selling is nowhere named. In practice a short position in CWY would be taken through a derivative (prohibited under 3.4) and a physical short sale would breach the three-month same-securities rule, but the policy contains no short selling clause.
Securities lending is not mentioned and there is no definition of dealing that would sweep it in.
CFDs are not named, but a CFD over CWY shares is a CWY derivative and so falls within the flat prohibition in 3.4; it would also breach the ban on short-term or speculative trading.
rules.evidence: Directors and Employees must not engage in short-term or speculative trading in CWY securities.

rules.detail: Directors are prohibited directly or indirectly from entering into any margin loan facility against CWY securities unless the prior written consent of the Chairman of the CWY Board has been obtained. No criteria are given for consent, no validity period, no disclosure obligation and no rules on margin calls or forced sales.

rules.detail: Granting security, a charge, lien, pledge or mortgage over CWY securities is not itself treated as a dealing or otherwise regulated; there is no dealing definition at all. The only encumbrance-adjacent provision is the margin loan clause in 3.5.

There is no general ban on secured financing; the only regulated form is a 'margin loan facility against CWY securities', which needs the Chairman's prior written consent. A limited-recourse or collar loan secured on CWY shares with loan-to-value top-up or margin features would in substance be treated as a margin loan facility 'directly or indirectly' against CWY securities and so require that consent; a plain secured loan with no margin mechanics is not expressly addressed.

rules.detail: Bright-line ban: no dealing in the same CWY securities within any three month period, in addition to a general ban on short-term or speculative trading. No carve-out is given for plan securities or for the exempt dealings in 3.6.
rules.evidence: Directors and Employees must not engage in short-term or speculative trading in CWY securities. Specifically, for the purposes of this policy, this means that Directors and Employees must not deal in the same CWY securities within any three month period.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and Employees must not trade in CWY derivatives. This applies to all CWY securities including performance rights issued under CWYs incentive schemes.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Both legs of a collar are CWY derivatives, so the structure is prohibited outright for every Director and Employee with no clearance or hardship route available.

bespoke_clauses.clause: you cannot enter into any hedging arrangements or acquire financial products (such as equity swaps, caps and collars or other hedging products) over unvested performance rights which have the effect of reducing or limiting exposure to risks associated with the market value of CWY securities
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Collars are named in terms, removing any argument that the ban was not intended to reach this product, although the explanatory sentence is drafted by reference to unvested performance rights only.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Section 3.4 first bans trading in CWY derivatives over 'all CWY securities', then explains the ban only by reference to hedging 'over unvested performance rights'.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The only conceivable opening for a collar over vested shares is to read the operative ban down to the explanatory sentence, which would require the Board to confirm the narrow reading in writing before a bank could rely on it.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Unless the prior written consent of the Chairman of the CWY Board has been obtained, all Directors, Executives, Employees (to the extent that their margin loans are considered material) and Related parties of the above persons are prohibited directly or indirectly from entering into any margin loan facility against CWY securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg is not banned outright, unlike the derivative legs, but a facility secured on CWY shares would need the Chairman's prior written consent, and 'directly or indirectly' catches structures routed through related entities.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Each Director and Executive must also take all reasonable steps to ensure that their Related Parties do not deal in CWY securities without the Director or Executive obtaining approval ... Related party ... An immediate family member ... A company, trust or other entity that is controlled by the relevant Director or Executive; or The trustee of a trust or fiduciary arrangement of which the relevant Director or Executive is a beneficiary.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Placing the collar or the borrowing in a family trust or controlled company does not escape the derivatives ban, the approval requirement or the margin loan consent gateway.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and Employees must not deal in the same CWY securities within any three month period.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even if a hedge were permitted, entry, roll, partial unwind and physical settlement over the same parcel inside three months would breach the policy, so any structure must be long dated with settlement outside the window.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If an approval to trade is granted, it may be revoked by the Company at any time at its absolute discretion. If an approved share trade is conducted, it must occur within 3 business days from the date that the approval is provided and must not exceed the number of shares that were the subject of the request.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Pricing, documentation and execution of any approved transaction must complete within three business days and remain revocable until done, which is difficult for a negotiated OTC structure.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and Executives will not be given approval to deal in CWY securities under sections 3.2 or 3.3 of this policy where price sensitive, non-public information exists in relation to a matter, even though they may not be aware of it.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Approval can be withheld for information the executive does not hold, so a bank cannot treat a clean insider-trading representation as sufficient for the transaction to proceed.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where a request for approval is refused, that refusal must be kept confidential.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The executive may be unable to tell the bank why an agreed collar or unwind cannot proceed, so documentation needs a no-reasons termination right.

bespoke_clauses.clause: For the purpose of this policy, securities can be more than just shares. They also include options, rights and warrants or any instrument which has the feature of converting into an equity interest in the Company. They can include bonds and other financial products.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: OTC options over CWY shares are securities under the policy, with no venue limitation, so an off-market bank trade is treated the same as an on-market one.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The exceptional circumstances relief in section 3.2 is expressed only as approval to 'dispose of securities outside these Trading Windows'.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The hardship route can unlock a sale but cannot authorise a derivative or hedging transaction, so it offers no path to a collar.

CWY.summary: A funded collar is not possible under this policy as drafted. Section 3.4 bans Directors and Employees from trading in CWY derivatives, expressly extends that ban to all CWY securities, and names 'caps and collars' among the prohibited hedging products, so both the purchased put and the written call are prohibited outright, with no clearance, hardship or exemption route; the only textual counter-argument is that the explanatory sentence is framed around unvested performance rights, which would need express Board confirmation before a bank could rely on it. The loan leg is treated more leniently: a margin loan facility against CWY securities, directly or indirectly, is permitted with the prior written consent of the Chairman of the CWY Board, and no disclosure, price trigger or forced sale rules are imposed. Even if the derivative legs were permitted, execution would have to occur inside a Trading Window (six weeks after each results release and after the AGM), with prior written approval from the Chairman and Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee that lasts only three business days, is revocable at absolute discretion, and can be refused because of price sensitive information the executive does not know about. The three-month same-securities rule would also require a long-dated structure with no early unwind, and the whole regime extends to related parties, so routing the trade through a family trust or controlled company changes nothing.
