If permission to Trade is refused, the Restricted Person seeking the permission must keep that information confidential and not disclose it to anyone.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The executive cannot tell the bank why a collar entry, roll or unwind is blocked, so the documentation needs an unexplained termination or extension right.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Permission to Trade will generally not be granted if ... there is a risk the market will suspect the person seeking permission to trade had Inside Information, or there is a risk of reputational damage to Paladin.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even a fully compliant collar can be refused on optics alone, which makes any committed bank facility contingent on a discretionary judgement.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the periods commencing from the end of: a financial quarter up to the day after the release date of the quarter's results; a half-year ...; and a financial year ...
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: As a quarterly reporter Paladin closes the window four times a year, so execution and any unwind must be timed to the narrow post-release periods.

bespoke_clauses.clause: if you have entered into any margin lending arrangement, hedging or any other secured financing arrangement with the Board's approval, you must keep the Company Secretary informed of any change in circumstances that may be relevant to Paladin's continuous disclosure obligations
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Amendments, LVR breaches or enforcement steps under the facility must be reported to the Company Secretary on an ongoing basis and may become publicly disclosed.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A Restricted Person must not, and must take all reasonable steps to ensure that their Closely Connected Persons do not, Trade in securities without the Restricted Person obtaining permission to do so under this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Booking the collar or the loan in a spouse's name or a family trust does not avoid the approval, blackout or hedging restrictions.

bespoke_clauses.topic: no closed-period relief for anything but a sale
bespoke_clauses.clause: In exceptional circumstances, permission may be given by an Authorising Officer for a Restricted Person or their Closely Connected Person to Trade securities in Paladin (where such Trade only involves a proposed sale of securities) during a 'blackout' period.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Blackout relief is available only for outright sales, so a collar cannot be struck, rolled or hedged during a blackout even in hardship.

PDN.summary: A funded collar is possible for a Paladin Restricted Person, but only over a narrow slice of stock and only with Board sign-off. Section 6 expressly contemplates 'margin lending, hedging or any other secured financing arrangement in relation to Paladin's securities' with the Board's approval, given on disclosure of the material terms including the lender's right to sell unilaterally and the trigger events, which covers both the option legs and the loan secured on the collared shares. The decisive limitation is the collateral pool: hedging of securities granted under any Paladin employee incentive scheme is prohibited outright and expressly 'relates to both vested and unvested securities', and no arrangement may limit exposure to remuneration that is unvested or has vested but remains subject to a holding lock, so only shares acquired outside the incentive schemes can be collared and provenance must be evidenced. Execution also needs the Authorising Officer's written permission to Trade (Chairperson for directors, CEO and Company Secretary; Company Secretary for everyone else), which lasts five business days, may be withdrawn, may be refused without reasons or on reputational grounds alone, and cannot be given during the quarterly, half-year and full-year blackout periods except for an outright sale. Tenor must exceed 90 days to avoid the short-term trading ban, cash-settled structures risk the contracts-for-difference catch-all, and any later change to the facility must be reported to the Company Secretary for continuous disclosure purposes.

HVN.title: Share Trading Policy

tiers.name: Key Management Personnel
tiers.description: Those persons having authority and responsibility for planning, directing and controlling the activities of the Company, directly or indirectly, including each Director (executive or non-executive) and each Executive (a person who is an 'officer' as defined in the Corporations Act). Individually a 'Key Management Member'. This is the only tier subject to the Trading Window restriction, the hedging and short term trading restrictions, the Secured Financing Arrangement consent requirement and the notification duties in clause 5.

tiers.name: Restricted Person
tiers.description: A person who is subject to trading restrictions as a result of the application of the Policy. Used in the clearance, Prohibited Period and excluded trading provisions (clauses 6, 7 and 8); in practice it captures Key Management Members and anyone else the Policy restricts.

tiers.name: Employee
tiers.description: Includes each Director, Executive, employee of, or contractor to the Company and each controlled entity. Subject to the insider trading prohibitions in clause 3, but the clause 5 additional restrictions and the clause 4 Trading Window requirement are expressed to apply only to Key Management Members.

windows.start_anchor: one day after the announcement of half-yearly financial results of the Company
windows.end_anchor: thirty days later (or such other period as may be determined by the Chairman or a Committee)

windows.end_anchor: thirty days later (or such other period as may be determined by the Chairman or a Committee)

windows.end_anchor: thirty days later (or such other period as may be determined by the Chairman or a Committee)

HVN.ad_hoc_blackout_authority: No express power to impose an additional blackout: a Prohibited Period arises automatically as any period that is not a Trading Window, or (for a Key Management Member) any period when that person holds Price Sensitive Information. The Chairman or a Committee may set a Trading Window at a length other than thirty days, and the Chairman may declare a period to be a Trading Window, so the window can effectively be shortened. Nothing is said about confidentiality of a refusal.

rules.detail: Derivatives over Shares are not banned. 'Shares' includes options or rights over shares, and clause 5.8 prohibits a Key Management Member from trading in financial products issued or created over or in respect of Shares only during a Prohibited Period, with no venue limitation. Inside a Trading Window, and with no Price Sensitive Information, a Key Management Member may deal without prior consent; outside a Trading Window the Chairman's consent (clause 4.2), or written consent from the Chairman or CEO in exceptional circumstances (clauses 6.1 and 7.1), is required.
rules.evidence: Each Key Management Member is prohibited from trading during any Prohibited Period in financial products issued or created over or in respect of any Shares.

rules.detail: The clause 5 restrictions, including clause 5.8 on financial products over Shares, are headed 'Additional restrictions upon Key Management Personnel' and are expressed to bind only a Key Management Member. Employees below that level are constrained only by the insider trading prohibition in clause 3.
rules.evidence: ADDITIONAL RESTRICTIONS UPON KEY MANAGEMENT PERSONNEL

rules.detail: Flat ban on hedging Performance Rights, which are defined as Shares, or rights or options over Shares, granted under a shareholder-approved plan. No consent route is offered.
rules.evidence: Each Key Management Member must not hedge any Performance Rights.

rules.detail: Shares received on exercise or vesting of Performance Rights cannot be dealt or traded in at all while subject to any transfer restriction, which rules out pledging or hedging them until the restriction lifts.
rules.evidence: Each Key Management Member must not deal or trade in any Shares received upon exercise or vesting of any Performance Rights while those Shares are subject to any transfer restriction.

rules.detail: Hedging of Shares acquired on exercise of Performance Rights is contemplated and permitted, subject only to notifying the Chairman; there is no approval requirement and no deadline for the notice. The hedge is still a dealing in Shares, so it must occur in a Trading Window (or with consent) and not while the member holds Price Sensitive Information. Hedging of Shares acquired otherwise than under a plan is not addressed at all.
rules.evidence: Each Key Management Member must notify the Chairman if that person hedges any Shares acquired as a result of the exercise of any Performance Rights.

rules.detail: The Policy names the exact product: a 'capital protected loan with put and call options' is a Secured Financing Arrangement, permitted with the prior written consent of the Chairman or Chief Executive Officer. Sufficient details must be given to the Company for its ASX Listing Rule disclosure, and the Company may be obliged to announce the existence and terms.
rules.evidence: "Secured Financing Arrangement" means any financing arrangement pursuant to which Shares are provided as security, and includes (without limitation) a margin loan facility and a capital protected loan with put and call options.

rules.detail: Short selling is nowhere mentioned; the only indirect constraints are the Trading Window restriction and the short term trading restriction in clause 5.5.
Securities lending is not mentioned and there is no definition of dealing or trading that would sweep it in.

CFDs are not named. A CFD over Harvey Norman shares is a financial product created over or in respect of Shares, so clause 5.8 bars a Key Management Member from trading it during a Prohibited Period; outside a Prohibited Period it is unregulated except by the short term trading restriction in clause 5.5.
rules.evidence: Each Key Management Member is prohibited from trading during any Prohibited Period in financial products issued or created over or in respect of any Shares.

rules.detail: A margin loan facility is a named Secured Financing Arrangement, permitted with prior written consent of the Chairman or CEO. A forced sale to meet an unmet margin call or on default is a breach of the Policy unless approval to the arrangement was first obtained; anticipated margin calls or defaults must be disclosed immediately.
rules.evidence: A Key Management Member must obtain the written consent of the Chairman or Chief Executive Officer prior to entering into a Secured Financing Arrangement. A forced sale of Shares under a margin loan to satisfy an unmet margin call or default, or otherwise pursuant to a Secured Financing Arrangement will be a breach of this Policy unless the Key Management Member has first obtained approval to the Secured Financing Arrangement in accordance with this clause.

rules.detail: Providing Shares as security is regulated only through the Secured Financing Arrangement definition, which catches any financing arrangement under which Shares are provided as security and requires the Chairman's or CEO's prior written consent. A charge or pledge unconnected with a financing is not addressed and is not described as a dealing.
rules.evidence: "Secured Financing Arrangement" means any financing arrangement pursuant to which Shares are provided as security

rules.detail: Shares from Performance Rights that remain subject to a transfer restriction cannot be dealt or traded in at all, so they cannot be pledged as collateral while the restriction subsists, and consent under clause 5.6 cannot cure that.
rules.evidence: Each Key Management Member must not deal or trade in any Shares received upon exercise or vesting of any Performance Rights while those Shares are subject to any transfer restriction.

rules.detail: Any financing arrangement under which Shares are provided as security is permitted with the prior written consent of the Chairman or CEO. Once approved, a disposal by the secured lender exercising its rights is excluded trading under clause 8.1(f), so enforcement outside a Trading Window is not a breach. The member must supply sufficient details for the Company's continuous disclosure and Listing Rule obligations.
rules.evidence: A Key Management Member who has, or proposes to enter into a Secured Financing Arrangement must comply with this Policy. A Key Management Member must obtain the written consent of the Chairman or Chief Executive Officer prior to entering into a Secured Financing Arrangement.

rules.detail: Clause 5.6 binds only a Key Management Member; an employee or contractor below that level who pledges Shares is not covered by the consent or disclosure requirements.
rules.evidence: A Key Management Member who has, or proposes to enter into a Secured Financing Arrangement must comply with this Policy.

rules.detail: Short term trading in Shares is prohibited with one narrow cumulative exception: a specific request to the Chairman or CEO explaining a specific circumstance, the request must relate to exercised or vested Performance Rights, and prior written approval must be given. 'Short term' is not defined, so there is no bright-line holding period.
rules.evidence: Each Key Management Member must not engage in short term trading in Shares except where: (a) the Key Management Member makes a specific request to the Chairman or Chief Executive Officer, explaining a specific circumstance or requirement of that Key Management Member; (b) the request relates to exercised or vested Performance Rights; and (c) the Chairman or Chief Executive Officer gives prior written approval to the proposed short term trading.

clearance.approver: Chairman (notice and consent to deal outside a Trading Window, clause 4.2); Chairman or Chief Executive Officer (written consent to deal in a Prohibited Period in exceptional circumstances under clauses 6.1 and 7.1, to sell Performance Rights shares outside a Trading Window under clause 4.3(b)(ii), to enter into a Secured Financing Arrangement under clause 5.6, and to short term trade under clause 5.5)
clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary (notice when a Key Management Member buys or sells shares, so the ASX can be informed); Chairman (notice if the member hedges Shares acquired on exercise of Performance Rights)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: not stated
clearance.evidence: A Restricted Person may buy, sell, otherwise acquire, or deal in Shares during any Prohibited Period within twenty eight (28) days after the grant of written consent to that action from the Chairman or the Chief Executive Officer of the Company.  Written consent may be provided by email.

clearance.approver: Chairman or Chief Executive Officer
clearance.evidence: Any consent granted pursuant to clause 7.1 is automatically revoked if the Restricted Person receives Price Sensitive Information, without the need for the Chairman or Chief Executive Officer of the Company to provide written notice of the revocation.
Each Key Management Member may buy, sell, otherwise acquire, or deal in Shares only in a Trading Window, and never when that Key Management Member is in possession of Price Sensitive Information.

short_term.basis: 'short term trading' is used without definition; no holding period, window or LIFO basis is stated
carve_outs: a specific request to the Chairman or Chief Executive Officer explaining a specific circumstance or requirement, where the request relates to exercised or vested Performance Rights and prior written approval is given
short_term.evidence: Each Key Management Member must not engage in short term trading in Shares except where: ... (b) the request relates to exercised or vested Performance Rights; and (c) the Chairman or Chief Executive Officer gives prior written approval to the proposed short term trading.

exceptions.approver: Chairman or Chief Executive Officer (approval of the underlying arrangement under clause 5.6)
exceptions.evidence: a disposal of Shares that is the result of a secured lender exercising rights under a Secured Financing Arrangment where approval of the arrangement was obtained pursuant to clause 5.6;
transfers of Shares already held by a Restricted Person to a superannuation fund or other saving scheme in which the Restricted Person is a beneficiary;

an investment in, or trading in units of, a fund or other scheme (other than a scheme only investing in the Shares) where the assets of the fund or other scheme are invested at the discretion of a third party;

where a Restricted Person is a trustee, trading in the Shares by that trust provided the Restricted Person is not a beneficiary of the trust and any decision to trade during a Prohibited Period is taken by the other trustees or by the investment managers independently of the Restricted Person;
undertakings to accept, or the acceptance of, a takeover offer;

trading under an offer or invitation made to all or most of the security holders, such as, a rights issue, a security purchase plan, a dividend or distribution reinvestment plan and an equal access buy-back, where the plan that determines the timing and structure of the offer has been approved by the board of the Company

the exercise (but not the sale of Shares following exercise) of an option or a right under an employee incentive scheme, or the conversion of a convertible security, where the final date for the exercise of the option or right, or the conversion of the security, falls during a Prohibited Period

exceptions.approver: prior written clearance in accordance with the Policy
exceptions.evidence: trading under a non-discretionary trading plan for which prior written clearance has been provided in accordance with procedures set out in this Policy and where: (i) the Restricted Person did not enter into the plan or amend the plan during a Prohibited Period; (ii) the trading plan does not permit the Restricted Person to exercise any influence or discretion over how, when, or whether to trade;
a disposal of Shares compelled by court order.

exceptions.approver: Chairman or Chief Executive Officer
exceptions.evidence: A Restricted Person may buy, sell, otherwise acquire, or deal in Shares during any Prohibited Period upon receiving written consent pursuant to clause 7 in certain circumstances deemed exceptional by the Chairman or the Chief Executive Officer, including but not limited to circumstances where that person has a pressing financial commitment that cannot be satisfied otherwise than selling the relevant Shares.

financing.price_trigger_guidance: No loan-to-value ratio, buffer or price trigger level is prescribed. A Key Management Member who, acting reasonably, would believe there will be an unmet margin call, event of default or other circumstance that may result in a financier forcing an acquisition or disposal of Shares must immediately disclose full and complete details to the Chairman, Company Secretary or Chief Executive Officer so the Company can meet its continuous disclosure obligations.
financing_disclosure: Key Management Personnel: at inception, obtain the written consent of the Chairman or Chief Executive Officer before entering into a Secured Financing Arrangement.

Key Management Personnel: for any existing or proposed Secured Financing Arrangement, provide the Company sufficient details to allow it to fulfil its ASX Listing Rule and legal obligations, since the Company may be obliged to disclose the existence and terms to the market; no deadline stated.

Key Management Personnel: immediately on reasonably believing there will be an unmet margin call, event of default or other circumstance that may result in a financier forcing an acquisition or disposal of Shares, disclose full and complete details to the Chairman, Company Secretary or Chief Executive Officer.
Key Management Personnel: notify the Chairman if the member hedges any Shares acquired as a result of the exercise of Performance Rights; no deadline stated.
Key Management Personnel: notify the Company Secretary when the member buys or sells shares in the Company so the ASX can be informed; no deadline stated.

HVN.exemption_authority: The Chairman or the Chief Executive Officer may consent in writing to dealing during a Prohibited Period in circumstances they deem exceptional (including a pressing financial commitment), to a sale of Performance Rights shares outside a Trading Window, to short term trading relating to exercised or vested Performance Rights, and to a Secured Financing Arrangement. The Chairman alone consents to a Key Management Member dealing outside a Trading Window under clause 4.2, and the Chairman or a Committee may set the length of a Trading Window. No one may consent to hedging Performance Rights or to dealing in Shares still subject to a transfer restriction, and no consent overrides the insider trading prohibition.

bespoke_clauses.clause: "Secured Financing Arrangement" means any financing arrangement pursuant to which Shares are provided as security, and includes (without limitation) a margin loan facility and a capital protected loan with put and call options.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The funded collar is described almost exactly and is treated as permissible with consent rather than prohibited, which makes this one of the few ASX policies that expressly contemplates the product.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A Key Management Member must obtain the written consent of the Chairman or Chief Executive Officer prior to entering into a Secured Financing Arrangement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A single executive consent, not a full Board resolution, unlocks the loan and security leg, and it may be given by email.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A forced sale of Shares under a margin loan to satisfy an unmet margin call or default, or otherwise pursuant to a Secured Financing Arrangement will be a breach of this Policy unless the Key Management Member has first obtained approval to the Secured Financing Arrangement in accordance with this clause. ... a disposal of Shares that is the result of a secured lender exercising rights under a Secured Financing Arrangment where approval of the arrangement was obtained pursuant to clause 5.6 [is excluded trading].
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: With prior consent, the bank's enforcement or close-out sale is excluded trading and can occur even in a Prohibited Period; without consent the same sale puts the executive in breach, so obtaining consent before signing is critical to the bank's enforcement rights.

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedging plan shares permitted on notice
bespoke_clauses.clause: Each Key Management Member must notify the Chairman if that person hedges any Shares acquired as a result of the exercise of any Performance Rights.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Hedging vested plan shares is treated as a notifiable event rather than a prohibited one, which is the opposite of the standard ASX approach and leaves the option legs available over vested stock.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Each Key Management Member must not hedge any Performance Rights.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Because Performance Rights are defined to include Shares granted under a shareholder-approved plan, unexercised rights and plan-granted shares that have not been acquired 'as a result of the exercise' of a right sit on the wrong side of the line and cannot form part of the collared parcel.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Each Key Management Member must not deal or trade in any Shares received upon exercise or vesting of any Performance Rights while those Shares are subject to any transfer restriction.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Shares still inside a holding lock or disposal restriction cannot be pledged or hedged at all, so the collateral pool is limited to plan shares whose restriction period has ended plus shares acquired on market.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Company may be obliged to disclose the existence and terms of any Secured Financing Arrangement to the market pursuant to the ASX Listing Rules and the Key Management Member must provide the Company sufficient details of any existing or proposed Secured Financing Arrangement so as to allow the Company to fulfil its obligations.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank must expect the terms of the collar and loan, including LVR and trigger events, to be given to the Company and potentially announced, so confidentiality provisions in the facility need to accommodate that.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If a Key Management Member, acting reasonably, would believe that there will be an unmet margin call, event of default or other circumstance in relation to any Secured Financing Arrangement which may result in a financier exercising its rights to force an acquisition or disposal of Shares, the Key Management Member must immediately disclose to the Chairman, Company Secretary or Chief Executive Officer, full and complete details.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Approaching an LVR trigger creates an immediate internal reporting obligation before the bank acts, so margin call notices should be structured to give the executive time to comply.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A Restricted Person may buy, sell, otherwise acquire, or deal in Shares during any Prohibited Period within twenty eight (28) days after the grant of written consent ... Any consent granted pursuant to clause 7.1 is automatically revoked if the Restricted Person receives Price Sensitive Information, without the need for ... written notice of the revocation.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Twenty eight days is generous by ASX standards and comfortably accommodates negotiation and pricing of an OTC structure, but the consent evaporates automatically and silently if the executive receives price sensitive information before execution.

bespoke_clauses.topic: derivatives only blocked in Prohibited Periods
bespoke_clauses.clause: Each Key Management Member is prohibited from trading during any Prohibited Period in financial products issued or created over or in respect of any Shares.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The put and call legs are restricted by timing rather than by subject matter, so they can be struck inside a thirty day Trading Window without any express derivatives ban applying.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Policy contains no definition of associates, closely connected persons or related parties, and no clause extending the restrictions to spouses, dependants or controlled entities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no express look-through to family trusts or controlled companies, though the insider trading law and clause 3.2(f) on procuring family members or trusts still apply.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Each Key Management Member must not engage in short term trading in Shares except where ... the request relates to exercised or vested Performance Rights ... and the Chairman or Chief Executive Officer gives prior written approval.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: With no defined period, a short-dated or early-terminated collar carries characterisation risk, so a longer tenor and consent that expressly covers the unwind are prudent.

HVN.summary: A funded collar is possible under this policy and is, unusually, contemplated in terms: a 'capital protected loan with put and call options' is expressly included in the definition of a Secured Financing Arrangement, which a Key Management Member may enter into with the prior written consent of the Chairman or the Chief Executive Officer. Hedging is not banned for vested stock either; clause 5.3 requires only that the member notify the Chairman if they hedge Shares acquired on exercise of Performance Rights, in contrast to clause 5.1's ban on hedging the Performance Rights themselves and clause 5.2's ban on dealing in plan shares still subject to a transfer restriction, so the collateral must be limited to unrestricted shares. Execution must occur inside a thirty day Trading Window following the half-year or full-year results, the AGM, a disclosure document filing or a Chairman's declaration, or within twenty eight days of a written consent granted in circumstances deemed exceptional, and any consent lapses automatically if the member receives Price Sensitive Information. The bank's position on enforcement is strong: once the arrangement has been approved under clause 5.6, a disposal by the secured lender exercising its rights is excluded trading under clause 8.1(f), whereas an unapproved forced sale is a breach. The trade-offs are that the Company must be given sufficient details of the arrangement and may announce its existence and terms, that any looming margin call or default must be reported immediately to the Chairman, Company Secretary or CEO, and that 'short term trading' is undefined, so a long tenor with consent covering the unwind is advisable.

TLX.title: Securities Dealing Policy

tiers.name: Employees
tiers.description: The Group worldwide, its directors, officers, executive and senior management, and other employees. All of the substantive prohibitions (blackout periods, short-term dealing, short selling, hedging, margin lending and secured financing) apply to this tier without differentiation.

tiers.name: Partners
tiers.description: Telix's consultants, contractors, vendors, collaboration partners or advisors acting on behalf of Telix or the Group with access to Inside Information. Subject to the same substantive prohibitions as Employees.

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: Each Director; the Group Company Secretary; each member of the Telix Group Executive Team and key management team members and their respective direct reports; and any other Employee or Partner designated by the Group Company Secretary. A list is maintained by People & Culture with oversight by the Group Company Secretary. Subject to two additional quarterly blackout periods and, if not a Director, to prior notification and post-trade confirmation to the Group Company Secretary.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Directors of Telix, including the CEO. Uniquely, they and their Connected Persons must obtain prior approval to deal even during a Trading Window, and must send written confirmation with a broker trade statement to the Group Company Secretary after each trade.

tiers.name: Connected Persons
tiers.description: A person or entity connected to another person or entity in a way that allows for influence over dealings, including individuals with close family ties, business partners, associated companies or trusts, and any company or entity the Employee or Partner has an ability to control, including its directors and officers. The Employee or Partner must inform them of the Policy and communicate on their behalf in relation to approval requests.

definitions.hedging_definition: Hedging is a form of dealing and includes entering into transactions in financial products that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding Telix Securities.

windows.end_anchor: start of trading on the day following the release of the Full Year Results

windows.start_anchor: close of trading on the ASX on 30 June each year
windows.end_anchor: start of trading on the day following the release of the Half Year Results

windows.end_anchor: start of trading on the day following the release of the Q1 Business Update

windows.end_anchor: start of trading on the day following the release of the Q3 Business Update

windows.end_anchor: close of trading on the ASX on the next period end (31 December or 30 June, and additionally 31 March or 30 September for Restricted Persons), or the start of any special blackout period specified by the Board

TLX.ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may specify any other special blackout period from time to time, both for everyone and separately for Restricted Persons only. Special blackouts are effectively confidential: the existence of a special blackout period is itself listed as an example of Inside Information.

rules.detail: Unqualified ban on hedging Telix Securities by all Employees and Partners, with no vesting, tier or venue distinction and no approval or exceptional-circumstances route. The definition is effects-based, catching any transaction in financial products that operates to limit the economic risk of holding Telix Securities, which is precisely what a collar does.
rules.evidence: Employees and Partners must not engage in hedging of Telix Securities. Hedging is a form of dealing and includes entering into transactions in financial products that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding Telix Securities.

rules.detail: There is no express derivatives clause, but a purchased put and a written call over Telix shares are transactions in financial products that operate to limit economic risk, so both legs of a collar are prohibited hedging. A short derivative would separately breach the short selling ban.
rules.evidence: Hedging is a form of dealing and includes entering into transactions in financial products that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding Telix Securities.

rules.detail: Exchange traded options and warrants over Telix ordinary shares are expressly Telix Securities, so dealing in them is subject to the Blackout Periods and, for Directors and their Connected Persons, prior approval. Any such option that limits economic risk is nevertheless prohibited hedging under 4.6, which leaves almost no permitted use.
rules.evidence: The definition of a security is complex and includes not only ordinary shares but also options, performance share appreciation rights and rights over ordinary shares, as well as exchange traded options and warrants.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward, collar loan or similar structure is caught twice over: it limits the economic risk of holding Telix Securities (prohibited hedging under 4.6) and, where it is funded against the shares, it is a secured financing arrangement in respect of Telix Securities (prohibited under 4.7). Outright disposal in a Trading Window remains the only monetisation route.
rules.evidence: Employees and Partners must not obtain margin loans using Telix Securities (either solely or as part of a portfolio) as security for the loans, or enter into any other secured financing arrangements in respect of Telix Securities.

rules.detail: Flat ban, with a definition confined to selling financial products the person does not own with a view to repurchasing them later at a lower price.
rules.evidence: Employees and Partners must not engage in any short selling of Telix Securities. Short selling occurs when a person sells financial products they do not own with a view to repurchasing them later at a lower price.

rules.detail: Securities lending is not mentioned and there is no dealing definition that would sweep it in, though lending stock to support a short position would engage section 4.5.

CFDs are not named. A CFD over Telix Securities is a transaction in a financial product that operates to limit or invert economic exposure and so is prohibited hedging; a short CFD also engages the short selling ban and any in-and-out position engages the three-month short-term dealing ban.
rules.evidence: Employees and Partners must not engage in hedging of Telix Securities.

rules.detail: Absolute ban on margin loans using Telix Securities as security, whether the securities are pledged alone or as part of a wider portfolio. No approval, materiality threshold or grandfathering is provided.
rules.evidence: Employees and Partners must not obtain margin loans using Telix Securities (either solely or as part of a portfolio) as security for the loans

rules.detail: Granting security over Telix Securities to support a financing is prohibited as a secured financing arrangement. A charge, lien or pledge unconnected with any financing is not named and is not described as a dealing, but that is a narrow gap.
rules.evidence: or enter into any other secured financing arrangements in respect of Telix Securities.

rules.detail: Blanket ban on any secured financing arrangement in respect of Telix Securities, not limited to margin loans, with no tier, security-state or approval carve-out. The exemptions in section 5 are confined to plan participation, exceptional-circumstances disposals and the listed excluded dealings, none of which reaches a financing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Employees and Partners must not engage in hedging of Telix Securities. Hedging is a form of dealing and includes entering into transactions in financial products that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding Telix Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The test is economic effect rather than instrument type or venue, so an OTC put and call with a bank over vested shares is squarely prohibited and cannot be re-engineered around.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Employees and Partners must not obtain margin loans using Telix Securities (either solely or as part of a portfolio) as security for the loans, or enter into any other secured financing arrangements in respect of Telix Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar is separately and independently prohibited, so even if the hedge could be justified there is no route to the borrowing.

bespoke_clauses.topic: no exemption authority for the bans
bespoke_clauses.clause: The exemptions in section 5 are limited to plan participation, disposals in exceptional circumstances, and a closed list of excluded dealings; sections 4.5, 4.6 and 4.7 have no approval or exceptional-circumstances carve-out.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no person or committee that can waive the hedging or secured financing prohibitions, so a bank cannot cure the problem with a company consent letter.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where any approval is required for a dealing under this Policy under section 6.1, approval will not be granted where the dealing would not satisfy the Front Page Test. ... How would it look if the transaction were reported on the front page of the newspaper?
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An optics-based veto sits over every approval, so even an otherwise compliant transaction can be blocked on perception grounds alone.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any other special blackout period that the Board specifies from time to time. ... Some examples which may constitute Inside Information include ... (l) the existence of a special blackout period.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An undisclosed Board-imposed blackout can block execution or unwind at any time and the executive may not be able to explain the delay to the bank.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If approval to deal in Telix Securities is granted, the dealing must be conducted within three business days of the approval. ... it may be withdrawn at any time prior to the order for dealing being lodged or otherwise authorised.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any permitted dealing must be documented, priced and executed inside three business days and remains revocable until lodged, which is unworkable for a negotiated bilateral structure.

bespoke_clauses.topic: directors need approval even in a window
bespoke_clauses.clause: Prior approval to deal in Telix Securities: (a) by Directors (including the CEO) and their Connected Persons during a Trading Window ... must be sought.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Directors have no self-executing dealing right at all, so every step of any structure, including a permitted outright sale, needs the Chair's sign-off.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Connected Person is a person or entity that is connected to another person or entity in a way that allows for influence over dealings, including ... individuals with close family ties, business partners, and associated companies or trusts; a company or any other entity which the Employee or Partner has an ability to control, including its directors and officers.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Booking the collar or the loan through a family trust, controlled company or business partner does not escape the hedging and secured financing bans.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Subsequent dealings with Telix Securities issued on exercise or conversion of any Telix Share Plan Derivative are always subject to this Policy, including section 4.1.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Vesting confers no freedom: shares issued out of the plans remain fully subject to the hedging and financing prohibitions.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Prompt notification to the Group Company Secretary is essential to assist Telix in complying with its disclosure obligations under the Corporations Act, the U.S. Securities Exchange Act, the Listing Rules, the U.S. federal securities laws and related compliance policies.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any transaction would also engage Nasdaq and SEC insider reporting and, for a pledge or hedge by an officer or director, US disclosure regimes on top of the ASX rules.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Employees or Partners who fail to adhere to the requirements of this policy may face disciplinary action, including suspension or termination of employment, forfeiture of securities issued under any equity incentive plan of the Group, and/or exclusion from participating in any equity incentive plan of the Group.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Breach can extinguish the very shares a bank is relying on as collateral, which is a direct credit risk to a secured lender.

bespoke_clauses.topic: OTC derivatives not named in the securities definition
bespoke_clauses.clause: Telix Securities means shares, American Depositary Shares representing shares, and other instruments considered to be a security for the purposes of the Corporations Act or Listing Rules ... as well as exchange traded options and warrants.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The securities definition names only exchange traded options, but the hedging prohibition is drafted by economic effect rather than by reference to Telix Securities, so the venue gap gives no opening for an OTC structure.

TLX.summary: A funded collar is not possible under this policy, and both legs fail independently. Section 4.6 prohibits all Employees and Partners from hedging Telix Securities, defined by economic effect as entering into transactions in financial products that operate to limit the economic risk of holding Telix Securities, which captures a purchased put and a written call over vested shares regardless of venue, tier or how long ago the shares vested. Section 4.7 separately bans margin loans secured on Telix Securities and any other secured financing arrangement in respect of them, so the loan leg is prohibited as well. Neither prohibition has an approval, hardship or exceptional-circumstances route: the section 5 exemptions are confined to plan participation, disposals in exceptional circumstances and a closed list of excluded dealings, and no officer can waive sections 4.5 to 4.7. Even a permitted outright sale is tightly controlled, requiring the Chair's prior approval for Directors even inside a Trading Window, execution within three business days, satisfaction of the Front Page Test, and compliance with the three-month short-term dealing ban, with breach exposing the executive to forfeiture of plan securities.

rules.detail: Effects-based ban with no vesting, tier, venue or approval qualification. It reaches both Securities held and entitlements to acquire Securities such as options or share rights, and the words 'or similar arrangements' close off economically equivalent structures. Notably, the excluded dealings in paragraph 12.1 relieve only paragraphs 5.1, 6.1, 9.1(b), 9.1(c) and section 7, not paragraph 9.2, so there is no exemption at all.

rules.detail: There is no free-standing derivatives clause. A charge unconnected with any borrowing is genuinely unaddressed.

NHC.summary: A funded collar is not possible for any New Hope director or executive. Paragraph 9.2(a) prohibits Restricted Personnel and their Associates from entering into transactions in financial products that operate to limit the economic risk of Securities or entitlements to acquire Securities, including hedging or similar arrangements, which captures both the purchased put and the written call irrespective of venue or vesting state, and paragraph 9.2(b) separately prohibits stock lending, margin lending or similar arrangements in relation to Securities, which covers the loan secured on the collared shares. Every director and all key management personnel are Restricted Personnel, their Associates (spouse, dependants, controlled entities) are themselves defined as Restricted Personnel, and the excluded dealings in paragraph 12.1 are drafted to relieve only paragraphs 5.1, 6.1, 9.1(b), 9.1(c) and section 7, so paragraph 9.2 has no exception and no approver can waive it. Even an outright sale is tightly controlled: pre-approval is required for every dealing, approval lasts two business days, may be refused or revoked at any time without reasons, must be kept confidential if refused, and will not be granted where the dealing fails the Front Page Test. Breach can result in compulsory divestment or forfeiture of the securities as well as summary dismissal.

tiers.name: SEEK Personnel

Subject only to the insider trading prohibition in section 2; the blackout, clearance, hedging, margin loan, short selling and short-term dealing restrictions do not apply to them unless they are also Designated Persons.

rules.detail: Derivatives are not separately regulated. 'Securities' expressly includes any derivatives including options in respect of shares, with no venue limitation, so writing a call or buying a put over SEEK shares with a bank is dealing in SEEK Securities: it needs prior written clearance from the relevant approver, must occur within 5 Trading Days of clearance, is barred in Blackout Periods absent exceptional circumstances, and is barred while holding Inside Information.

rules.detail: SEEK Personnel who are not Designated Persons face no clearance or blackout restriction; only the insider trading prohibition applies, so derivatives over SEEK Securities are unrestricted provided they hold no Inside Information.
rules.evidence: In addition to the Insider Trading prohibitions set out in this Policy which apply to all SEEK Personnel, additional restrictions on dealing in SEEK Securities apply to Designated Persons who are specified in the Annexure to this Policy (and their Associates).

rules.detail: Absolute ban, with no clearance route, on any arrangement limiting the economic risk of an unvested share, option or other Security granted or awarded under a SEEK employee incentive scheme.
rules.evidence: SEEK prohibits Designated Persons from entering into arrangements which have the effect of limiting the economic risk related to an unvested share, option or other Security granted or awarded under a SEEK employee incentive scheme

rules.detail: The ban expressly extends to vested plan securities that remain subject to disposal restrictions, so shares vested but still in a holding lock or restriction period cannot be collared.
rules.evidence: (or a vested share, option or other Security granted, awarded or acquired under a SEEK employee incentive scheme that is still subject to disposal restrictions)

rules.detail: The hedging ban is confined to unvested plan securities and vested plan securities still subject to disposal restrictions. Hedging vested, unrestricted shares (whether plan-derived or bought on market) is not prohibited, but the hedge is itself dealing in Securities and so requires prior written clearance, execution within 5 Trading Days, and an open period.
rules.evidence: SEEK prohibits Designated Persons from entering into arrangements which have the effect of limiting the economic risk related to an unvested share, option or other Security granted or awarded under a SEEK employee incentive scheme

rules.detail: Monetisation, prepaid forwards and collar-plus-loan structures are not named. Each leg is a dealing in SEEK Securities (or in derivatives over them), and for Directors and ELT any security taken over the shares also engages section 5(A). Clearance from the relevant approver is therefore required for entry, and again for any unwind or physical settlement.
rules.evidence: Dealing in SEEK Securities by Designated Persons outside the Blackout Periods set out in section 3(A) above, is only permitted: (a) if the Designated Person is not, at the time of the proposed dealing, in possession of any Inside Information

rules.detail: Outright ban at any time, with no clearance route. A collar over shares the executive actually owns is covered rather than naked, but any leg that leaves the person net short of shares they do not hold would breach this.
rules.evidence: engage in short selling SEEK Securities at any time.

rules.detail: Securities lending is not named anywhere in the Policy and is not brought in by any definition. A lend that transfers title would, however, be a change in beneficial control and so a dealing requiring clearance.

CFDs are not named. A CFD over SEEK shares is a derivative in respect of shares and so a Security, making it a dealing that needs clearance; a short CFD would breach the absolute short selling ban and a CFD closed out within three months would engage the short-term dealing restriction.
rules.evidence: any derivatives including but not limited to options in respect of any of (a) to (d) above

rules.detail: Margin loans over SEEK Securities are not banned but require prior written clearance from the Chairman (from the ARMC Chairman for an arrangement proposed by the Chairman). Once cleared, the Disclosure Committee in consultation with the Chairman reviews the terms for materiality and SEEK may disclose the loan, its trigger points and the financier's unilateral sale rights to the market.
rules.evidence: Directors and members of the ELT must not enter into a margin loan or other security arrangement in respect of SEEK Securities except with prior written clearance from the Chairman, or in the case of an arrangement proposed to be entered into by the Chairman, the ARMC Chairman.

rules.tier: Members of the Executive Leadership Team
rules.detail: Same clearance requirement as Directors: prior written clearance from the Chairman. For ELT members other than the CEO the Disclosure Committee reviews materiality in consultation with the CEO; for the CEO, in consultation with the Chairman.
rules.evidence: Directors and members of the ELT must not enter into a margin loan or other security arrangement in respect of SEEK Securities except with prior written clearance from the Chairman

rules.detail: Section 5(A) is confined to Directors and ELT members. Designated Persons below that level (plan participants, finance and legal staff) are not subject to any margin loan restriction, although the transfer of shares into or out of a margin facility is not addressed as a dealing.

Granting security over SEEK Securities is caught by the words 'or other security arrangement in respect of SEEK Securities' and is permitted with prior written clearance from the Chairman, followed by a Disclosure Committee materiality review. Encumbrance is not itself defined as a dealing, so the blackout periods do not on their face bite on the grant of security, only the clearance requirement in 5(A).
rules.evidence: must not enter into a margin loan or other security arrangement in respect of SEEK Securities except with prior written clearance from the Chairman

rules.tier: Members of the Executive Leadership Team
rules.detail: Identical to Directors: any security arrangement over SEEK Securities requires prior written clearance from the Chairman and is then reviewed for continuous disclosure materiality by the Disclosure Committee in consultation with the CEO.
rules.evidence: Directors and members of the ELT must not enter into a margin loan or other security arrangement in respect of SEEK Securities except with prior written clearance from the Chairman

rules.detail: There is no blanket ban on secured financing. A loan secured on SEEK shares is an 'other security arrangement in respect of SEEK Securities' and is permitted with prior written clearance from the Chairman (ARMC Chairman for the Chairman), subject to materiality review and possible market disclosure of the terms.
rules.evidence: Where it is determined that the relevant margin loan or other security arrangement is material, SEEK will make a disclosure to the market in accordance with SEEK's Continuous Disclosure Policy.

rules.tier: Members of the Executive Leadership Team
rules.detail: Same regime as Directors. The Policy does not distinguish between unvested and vested shares for this purpose, but plan securities that are unvested or still subject to disposal restrictions would usually be unavailable as collateral in fact and any accompanying hedge over them is prohibited by 5(B).
rules.evidence: Directors and members of the ELT must not enter into a margin loan or other security arrangement in respect of SEEK Securities except with prior written clearance from the Chairman

rules.detail: Buying and selling within a three month period is restricted but not banned: it may be done with prior written clearance obtained under the Policy. A collar entered and unwound inside three months, or a short-dated collar settled physically, could be treated as short-term dealing and so needs express clearance.
rules.evidence: A Designated Person must not: (a) buy and sell SEEK Securities on a short term basis (that is, within a three month period) except with prior written clearance obtained in accordance with this Policy

SEK.exemption_authority: Dealing in a Blackout Period may be cleared by the CEO (for ELT and Management), the Chairman (for the CEO and Directors) or the ARMC Chairman (for the Chairman) where there are exceptional circumstances such as severe financial hardship, a court order or other legal or regulatory requirement, and the person holds no Inside Information. Section 5(A) margin loan and security arrangement clearance sits with the Chairman or, for the Chairman, the ARMC Chairman. There is no exemption power over the section 5(B) hedging ban or the short selling ban.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and members of the ELT must not enter into a margin loan or other security arrangement in respect of SEEK Securities except with prior written clearance from the Chairman, or in the case of an arrangement proposed to be entered into by the Chairman, the ARMC Chairman.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike most ASX policies this is a consent regime rather than a ban, so the secured loan leg of a funded collar is available to Directors and ELT if the Chairman approves, and is entirely unrestricted for Designated Persons below ELT.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The following types of dealings are excluded from the operation of section 3 of this Policy and may be undertaken by Designated Persons at any time without prior notification or approval ... (lender disposal) a disposal of SEEK Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement or close-out sale of the collared shares is expressly outside the blackout and clearance regime, so lender enforcement during a Blackout Period is not a breach.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where it is determined that the relevant margin loan or other security arrangement is material, SEEK will make a disclosure to the market ... Such disclosure will address the existence of the margin loan and set out relevant terms such as the trigger points or the right of the financier to sell unilaterally.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A material funded collar loan for a Director or ELT member will be publicly disclosed including its trigger levels and the bank's unilateral sale rights, so confidentiality cannot be assumed.

bespoke_clauses.clause: arrangements which have the effect of limiting the economic risk related to an unvested share, option or other Security granted or awarded under a SEEK employee incentive scheme (or a vested share, option or other Security granted, awarded or acquired under a SEEK employee incentive scheme that is still subject to disposal restrictions).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The collar must be sized only to shares that have vested and are free of disposal restrictions; unvested and still-restricted plan shares cannot be included in the collar pool at all.

bespoke_clauses.clause: SEEK may grant or refuse clearance to trade in its absolute discretion. A clearance to trade can also be withdrawn by SEEK if new information comes to light or there is a change in circumstances.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Clearance for the collar can be revoked between approval and execution, so the bank should not treat clearance as a firm condition precedent until the trade is actually struck.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any dealing in SEEK Securities by a Designated Person in respect of which clearance is given under this section 3 must occur within 5 Trading Days of receipt of the clearance.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Pricing, documentation and execution of both derivative legs and the loan drawdown must all be completed inside five trading days of clearance, or clearance must be sought again.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A Designated Person must not: (a) buy and sell SEEK Securities on a short term basis (that is, within a three month period) except with prior written clearance obtained in accordance with this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar unwound or rolled within three months is not banned outright but requires separate express clearance, so short-tenor or frequently rolled structures carry extra approval risk.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Associate includes ... a trustee where the beneficiaries of the relevant trust include the Designated Person or his or her spouse, partner, child or step-child; and any other persons over whom a Designated Person ... has, or may be expected to have, investment control or influence.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Structuring the collar through a family trust or controlled company does not avoid the blackout and clearance regime, and the Designated Person must procure the associate's compliance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: additional restrictions on dealing in SEEK Securities apply to Designated Persons who are specified in the Annexure to this Policy (and their Associates).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: All equity plan participants are Designated Persons under the Annexure, so any executive holding vested plan shares will be inside the restricted population.

SEK.summary: A funded collar is possible under this policy, which is unusually permissive on the financing leg. Both derivative legs are dealings in SEEK Securities (Securities expressly includes derivatives and options with no venue limit), so a Director needs prior written clearance from the Chairman and an ELT member from the CEO, the trade must be executed within 5 Trading Days of clearance, outside the 1 December, 1 June and pre-AGM Blackout Periods and any additional period notified by the Company Secretary, and while holding no Inside Information. The secured loan leg is not banned: section 5(A) permits a margin loan or other security arrangement over SEEK Securities for Directors and ELT with prior written clearance from the Chairman (ARMC Chairman for the Chairman), after which the Disclosure Committee assesses materiality and SEEK may publicly disclose the arrangement including its trigger points and the financier's unilateral sale rights. The collar must cover only shares that have vested and are free of disposal restrictions, because section 5(B) bans any arrangement limiting the economic risk of unvested plan securities or vested plan securities still subject to disposal restrictions, and no leg may leave the executive short selling. Helpfully, a disposal resulting from a secured lender exercising its rights is an excluded dealing that may occur at any time without approval, so the bank's enforcement is not a breach even in a Blackout Period, but a collar entered and closed within three months needs additional express clearance and clearance can be withdrawn before execution.

NWL.title: Netwealth Trading Policy (previously known as the Securities Trading Policy)
NWL.date_approved: 3 June 2021 (Netwealth Group Limited); pending approval by Netwealth Investments Limited, Netwealth Superannuation Services Pty Ltd and Netwealth Group Services Pty Ltd

tiers.name: Employees
tiers.description: Any person employed by, contracted by or appointed by the Group for the provision of services to the Company or a related entity, and any director of the Group or its subsidiaries. All substantive rules (blackouts, prior approval for every trade, short-term trading ban, margin lending approval, hedging rules, trading register, annual declaration) apply to this whole population without differentiation; only the identity of the approver changes by seniority.

tiers.name: Senior Executives and Nominated Employees
tiers.description: Senior Executives and Nominated Employees, distinguished only for approval: the Joint Managing Directors must be informed and must approve before a trade, and they also decide exceptional-circumstances applications for this group.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Directors of the Group other than the Chair of the Board. Distinguished only for approval: the Chair of the Board must be informed and must approve before a trade, and decides their exceptional-circumstances applications. Non-executive directors may also use a pre-approved non-discretionary trading plan.

tiers.name: Chair of the Board
tiers.description: The Chair of the Board, whose trades and exceptional-circumstances applications must be approved by the Chair of the Group's Compliance and Risk Management Committee.

tiers.name: Connected Persons
tiers.description: Family members who may be expected to influence or be influenced by the Employee (spouse, partner, children, partner's children, dependants); trustees of trusts or fiduciary arrangements including SMSFs under which the Employee, their spouse or partner or dependent children is or may be a beneficiary; companies in which the Employee holds a majority of shares or otherwise has control; and any entity in which the Employee is a director, secretary or executive officer or which they can control. Employees must take steps to ensure their Connected Persons do not breach the Policy.

definitions.hedging_definition: Hedging includes entering into transactions in Financial Products that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding Company securities.

NWL.ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may specify any other blackout period from time to time. The Company Secretary provides an email confirming when Netwealth commences 'blackout', and employees must check that the open-window notification from the Company Secretary has been received and not removed before trading. Separately, the Company Secretary or delegate may direct a person not to trade or impose conditions in their discretion and is not obliged to give reasons.

rules.detail: Derivatives and options are Financial Products, and section 5.4(d) expressly treats a hedge transaction in a Financial Product as a dealing in Company securities for the purposes of the Policy. A purchased put and written call over Netwealth shares therefore require prior approval through trading@netwealth.com.au from the relevant approver, must be executed within five business days of approval, may not be entered during a blackout period, and must be confirmed to the trading mailbox after execution. No venue distinction is drawn, so an OTC structure with a bank is treated the same as an exchange-traded option.
rules.evidence: Financial Product Includes: Securities; Derivatives; Options; ... Employees and their Connected Persons are permitted to hedge their vested and unrestricted Company securities provided that the hedge transaction is treated as a dealing in Company securities for the purposes of this Policy

rules.detail: Absolute ban with no approval route on hedging securities acquired under a Company employee share plan before vesting.
rules.evidence: Company securities acquired under an Employee share plan operated by the Company must never be hedged prior to vesting;

rules.detail: Securities subject to a holding lock or a dealing restriction under an employee share plan may never be hedged, even after vesting. No approval route and no time limit.
rules.evidence: Company securities that are subject to a holding lock or restriction on dealing under the terms of an Employee share plan operated by the Company must never be hedged;

rules.detail: Hedging vested and unrestricted Company securities is expressly permitted, on condition that the hedge is treated as a dealing and so goes through the section 4 approval and post-trade notification machinery: no entry, renewal, alteration or close-out while in possession of Inside Information, prior approval from the relevant approver, execution within five business days, no dealing in a blackout period absent exceptional circumstances, and prompt confirmation to the trading mailbox.
rules.evidence: Employees and their Connected Persons are permitted to hedge their vested and unrestricted Company securities provided that the hedge transaction is treated as a dealing in Company securities for the purposes of this Policy, and the relevant approvals and notifications required under section 4 are made on that basis.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named as such. A prepaid forward or collar-plus-loan is a transaction in Financial Products limiting the economic risk of holding Company securities and so is a hedge, permitted over vested and unrestricted shares with prior approval. Forward contracts are, however, given as an example of a prohibited short-term dealing, so a short-dated forward or prepaid forward is likely to be caught by section 5.2 and would need NWL Board authorisation.
rules.evidence: Short-term trading includes the buying and selling securities on market within a 3 month period, and entering into other short-term dealings (for example, forward contracts).

rules.detail: Short selling is not mentioned anywhere in the Policy and is not caught by any definition. A naked short would still need approval as a dealing in a Financial Product and would be tested against the Front Page Test and the short-term trading ban.

Securities lending is not named and no definition sweeps it in. A lend that changed the beneficial interest would be a dealing requiring approval, since only dealings with no material change to the beneficial interest are excluded.

CFDs are not named. A CFD over Netwealth securities is a derivative and so a Financial Product, and if it limits the economic risk of a holding it is also a hedge; either way it requires prior approval. In practice a CFD position opened and closed inside three months would breach the short-term trading ban unless the NWL Board authorises it.
rules.evidence: Financial Product Includes: Securities; Derivatives; Options;

rules.detail: Margin lending is not banned. Entering into a margin lending arrangement over Netwealth securities, transferring Netwealth securities into an existing margin loan account, and selling Netwealth securities to satisfy a margin call are each dealings requiring approval under the section 4 procedure. The approver may attach conditions, expressly including conditions on the circumstances in which the securities may be sold to satisfy a margin call.
rules.evidence: Employees and their Connected Persons must obtain approval in accordance with the procedure set out within this Policy for any proposed dealing in the Netwealth's securities in connection with a margin lending arrangement.

rules.detail: Granting security is addressed only through the margin lending lens: entering into a margin lending arrangement in respect of Netwealth securities, and transferring securities into a margin loan account, are expressly dealings requiring approval. Granting a charge or pledge outside a margin lending arrangement is not separately named, but the substance over form clause and the wording 'in connection with a margin lending arrangement' would be read to capture a bank facility secured on the shares.
rules.evidence: Examples of such dealings include: 1) entering into a margin lending arrangement in respect of the Netwealth's securities; 2) transferring securities in Netwealth into an existing margin loan account;

rules.detail: There is no prohibition on secured financing. The only express regime is section 5.3 on margin lending arrangements, which is an approval regime, and section 6(e) recognises secured lenders over Netwealth securities by excluding their enforcement sales from the Policy. A loan from a bank secured on the collared shares is not named but would be treated on a substance over form basis as a dealing in connection with a lending arrangement requiring approval on the same terms.
rules.evidence: a disposal of securities of Netwealth that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.

rules.detail: Buying and selling (or selling and buying) within three months is prohibited, measured from the last purchase or last sale, as is entering into other short-term dealings, with forward contracts given as the example. Employees and Connected Persons are assessed separately unless securities have been transferred between them. The NWL Board has discretion to authorise a short-term trade on reasonable grounds. Section 5.2 does not apply to the section 6 excluded dealings.
rules.evidence: Employees and their Connected Persons must not deal in Netwealth's securities on a short-term trading basis. Short-term trading includes the buying and selling securities on market within a 3 month period, and entering into other short-term dealings (for example, forward contracts).

All Employees: annually, via the Netwealth Employee Annual Trading Declaration, each person must confirm 'I do not have a margin loan associated with my NWL securities and / or have not hedged my NWL Securities'.

Directors and Key Management Personnel: Finance maintains the register of Directors' and Key Management Personnel's interests and publishes appropriate statements to the market where required; no deadline stated in the Policy.
