NWL.exemption_authority: Trading in a blackout period may be approved on exceptional-circumstances grounds by either Joint Managing Director (Senior Executives, Nominated Employees), the Chair of the Board (directors) or the Chair of the Compliance and Risk Management Committee (Chair of the Board), on written application to trading@netwealth.com.au with sufficient evidence that the trade is the most reasonable course of action available; approval lasts five business days. The NWL Board has a separate discretion to authorise a short-term trade on reasonable grounds. There is no exemption power over the bans on hedging unvested or holding-locked plan securities.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Employees and their Connected Persons are permitted to hedge their vested and unrestricted Company securities provided that the hedge transaction is treated as a dealing in Company securities for the purposes of this Policy, and the relevant approvals and notifications required under section 4 are made on that basis.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is an express positive permission for the derivative legs of a collar over vested unrestricted shares, rather than the more common outright hedging ban, so the structure has a clear policy pathway.

bespoke_clauses.clause: any Employee or their Connected Persons must not enter into, renew, alter or close out a hedge transaction when they are in possession of Inside Information;
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Rolls, amendments, resets and unwinds of the collar are each separately regulated events, so the bank must build in approval and inside-information checkpoints at every lifecycle step, not just at inception.

bespoke_clauses.topic: margin lending is an approval regime
bespoke_clauses.clause: Employees and their Connected Persons must obtain approval ... for any proposed dealing in the Netwealth's securities in connection with a margin lending arrangement. Examples of such dealings include: entering into a margin lending arrangement in respect of the Netwealth's securities; transferring securities in Netwealth into an existing margin loan account; and selling securities in Netwealth to satisfy a call pursuant to a margin loan.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The secured loan leg is permitted with approval rather than banned, but each of inception, the transfer of the collared shares into the lender's account, and any self-help sale to meet a call is a separate dealing needing its own approval.

bespoke_clauses.topic: conditional approval on margin call sales
bespoke_clauses.clause: The relevant approver may, at its discretion, make any approval granted in accordance with this Policy conditional upon such terms and conditions as Netwealth sees fit (for example, regarding the circumstances in which Netwealth's securities may be sold to satisfy a margin call).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Netwealth can impose conditions that constrain the bank's enforcement rights, so the facility documentation should anticipate company-imposed limits on when collateral may be sold.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Sections 4.1, 4.3 and 5.2 of this Policy do not apply to ... a disposal of securities of Netwealth that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Lender enforcement is outside the blackout, prior-approval and short-term trading rules, so the bank can realise the collateral even in a blackout period without putting the executive in breach.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Short-term trading includes the buying and selling securities on market within a 3 month period, and entering into other short-term dealings (for example, forward contracts).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A prepaid forward or a short-dated collar risks being characterised as a prohibited short-term dealing, so tenor should comfortably exceed three months or NWL Board authorisation should be obtained.

bespoke_clauses.topic: 14 day cooling off in the annual declaration
bespoke_clauses.clause: Appendix A, question 8: 'I have not traded or transferred NWL securities within 14 days of purchasing or selling one or more NWL securities.'
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The annual declaration asserts a 14-day gap between trades that has no counterpart in the body of the Policy, so paired legs or a same-window loan drawdown and share transfer may need to be spaced or explained.

bespoke_clauses.clause: We will take a substance over form approach and will have regard to the intent and spirit of this Policy when applying and enforcing it.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar or loan structured to sit outside the literal wording of the margin lending and hedging sections will still be assessed on its economic substance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where any approval is required for a trading under this Policy, approval will not be granted where the trading would not satisfy the Front Page Test.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Approval for the collar can be refused on pure reputational grounds regardless of technical compliance, and the approver need give no reasons.

bespoke_clauses.topic: no reasons for direction or condition
bespoke_clauses.clause: The Company Secretary (or their delegate) may direct the person who is proposing to trade in the Company's securities not to trade, or impose conditions on the trading in their discretion, and is not obliged to provide reasons for any direction or condition.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Execution of the collar can be blocked or conditioned at short notice without explanation, so the bank should treat approval as revocable until the trade is struck.

bespoke_clauses.clause: All Employees must keep an up to date register containing information relating to all trading of Financial Products (Trading Register). ... I confirm I do not have a margin loan associated with my NWL securities and / or have not hedged my NWL Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The existence of the collar and any associated loan must be recorded and annually declared, so it cannot be kept confidential from the company.

NWL.summary: A funded collar is possible under this policy, which is one of the more permissive on the ASX. Section 5.4(d) expressly permits Employees and their Connected Persons to hedge vested and unrestricted Company securities, provided the hedge is treated as a dealing: prior approval through trading@netwealth.com.au from the Joint Managing Directors (Senior Executives and Nominated Employees), the Chair of the Board (directors) or the Chair of the Compliance and Risk Management Committee (the Chair), execution within five business days, no dealing in the 30 June or 31 December blackout periods or any Board-specified period, no Inside Information at entry, renewal, alteration or close-out, and prompt post-trade confirmation. The loan leg is likewise an approval regime rather than a ban: section 5.3 requires approval for entering a margin lending arrangement over Netwealth securities, transferring shares into the lender's account and selling shares to meet a call, and the approver may impose conditions on when the collateral may be sold, while section 6(e) puts a secured lender's enforcement sale outside the blackout, approval and short-term trading rules entirely. The collar must be sized only to vested, unrestricted shares, because plan securities may never be hedged before vesting or while subject to a holding lock. The main traps are tenor and disclosure: forward contracts are given as an example of prohibited short-term dealing so the structure should run well beyond three months or be authorised by the NWL Board, and the arrangement must be entered in the personal Trading Register and disclosed in the annual declaration, with directors' and KMP interests published to the market where required.

VEA.title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Company Personnel
tiers.description: All Directors and Senior Management, employees of Viva Energy (permanent, fixed-term, casual or temporary) and Affected Parties. Subject only to the insider trading prohibition in section 3; the trading window, clearance, protection arrangement, margin lending and speculative trading restrictions bite only on Designated Persons.

tiers.name: Designated Persons
tiers.description: All Directors and Senior Management and any other person designated as a Designated Person by the Board and/or Company Secretary from time to time. Bears every additional restriction: dealing only in a Trading Window and only with clearance, the section 5.1 speculative trading ban, the section 5.2 protection arrangements regime and the section 5.3 margin lending prohibition, and must procure compliance by their Affected Parties.

tiers.name: Directors and Senior Management
tiers.description: Each director of the Company, the Company Secretary, the Chief Executive Officer, the Chief Financial Officer and Key Management Personnel of Viva Energy. Distinguished only for clearance: the chair of the Board is their Authorising Officer. Directors additionally have a three business day notification duty to the Company Secretary for ASX notifiable interest changes.

tiers.name: Chair of the Board
tiers.description: The chair of the Board, whose Authorising Officer and exceptional-circumstances Clearance Officer is the chair of the Audit and Risk Committee.

tiers.name: Affected Parties
tiers.description: Immediate family members living with a Designated Person and other immediate family members whose investment decisions the Designated Person controls; any company, trust, managed superannuation fund or other entity controlled by the Designated Person or such a family member; and, for directors only, any person or entity whose dealing would require the director's disclosure to ASX, including where the director controls the right to vote or dispose of Company securities or is entitled to benefit from a contract to call for or deliver Company securities.

definitions.hedging_definition: entering into protection arrangements includes entering into transactions which: (c) amount to 'short selling' of securities beyond the relevant person's holding of securities; (d) operate to limit the economic risk of the relevant person's security holding (e.g. hedging arrangements) including the Company's securities held beneficially (for example, in trust or under an incentive plan) on that person's behalf; or (e) otherwise enable the relevant person to profit from a decrease in the market price of securities.

VEA.ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Company may impose additional restrictions on dealing by any or all Designated Persons and their Affected Parties, even where the dealing would otherwise be permitted in a Trading Window. Any such restriction must be kept confidential by the Designated Person, who may pass it to affected Affected Parties on the same confidential basis.

rules.detail: Derivatives over Company securities are addressed as 'Company products in the derivatives markets' within the protection arrangements regime. Over vested, unrestricted shares a put and call are permitted but require approval under section 4.3(a): notification of the type of dealing and number of securities, confirmation of no Inside Information, written consent from the Authorising Officer, execution within five clear trading days, and a post-trade transaction confirmation. Dealing is confined to a four-week Trading Window unless the Clearance Officer grants exceptional-circumstances clearance. No venue distinction is drawn, so OTC legs with a bank are treated the same as listed options.
rules.evidence: The entering by a Designated Person or their Affected Parties into all types of "protection arrangements" for any of the Company's securities (or Company products in the derivatives markets): ... (b) otherwise, requires approval under section 4.3(a).

rules.detail: Derivative protection arrangements over unvested Company securities are banned at any time with no approval route.
rules.evidence: is prohibited at any time in respect of any Company securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock;

rules.detail: Employees who are not Designated Persons are subject only to the insider trading prohibition; the Trading Window, clearance, protection arrangement and margin lending rules in sections 4 and 5 are expressly framed as additional restrictions on Designated Persons and their Affected Parties.
rules.evidence: Additional restrictions are imposed on Designated Persons and their Affected Parties when dealing in the Company's securities.

rules.detail: Arrangements limiting the economic risk of unvested Company securities are prohibited at any time, with no approval route. The ban expressly reaches securities held beneficially on the person's behalf, including under an incentive plan or in trust.
rules.evidence: The entering by a Designated Person or their Affected Parties into all types of "protection arrangements" for any of the Company's securities ... is prohibited at any time in respect of any Company securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock;

rules.detail: Securities subject to a holding lock are treated identically to unvested securities: hedging them is prohibited at any time regardless of vesting, so post-vesting restricted shares cannot form part of the collared parcel.
rules.evidence: is prohibited at any time in respect of any Company securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock;

rules.detail: For vested shares free of a holding lock the policy does not prohibit hedging; it channels it into the ordinary clearance process. The hedge must be approved by the Authorising Officer, executed within five clear trading days, entered inside a Trading Window (or with exceptional-circumstances clearance), and confirmed to the Authorising Officer afterwards. Section 5.1's ban on short-term or speculative derivative transactions still constrains tenor.
rules.evidence: operate to limit the economic risk of the relevant person's security holding (e.g. hedging arrangements) ... otherwise, requires approval under section 4.3(a).

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named, but a prepaid forward or collar-plus-loan both limits economic risk and enables the person to profit from a decrease in the market price, so it is a protection arrangement: prohibited over unvested or holding-locked securities and otherwise requiring approval under section 4.3(a). The accompanying loan is separately constrained by the margin lending prohibition in section 5.3 if it has margin lending characteristics.
rules.evidence: otherwise enable the relevant person to profit from a decrease in the market price of securities.

rules.floor: the relevant person's holding of securities
rules.detail: Short selling is dealt with only as a species of protection arrangement: transactions that amount to short selling beyond the person's holding are prohibited over unvested or holding-locked securities and otherwise require approval under section 4.3(a). Read with section 5.1, which says Designated Persons should under no circumstances engage in speculative trading, a naked short would in practice be refused. A covered collar written against shares actually held does not exceed the holding and so is not short selling for this purpose.
rules.evidence: entering into protection arrangements includes entering into transactions which: (c) amount to "short selling" of securities beyond the relevant person's holding of securities;

rules.detail: Securities lending is not named and no definition sweeps it in. A lend transferring title would change the beneficial interest and so fall outside the section 6(a)(i) exemption, making it a dealing that needs a Trading Window and clearance.

Contracts for difference are named as an example of derivative market transactions caught by the absolute ban on short-term or speculative trading. A CFD that was neither short-term nor speculative would still be a protection arrangement under section 5.2 if it limited economic risk or allowed profit from a price fall, and so would be prohibited over unvested or locked securities and need approval otherwise.
rules.evidence: This prohibition includes short-term direct dealing in the Company's securities (within a period of less than three months) as well as transactions in the derivative markets (including exchange traded options, share warrants, contracts for difference and other similar instruments) which are short-term or speculative.

rules.detail: Absolute ban at any time, direct or indirect, on entering into any margin lending arrangement involving Company securities, extending to Affected Parties whom the Designated Person must procure to comply. Entering the arrangement, transferring Company securities into an existing margin loan account and selling Company securities to satisfy a margin call are each given as prohibited examples. There is no approval or exceptional-circumstances route.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons may not at any time, and must procure that their Affected Parties do not at any time, directly or indirectly, enter into any margin lending arrangement involving the Company's securities.

rules.detail: Granting security, a charge or a pledge over Company securities is not itself defined as a dealing and is prohibited only where it forms part of a margin lending arrangement. The exemption for disposals resulting from a secured lender exercising rights 'under a loan or security agreement' shows the policy contemplates Designated Persons pledging shares under a non-margin secured facility without that pledge being banned.

There is no general ban on secured financing; only margin lending arrangements are prohibited. Section 6(a)(vii) expressly exempts a disposal resulting from a secured lender exercising rights under a loan or security agreement, which presupposes that a Designated Person may have granted security over Company securities under a non-margin facility. The risk is characterisation: a facility with an LVR, margin call or top-up mechanic over Company securities would be an indirect margin lending arrangement and so prohibited.
rules.evidence: dispose of Company securities that are the result of a secured lender exercising their rights under a loan or security agreement;

rules.detail: Absolute prohibition, with no approval route, on short-term or speculative trading: direct dealing within a period of less than three months, and short-term or speculative transactions in the derivative markets including exchange traded options, share warrants and CFDs. Tenor and speculative character are therefore a live constraint on the derivative legs of any structure.
rules.evidence: Under no circumstances should Designated Persons or their Affected Parties engage in short-term or speculative trading in the Company's securities.

Additional restrictions are imposed on Designated Persons and their Affected Parties when dealing in the Company's securities.

short_term.evidence: This prohibition includes short-term direct dealing in the Company's securities (within a period of less than three months) as well as transactions in the derivative markets (including exchange traded options, share warrants, contracts for difference and other similar instruments) which are short-term or speculative.

Selling Company securities to satisfy a margin call is listed as an example of a prohibited margin lending dealing rather than something that can be cleared, whereas a disposal resulting from a secured lender exercising its rights under a loan or security agreement is an outright exemption available at any time, subject only to advising the Authorising Officer afterwards.
financing_disclosure: Designated Persons: after relying on any section 6 exemption (including a secured lender's enforcement sale), the Designated Person must advise the relevant Authorising Officer; no deadline stated.

Directors: must notify the Company Secretary in writing immediately and no later than 3 business days after any relevant event, so that the Company can notify ASX of a change to notifiable interests within 5 business days.
Designated Persons: the Company Secretary or delegate maintains a copy of all approval requests and details of all dealings by Designated Persons and their Affected Parties.

VEA.exemption_authority: The chair of the Board, or where the chair is the applicant the chair of the Audit and Risk Committee, acts as Clearance Officer and may in exceptional circumstances (assessed in absolute discretion, and which may include severe financial hardship or compliance with a court order or court enforceable undertaking) clear a dealing outside a Trading Window; approval must be given by email, the section 4.3(a) notification steps still apply, the clearance may be withdrawn, and it must be kept confidential. There is no power to waive the section 5.3 margin lending prohibition, the section 5.1 speculative trading ban or the section 5.2(a) ban on protection arrangements over unvested or holding-locked securities. Amendment of the Policy requires Board approval.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The entering by a Designated Person or their Affected Parties into all types of "protection arrangements" for any of the Company's securities (or Company products in the derivatives markets): (a) is prohibited at any time in respect of any Company securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock; and (b) otherwise, requires approval under section 4.3(a).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is a two-tier regime rather than a blanket hedging ban: the collar is available over vested unrestricted shares with Authorising Officer approval, but can never touch unvested or holding-locked stock.

bespoke_clauses.clause: operate to limit the economic risk of the relevant person's security holding (e.g. hedging arrangements) including the Company's securities held beneficially (for example, in trust or under an incentive plan) on that person's behalf
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Shares sitting in an employee share trust are within the protection arrangement definition, so the collar cannot be run over trust-held plan shares while they remain unvested or locked.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons may not at any time, and must procure that their Affected Parties do not at any time, directly or indirectly, enter into any margin lending arrangement involving the Company's securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The word 'indirectly' means a loan documented as something other than a margin loan but carrying LVR, margin call or top-up mechanics over the collared shares would be prohibited, so the funding leg must be a genuinely non-margin term facility.

bespoke_clauses.clause: dispose of Company securities that are the result of a secured lender exercising their rights under a loan or security agreement;
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The exemption confirms that non-margin secured lending against Company securities is contemplated and is not caught by section 5.3, and that the bank's enforcement sale may occur at any time, including outside a Trading Window.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Under no circumstances should Designated Persons or their Affected Parties engage in short-term or speculative trading in the Company's securities. This prohibition includes short-term direct dealing ... (within a period of less than three months) as well as transactions in the derivative markets ... which are short-term or speculative.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no approval route around this, so the collar must be long-dated and defensively characterised as risk management of an existing holding rather than a speculative derivative position.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons and their Affected Parties are only permitted to buy or sell, or otherwise deal in, Company securities: during a Trading Window; and if they have received clearance in accordance with this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is a positive-permission regime with only four four-week windows a year, so entry, any roll and any unwind of the collar must each be timed into a window or need exceptional-circumstances clearance from the chair.

bespoke_clauses.clause: order or otherwise authorise the dealing in Company securities within five clear trading days of receiving approval from the Authorising Officer ... if the approval is given during or after trading on one day, the order for the dealing must be lodged or otherwise authorised ... before the close of trading on the fifth trading day after the approval is given.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Both derivative legs and the associated share transfer must be authorised inside a tightly defined five trading day window from approval, which constrains documentation and pricing timetables.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the Company may impose such restrictions notwithstanding that the dealing in the Company's securities may otherwise be permitted under section 4.1. Any restriction communicated by the Company to any or all Designated Persons under this section 4.2 must be kept confidential
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An undisclosed company-imposed restriction can block entry, roll or unwind of the collar even inside a Trading Window, and the executive cannot tell the bank why.

bespoke_clauses.clause: clearance can be given or refused at the discretion of the Authorising Officer, without giving reasons; clearance can be withdrawn by the Authorising Officer at any time prior to the order for dealing being lodged or otherwise authorised
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Approval is not a bankable condition precedent: it can be revoked at any point before the trade is authorised and no reason need be given.

bespoke_clauses.clause: in relation to directors of the Company only, any other person or entity where dealing in securities of the Company by that person or entity would require disclosure to the ASX by the director. This includes where the director ... is entitled to benefit from a contract to call for or deliver securities in the Company;
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A director's rights under the collar are themselves a contract to call for or deliver Company securities, which points to the arrangement being a notifiable interest change requiring ASX disclosure within five business days.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Company Secretary (or a delegate) will maintain a copy of: all requests for an approval to deal in the Company's securities submitted by a Designated Person; and details of all dealings in the Company's securities by a Designated Person and their Affected Parties.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The full collar and its lifecycle will sit on the company's register, so the structure cannot be kept off the company's books.

VEA.summary: A funded collar is possible for a Viva Energy Designated Person, but only over vested shares free of any holding lock and on tight timing conditions. Section 5.2 treats the put and call as 'protection arrangements': prohibited outright at any time over unvested or holding-locked securities, including plan shares held beneficially in trust, but otherwise permitted with approval under section 4.3(a) from the chair of the Board (Directors and Senior Management), the chair of the Audit and Risk Committee (the chair of the Board) or the Company Secretary (other Designated Persons), with execution within five clear trading days and a post-trade confirmation. Dealing is confined to the four four-week Trading Windows following the half year, full year and first and third quarter releases, subject to confidential ad hoc restrictions and to exceptional-circumstances clearance from the Clearance Officer, and section 5.1's absolute ban on short-term or speculative trading (under three months, and short-term or speculative derivative market transactions) means the collar must be long-dated and framed as risk management rather than speculation. The loan leg is the sharper risk: section 5.3 bans directly or indirectly entering into any margin lending arrangement involving Company securities with no approval route, so the facility must be a genuine term loan without LVR, margin call or top-up mechanics, although section 6(a)(vii) confirms that secured lending under a loan or security agreement is contemplated and that the bank's enforcement sale is exempt and may occur at any time. Directors should also expect the arrangement to be a notifiable interest change requiring ASX disclosure, since the Affected Party definition reaches contracts to call for or deliver Company securities.

360.title: Insider Trading Policy

tiers.name: Insiders
tiers.description: Employees, contractors, consultants and Board members, together with their immediate family members and anyone otherwise subject to their influence or control, and entities such as venture capital funds, partnerships, trusts and corporations associated or affiliated with them. Every substantive prohibition in the Policy (derivatives, hedging and monetisation, short selling, short-term trading, pledging as collateral) applies to this whole population; only blackout periods and pre-approval are confined to Section 16 Officers and Designated Insiders.

tiers.name: Section 16 Officers
tiers.description: The Company's executive officers and directors. Subject to all Insider restrictions plus Blackout Periods, pre-approval from the General Counsel and Chief Financial Officer before any trade, and a one business day post-trade notification to the General Counsel covering trades by them and their associates.

tiers.name: Designated Insiders
tiers.description: Individuals identified as having MNPI who are not Section 16 Officers but have regular access to MNPI in the normal course of their job: all Vice President level employees and above, administrative assistants to Section 16 Officers and Designated Insiders, legal function members preparing SEC filings and earnings materials, Investor Relations members assisting with earnings releases, Disclosure Committee members, designated Finance and Accounting members, and anyone else notified by the General Counsel and/or Chief Financial Officer. Subject to Blackout Periods and pre-approval but not to the one business day post-trade notification.

tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: Immediate family members of Section 16 Officers and anyone otherwise subject to their influence or control (including household members), as well as entities such as venture capital funds, partnerships, trusts and corporations associated or affiliated with Section 16 Officers. 'Immediate family member' means any child, stepchild, parent, stepparent, spouse, domestic partner, sibling or in-law, and any person other than a tenant or employee sharing the household.

definitions.hedging_definition: Engage in hedging or monetization transactions involving our securities, such as zero cost collars and forward sale contracts, or contribute our securities to exchange funds in a manner that could be interpreted as hedging in our stock or otherwise limiting economic risk relating to the securities.

360.ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The General Counsel and Chief Financial Officer may designate special trading Blackout Periods applying to specific individuals or groups, and the Board may decide any other period. Special Blackout Periods are strictly confidential: no one may tell anyone that a special Blackout Period has been designated or that one previously was in place, internally or externally.

rules.section: Prohibited Activities and Other Restrictions - Insider Restrictions
rules.detail: Flat ban on transactions in options or other derivative securities on Company stock, with puts and calls named and with express extension to off-exchange markets, so an OTC put and call written with a bank are squarely prohibited. The only carve-out is the exercise of equity awards issued by the Company. The ban applies to every Insider, not just Section 16 Officers and Designated Insiders, and there is no pre-approval route: only a Board waiver could permit it.
rules.evidence: Other than the exercise of equity awards issued by us, engage in transactions involving options or other derivative securities on our stock, such as puts and calls, whether on an exchange or in any other market.

rules.section: Prohibited Activities and Other Restrictions - Insider Restrictions
rules.detail: Hedging is prohibited outright with no distinction by vesting or restriction status and no approval route. Zero cost collars are named as an example, and the drafting reaches anything 'that could be interpreted as hedging in our stock or otherwise limiting economic risk relating to the securities', which captures a funded collar however documented.
rules.evidence: Engage in hedging or monetization transactions involving our securities, such as zero cost collars and forward sale contracts, or contribute our securities to exchange funds in a manner that could be interpreted as hedging in our stock or otherwise limiting economic risk relating to the securities.

rules.section: Prohibited Activities and Other Restrictions - Insider Restrictions
rules.detail: The hedging ban is not limited to plan or unvested securities. Vested, unrestricted shares and CDIs held outright are 'our securities' and hedging them is equally prohibited, which is the critical difference from most ASX policies that permit hedging of vested unrestricted holdings.
rules.evidence: Engage in hedging or monetization transactions involving our securities, such as zero cost collars and forward sale contracts

rules.section: Prohibited Activities and Other Restrictions - Insider Restrictions
rules.detail: Monetisation transactions are named and banned in the same breath as hedging, with forward sale contracts given as the example. A prepaid forward, a collar with a loan against the collared stock, or an exchange fund contribution are each prohibited.
rules.evidence: Engage in hedging or monetization transactions involving our securities, such as zero cost collars and forward sale contracts, or contribute our securities to exchange funds

rules.section: Prohibited Activities and Other Restrictions - Insider Restrictions
rules.detail: Absolute ban on short sales of Company securities, expressly including short sales 'against the box' (short positions taken while owning an equivalent long holding). This forecloses the argument that a covered downside position over shares actually held is acceptable.
rules.evidence: Engage in short sales of our securities, meaning a sale of securities that you do not own, including short sales "against the box."

rules.detail: Securities lending is not named and no definition sweeps it in. In practice a lend supporting a short position would engage the short sale ban, and a lend that transferred the securities as collateral would engage the pledging restriction.

rules.section: Prohibited Activities and Other Restrictions - Insider Restrictions
rules.detail: CFDs are not named. They are 'other derivative securities on our stock' traded in a market other than an exchange, so they fall within the express derivatives ban, and a short CFD would also breach the short sale ban and, if it limited economic risk of a holding, the hedging ban.
rules.evidence: engage in transactions involving options or other derivative securities on our stock, such as puts and calls, whether on an exchange or in any other market.

rules.section: Prohibited Activities and Other Restrictions - Insider Restrictions
rules.detail: Using or pledging Company securities as collateral in a margin account is prohibited unless the pledge has been approved by the General Counsel and complies with any applicable Company policy or guidelines regarding pledging. Margin lending is named as the example. The pledging guidelines are not part of this document.
rules.evidence: Use or pledge our securities as collateral in a margin account or as collateral for a loan (e.g. margin lending or similar funding arrangements) unless the pledge has been approved by our General Counsel and in accordance with any applicable policy or guidelines of the Company regarding pledging.

rules.section: Prohibited Activities and Other Restrictions - Insider Restrictions
rules.detail: Any pledge of Company securities as collateral, whether into a margin account or for a loan, requires General Counsel approval and compliance with the Company's pledging guidelines. Section 16 Officers and Designated Insiders would in addition need pre-approval for any associated transfer of securities.
rules.evidence: Use or pledge our securities as collateral in a margin account or as collateral for a loan ... unless the pledge has been approved by our General Counsel

rules.section: Prohibited Activities and Other Restrictions - Insider Restrictions
rules.detail: The restriction is drafted broadly to cover collateral 'for a loan (e.g. margin lending or similar funding arrangements)', so it is not confined to margin loans. A bank loan secured on Life360 shares or CDIs is therefore available in principle, but only with General Counsel approval and subject to unseen Company pledging guidelines. It cannot rescue the collar, whose derivative legs are separately banned.
rules.evidence: Use or pledge our securities as collateral in a margin account or as collateral for a loan (e.g. margin lending or similar funding arrangements) unless the pledge has been approved by our General Counsel

rules.section: Prohibited Activities and Other Restrictions - Insider Restrictions
rules.detail: Intention-based six month rule running in both directions: acquiring securities with a view to selling within six months, and selling with a view to repurchasing within six months, are both prohibited. Exercise of an option or sale of any grant under a Company equity incentive plan is carved out of the acquisition limb. Section 16 Officers are separately subject to the US short swing profit rules.
rules.evidence: Purchase of Life360 securities on the open market and trading the same on a short-term basis. For the purposes of this Policy, short-term trading includes acquiring securities (but not including the exercise of an option or sale of any grant under an equity incentive plan operated by the Company) with a view to selling the securities within a 6 month period as well as selling securities with a view to repurchase within a 6 month period.

clearance.approver: General Counsel and Chief Financial Officer; email confirmation comes from the General Counsel. Approval can be withdrawn or refused by the General Counsel, the Chief Financial Officer, the CEO or the Company in its discretion
clearance.post_trade_to: General Counsel (details of the trade including the number and price of the securities involved), for trades by the Section 16 Officer and their associates

An approval to trade expires five business days from its date, unless the approval specifies a different date.

clearance.evidence: Insiders who are not Section 16 Officers or Designated Insiders and who are not in possession of MNPI may trade Company securities consistently with this Policy at any time.

carve_outs: the exercise of an option under an equity incentive plan operated by the Company
sale of any grant under an equity incentive plan operated by the Company
short_term.evidence: short-term trading includes acquiring securities (but not including the exercise of an option or sale of any grant under an equity incentive plan operated by the Company) with a view to selling the securities within a 6 month period as well as selling securities with a view to repurchase within a 6 month period.

exceptions.evidence: 401(k) Plan. Investing 401(k) plan contributions in a company stock fund in accordance with the terms of our 401(k) plan. However, any changes in your investment election regarding the Company's securities are subject to trading restrictions under this Policy.

Options. Exercising stock options granted under our equity incentive plans for cash or by delivering to the Company previously owned Company stock or through a net exercise of a stock option ... that does not involve a sale of shares in the open market.

exceptions.approver: General Counsel and Chief Financial Officer, for Section 16 Officers and Designated Insiders
exceptions.evidence: Estate Planning. Transfers of securities in connection with bona fide estate planning purposes, such as a transfer to or from a family trust or partnership. However, Section 16 Officers and Designated Insiders must get pre-approval from the General Counsel and Chief Financial Officer to transfer any Company securities.

exceptions.approver: Board of Directors
exceptions.evidence: Our Board reserves the right in its sole discretion to modify or grant waivers to this Policy. Any amendments or waiver may be publicly disclosed if required by applicable laws, rules and regulations.

financing.price_trigger_guidance: No trigger guidance in the Policy itself. Any pledge must be 'in accordance with any applicable policy or guidelines of the Company regarding pledging', a separate document that is not attached and that may contain loan-to-value or trigger constraints.
financing_disclosure: All Insiders: at inception, the pledge of Company securities as collateral in a margin account or for a loan requires the approval of the General Counsel; no deadline or form stated.

Section 16 Officers: within one business day following a trade, they and their associates must notify the General Counsel of the details of the trade including the number and price of the securities involved.
Section 16 Officers: separately subject to US beneficial ownership and short swing profit reporting under Section 16, and to Rule 144 resale limits, which the Policy notes but does not detail.

Life360 equity incentive plans
Life360 401(k) plan
Whistleblower Policy
360.exemption_authority: The Board reserves the right in its sole discretion to modify or grant waivers to this Policy, and any waiver may be publicly disclosed if required by applicable laws, rules and regulations. Below that, the General Counsel administers and interprets the Policy, approves pledges of securities as collateral, and may approve gifts or transfers during a period when the Insider cannot otherwise trade; the General Counsel may delegate these duties. There is no hardship or exceptional-circumstances mechanism for trading during a Blackout Period.
jurisdiction_overlays: US federal securities laws: Section 16 short swing profit rules for executive officers and directors, and Section 16 reporting
Rule 144 under the US Securities Act of 1933 (resale limits)

Regulation S: the CDIs are 'restricted securities' under Rule 144 and bear a FOR Financial Product designation restricting sale on ASX to US persons other than QIBs; hedging transactions with regard to the CDIs may only be conducted in accordance with the Securities Act
US SEC filing regime (Forms 10-K and 10-Q drive the Blackout Period end dates alongside ASX release)
Australian Corporations Act insider trading provisions and ASX Listing Rules

bespoke_clauses.clause: Engage in hedging or monetization transactions involving our securities, such as zero cost collars and forward sale contracts, or contribute our securities to exchange funds in a manner that could be interpreted as hedging in our stock or otherwise limiting economic risk relating to the securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The precise structure a funded collar uses is named as a prohibited activity for every Insider, with no vesting carve-out and no clearance route, so the transaction cannot be done without a Board waiver.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Other than the exercise of equity awards issued by us, engage in transactions involving options or other derivative securities on our stock, such as puts and calls, whether on an exchange or in any other market.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Documenting the put and call bilaterally with a bank rather than on an exchange does not avoid the prohibition, which expressly reaches any other market.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Engage in short sales of our securities, meaning a sale of securities that you do not own, including short sales "against the box."
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even a fully covered downside position against shares the executive already owns is caught, removing the usual argument that a collar over an existing holding is not a short sale.

bespoke_clauses.topic: pledging is the one permitted financing route
bespoke_clauses.clause: Use or pledge our securities as collateral in a margin account or as collateral for a loan (e.g. margin lending or similar funding arrangements) unless the pledge has been approved by our General Counsel and in accordance with any applicable policy or guidelines of the Company regarding pledging.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg alone is achievable with General Counsel approval, so a plain share-secured loan without any hedge is the only part of the funded collar that survives, subject to unseen pledging guidelines.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Our Board reserves the right in its sole discretion to modify or grant waivers to this Policy. Any amendments or waiver may be publicly disclosed if required by applicable laws, rules and regulations.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The only route to a collar is an express Board waiver, which may have to be publicly disclosed under US rules, making it a high-visibility ask.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Our General Counsel and Chief Financial Officer may designate special trading Blackout Periods that apply to specific individuals or groups of people ... no one may tell anyone that a special Blackout Period has been designated or that one previously was in place because that also is confidential information that cannot be disclosed internally or externally.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An executive could be blocked from any permitted step, such as pledging or unwinding, without being able to explain the reason to the bank.

bespoke_clauses.clause: short-term trading includes acquiring securities ... with a view to selling the securities within a 6 month period as well as selling securities with a view to repurchase within a 6 month period.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The look-forward period is six months rather than the usual three, so even the share transfers and repurchases around a financing would need a longer horizon.

bespoke_clauses.topic: Regulation S hedging restriction on CDIs
bespoke_clauses.clause: From the ASX announcement cover page: 'the CDIs are restricted securities under Rule 144 of the Securities Act ... In addition, hedging transactions with regard to the CDIs may only be conducted in accordance with the Securities Act.'
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even if the Policy were waived, US securities law independently constrains hedging of the CDIs, so the bank would need a Regulation S and Rule 144 analysis on top of the trading policy.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any approval to trade can be withdrawn or refused by the General Counsel, the Chief Financial Officer, the CEO or the Company in its discretion (and will be automatically deemed to have been withdrawn where the person seeking approval becomes aware of MNPI).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Approval is not a bankable condition precedent; it lapses automatically on the executive becoming aware of material nonpublic information before execution.

bespoke_clauses.topic: gifts and transfers in closed periods
bespoke_clauses.clause: Unless approved in advance by our General Counsel, make a gift, charitable contribution or other transfer of our securities during a period when the Insider cannot otherwise trade.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Delivering or transferring the collateral shares to a lender or custodian during a Blackout Period would itself require prior General Counsel approval.

360.summary: A funded collar is not possible under this policy. The Insider Restrictions ban, for every Insider and with no vesting carve-out and no pre-clearance route, both transactions in options or other derivative securities on Company stock (puts and calls, expressly whether on an exchange or in any other market) and hedging or monetization transactions, with zero cost collars and forward sale contracts named as the paradigm examples and the drafting extending to anything that could be interpreted as limiting economic risk relating to the securities. Short sales, including short sales against the box, are separately banned, which forecloses the argument that a collar over shares actually held is merely covered risk management. Only the financing leg is achievable in isolation: pledging Company securities as collateral in a margin account or for a loan is permitted if the General Counsel approves and the Company's separate pledging guidelines are met, and Section 16 Officers and Designated Insiders would also need pre-approval from the General Counsel and Chief Financial Officer, execution within five business days, and to stay outside the January, April, July and October Blackout Periods, with a one business day post-trade notification for Section 16 Officers. The only route to the full structure is a Board waiver, which the Board may grant in its sole discretion but which may have to be publicly disclosed, and US Regulation S and Rule 144 constraints on hedging the CDIs would still have to be cleared separately.

WOR.title: Securities Dealing Policy (MS-CP-POL-0008 Rev 2)

tiers.name: Worley personnel
tiers.description: Directors, officers, executives, managers, supervisors, employees, contractors and service providers of Worley, its subsidiaries and joint ventures, wherever located. All prohibitions (short selling, hedging of restricted holdings, short term dealing, selling minimum-holding shares, dealing in a closed period) apply to this whole population, and personnel are responsible for ensuring their associates comply.

tiers.name: Designated personnel
tiers.description: Directors of Worley, each direct report of Worley's CEO and each direct report of the CEO's direct reports. In addition to the general prohibitions they must notify Worley two business days before any dealing and within two business days after it, and must receive confirmation that there are no trading restrictions before they trade.

tiers.description: Directors of Worley other than the Chairman of the Board. They are Designated personnel and seek consent from the Chairman of the Board, with the Group Company Secretary copied.

tiers.name: Chairman of the Board
tiers.description: The Chairman, who seeks consent from the Deputy Chairman and Lead Independent Director.

tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: Family members and controlled entities of Worley personnel, wherever located. Personnel are responsible for ensuring their associates comply with the policy, and permitted-dealing carve-outs are drafted to cover the associate as well as the person.

WOR.ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The policy refers to 'any other period where restrictions on dealings are imposed' without naming who may impose it; in practice this sits with the Group Company Secretary and the approvers, since Designated personnel must receive confirmation that there are no restrictions on trading before they trade. Confidentiality of such restrictions is not addressed. The procedural detail is in the separate Securities Dealings Standard.

rules.detail: Derivatives are not named. A put and call over shares held subject to dealing restrictions or minimum holding requirements, or over performance rights or bonus entitlements, is hedging and so falls within the express prohibition with no consent route.
rules.evidence: this policy prohibits personnel from: ... hedging performance rights, bonus entitlements or shares held subject to dealing restrictions or minimum holding requirements;

rules.detail: The policy contains no definition of dealing or securities and does not name derivatives, options, warrants or OTC instruments. Its prohibitions are an exhaustive list that does not reach derivatives over vested, unrestricted shares that are not part of a minimum holding. Procedural detail is deferred to the Securities Dealings Standard, which is not part of this document, so the venue and instrument treatment cannot be determined from the policy alone.

Hedging performance rights and bonus entitlements is prohibited outright, with no consent route offered. The consent mechanism in the policy is expressed to apply to closed period dealing, short term dealing and sales of minimum-holding shares, not to the hedging or short selling bans.
rules.evidence: In addition to insider trading prohibitions, this policy prohibits personnel from: ... hedging performance rights, bonus entitlements or shares held subject to dealing restrictions or minimum holding requirements;

rules.detail: Shares held subject to dealing restrictions, and shares held to satisfy a minimum holding requirement, may not be hedged. The minimum holding limb is unusual: it means the tranche of vested shares an executive must retain is permanently outside any collar even though it is otherwise freely held.
rules.evidence: hedging performance rights, bonus entitlements or shares held subject to dealing restrictions or minimum holding requirements;

rules.detail: The hedging prohibition is defined by the character of the holding, not by the transaction. Vested shares that are not subject to dealing restrictions and are not needed to satisfy a minimum holding requirement fall outside its words, so hedging them is not prohibited by this policy. Any such hedge would still have to satisfy the insider trading prohibition, the Front Page Test, the closed period rule if it amounts to dealing in Worley shares, and the Securities Dealings Standard.

rules.floor: shares held to fulfil any minimum holding requirements
rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. It is not prohibited over free vested shares, but any structure that could result in the disposal of shares held to satisfy a minimum holding requirement is caught by the express ban on selling those shares without consent, and hedging them is banned outright. The collar must therefore be sized to the surplus above the minimum holding, and physical settlement or lender enforcement must not cut into that floor.
rules.evidence: selling shares held to fulfil any minimum holding requirements (unless consent is granted); and

rules.detail: Flat ban on short selling with no consent route and no definition. A covered position written against shares actually held is not short selling on the ordinary meaning, but the policy gives no guidance and the Front Page Test would be applied.
rules.evidence: In addition to insider trading prohibitions, this policy prohibits personnel from: short selling;

rules.detail: Securities lending is not named and there is no dealing definition to sweep it in. A lend supporting a short position would engage the short selling ban.

Contracts for difference are not named and no definition captures them. A short CFD would be caught by the short selling ban and a CFD over restricted or minimum-holding shares by the hedging ban; otherwise the policy is silent and the Securities Dealings Standard would need to be checked.

Margin lending is not prohibited and is expressly contemplated: a lender who is not an associate may deal in Worley shares provided as security for a margin loan at any time in accordance with the terms of the loan, including during a closed period, without consent. The policy places the risk on the individual, warning that a lender's sale while the person holds inside information may still breach insider trading laws or the policy, and that it is the person's responsibility to consider the circumstances in which they pledge shares.
rules.evidence: A lender (who is not a personnel's associate) may deal in Worley shares that they have provided as security for a margin loan at any time in accordance with the terms of the loan, provided that the lender complies with the law when doing so.

rules.detail: Granting security over Worley shares is not prohibited, is not listed among the prohibitions, and is not itself defined as a dealing. The policy assumes personnel may provide Worley shares as security for a margin loan and regulates only the consequences. Shares subject to dealing restrictions or forming part of a minimum holding should not be pledged, since their sale needs consent and their hedging is banned.
rules.evidence: It is personnel's responsibility to consider carefully the circumstances, if any, in which they provide Worley shares as security for a margin loan to ensure that this does not occur.

rules.detail: There is no prohibition on secured financing of any kind. The prohibition list is closed and does not mention margin loans, pledges or secured facilities, and the permitted dealings section positively accommodates a secured lender. A bank facility secured on vested unrestricted Worley shares is therefore available without consent, subject to the insider trading rules, the Front Page Test, the minimum holding floor and the Designated personnel notice requirements.
rules.evidence: A lender (who is not a personnel's associate) may deal in Worley shares that they have provided as security for a margin loan at any time in accordance with the terms of the loan

rules.detail: Short term dealing is prohibited unless consent is granted, and consent is only given in exceptional circumstances such as financial hardship or compulsion by court order, or anything else the approver considers exceptional. The policy does not define short term dealing or state any period; that definition sits in the Securities Dealings Standard, which is not part of this document.
rules.evidence: this policy prohibits personnel from: ... short term dealing (unless consent is granted);

clearance.evidence: Person seeking consent: Chairman of the Board - Approver: Deputy Chairman and Lead Independent Director ... Any consent provided must be acted upon within five business days, unless the consent specifies otherwise.

engage in indirect and incidental trading that occurs because of them or their associate dealing in securities issued by a managed investment scheme, listed investment company, exchange-traded fund or similar investment vehicle that is managed by a third party and that happens to hold Worley shares as part of its portfolio and those shares represent <20% of the portfolio.

A lender (who is not a personnel's associate) may deal in Worley shares that they have provided as security for a margin loan at any time in accordance with the terms of the loan, provided that the lender complies with the law when doing so.

The policy instead places the burden on the individual: 'If the lender does so when the personnel has inside information, they may still be in breach of insider trading laws or this policy. It is personnel's responsibility to consider carefully the circumstances, if any, in which they provide Worley shares as security for a margin loan to ensure that this does not occur.'
financing_disclosure: Designated personnel (directors, CEO direct reports and their direct reports): must notify Worley of any dealing in Worley shares two business days in advance and within two business days after the dealing, and must receive confirmation that there are no trading restrictions before trading.

Designated personnel: the notice requirements are expressly stated to continue to apply even where the person is not involved in the decision to deal, which captures a lender's enforcement sale of pledged shares.
All personnel: the Group Company Secretary must be copied on any consent request.
financing.minimum_shareholding_requirement: Yes. A minimum holding requirement is referenced twice and is doubly protective: hedging 'shares held subject to dealing restrictions or minimum holding requirements' is prohibited outright, and 'selling shares held to fulfil any minimum holding requirements' is prohibited unless consent is granted. Shares within the minimum holding are therefore excluded from any collar, and the policy does not contemplate hedged shares counting towards the requirement.

external_documents: Securities Dealings Standard (procedures that personnel must also follow; contains the operative definitions such as short term dealing)
Worley minimum holding requirement (referenced but not set out)
Worley employee incentive scheme rules
WOR.exemption_authority: Consent, where the policy requires it, is granted by the Deputy Chairman and Lead Independent Director (for the Chairman of the Board), the Chairman of the Board (for other directors), the Chief Executive Officer (for other Designated personnel) or the Group Company Secretary (for all other personnel), with the Group Company Secretary copied on the request. Consent is only granted in exceptional circumstances, which include financial hardship, compulsion by court order and anything else the approver considers exceptional, and the approver may also apply the Front Page Test. Consent must be acted on within five business days unless it specifies otherwise. There is no consent route out of the short selling ban or the hedging ban.

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedging ban keyed to the holding, not the instrument
bespoke_clauses.clause: this policy prohibits personnel from: ... hedging performance rights, bonus entitlements or shares held subject to dealing restrictions or minimum holding requirements;
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The ban is defined by which shares are hedged rather than by transaction type, so a collar is available over vested shares that are free of dealing restrictions and surplus to the minimum holding, but nothing else.

bespoke_clauses.clause: selling shares held to fulfil any minimum holding requirements (unless consent is granted);
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The collar and the security package must be sized only to the surplus above the executive's minimum holding, because physical settlement or lender enforcement over those shares would be a prohibited sale absent consent.

bespoke_clauses.topic: lender may sell at any time
bespoke_clauses.clause: A lender (who is not a personnel's associate) may deal in Worley shares that they have provided as security for a margin loan at any time in accordance with the terms of the loan, provided that the lender complies with the law when doing so.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement rights over pledged shares are expressly preserved, including during a closed period, provided the lender is not an associate and acts in accordance with the loan terms.

bespoke_clauses.topic: residual inside information risk on enforcement
bespoke_clauses.clause: If the lender does so when the personnel has inside information, they may still be in breach of insider trading laws or this policy. It is personnel's responsibility to consider carefully the circumstances, if any, in which they provide Worley shares as security for a margin loan to ensure that this does not occur.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The executive, not the bank, bears the risk that an enforcement sale coincides with their possession of inside information, which argues for a facility structured to avoid discretionary sales or with long cure periods.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The insider trading laws, Front Page Test and notice requirements still apply in these circumstances, even if personnel are not involved in the decision to deal in Worley shares.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A director or senior executive must still give Worley two business days advance notice and post-trade notice of a lender's sale, which is impractical for an unannounced enforcement and should be addressed in the facility's notification mechanics.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated personnel are required to notify Worley of any dealing in Worley shares two business days in advance of the dealing and within two business days after the dealing. They must receive confirmation that there are no restrictions on trading in the particular circumstances before they trade.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Entry, roll, unwind and settlement of the collar each need two business days lead time and a positive no-restrictions confirmation, which sits awkwardly with market-priced derivative execution.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where consent to deal in Worley shares is required under this policy, consent will only be granted to personnel in exceptional circumstances.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any step needing consent, such as a closed period unwind or a sale of minimum-holding shares, is very unlikely to be approved, so the structure must be timed entirely outside closed periods.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Worley personnel must also follow the procedures set out in the Securities Dealings Standard.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The operative definitions, including what counts as short term dealing and how derivatives are treated, are in a document that is not lodged with ASX and must be obtained before the structure can be confirmed as compliant.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If the market was aware of all the current circumstances, could I be perceived to be taking advantage of my position in an inappropriate way? How would it look if the transaction were reported on the front page of the newspaper?
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A funded collar by a senior executive is exactly the kind of arrangement this reputational test targets, and the approver may refuse or the individual may be criticised even where the technical rules are met.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This policy applies to Worley personnel ... and any "associates", which are family members and controlled entities of those persons, wherever they are located. Personnel are responsible for ensuring their associates comply.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Booking the collar or the loan through a family trust or controlled company does not escape the policy, and the lender must not be an associate for the enforcement carve-out to apply.

WOR.summary: A funded collar is possible under this policy, but only over a narrow slice of shares and with an important gap in the documentation. The hedging prohibition is keyed to the holding rather than the instrument: performance rights, bonus entitlements, shares subject to dealing restrictions and shares held to satisfy a minimum holding requirement can never be hedged, while vested shares that are free of restrictions and surplus to the minimum holding are not caught, so the collar must be sized to that surplus only. The financing leg is unusually accommodating: there is no prohibition on margin loans, pledges or secured facilities, and the policy expressly allows a lender who is not an associate to deal in pledged Worley shares at any time in accordance with the loan terms, including during a closed period, while warning that the executive still bears the insider trading risk if enforcement coincides with their possession of inside information. The practical constraints are timing and notice: dealing in Worley shares in the 30 June and 31 December closed periods needs consent that is granted only in exceptional circumstances, short term dealing needs the same consent, and Designated personnel (directors, CEO direct reports and their direct reports) must give two business days advance notice, obtain confirmation that there are no restrictions, and give post-trade notice within two business days, obligations that expressly continue even for dealings they did not decide on such as a lender's enforcement sale. Because the policy contains no definition of dealing or securities, does not mention derivatives or OTC instruments, and defers procedure to a separate Securities Dealings Standard that is not lodged, the Standard must be obtained before the structure can be confirmed.

A2M.ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Company may declare 'any other period that the Company specifies from time to time' as a blackout period (rule 6.3). The policy does not name the decision-maker, any notification mechanism, or whether the reason is confidential.

rules.detail: Dealing in derivatives, including put and call options and equity swaps, is expressly named and is permitted with prior written approval from the rule 7 person. There is no venue limitation, so an OTC put and call written by a bank is squarely within the clause. 'Securities' is separately defined to include options over existing shares, warrant contracts and other derivatives relating to the shares, so dealing in them is also a dealing subject to blackouts and rule 6.6 clearance.
rules.evidence: A Restricted Person must not, without prior written approval by the relevant person specified in rule 7, engage in hedging arrangements, deal in derivatives or enter into other arrangements which vary economic risk related to the Company's Securities including, for example, dealing in warrants, equity swaps, put and call options, contracts for difference and other contracts intended to secure a profit or avoid a loss based on fluctuations in the price of the Company's Securities.

rules.detail: The policy draws no distinction between exchange-traded and OTC derivatives; both are caught by rule 6.9 and by the definition of Securities, and both require prior written approval and compliance with the blackout periods.
rules.evidence: “Securities” means shares, debentures, options to subscribe for new shares and options over existing shares, warrant contracts and other derivatives relating to the shares.

rules.detail: Hedging of Company Securities generally is not prohibited outright; it requires prior written approval from the rule 7 person. It remains subject to the blackout periods in 6.3 and the general insider trading prohibition, and the approval discretion is unfettered.
rules.evidence: A Restricted Person must not, without prior written approval by the relevant person specified in rule 7, engage in hedging arrangements, deal in derivatives or enter into other arrangements which vary economic risk related to the Company's Securities.

rules.detail: Unusually, hedging of unvested plan securities is not an absolute ban: the second sentence of 6.9 simply confirms that unvested plan securities fall within the same prior written approval requirement rather than carving out a prohibition.
rules.evidence: This provision includes engaging in hedging or other arrangements that have the effect of limiting the economic risk in connection with unvested securities issued pursuant to any employee option or share plan.

rules.detail: The rule 6 additional restrictions, including the hedging clause, are expressed to apply only to Restricted Persons. Employees and contractors who are not Restricted Persons are addressed only by the insider trading prohibition and the confidentiality duty.

Monetisation, prepaid forwards and collars are not named. A monetising structure is an 'other arrangement which varies economic risk related to the Company's Securities' and a 'contract intended to secure a profit or avoid a loss based on fluctuations in the price', so it needs prior written approval; the funding leg is separately caught by rule 6.10.
rules.evidence: enter into other arrangements which vary economic risk related to the Company's Securities including, for example, dealing in warrants, equity swaps, put and call options, contracts for difference and other contracts intended to secure a profit or avoid a loss based on fluctuations in the price of the Company's Securities.

rules.detail: Expressed hortatorily ('should not') rather than as an absolute bar, and a waiver from rule 6.4 is available for exceptional circumstances under rule 6.5. A physically settled collar over shares already held is not a short sale, but a cash-settled or naked short leg would be.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons should not trade in the Company Securities on a short term basis or for speculative trading gain or short sell any Company Securities.

rules.detail: Securities lending arrangements are expressly named alongside margin lending: advance notification to the rule 7 person plus written clearance before the arrangement is entered into. No prohibition.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must notify the Company in advance before engaging in any margin or securities lending arrangements or granting a security interest or other encumbrance over Company Securities.

rules.detail: Contracts for difference are named in the rule 6.9 list and so require prior written approval. In practice a CFD would also engage the rule 6.4 discouragement of short term and speculative trading and, if short, the short selling limb.
rules.evidence: including, for example, dealing in warrants, equity swaps, put and call options, contracts for difference and other contracts intended to secure a profit or avoid a loss based on fluctuations in the price of the Company's Securities.

rules.detail: Margin lending is permitted subject to advance notification and prior written clearance from the rule 7 person. The policy is silent on forced sales, margin calls, price triggers, gearing limits and ongoing disclosure.
rules.evidence: The proposed arrangement must not be entered into or grant made until written clearance has been given by the person nominated in rule 7.

rules.detail: Granting a security interest or other encumbrance over Company Securities is expressly permitted subject to advance notification and prior written clearance. The grant is treated as its own regulated act rather than as a dealing, so rule 6.3 blackouts are not in terms applied to it, though prudence would suggest otherwise.
rules.evidence: granting a security interest or other encumbrance over Company Securities. The notification must be made to the person in rule 7.

rules.detail: There is no general ban on secured financing. Any loan secured on Company Securities is caught by the encumbrance limb of rule 6.10 and requires advance notification and written clearance; the security interest may not be granted until clearance is given. Nothing distinguishes vested from unvested shares.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must notify the Company in advance before engaging in any margin or securities lending arrangements or granting a security interest or other encumbrance over Company Securities.

rules.detail: No defined holding period or LIFO rule; a general standard against short term or speculative trading, drafted as 'should not', and waivable under rule 6.5 for exceptional circumstances. A short-dated or speculative-looking collar risks characterisation under this rule.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons should not trade in the Company Securities on a short term basis or for speculative trading gain or short sell any Company Securities.

A2M.exemption_authority: Rule 6.5: the person specified in rule 7 may grant a written waiver from rule 6.3 (blackout periods) or rule 6.4 (short term trading, speculative gain, short selling) for exceptional circumstances including severe financial hardship, compulsion by a court order, or any other circumstances deemed exceptional. The applicant must apply in writing, explain the circumstances, confirm no inside information, and supply sufficient evidence that the dealing is the most reasonable course of action available. A granted waiver lasts 2 business days.
