NZX and ASX change of interests notification and the Company's interests register for Directors and Senior Executives

bespoke_clauses.clause: A Restricted Person must not, without prior written approval by the relevant person specified in rule 7, engage in hedging arrangements, deal in derivatives or enter into other arrangements which vary economic risk related to the Company's Securities including, for example ... put and call options ...
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The put and call legs of a collar are expressly contemplated and are permissible with prior written approval, so the derivative side of the structure has a clear approval route rather than a prohibition.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This provision includes engaging in hedging or other arrangements that have the effect of limiting the economic risk in connection with unvested securities issued pursuant to any employee option or share plan.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unusually, unvested plan securities are brought within the same approval gate rather than an absolute ban, so a collar is not automatically confined to vested shares, although approval over unvested holdings would be difficult to obtain in practice.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons must notify the Company in advance before engaging in any margin or securities lending arrangements or granting a security interest or other encumbrance over Company Securities. ... The proposed arrangement must not be entered into or grant made until written clearance has been given by the person nominated in rule 7.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg secured on the collared shares is permitted subject to notification and written clearance, so both legs of a funded collar can be approved by the same approver.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Clearance to deal in Company Securities can be revoked at any time but will otherwise be valid (unless another period is otherwise specified in the clearance) for a period of ten trading days commencing on the date following the clearance being obtained.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A ten trading day window is long enough to document and price a collar, but the unrestricted revocation right means the bank should not rely on clearance surviving to settlement and should build a termination right for revoked clearance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: In determining whether to clear the proposed dealing, the relevant person nominated in rule 7 will consider whether the proposed dealing is appropriate having regard to all relevant circumstances.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no SLA, no criteria and no appeal, so approval of a collar turns entirely on the Chair's or Board's view of appropriateness and cannot be assumed.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Rule 6.10 requires clearance for margin and securities lending and encumbrances but says nothing about margin calls, forced sales, price triggers or what happens if the lender sells during a blackout period.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The policy gives the executive no protection if the bank enforces during a blackout, so enforcement and physical settlement mechanics must be negotiated into the loan and collar documents rather than relied on from the policy.

bespoke_clauses.clause: any other period that the Company specifies from time to time
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Ad hoc blackouts with no stated notice or duration can block entry, roll, unwind or settlement of the collar at any time.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If a Restricted Person needs to deal in the Company Securities due to exceptional circumstances ... the Restricted Person must apply to the person specified in rule 7 for a waiver ... in each circumstance the duration of the waiver to deal in securities will be 2 business days.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A blackout-period unwind or settlement is theoretically possible on a severe financial hardship or court order waiver, but only for 2 business days and only on evidence that dealing is the most reasonable course available.

bespoke_clauses.clause: their associates (as defined in the Takeovers Code)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Holding the collared shares through a spouse, family trust or controlled entity does not avoid the clearance and notification gates, since associates are themselves Restricted Persons.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons should not trade in the Company Securities on a short term basis or for speculative trading gain or short sell any Company Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: No fixed period is set, so a short-dated collar or one with knock-out features could be characterised as short term or speculative; a longer tenor and physical settlement reduce that risk.

A2M.summary: A funded collar is available to a2 Milk Directors and Senior Executives, but only with express prior written approval of both legs. Rule 6.9 names put and call options, equity swaps and arrangements varying economic risk in the Company's Securities, and permits them with prior written approval from the rule 7 approver (the Board for the Chair, the Chair for other Directors and the CEO, the Chair and CEO for Senior Executives); rule 6.10 separately permits granting a security interest or other encumbrance over Company Securities, and margin or securities lending, on advance notification plus written clearance, so the loan leg is not prohibited. Approval discretion is unfettered and clearance is revocable at any time and otherwise lasts ten trading days, so the trade must be entered promptly and the bank should provide for revoked clearance. Entry must sit outside the two blackout periods and any ad hoc period the Company specifies, and the arrangement should not look short term or speculative under rule 6.4. The policy says nothing about forced sales, margin calls or price triggers, so enforcement mechanics and any blackout-period settlement risk must be handled contractually, with only the 2 business day exceptional circumstances waiver in rule 6.5 as relief.

BRG.title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Employees
tiers.description: All directors and employees of Breville and its controlled entities, as well as any contractors or consultants whose terms of engagement apply Breville policies to them. The insider trading prohibition, the section 5.1 ban on limiting economic risk and the section 5.2 short-term trading ban apply to this whole tier.

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: Employees likely to have regular access to Inside Information: Breville's Directors, Chief Executive Officer, Group Executives and their senior direct reports, Company Secretaries, Group financial reporting personnel, and any other Employee designated by a Company Secretary from time to time. Closed Periods, the universal approval-to-deal requirement, the short selling and securities lending bans and the margin lending approval attach to this tier.

tiers.description: Certain family members of a Restricted Person, such as their spouse and dependent children, and any entity which the Restricted Person or such a family member controls or has an ability to control. definitions.hedging_definition: No Employee may enter into any agreement, arrangement or scheme (including options, hedging arrangements or other Derivative products) whereby the Employee changes the economic benefit or risk derived by the Employee in relation to any holding of Breville shares or an equity-based incentive award or grant made by Breville to the Employee, irrespective of the outcome under that incentive award or grant. 'Derivative includes a derivative within the meaning of section 761D of the Corporations Act (such as an option, forward contract, swap, future, warrant, cap and collar) and any other transaction in a financial product that limits the economic risk associated with holding the relevant Securities.'

BRG.ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Breville Board may specify any other period as a Closed Period from time to time (section 4.2(c)). The policy does not say whether such a period or its reasons are confidential, but a refusal of a request to deal is final, unreasoned and must be kept confidential by the applicant.

rules.detail: Section 5.1 bans any agreement, arrangement or scheme including options, hedging arrangements or other Derivative products that changes the Employee's economic benefit or risk in Breville shares or an equity incentive award. The defined term Derivative expressly names 'cap and collar' among section 761D derivatives, and there is no venue limitation, so both exchange-traded and OTC puts and calls over Breville shares are caught. The ban applies to every Employee, not just Restricted Persons, and has no approval route.
rules.evidence: Derivative includes a derivative within the meaning of section 761D of the Corporations Act (such as an option, forward contract, swap, future, warrant, cap and collar) and any other transaction in a financial product that limits the economic risk associated with holding the relevant Securities.

rules.detail: The prohibition is not confined to plan securities: it reaches 'any holding of Breville shares'. There is no carve-out for vested, unrestricted shares and no approval, waiver or exemption route; the section 4.4 exceptional circumstances mechanism relieves only the Closed Period restriction, not section 5.1.
rules.evidence: No Employee may enter into any agreement, arrangement or scheme (including options, hedging arrangements or other Derivative products) whereby the Employee changes the economic benefit or risk derived by the Employee in relation to any holding of Breville shares or an equity-based incentive award or grant made by Breville to the Employee

rules.detail: Hedging of unvested equity-based incentive awards or grants is prohibited, and the closing words make clear this holds whether or not the award ultimately vests.
rules.evidence: in relation to any holding of Breville shares or an equity-based incentive award or grant made by Breville to the Employee, irrespective of the outcome under that incentive award or grant.

rules.detail: Monetisation structures are not named as such, but a prepaid variable forward, a share swap or an exchangeable is a forward contract or swap within the defined term Derivative and, being an arrangement that changes the Employee's economic benefit or risk in Breville shares, is banned by section 5.1. The words 'any agreement, arrangement or scheme' and 'any other transaction in a financial product that limits the economic risk' give the clause a substance-over-form reach.
rules.evidence: No Employee may enter into any agreement, arrangement or scheme (including options, hedging arrangements or other Derivative products) whereby the Employee changes the economic benefit or risk derived by the Employee in relation to any holding of Breville shares

rules.detail: Absolute prohibition at any time, with no approval or exceptional circumstances route. Section 4.7 is directed to Restricted Persons and their Closely Connected Parties; the summary in section 9 also lists short selling as a Restricted Persons-only item.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons and their Closely Connected Parties are prohibited from short selling Breville Securities at any time.

rules.detail: An unusually wide ban: lending Breville Securities to any other party for securities lending or for any other purpose is prohibited outright, not merely lending that facilitates short selling. This bites on any collar or financing structure that contemplates the bank on-lending or rehypothecating the collateral shares.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons and their Closely Connected Parties are also prohibited from “lending” their Breville Securities to any other party for the purposes of short selling, Securities lending or for any other purpose.

rules.detail: Contracts for difference are not named but are section 761D derivatives and transactions in a financial product that alter the economic risk of holding Breville shares, so they fall within the section 5.1 ban; a short CFD would additionally offend the section 4.7 short selling prohibition for Restricted Persons.
rules.evidence: and any other transaction in a financial product that limits the economic risk associated with holding the relevant Securities.

rules.detail: Including Breville Securities in a margin loan portfolio or similar funding arrangement is permitted with the prior approval of the Chair, sought through the section 4.3 Request to Deal Form process. Approval may be refused or conditioned without reasons and may be revoked. Involuntary disposals by an approved margin lender exercising its rights are excluded dealings under section 6(e).
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons and their Closely Connected Parties may not include their Breville Securities in a margin loan portfolio or similar funding arrangement without first seeking the approval of the Chair using the approval procedures described in section 4.3 above.

rules.detail: Granting security, a charge, lien or pledge is not named in the policy and is not within the Dealing definition. An encumbrance granted as part of a loan facility is caught only because the shares are thereby included in a 'similar funding arrangement' under section 4.6, requiring the Chair's approval. A charge unconnected with any funding arrangement is not addressed.
rules.evidence: may not include their Breville Securities in a margin loan portfolio or similar funding arrangement without first seeking the approval of the Chair

rules.detail: There is no general ban on secured financing. The words 'or similar funding arrangement' extend section 4.6 beyond margin loans to a bespoke loan secured on Breville shares, so the funding leg of a collar would be approvable by the Chair even though the derivative legs are not. Nothing distinguishes vested from unvested shares as collateral.
rules.evidence: may not include their Breville Securities in a margin loan portfolio or similar funding arrangement without first seeking the approval of the Chair using the approval procedures described in section 4.3 above.

rules.detail: A three-month buy-and-sell window test applying to all Employees, expressly extended to 'other short-term dealings such as forward contracts', which sweeps in short-dated derivative structures independently of section 5.1.
rules.evidence: No Employee may deal in Breville Securities on a short-term basis. Short-term trading includes buying and selling securities on market within a 3-month period or entering into other short-term dealings such as forward contracts.

BRG.exemption_authority: Section 4.4 only: the Chair of the Board (or, for the Chair, the Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee) may approve dealing during a Closed Period in exceptional circumstances (severe and unforeseen financial hardship, legal compulsion, or otherwise exceptional circumstances where the dealing is the only reasonable course of action), for 5 business days and only if the person is not in possession of Inside Information. There is no authority anywhere in the policy to waive the section 5.1 ban on limiting economic risk, the section 4.7 short selling and lending bans, or the section 5.2 short-term trading ban.

bespoke_clauses.topic: collar named in the derivative definition
bespoke_clauses.clause: Derivative includes a derivative within the meaning of section 761D of the Corporations Act (such as an option, forward contract, swap, future, warrant, cap and collar) and any other transaction in a financial product that limits the economic risk associated with holding the relevant Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The policy names a collar as a Derivative product, so the derivative legs of a funded collar fall squarely within the section 5.1 prohibition and cannot be argued outside it.

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedging ban reaches all shares and all staff
bespoke_clauses.clause: No Employee may enter into any agreement, arrangement or scheme ... whereby the Employee changes the economic benefit or risk derived by the Employee in relation to any holding of Breville shares or an equity-based incentive award or grant ...
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The ban is not limited to plan or unvested securities and applies to every director, employee, contractor and consultant, so there is no class of shares or class of person over whom a collar could be written.

bespoke_clauses.topic: no waiver of the hedging ban
bespoke_clauses.clause: Section 4.4 permits approval to deal during a Closed Period in exceptional circumstances; it relieves only the Closed Period restriction and no provision permits a waiver of section 5.1.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even severe financial hardship or a court order gives no route to a permitted collar; the only relief available goes to timing, not to the prohibited structure.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons and their Closely Connected Parties may not include their Breville Securities in a margin loan portfolio or similar funding arrangement without first seeking the approval of the Chair using the approval procedures described in section 4.3 above.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A loan secured on Breville shares is permitted with the Chair's approval, so the funding leg is available in isolation even though the protective legs of a collar are not.

bespoke_clauses.topic: approved lender enforcement is an excluded dealing
bespoke_clauses.clause: an involuntary disposal of Breville Securities that results from a margin lender or financier exercising its rights under a margin lending arrangement (provided the arrangement was previously approved in accordance with this policy).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unusually protective: a bank enforcing over collateral, including during a Closed Period, does not breach the policy so long as the facility was approved up front, which makes a plain secured loan workable.

bespoke_clauses.topic: no rehypothecation or lending of collateral
bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons and their Closely Connected Parties are also prohibited from “lending” their Breville Securities to any other party for the purposes of short selling, Securities lending or for any other purpose.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any structure in which the bank borrows or rehypothecates the pledged shares to hedge its own position is prohibited, so collateral must be held on a no-reuse basis.

bespoke_clauses.topic: forward contracts caught by the short-term rule
bespoke_clauses.clause: Short-term trading includes buying and selling securities on market within a 3-month period or entering into other short-term dealings such as forward contracts.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A forward or short-dated derivative is independently prohibited as short-term dealing, so tenor cannot be used to cure the section 5.1 problem.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The approver may refuse a request, impose conditions on a proposed dealing or revoke a previously granted request, and in each case is not obliged to provide reasons for their action. Any refusal to approve a request will be final and binding, and the person seeking approval must keep that decision confidential.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Approval for the financing leg can be revoked or conditioned without reasons and lapses after 5 business days, so the bank should not treat an approval as a durable condition precedent.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Closely Connected Parties includes: certain family members of a Restricted Person, such as their spouse and dependent children; and any entity which the Restricted Person or a person referred to in (a) above controls or has an ability to control.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Routing a collar through a spouse or a controlled trust or company does not avoid the prohibitions, and section 5.1 in any event binds the Employee personally.

BRG.summary: A funded collar is not possible for any Breville director or executive. Section 5.1 prohibits every Employee from entering into any agreement, arrangement or scheme, including options, hedging arrangements or other Derivative products, that changes their economic benefit or risk in any holding of Breville shares or in an equity incentive award, and the defined term Derivative expressly names 'cap and collar'; the ban covers vested and unvested holdings alike, applies to all staff rather than only Restricted Persons, and has no approval, waiver or exceptional-circumstances route. Short-dated structures are separately barred by the section 5.2 three-month short-term trading rule, which names forward contracts, and Restricted Persons may not lend their Breville Securities to any party for any purpose, which blocks rehypothecation of collateral. Only the funding leg is available: including Breville Securities in a margin loan portfolio or similar funding arrangement requires the Chair's prior approval under section 4.6, and an involuntary disposal by an approved financier exercising its rights is an excluded dealing under section 6(e), even in a Closed Period. A bank could therefore offer an approved secured loan against Breville shares, but not the put and call legs that would make it a collar.

SGM.title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Employees
tiers.description: All Directors, employees and contractors of Sims Limited and its related bodies corporate, globally. This tier is bound by the insider trading prohibition and the black-out periods, but not by the approval-to-deal process or the 'other types of restricted dealings' bans.

tiers.name: Restricted Employees
tiers.description: Employees notified by the Company Secretary that they are restricted because they are likely to possess inside information. Comprises Directors and Officers, Key Management Personnel, Executives, and employees formally notified because they regularly access sensitive information or are on a distribution, confidential project or insider list. All the substantive bans (secured financing, derivatives, short-term trading, short selling, hedging) and the prior approval requirement attach to this tier.

tiers.name: Directors and Officers
tiers.description: Directors and officers of Sims Limited, a listed sub-category of Restricted Employees. No separate rules or approver are specified for them.

tiers.name: Key Management Personnel
tiers.description: Persons named in Sims' Remuneration Report, a listed sub-category of Restricted Employees. No separate rules or approver are specified for them.

tiers.name: Executives
tiers.description: Members of Sims' Executive Leadership Team, a listed sub-category of Restricted Employees. No separate rules or approver are specified for them.

tiers.name: Company Secretary
tiers.description: The Company Secretary, who administers approvals for everyone else and must direct their own requests to deal, including exceptional circumstances requests, to the Chief Executive Officer.

tiers.name: Persons closely associated with Employees
tiers.description: Family members (spouse, civil partner, dependent children or stepchildren and relatives sharing the household for at least one year) and companies, trusts, partnerships or entities managed by, established for the benefit of, controlled directly or indirectly by, or whose economic interests are substantially equivalent to, the Employee or a family member. Subject to the same dealing restrictions as the Employee.

SGM.ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Sims Board may specify any other period as a black-out period from time to time. The policy does not state how such a period is communicated or whether the reason is confidential, though a refusal or revocation of approval must be kept confidential by the applicant.

rules.detail: A flat ban on trading in derivative products issued over or in respect of Sims' securities, with no venue limitation, so exchange-traded and OTC puts and calls are equally caught. No approval, waiver or exceptional circumstances route applies to this list of restricted dealings; the Company Secretary's approval power is directed at ordinary dealings and at black-out period sales.
rules.evidence: Restricted Employees must not undertake any of the following dealings with respect to Sims’ securities: ... trade in derivative products issued over or in respect of Sims’ securities;

rules.section: Insider Trading Restrictions; Other types of restricted dealings
rules.detail: The derivatives ban is expressed to bind Restricted Employees only. For other Employees, a derivative over Sims' securities is a dealing in 'financial instruments linked to' Sims' securities, so it is barred during black-out periods and while holding inside information, but no prior approval is required.
rules.evidence: dealing (including on behalf of a third party) in Sims’ securities, including in any shares, options or rights to shares, bonds or other forms of securitised debt, notes, depositary receipts and any financial instruments linked to them.

rules.detail: Absolute prohibition on hedging arrangements that limit exposure to Sims' securities. The policy draws no distinction between unvested plan securities, vested but restricted securities and freely held shares, so the ban covers all of them.
rules.evidence: enter into any hedging arrangements that limit exposure to Sims’ securities.

rules.detail: The hedging prohibition sits in the 'Other types of restricted dealings' section, which applies only to Restricted Employees. Hedging by other Employees is not addressed, and remains subject only to the insider trading prohibition and the black-out periods.

Monetisation, prepaid forwards and collars are not named. Any such structure is a derivative product in respect of Sims' securities and a hedging arrangement limiting exposure to them, and if it is funded it is also a secured financing arrangement, so it fails three of the five restricted dealing bullets at once.
rules.evidence: trade in derivative products issued over or in respect of Sims’ securities; ... enter into any hedging arrangements that limit exposure to Sims’ securities.

rules.detail: Short selling is prohibited outright for Restricted Employees, with no definition of the practice and no approval route. Not addressed for other Employees.

rules.section: Insider Trading Restrictions; Additional Dealing Restrictions on Restricted Employees
rules.detail: Securities lending is not named in the restricted dealings list. A stock loan is a transaction affecting title to, or an interest in, securities and involves transferring shares, so it is a dealing requiring the Company Secretary's prior written approval and is barred in black-out periods. Lending to facilitate a short position would also offend the short selling ban.
rules.evidence: Dealing includes any transaction or change affecting title to, or an interest in securities, such as buying, selling or transferring shares, using Sims’ shares as security for a loan and entering into an agreement (or exercising an option) to buy or sell securities.

rules.detail: Contracts for difference are not named, but a CFD is a derivative product issued in respect of Sims' securities and so falls within the derivatives ban; a short CFD would also breach the short selling prohibition.
rules.evidence: trade in derivative products issued over or in respect of Sims’ securities;

rules.detail: Margin loans in respect of Sims' securities are prohibited for Restricted Employees, with no grandfathering language, no approval route and no guidance on gearing levels, price triggers, margin calls or forced sales.

rules.detail: The ban is not limited to margin loans: 'other secured financing arrangements in respect of Sims' securities' captures a bespoke bank loan secured on the shares, whatever the lender or the loan to value ratio, and applies to vested and unvested holdings alike. SGM.exemption_authority: The Company Secretary (or delegate) may approve a sale, but not a purchase, during a black-out period in exceptional circumstances such as severe financial hardship (excluding tax liabilities) or compulsion by a court order, where the sale is the only reasonable course of action available; the Chief Executive Officer decides such requests from the Company Secretary. No provision permits any waiver of the 'other types of restricted dealings' prohibitions on secured financing, derivatives, hedging, short selling or short-term trading.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Employees must not ... enter into margin loans or other secured financing arrangements in respect of Sims’ securities;
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar, secured on the collared shares, is prohibited outright for every director, officer, KMP and executive, with no approval or hardship route.

bespoke_clauses.topic: derivatives ban with no venue limit
bespoke_clauses.clause: trade in derivative products issued over or in respect of Sims’ securities;
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The purchased put and written call are derivative products in respect of Sims' securities, so the protective legs are prohibited regardless of whether they are exchange-traded or written OTC by a bank.

bespoke_clauses.clause: enter into any hedging arrangements that limit exposure to Sims’ securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The prohibition is not confined to unvested or plan securities, so even a collar over long-held, freely tradeable shares is caught.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Dealing includes any transaction or change affecting title to, or an interest in securities, such as buying, selling or transferring shares, using Sims’ shares as security for a loan and entering into an agreement (or exercising an option) to buy or sell securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Granting the bank security over the shares is itself a dealing, so it is caught by black-out periods and the approval process even before the secured financing ban is reached.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The exceptional circumstances mechanism permits an Employee 'who need[s] to sell (but not buy) Sims’ securities during a black-out period' to seek approval; nothing in the policy permits approval of a restricted dealing.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even severe financial hardship gives access only to a sale during a black-out period, never to a collar or a secured loan, so there is no route to the structure at all.

bespoke_clauses.topic: restrictions follow the tier, not the person
bespoke_clauses.clause: there are certain Employees that will be notified by the Company Secretary that they are restricted employees ... Restricted Employees include: Directors and Officers ... Key Management Personnel ... Executives
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bans bite on exactly the population a bank would target for a funded collar, while ordinary employees, who face no such bans, are not a commercially relevant client group.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Persons closely associated with Employees (including Restricted Employees) are subject to the same dealing restrictions that apply to that Employee ... companies, trusts, partnerships or entities ... the economic interests of which are substantially equivalent to the Employee or a family member.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The economic equivalence limb defeats any attempt to place the collar or the loan in a family trust, controlled company or other vehicle.

bespoke_clauses.clause: How would it look if the transaction were reported on the front page of the newspaper?
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even for a dealing that is not prohibited, the Company Secretary applies a reputational perception test, and a director hedging their exposure would rarely survive it.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Upon receipt of approval, complete the dealing within two business days (commencing the day after approval is provided) otherwise approval must be sought again. ... Approval to deal can be withdrawn if circumstances change.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any permitted dealing must be documented and executed inside two business days and approval can be withdrawn, which would be impractical for a negotiated derivative even if one were permitted.

SGM.summary: A funded collar is not possible for any Sims director, officer, KMP or executive. The 'Other types of restricted dealings' section prohibits Restricted Employees from entering margin loans or other secured financing arrangements in respect of Sims' securities, from trading in derivative products issued over or in respect of Sims' securities, and from entering any hedging arrangements that limit exposure to them, so every element of the structure is separately banned. The bans apply to all holdings without distinguishing vested from unvested shares, extend to persons closely associated including controlled trusts and entities whose economic interests are substantially equivalent, and carry no approval, waiver or grandfathering route. The Company Secretary's exceptional circumstances power reaches only a sale, not a purchase, during a black-out period, so it cannot authorise a collar or a secured loan. Only Employees who are not Restricted Employees escape these bans, and for them a derivative or a share-secured loan is merely a dealing subject to the black-out periods and the insider trading prohibition.

EMR.title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Staff
tiers.description: EMR Directors, Key Management Personnel, officers, employees and consultants. The insider trading prohibition, the blackout periods, board suspensions, the six month short-term trading ban and the section 11 hedge contract ban all apply to this tier.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: EMR Directors. Must obtain written approval from the Chairman for all dealings in EMR securities, must notify the Company Secretary within five business days for Listing Rule 3.19A and 3.19B purposes, and are prohibited from margin lending arrangements.

tiers.name: Chairman
tiers.description: The Chairman of the EMR board, who approves other Directors' and the Company Secretary's dealings and financial hardship blackout trading, and whose own dealings require written approval from the Managing Director.

tiers.name: Key Management Personnel
tiers.description: Key Management Personnel other than the Company Secretary. Must obtain written approval from the Managing Director for all dealings and provide written confirmation to the Company Secretary once the dealing has taken place; prohibited from margin lending arrangements.

tiers.name: Company Secretary
tiers.description: The Company Secretary, treated with Directors for approval purposes: written advice to, and written approval from, the Chairman for all dealings in EMR securities.

tiers.name: Associated parties
tiers.description: A Staff member's spouse or partner, any dependent child, family company or family trust, and trusts of which Staff are trustees that invest in EMR securities. The policy applies equally to their dealings and Staff must so far as they are able prevent dealings at a time when they themselves are not free to deal.

definitions.hedging_definition: 'hedge contracts' or other forms of arrangements which may have the effect of fixing the value of, or return on, securities which form part of the incentive component of their remuneration or salary package (whether the securities are fully vested or not)

EMR.ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The EMR board or the Managing Director may impose a suspension on the ability of Staff to trade at a time when trading might otherwise have been allowed, generally only in exceptional circumstances, and will endeavour to keep it to the shortest possible period. The policy does not say whether the existence or the reason for a suspension is confidential.

rules.detail: There is no derivatives rule. 'EMR securities' means shares, rights and options in EMR or associated companies, which is capable of covering an option over EMR shares written by a bank but does not clearly extend to a cash-settled OTC contract. Directors and the Company Secretary need the Chairman's written approval for all dealings in EMR securities, so an OTC put or call would on the wider reading require approval and be barred in blackout periods and suspensions.
rules.evidence: In the case of Directors and the Company Secretary, written advice must be given to, and written approval obtained from, the Chairman in respect of all dealings in EMR securities.

rules.detail: The policy contains no rule on derivatives, defines no term 'dealing', and imposes no approval requirement on Staff other than Directors, the Company Secretary and Key Management Personnel. For such Staff a derivative over EMR shares is constrained only by the insider trading prohibition, the blackout periods and, for incentive securities, the section 11 hedge contract ban.

Hedge contracts and other arrangements that may fix the value of or return on unvested incentive securities are prohibited for all Staff, covering both LTI plan securities and other securities issued as incentive remuneration such as sign-on or retention grants under employment agreements. No approval or waiver route is provided.
rules.evidence: EMR Staff are not permitted to enter into 'hedge contracts' or other forms of arrangements which may have the effect of fixing the value of, or return on, securities which form part of the incentive component of their remuneration or salary package (whether the securities are fully vested or not).

rules.detail: The ban follows the securities rather than their vesting state: incentive securities remain within it after they have fully vested. In practice any share traceable to an LTI grant or to incentive remuneration is permanently off limits for hedging, however long it has been held.
rules.evidence: securities which form part of the incentive component of their remuneration or salary package (whether the securities are fully vested or not). This not only includes EMR securities issued under the LTI plans but also other EMR securities issued by way of incentive remuneration

rules.detail: Shares that are not part of the incentive component of remuneration, such as shares bought on market or acquired in a placement or rights issue, fall outside the section 11 ban, which is expressed only by reference to incentive securities. Hedging such shares is not addressed anywhere in the policy.

For a Director or the Company Secretary, hedging non-incentive shares is not prohibited but, if it involves a dealing in EMR securities, it requires the Chairman's prior written approval (the Managing Director's, for the Chairman) and cannot occur in a blackout period or during a board suspension.
rules.evidence: In all cases, approval is to be given by the Chairman or Managing Director acting in accordance with this policy.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. Over incentive securities, a prepaid forward, collar or similar structure is an arrangement that may have the effect of fixing the value of or return on those securities and is prohibited by section 11. Over other securities it is not prohibited as such, but if the structure advances loaned monies supported by security over or transfer of EMR securities it becomes a margin lending arrangement barred to Directors and Key Management Personnel.
rules.evidence: not permitted to enter into 'hedge contracts' or other forms of arrangements which may have the effect of fixing the value of, or return on, securities which form part of the incentive component of their remuneration or salary package

rules.detail: Short selling is nowhere mentioned. The closest provision is the section 8 speculative trading ban, which is framed around purchase followed by sale rather than sale followed by purchase, although its parenthetical does capture a sale and subsequent purchase within six months.

Securities lending is not mentioned. A transfer of EMR securities is caught by the section 9 margin lending definition only where it supports loaned monies, which a stock loan for a fee would not ordinarily involve.

Contracts for difference are not mentioned. A CFD used to fix the return on incentive securities would be caught by the section 11 hedge contract ban, and a CFD entered by a Director or KMP might require approval as a dealing in EMR securities, but the instrument itself is not addressed.

An outright ban with no approval, hardship or exceptional circumstances route. The definition is deliberately wide and substance-based, catching any arrangement in the nature of loaned monies secured or otherwise supported by security over or transfer of EMR securities, regardless of form.
rules.evidence: Directors and Key Management Personnel are prohibited from entering into any dealing in EMR securities where such margin lending arrangements apply.

rules.detail: Key Management Personnel are subject to the same outright ban as Directors, with no distinction between vested and unvested securities and no waiver power.
rules.evidence: Margin lending refers to any arrangement which is in the nature of, or parties intend it to be in the nature of, loaned monies which are secured or are otherwise supported by a security over, or transfer of, EMR securities (regardless of the form the security or transfer takes).

rules.detail: Section 9 binds only Directors and Key Management Personnel. Officers, employees and consultants who are not KMP are not prohibited from margin lending and no notification or approval is required of them.

Granting security over, or transferring, EMR securities to support loaned monies is expressly within the margin lending definition and so prohibited for Directors and Key Management Personnel, whatever legal form the security or transfer takes. A charge or lien unconnected with borrowed money is not addressed.
rules.evidence: loaned monies which are secured or are otherwise supported by a security over, or transfer of, EMR securities (regardless of the form the security or transfer takes)

rules.detail: For Staff who are neither Directors nor Key Management Personnel, granting security over EMR securities is not addressed and requires no approval or notification.

Although headed 'Margin lending', section 9 operates as a general secured financing ban: it captures any arrangement in the nature of loaned monies secured or otherwise supported by EMR securities, so a bespoke bank facility secured on the shares, or a title-transfer collateral arrangement, is prohibited for Directors.
rules.evidence: Margin lending refers to any arrangement which is in the nature of, or parties intend it to be in the nature of, loaned monies which are secured or are otherwise supported by a security over, or transfer of, EMR securities (regardless of the form the security or transfer takes).

rules.detail: The same general secured financing ban applies to Key Management Personnel, and there is no exemption authority anywhere in the policy that could relieve it.
rules.evidence: Directors and Key Management Personnel are prohibited from entering into any dealing in EMR securities where such margin lending arrangements apply.

rules.detail: Six month intention-based test covering purchase with a view to selling or otherwise dealing, and expressly including a sale and subsequent purchase. Sales of shares converted on exercise of options or rights are excluded, and the Chairman or Managing Director may waive the prohibition in some circumstances.
rules.evidence: EMR's policy is also that Staff shall not engage in speculative trading whereby EMR securities are purchased with a view to selling or otherwise dealing (including by way of a sale and subsequent purchase) in those securities within a 6 month period.

clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary, in writing, to enable EMR to satisfy Listing Rules 3.19A and 3.19B
clearance.post_trade_deadline: as soon as practicable, but in any event within five business days of the dealing
clearance.evidence: In the case of Directors and the Company Secretary, written advice must be given to, and written approval obtained from, the Chairman in respect of all dealings in EMR securities.

clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary, in writing, to enable EMR to satisfy Listing Rules 3.19A and 3.19B
clearance.post_trade_deadline: as soon as practicable, but in any event within five business days of the dealing
clearance.evidence: In the case of the Chairman, written advice must be given to, and written approval obtained from, the Managing Director in respect of all dealings in EMR securities.

clearance.approver: Chairman
clearance.evidence: In all cases, approval is to be given by the Chairman or Managing Director acting in accordance with this policy.

clearance.approver: Managing Director
clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary (written confirmation that the dealing has taken place)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: when the dealing has taken place; no deadline stated
clearance.evidence: In the case of Key Management Personnel (excluding the Company Secretary) written advice must be given to, and written approval obtained from, the Managing Director in respect of all dealings in EMR securities. Key Management Personnel are to provide written confirmation to the Company Secretary when the dealing has taken place.

Unless in possession of price sensitive information at the time of trading, Staff may generally trade EMR securities except: in a blackout referred to below, or if EMR suspends trading as referred to in section 6 above.

short_term.basis: from purchase, including a sale and subsequent purchase
carve_outs: the sale of shares that have been converted after exercising options or rights
circumstances waived by the Chairman of the EMR board or the Managing Director, for example the exercise of options or rights granted under the EMR Long-Term Incentive (LTI) Plans
short_term.evidence: However, the sale of shares that have been converted after exercising options or rights will not be regarded as short term trading.

exceptions.approver: Chairman (written approval)
exceptions.evidence: Only in cases of financial hardship can Staff trade EMR securities in a blackout period and in these circumstances written approval must be received from the Chairman.
an undertaking to accept, or acceptance of a takeover offer;
transfers in EMR securities already held by staff into a superannuation fund in which that person is a beneficiary;

dealings under an offer or invitation made to all or most of the shareholders of EMR, such as a rights issue, a security purchase plan or a dividend or dividend reinvestment plan approved by the Board;
the cancellation, lapsing or surrender of an option or right under an LTI plan; and
an investment in, or trading in units of a fund (other than a fund only investing in EMR securities) where the assets of the fund are invested at the discretion of the third party.

exceptions.approver: Chairman of the EMR board or the Managing Director
exceptions.evidence: This prohibition on short-term trading may be waived by the Chairman of the EMR board or the Managing Director in some circumstances (e.g. exercise of options or rights granted under the EMR Long-Term Incentive (LTI) Plans).

external_documents: EMR Long-Term Incentive (LTI) Plans
Employment agreements under which EMR securities are issued as incentive remuneration
EMR.exemption_authority: Limited and specific. The Chairman may give written approval for Staff to trade in a blackout period, but only in cases of financial hardship (section 7). The Chairman or the Managing Director may waive the six month short-term trading prohibition in some circumstances (section 8). The EMR board or Managing Director may impose or lift a trading suspension (section 6). There is no power anywhere to waive the section 9 margin lending prohibition or the section 11 hedge contract prohibition.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Margin lending refers to any arrangement which is in the nature of, or parties intend it to be in the nature of, loaned monies which are secured or are otherwise supported by a security over, or transfer of, EMR securities (regardless of the form the security or transfer takes).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The definition is drafted to defeat form-based structuring, so a bespoke bank loan, a limited recourse facility or a title transfer collateral arrangement supporting the collar is all margin lending and prohibited for Directors and KMP.

bespoke_clauses.topic: prohibition bites on the dealing, not just the loan
bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and Key Management Personnel are prohibited from entering into any dealing in EMR securities where such margin lending arrangements apply.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: It is the dealing itself that is banned once a margin lending arrangement applies, so the collar legs and the pledge fall together with the loan rather than being severable from it.

bespoke_clauses.clause: EMR Staff are not permitted to enter into 'hedge contracts' or other forms of arrangements which may have the effect of fixing the value of, or return on, securities which form part of the incentive component of their remuneration or salary package (whether the securities are fully vested or not).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any share traceable to an LTI grant or to incentive remuneration can never be collared, however long ago it vested, so only shares bought or subscribed for independently are candidates.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The policy contains no general hedging, derivatives or short selling prohibition; section 11 is confined to incentive securities and section 9 to margin lending.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An unfunded collar over shares that a Director bought on market is not prohibited, and would need only the Chairman's written approval outside a blackout period; the funding leg is what makes the structure impossible.

bespoke_clauses.clause: In all cases, approval is to be given by the Chairman or Managing Director acting in accordance with this policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no stated validity period, response time, revocation right or condition-imposing power, so the parties must agree contractually how long an approval is treated as good for.

bespoke_clauses.clause: there may be occasions when the EMR board imposes a suspension on the ability of Staff to trade at a time when trading might otherwise have been allowed ... If a suspension occurs, Staff must not trade while the suspension is in force.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An ad hoc suspension can block entry, roll, unwind or physical settlement at any time, and only financial hardship approval by the Chairman relieves a blackout, not a suspension.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the blackout period starts 10 business days before the planned date for release of the relevant quarterly report ... and ends on the business day after the day of release
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: As a quarterly reporting explorer EMR has four blackout periods a year rather than two, materially narrowing the windows in which a collar could be entered or unwound.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Staff shall not engage in speculative trading whereby EMR securities are purchased with a view to selling or otherwise dealing (including by way of a sale and subsequent purchase) in those securities within a 6 month period.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Tenor should exceed six months, and shares recently acquired should not be collared, since the arrangement could be read as purchase with a view to otherwise dealing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This Policy applies equally to any dealings in EMR securities by a Staff's spouse, partner or by or on behalf of any dependent child, family company or family trust.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Placing the shares, the pledge or the derivative in a family company or trust does not avoid the margin lending or hedge contract prohibitions.

EMR.summary: A funded collar is not possible for an EMR Director or Key Management Personnel, because the funding leg is prohibited. Section 9 defines margin lending in substance rather than form, as any arrangement in the nature of loaned monies secured or otherwise supported by a security over, or transfer of, EMR securities regardless of the form the security or transfer takes, and bars Directors and KMP from entering into any dealing in EMR securities where such an arrangement applies, with no waiver power. The derivative legs are separately impossible over any share that forms part of the incentive component of remuneration, since section 11 bans hedge contracts and arrangements fixing the value of or return on those securities whether or not they have fully vested. An unfunded collar over shares acquired independently of incentive remuneration is not prohibited and would need only the Chairman's prior written approval (the Managing Director's, for the Chairman), taken outside the four quarterly blackout periods and any board suspension, with notification to the Company Secretary within five business days and a tenor beyond the six month speculative trading rule. Staff who are neither Directors nor KMP are outside section 9 altogether, but they are not the relevant client group.

ATM.company: Perusahaan Perseroan (Persero) PT Aneka Tambang Tbk (PT Antam (Persero) Tbk)
ATM.title: Corporate Securities Trading Policy (Annex to Decision of the Board of Directors Number 38.K/09/DAT/2008)
ATM.date_approved: 18 February 2008 (Board of Directors of PT Antam (Persero) Tbk, Decision Number 38.K/09/DAT/2008, stipulated in Jakarta)
ATM.date_next_review: No fixed date; the Policy 'will be renewed from time to time' and the Corporate Secretary division must revise it when necessary to adapt to changes in laws and regulations

tiers.name: Company Insiders
tiers.description: Commissioners, directors or employees of the Company; major shareholders; individuals who by their position, profession or business relation with the Company are allowed to gain Insider Information; and any party who ceased to be such within the past 6 months. 'Position' means office in government organisations, institutes or bodies; 'business relation' includes customer, supplier, contractor, client and creditor relationships. Every substantive prohibition in the Policy attaches to this tier without differentiation.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Company Directors, a defined term in the General Provisions and a listed category of Company Insider. No separate rules, approver or reporting deadline is specified for them.

tiers.name: Special Relationship
tiers.description: An individual or body considered as having a special relationship with the Company: an employee of the Company, or a person who has, or submits a proposal in order to have, a business relationship or professional activity with or for the interest of the Company or its subsidiaries.

tiers.name: consultants, brokers, and other people interacting with the company
tiers.description: Consultants, brokers and other people interacting with the Company, its units or subsidiaries, including sales agents and partners in joint ventures, who gain or have access to Material Non-public Information or Fact. The Policy applies to them as it does to Company Insiders.

tiers.name: families, including all their close relatives
tiers.description: Families, including all close relatives, of persons within the scope of the Policy. Those persons are responsible for ensuring their families' compliance with the Policy. The Policy does not name spouses, dependants, trusts or controlled entities specifically.

ATM.ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Company Securities Trading Compliance Supervisory Officer (the Senior Vice President Corporate Secretary, or the Assistant Senior Manager Investor Relations in their absence) decides and announces special trading blackout periods in which no Company Insider at all may trade, and the company also applies a Blackout Period in certain situations where changes result in Material Information or Facts. These are confidential: Company Insiders are not allowed to disclose to any outside party that a certain blackout period has been determined. The Company may also ask Insiders not to trade for a particular reason outside a routine Blackout Period, which is why every trade must be reported in advance.

rules.detail: An outright ban on option or position trading referable to the future price of Company Securities, naming puts and calls. There is no venue limitation, no exception for hedging an existing holding, and no approval or waiver route: the Policy's only procedural gateway is advance reporting of permitted trades, not approval of prohibited ones. The definition of Company Securities is limited to instruments issued by the Company, but clause 5(e) operates on positions 'in relation to' their future price and so reaches derivatives written by a bank.
rules.evidence: Every Company Insider is prohibited to conduct option or position trading in relation to the future (future price) of Company Securities such as put, call, or short sale.

rules.detail: The Policy never uses the words hedging or economic risk and has no clause directed at protecting a shareholding. Hedging is nonetheless caught because the instruments used to do it, puts and calls, are the very positions banned by clause 5(e). No distinction is drawn between unvested plan securities, vested restricted securities and freely held shares.
rules.evidence: prohibited to conduct option or position trading in relation to the future (future price) of Company Securities such as put, call, or short sale.

rules.detail: Monetisation, prepaid forwards and exchangeables are not named. Such a structure is a 'position' taken in relation to the future price of Company Securities and so falls within clause 5(e); an outright sale of shares to raise cash remains permitted in a trading window on advance report.
rules.evidence: Every Company Insider is prohibited to conduct option or position trading in relation to the future (future price) of Company Securities

rules.detail: Short sale is named in the same clause as puts and calls and is prohibited at all times, in and out of trading windows, with no approval route.
rules.evidence: such as put, call, or short sale.

rules.detail: Securities lending is nowhere mentioned and there is no defined term 'dealing' that could sweep it in. The nearest provision is clause 5(f), which bars an Insider from giving or causing anyone to transfer Company Securities during a period in which they are not allowed to trade, so a stock loan delivery inside a blackout would be caught by that clause.

Contracts for difference are not named, but a CFD is a position taken in relation to the future price of Company Securities and, if short, is also a short sale, so it is prohibited on both limbs of clause 5(e).
rules.evidence: Every Company Insider is prohibited to conduct option or position trading in relation to the future (future price) of Company Securities such as put, call, or short sale.

rules.detail: Margin lending is not mentioned anywhere in the Policy. There is no prohibition, no approval requirement, no gearing or price trigger guidance, and no disclosure obligation, though the Policy's advance reporting requirement would apply to any trade in Company Securities associated with such an arrangement.

Granting security, a charge, lien or pledge over Company Securities is not addressed and is not within any definition. Clause 5(f) does prohibit an Insider from giving or causing anyone to transfer Company Securities during a period in which they may not trade, which would bite on a transfer of legal title to a collateral holder inside a blackout period.

The Policy contains no provision on borrowing against Company Securities, whether by margin loan or bespoke facility, and no reporting obligation attaches to the grant of security. This is a genuine gap rather than a permission: the trading and derivative prohibitions still govern any dealing in the shares themselves.

There is no minimum holding period, no LIFO or buy-sell window rule and no speculative trading prohibition. Timing is controlled solely by the trading window and blackout period structure, which in practice confines trading to the weeks after each quarterly or annual results dissemination.

ATM.exemption_authority: None. The Policy provides no hardship, court order, exceptional circumstances or discretionary waiver of any prohibition. The Company Securities Trading Compliance Supervisory Officer administers and interprets the Policy, answers questions, decides and announces special blackout periods and revises the Policy, but is given no power to permit a prohibited activity; clause 8(a) merely recognises that higher law may displace the Policy's restrictions.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Every Company Insider is prohibited to conduct option or position trading in relation to the future (future price) of Company Securities such as put, call, or short sale.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Both legs of a collar, the purchased put and the written call, are named prohibited positions, so the derivative side of the structure is impossible for any Insider with no approval route.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Company Insiders include: commissioners, directors, or employees of the Company; Major shareholders of the Company; Individuals who, due to their position or profession or to their business relation with the Company, are allowed to gain Insider Information; or Any parties which, within the past 6 (six) months, no longer become any Party referred to above. 'Business relation' ... includes customer relation, supplier, contractor, client, and creditor.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bank that becomes a creditor of the Company could itself fall within the Insider definition, and a departing executive remains an Insider for six months, so the prohibition follows the client past resignation.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Every Company Insider is prohibited to give or cause anyone to transfer Company Securities during a period where they are not allowed to conduct trading.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Delivery of collateral, physical settlement or a financier's enforcement sale occurring inside a blackout would be an Insider causing a transfer when not permitted to trade, and there is no lender enforcement carve-out.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Company Insiders are not allowed to disclose to any outside party that a certain blackout period has been determined.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A client cannot tell a bank why an execution, roll or unwind is being delayed, so a facility must tolerate unexplained inability to act.

bespoke_clauses.topic: quarterly closed periods with open-ended end
bespoke_clauses.clause: Blackout period commences on 30 March, 29 June, 29 September, and 30 December every year and ends when the company disseminates information which previously is non-public information.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Four blackouts a year, each of indeterminate length because it ends only on results dissemination, leaves narrow and unpredictable windows for any transaction in the shares.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Policy contains no reference to margin lending, secured financing, pledges, charges or securities lending.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg secured on the shares is neither prohibited nor regulated, so it is governed only by Indonesian law and the Company's other rules, and a bank would need separate confirmation from the Corporate Secretary rather than reliance on this Policy.

bespoke_clauses.clause: every trading of Company Securities by Company Insiders must be reported in advance to the Company Securities Trading Compliance Supervisory Officer. ... Company Insiders are required to report/confirm to the Company Securities Trading Compliance Supervisory Officer after a Company Securities trading transaction has been done.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The regime is notification rather than approval, with no validity period or response time, so any permitted share transaction supporting a financing must be pre-notified with reasons and confirmed afterwards.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The parties included in the scope of this Policy are also responsible for ensuring the compliance of their families, including all their close relatives with this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The prohibitions cannot be avoided by placing the position with a family member, although the Policy does not extend expressly to trusts or controlled companies.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Policy is a 2008 board decision translated from Indonesian, with no review date, no derivatives or financing framework and no cross-reference to ASX Listing Rule 12.12 content requirements.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Its silences should be treated as gaps to be checked with the Corporate Secretary rather than as permissions, and a bank should confirm no later Indonesian or ASX-facing policy supersedes it.

ATM.summary: A funded collar is not possible for a PT Antam Company Insider, because the derivative legs are expressly banned. Clause 5(e) prohibits every Company Insider from conducting option or position trading in relation to the future price of Company Securities, naming put, call and short sale, with no venue limitation, no distinction between vested and unvested holdings and no approval, hardship or exceptional circumstances waiver anywhere in the Policy. The funding leg is a different matter: margin lending, secured financing, pledges and securities lending are simply not addressed, so a loan secured on the shares is unregulated by this Policy, though clause 5(f) prohibits an Insider from giving or causing anyone to transfer Company Securities during a period in which they may not trade, which would catch collateral delivery or an enforcement sale inside a blackout. Any permitted transaction in the shares themselves must fall in a trading window, outside the blackouts commencing 30 March, 29 June, 29 September and 30 December and outside any confidential special blackout, and must be reported in advance to the Company Securities Trading Compliance Supervisory Officer with reasons and confirmed afterwards. Given the Policy's age, its translation from Indonesian and its silence on financing, a bank should verify the position with the Corporate Secretary rather than infer permission from the gaps.

rules.detail: Derivatives are not named as a category requiring approval, but 'deal' includes entering into an agreement to buy or sell securities and exercising options over securities, so a physically settled OTC put and written call over Company shares is a dealing requiring prior approval and is barred in blackout periods. No venue limitation appears anywhere in the policy, and the Company applies a substance over form approach.

rules.detail: Absolute ban, with no approval or exceptional-circumstances route, on hedging securities acquired under any employee, executive or Director equity plan before vesting. Applies to every TWE Person, not only Restricted Persons.
rules.evidence: Company securities acquired under an employee, executive or Director equity plan operated by the Company must never be hedged prior to vesting.

rules.detail: Vested plan securities that remain subject to a holding lock or a dealing restriction under the plan terms may never be hedged. The plan rules that create those locks are not part of the policy, so the collarable pool depends on external plan documents.

rules.evidence: In addition, members of the ELT must notify the Chief Sustainability and External Affairs Officer if they enter into a derivative or hedging arrangement over any other Company securities.

rules.detail: ELT members must notify the Chief Sustainability and External Affairs Officer of a hedging arrangement over vested unrestricted Company securities. No deadline, form or content is specified for the notification, and it sits on top of the 5.2 approval requirement.

rules.detail: The hedging prohibitions are confined to unvested and locked plan securities; hedging other Company securities is left permitted, with a notification duty imposed only on ELT members and an approval duty only on Restricted Persons.
rules.evidence: Company securities acquired under an employee, executive or Director equity plan operated by the Company must never be hedged prior to vesting.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward, collar-plus-loan or similar structure is an agreement to sell securities and so a dealing requiring prior approval. It is also an arrangement that limits economic risk, so the 4.4 hedging bans apply to the underlying shares, and section 4.3 gives 'forward contracts' as an example of prohibited short-term dealing.
rules.evidence: Short-term trading includes buying and selling securities on market within a 3 month period and entering into other short term dealings (for example, forward contracts).

rules.detail: Short selling is banned outright for all TWE People as a species of speculative dealing, and is defined as borrowing and selling securities to buy them back lower. There is no approval or exceptional-circumstances route.
rules.evidence: TWE People must not deal in the Company's securities on a speculative basis, including short-selling.

rules.detail: Securities lending is not regulated. Borrowing securities is mentioned only in the descriptive definition of short selling, and lending out Company shares is neither named nor caught by the definition of dealing.

CFDs are not named. A CFD over Company securities would be dealing on a speculative basis and, if short, would fall within the short-selling ban; a Restricted Person would in any event need approval that could not be given if the Front Page Test failed.
rules.evidence: TWE People must not deal in the Company's securities on a speculative basis, including short-selling.

rules.detail: The ban is purpose-limited: it catches only margin loans or similar funding arrangements entered into to acquire Company securities. A loan whose proceeds are not applied to acquire Company securities is outside the words of 5.5, even if Company securities secure it.
rules.evidence: No Director or member of the ELT may enter into a margin loan or similar funding arrangement to acquire any Company securities.

rules.detail: Same purpose-limited ban as for Directors. It does not extend to other Restricted Persons or to other TWE People.
rules.evidence: No Director or member of the ELT may enter into a margin loan or similar funding arrangement to acquire any Company securities.

rules.detail: Section 5.5 binds only Directors and ELT members. Margin lending by other Restricted Persons and other employees is not restricted, and section 6(f) assumes margin lending arrangements over Company securities may exist.

Granting security, a charge, mortgage or pledge over Company securities is nowhere named, is not within the definition of dealing (which is limited to acquiring, disposing and agreeing to acquire or dispose), and produces no change in beneficial interest. There is no disclosure obligation for encumbered shares.

There is no general secured financing prohibition. The only funding restriction is the Director and ELT ban on margin loans or similar arrangements to acquire Company securities, and section 6(f) expressly contemplates a secured lender holding and enforcing over Company securities. A loan secured on already-held vested shares is therefore not prohibited.
rules.evidence: a disposal of securities of the Company that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.

rules.detail: A buy-sell window test of three months, extended by an open-ended prohibition on 'other short term dealings' with forward contracts given as the example. Selling shares within three months of vesting under an equity plan is carved out. This is the clause most likely to be read against a short-dated or forward-settled collar.
rules.evidence: TWE People must not deal in the Company's securities on a short-term trading basis. Short-term trading includes buying and selling securities on market within a 3 month period and entering into other short term dealings (for example, forward contracts).

bespoke_clauses.clause: No Director or member of the ELT may enter into a margin loan or similar funding arrangement to acquire any Company securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The only funding prohibition bites on borrowing used to acquire Company shares, so a loan secured on shares the executive already owns, drawn to fund something else, is outside the ban on its literal terms, though a bank should expect the substance over form clause to be raised if the facility is characterised as a share-funding arrangement.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Sections 4.3, 5.1 and 5.2 of this Policy do not apply to ... a disposal of securities of the Company that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Enforcement by the bank over the collared shares, including in a blackout period, is an excluded dealing needing no approval, which removes the enforcement risk that defeats a funded collar under most other ASX policies.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Short-term trading includes buying and selling securities on market within a 3 month period and entering into other short term dealings (for example, forward contracts).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Forwards are singled out as the example of a prohibited short term dealing, so a collar should have a tenor comfortably beyond three months and avoid a forward-sale characterisation or early termination triggers.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Company securities must never be hedged while they are subject to a holding lock or restriction on dealing under the terms of an employee, executive or Director equity plan operated by the Company.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The collarable pool is defined by plan documents outside the policy, so the bank must confirm from the plan rules and the register that the specific parcel is vested and lock-free.

bespoke_clauses.topic: substance over form and Front Page Test
bespoke_clauses.clause: The Company will take a substance over form approach and will have regard to the intent and spirit of this Policy when applying and enforcing it. ... Where any approval is required for a dealing under this Policy, approval will not be granted where the dealing would not satisfy the Front Page Test.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Approval for a collar can be refused purely on perception grounds even where no rule is broken, and a structure that looks like a disguised sale or a disguised margin loan can be treated as one.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The approver is not obliged to provide reasons for any aspect of their decision, and may revoke their approval at any time. ... the approved dealing must occur as soon as possible, and no later than 3 business days following approval.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Pricing, documentation and execution of both collar legs must complete inside three business days of approval, and the approval can be withdrawn up to signing without reasons.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons must take appropriate steps to ensure that their Connected Persons only deal in securities in circumstances where the Restricted Person to whom they are connected would be permitted to deal under this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Holding the shares through a controlled company or family trust does not avoid the approval requirement or the hedging bans.

bespoke_clauses.clause: TWE People must not deal in the Company's securities if ... the Company has notified TWE People that they must not deal in securities (either for a specified period, or until the Company gives further notice).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An open-ended company notice can block entry, roll or unwind of a collar at any time, and it binds all employees, not just Restricted Persons.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Certain parts of this Policy apply only to Restricted Persons.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Blackout periods and prior approval do not apply to employees outside the Restricted Persons list, so for them a collar over vested unrestricted shares needs no company consent at all.

TWE.summary: A funded collar is realistically possible for a TWE director or executive over vested shares that are free of any plan holding lock. Both derivative legs are a dealing, so a Restricted Person needs prior written approval from the section 5.4 approvers (Chairman and CEO for a Director), obtained outside the 30 June, 31 December and pre-AGM blackout periods, executed within three business days, revocable at will and refusable on Front Page Test grounds alone; an ELT member must also notify the Chief Sustainability and External Affairs Officer of the hedge, and a Director must report the trade the same day. The loan leg is the unusual strength of this policy: there is no general secured financing or encumbrance prohibition, section 5.5 bans only margin loans or similar arrangements entered into to acquire Company securities, and section 6(f) expressly treats a secured lender's enforcement sale as an excluded dealing, so bank enforcement even in a blackout period is contemplated. The principal risks are the section 4.3 short-term dealing ban, which gives forward contracts as its example and argues for a tenor well beyond three months and against forward-sale characterisation, and the substance over form clause, under which a collar-plus-loan could be recast as a margin-style share funding arrangement. Shares that are unvested or subject to a plan holding lock can never form part of the collared parcel, and no hardship or exemption power can waive that.

rules.detail: There is no express derivatives rule, but Securities is defined to include rights to acquire or dispose of securities and derivatives and other financial products under section 1042A whose value is linked to Ventia securities, with no venue limitation, and Dealing includes buying, selling or agreeing to buy or sell a Security. Dealings that result in no effective change to the beneficial interest in the Securities (for example, transfers of Company securities already held into a superannuation fund or trust of which the Employee is a beneficiary);

trading under a pre-approved non-discretionary trading plan, where the Group Employee did not enter into the plan or amend the plan during a Blackout Period, the plan does not permit the Group Employee to exercise any influence or discretion in relation to trading under the plan and the plan cannot be cancelled during a Blackout Period
a disposal of Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.
