The written 'Clearance to Trade' request form referred to in section 4.4
VNT.exemption_authority: The section 4.2 exceptional circumstances route only: a Restricted Person may apply through the Group Company Secretary for approval to Deal in a Blackout Period on evidence of severe financial hardship or compulsion by court order, and the section 4.4 approver decides. There is no power to waive the section 3.4 hedging prohibitions or the section 3.3 speculative and short-term dealing ban, and any dealing allowed under section 4.2 must still comply with the rest of the Policy.
jurisdiction_overlays: New Zealand Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 (insider conduct, and section 260 trading plan requirements for securities listed on the NZX main board)
NZX Listing Rules disclosure of Directors' dealings

bespoke_clauses.clause: Approval must be obtained in accordance with the procedure set out in section 4.4 for any: entering into a margin lending arrangement in respect of Securities; and transferring Securities in Ventia into an existing margin loan account.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Ventia regulates rather than prohibits borrowing against its shares, so the loan leg of a funded collar has an approval pathway instead of an outright bar, and the same approval route covers moving existing shares into a lender's account.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Ventia may, at its discretion, make any approval granted in accordance with section 4.4 conditional upon such terms and conditions as Ventia sees fit (for example, with regard to the circumstances in which Securities may be sold to satisfy a margin call).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The company can dictate the enforcement mechanics of the facility as a condition of approval, so a bank should expect its close-out and top-up rights to be negotiated with Ventia before the facility is signed.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Sections 3.3, 4.1 and 4.3 of this Policy do not apply to ... a disposal of Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Enforcement by the bank over the collared shares, including during a Blackout Period, is an Excluded Dealing needing no clearance, which materially de-risks the security package.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Securities means ... any rights to subscribe for, acquire or dispose of securities (including future contracts, options, performance rights, share rights or other interests); derivatives and other financial products covered by section 1042A ... whose price or value is linked to the price or value of any of the securities referred to in (i) to (v) above.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no venue limitation, so an OTC put and call written with a bank are themselves Securities and dealing in them is squarely within the clearance requirement and the Blackout Periods.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Short-term trading includes buying and selling Securities on market within a 3 month period, and entering into other short term dealings (for example, forward contracts).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Forwards are the named example of prohibited short term dealing, so a collar should run well beyond three months and avoid a prepaid-forward characterisation or short-dated roll structure.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The approver is not obliged to provide reasons for any aspect of their decision and may revoke their approval at any time prior to the Dealing. ... the approved Dealing ... must occur within 2 business days following approval.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Both legs and the facility drawdown must be executed inside two business days of clearance, and clearance can be pulled without reasons at any point before signing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Approval will not be granted to Ventia Personnel to Deal in Ventia Securities where the Dealing would not satisfy the Front Page Test.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar can be refused purely on perception grounds even where no substantive rule is breached, and there is no appeal or reasons requirement.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons must take appropriate steps to ensure that their Connected Persons only Deal in Securities in circumstances where the Restricted Person to whom they are connected would be permitted to Deal under this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Holding the collared parcel through a controlled trust or company does not escape the clearance requirement, the hedging bans or the margin lending approval.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The policy contains a Front Page Test but no substance over form or anti-avoidance provision.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike several peer policies, Ventia has no express anti-avoidance hook to recharacterise a collar-plus-loan, so the analysis turns on the literal wording of sections 3.3, 3.4 and 3.6.

VNT.summary: A funded collar is achievable at Ventia over vested Securities that are free of any plan holding lock, and this is one of the more permissive policies in the market. Both derivative legs are Dealings, because Securities expressly includes derivatives and linked financial products with no venue limit, so a Restricted Person needs a written Clearance to Trade approved by the Board Chairman (for Directors) or the Group CEO (for employees), obtained outside the two results Blackout Periods, executed within two business days and revocable without reasons; a Director must also notify the Group Company Secretary the same day. The loan leg is not prohibited: section 3.6 subjects margin lending arrangements in respect of Securities, and transfers of Securities into an existing margin loan account, to the same approval process, Ventia may condition that approval on the margin call and sale mechanics, and section 5 treats a secured lender's enforcement sale as an Excluded Dealing even in a Blackout Period. The binding constraints are that unvested plan Securities and vested Securities still under a holding lock can never be hedged, with no exemption power, and that section 3.3 bans short term dealing and names forward contracts as its example, so the collar should have a tenor well beyond three months and avoid forward-sale characterisation. Practically, the bank should expect Ventia to negotiate the enforcement and top-up terms of the facility as conditions of approval.

WAF.ad_hoc_blackout_authority: WAF may impose additional Prohibited Periods when senior management becomes aware of a matter considered price sensitive, or which the Chairman or the Managing Director deems price sensitive. The policy does not say whether such periods are announced or kept confidential, and sets no limit on their length.

rules.detail: Derivatives as defined in section 761D of the Corporations Act, over shares, performance options or performance rights, are permitted only if all five criteria are met: the securities are fully vested, the maturity date falls outside a Prohibited Period, WAF is not a counterparty, the derivative is used to protect the value of an asset supporting a loan taken out to fund the exercise price of WAF options or to protect the value of the security against tax liabilities, and the transaction complies with all applicable laws. No Board approval is required outside a Prohibited Period, but the section 10 notification rules apply and evidence that the criteria are met must accompany the notification.
rules.evidence: Key Management Personnel may only enter into transactions involving derivatives (as defined in section 761D of the Corporations Act) (Derivatives) in respect of securities in WAF (including shares, performance options and performance rights) if the following criteria are satisfied

rules.detail: A derivative over securities that are not fully vested, including performance options and performance rights, fails the first criterion and is prohibited outright. There is no Board waiver of the section 9 criteria; the section 7 exemption power is confined to dealing during a Prohibited Period.
rules.evidence: a) the relevant securities are fully vested;

rules.detail: Section 9 binds only Key Management Personnel. Employees, advisers, contractors and consultants who are not KMP are subject to no derivatives criteria, no Closed Periods and no notification, only the insider trading prohibition.
rules.evidence: Key Management Personnel may only enter into transactions involving derivatives

rules.detail: Products which operate to limit economic risk in WAF holdings are securities for the purposes of the policy, and hedging by derivative is governed by the section 9 criteria. A hedge over fully vested shares is allowed only for the two permitted purposes, must mature outside a Prohibited Period, and must be notified two business days in advance with evidence that the criteria are satisfied.
rules.evidence: securities include shares, options, derivatives and other financial products that can be traded on a financial market including financial products issued or created over WAF securities by third parties and products which operate to limit economic risk in securities holdings in WAF

rules.detail: Hedging of unvested securities, expressly including performance options and performance rights, is prohibited because the section 9 vesting criterion cannot be satisfied.
rules.evidence: a) the relevant securities are fully vested;

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named, but any prepaid forward, collar or similar structure is a Derivative in respect of WAF securities and must satisfy the section 9 purpose test. A structure entered into to raise liquidity, diversify or fund general expenditure serves neither permitted purpose and is therefore prohibited. Only two purposes qualify: protecting the value of an asset supporting a loan taken out to fund the exercise price of WAF options, and protecting the value of the security against tax liabilities.
rules.evidence: d) the Derivative is used for the purposes of protecting the value of an asset supporting a loan taken out to fund the exercise price of options granted by WAF or to protect the value of the security in respect of tax liabilities that may become due and payable;

rules.detail: Short selling is nowhere mentioned. A short position established through a derivative would still have to satisfy the section 9 criteria, and a purchase and sale of the same securities within three months would breach the short-term trading ban.
Securities lending is not named and is not within the definition of dealing, which is limited to applying for, acquiring, disposing of or agreeing to apply for, acquire or sell securities.

CFDs are not named but are derivatives within section 761D of the Corporations Act, so they fall within section 9 and would fail the purpose criterion in 9(d), and a cash-settled CFD would also not be protecting an asset supporting an option exercise loan or a tax liability.
rules.evidence: Key Management Personnel may only enter into transactions involving derivatives (as defined in section 761D of the Corporations Act) (Derivatives) in respect of securities in WAF

rules.detail: Margin lending over WAF securities is permitted, for KMP and Related Persons, subject to a conduct requirement that the facility terms must not require dealings when the KMP is prohibited from dealing, and to disclosure to the Company Secretary within ten business days of the number of securities, the trigger events for disposal, and the ability to meet a margin call, with an ongoing duty to report changes.
rules.evidence: Within ten business days of a Key Management Personnel or a Related Person entering into a margin lending arrangement involving WAF's securities, the relevant Key Management Personnel must provide the Company Secretary with the following information

rules.detail: Section 8 binds only Key Management Personnel and their Related Persons; margin lending by other employees, advisers, contractors or consultants is unregulated.

Granting an encumbrance over WAF securities is not prohibited and is not a dealing, but the policy expressly contemplates it: the Board may seek information from KMP about encumbrances granted or margin loans taken out over their securities and may require them to keep the Company Secretary informed of changes. Disclosure is on Board demand rather than automatic.
rules.evidence: The Board may seek information from Key Management Personnel about their level of ownership of WAF's securities and about any encumbrances granted or margin loans taken out in respect of those securities.

rules.detail: The conduct requirement is drafted broadly around arranging finance where WAF securities are provided as collateral, not just margin lending, and requires that the obligations do not conflict with the policy, in particular that the terms do not require dealings in WAF securities during a Prohibited Period. There is no prohibition and no approval requirement; the ten business day disclosure obligation is expressed only for margin lending arrangements.
rules.evidence: Key Management Personnel should ensure that when arranging finance either for themselves or through their Related Persons, where WAF securities are provided as collateral, such obligations do not conflict with their obligations under this policy.

rules.detail: A three month holding period test defined as the purchase and sale of the same securities within three months, applying at all times to KMP and their Related Persons. Uniquely, the Board may on application exempt a person from this prohibition in exceptional circumstances.
rules.evidence: Short-term trading is defined as the purchase and sale of the same securities within a three month period. In order to prevent the unfair use of information, Key Management Personnel and their Related Persons are generally prohibited from short-term trading at all times.

WAF.exemption_authority: The Board only. It may give prior written clearance in exceptional circumstances, such as severe financial hardship or a court order requiring sale, for a member of Key Management Personnel or a Related Person to deal during a Prohibited Period (section 7.1), and may on application exempt them from the short-term trading prohibition in exceptional circumstances (section 5). Clearance is refused if WAF is in possession of Inside Information, and the Board may impose conditions including the effective period. There is no power to waive the section 9 derivatives criteria.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the Derivative is used for the purposes of protecting the value of an asset supporting a loan taken out to fund the exercise price of options granted by WAF or to protect the value of the security in respect of tax liabilities that may become due and payable
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is the decisive clause: a collar is permitted only where it protects collateral for a loan taken out to fund the exercise price of WAF options, or protects against a tax liability, so a funded collar raised for liquidity, diversification or general purposes is prohibited outright, while an option-exercise-funding facility with a protective collar fits the wording precisely.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the Derivative has a maturity date that falls outside a Prohibited Period
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Because Prohibited Periods run for one week before to one business day after every quarterly, half year and annual report, the expiry date of both collar legs must be diarised around a dense quarterly reporting calendar, and any roll or extension must land on a clear date.

bespoke_clauses.clause: WAF is not a counterparty to the Derivative
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bank counterparty is expressly contemplated and permitted; only the company itself is excluded.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the relevant securities are fully vested
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Performance options and performance rights cannot be collared until vesting, and there is no Board waiver of this criterion.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Key Management Personnel should ensure that when arranging finance either for themselves or through their Related Persons, where WAF securities are provided as collateral, such obligations do not conflict with their obligations under this policy. In particular, Key Management Personnel should ensure that the terms of any margin lending arrangements do not require dealings in WAF securities at a time when Key Management Personnel are prohibited from dealing.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The facility must be drafted so that no mandatory sale, top-up or delivery obligation can be triggered during a Prohibited Period, which constrains margin call mechanics even though section 6(b)(ii) excludes an actual enforcement sale from the policy.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The following dealings ... are excluded from the operation of this policy: ... The disposing of securities ... as a result of a secured lender exercising its right under a margin lending arrangement;
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An enforcement sale by the lender sits outside the policy entirely, including during a Prohibited Period, which protects the executive if the bank has to realise the collateral.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Board may seek information from Key Management Personnel about their level of ownership of WAF's securities and about any encumbrances granted or margin loans taken out in respect of those securities. The Board may also require them to keep the Company Secretary informed of changes to such information.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The security package over the collared shares is disclosable to the Board on demand and, through the continuous disclosure hook, potentially to the market.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Key Management Personnel are required to notify WAF of all intended dealings in WAF's securities ... two business days before such intended dealings.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Outside Prohibited Periods there is no approval gate at all, only a two business day advance notice and a post-trade price confirmation, so execution timing is within the executive's control, but the notice period must be built into pricing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Board may on application exempt Key Management Personnel or their Related Persons from this prohibition in exceptional circumstances.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike most peer policies the three month holding period ban can be waived by the Board, which gives a route to unwind or restructure a collar inside three months.

WAF.summary: A funded collar is possible for WAF Key Management Personnel only in a narrow form. Section 9 permits derivatives over WAF securities without Board approval, and expressly allows a bank counterparty, but only if the securities are fully vested, the derivative matures outside a Prohibited Period, and it is used to protect the value of an asset supporting a loan taken out to fund the exercise price of WAF options or to protect against a tax liability; a collar entered into to raise general liquidity or to diversify fails that purpose test and is prohibited. Where the purpose test is met the structure is otherwise well supported: there is no prohibition on encumbering WAF shares or on secured financing, an enforcement sale by a secured lender is excluded from the policy entirely, and the only gates are a two business day advance notice to the Company Secretary with evidence that the section 9 criteria are satisfied, a post-trade price confirmation within two business days, Appendix 3Y filing for directors, and margin lending disclosure within ten business days. The facility must be drafted so it cannot compel a dealing during a Prohibited Period, which is a real constraint given that Prohibited Periods surround every quarterly, half year and annual report. Tenor should exceed three months to avoid the short-term trading ban, although the Board can exempt that prohibition in exceptional circumstances.

BOQ.title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Everyone
tiers.description: All Directors, officers, Employees and Contractors, and their family and associates. Bound only by the Insider Trading Ban (paragraphs 8-23) and the Confidential Information obligation (paragraph 44); not by Prohibited Periods, the Clearance Procedures, the margin lending ban, the short term trading ban or the hedging ban.

tiers.name: Designated Persons
tiers.description: All Directors, officers and other Key Management Personnel; Employees at Group Executive, General Manager or Head of level (Tier 8 and above); Company Secretaries; Executive Assistants of Tier 8 and above; nominated Employees and Contractors in Legal, Corporate Affairs, Investor Relations, Finance, Treasury, Strategy, Compliance, Human Resources and Risk Management; and any other person designated by the Chairman, MD & CEO or General Counsel & Company Secretary. All parts of the policy apply.

tiers.name: Other Directors

tiers.name: Key Management Personnel

The policy applies to them, with the notification paragraphs applied as appropriate.

definitions.hedging_definition: enter into transactions or arrangements with anyone which could have the effect of limiting the exposure of the member to risk relating to an element of the member's remuneration that: i. has not vested in the member; or ii. has vested in the member but remains subject to a holding lock

BOQ.ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Chairman, MD & CEO or CFO may specify any extension to a closed period and any additional period, conditionally or unconditionally. The Chairman or MD & CEO may also extend the policy to the securities of other specified entities with which the Company has a relationship. The policy does not say whether these are announced or confidential.

rules.detail: Paragraph 31(b) prohibits dealing at any time in financial products over or in respect of Company Securities, except for the type of dealing permitted by law or under this policy, and applies to Designated Persons and their closely related parties. Financial Products is defined to include derivatives, options, warrants, futures, forward contracts, swaps and contracts for difference issued or created over or associated with Company Securities by third parties, with no venue limitation and no vesting qualification, so an OTC put and written call written by a bank are caught. Nothing elsewhere in the policy permits that type of dealing.
rules.evidence: Subject to the law, Designated Persons and their closely related parties (as defined in the Corporations Act) must not: ... b. deal at any time in financial products over or in respect of Company Securities, except for the type of dealing permitted by law or under this policy.

rules.detail: Only the Insider Trading Ban and the confidentiality obligation apply to Directors, officers, Employees and Contractors who are not Designated Persons, so the hedging and derivatives prohibitions in paragraph 31 do not reach them. In practice all Directors and KMP are Designated Persons.
rules.evidence: Everyone - including all Directors, officers, Employees and Contractors, and their family and associates | Insider Trading Ban (paragraphs 8-23) and Confidential Information (paragraph 44)

rules.detail: Designated Persons and their closely related parties must not enter into any transaction or arrangement with anyone that could have the effect of limiting exposure to risk relating to unvested remuneration. A put option on variable remuneration is given as an express example of a prohibited arrangement, which is the purchased put leg of a collar.
rules.evidence: enter into transactions or arrangements with anyone which could have the effect of limiting the exposure of the member to risk relating to an element of the member's remuneration that: i. has not vested in the member ... Examples of prohibited arrangements: a. a put option on variable remuneration;

rules.detail: The same absolute ban extends to remuneration that has vested but remains subject to a holding lock. There is no waiver power; the exceptional circumstances route in Appendix 2 addresses only dealing during a Prohibited Period and disposals.
rules.evidence: ii. has vested in the member but remains subject to a holding lock;

rules.detail: Paragraph 31(a) is confined to unvested and holding-locked remuneration, but paragraph 31(b) is a separate and wider prohibition on dealing at any time in financial products over or in respect of Company Securities. Hedging fully vested, unrestricted shares, whether plan-sourced or bought on market, therefore remains prohibited unless the type of dealing is permitted elsewhere in the policy, and none of the Appendix 1 Permitted Dealings covers a hedge.
rules.evidence: deal at any time in financial products over or in respect of Company Securities, except for the type of dealing permitted by law or under this policy.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named, but forward contracts and swaps are expressly within the definition of Financial Products, so a prepaid forward or collar-plus-loan is caught by the paragraph 31(b) prohibition. A structure with a tenor of less than 30 days would independently breach the short term trading ban, which expressly extends to derivatives and other financial products.
rules.evidence: Financial Products include derivatives, options, warrants, futures, forward contracts, swaps and contracts for difference issued or created over or associated with Company Securities by third parties but do not include portfolio products that are not specific to the Company eg index funds

rules.detail: Outright ban on short selling Company Securities. Paragraph 32(b) also gives a short position on remuneration shares as an example of a prohibited hedging arrangement and defines a short position as one where the quantity of shares held is less than the quantity the person is obliged to deliver, which is relevant to any over-hedged or physically settled call position.

BOQ.exemption_authority: The relevant Notification Officer may give prior confirmation, on request, for a Designated Person to deal during a Prohibited Period or to dispose of Company Securities otherwise prohibited under paragraph 24, where Appendix 2 exceptional circumstances exist (severe financial hardship, court order or legal or regulatory requirement, or other circumstances determined by the Chairman, or the MD & CEO where the Chairman is involved). The relief is expressly limited to paragraph 24 dealings and disposals; there is no power to waive the paragraph 26 margin lending ban, the paragraph 29 short term trading ban or the paragraph 31 hedging and financial products prohibition.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Subject to the law, Designated Persons and their closely related parties (as defined in the Corporations Act) must not ... deal at any time in financial products over or in respect of Company Securities, except for the type of dealing permitted by law or under this policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is the clause that defeats the collar: unlike the remuneration hedging ban in 31(a), it is not limited to unvested or locked shares, covers derivatives created by third parties including OTC options, swaps and forwards, and extends to closely related parties, and nothing in Appendix 1 permits a hedge.

bespoke_clauses.clause: except for the type of dealing permitted by law or under this policy
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Read literally, 'permitted by law' could swallow the prohibition, since a collar over vested shares held without inside information is lawful; the drafting is ambiguous and would need a written ruling from the General Counsel & Company Secretary before a bank could rely on it.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This restriction does not extend to other funding arrangements where Company Securities may be included as security. Designated Persons should consult the General Counsel & Company Secretary or Company Secretary if they are uncertain as to whether an arrangement should be classified as a margin lending arrangement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg secured on BOQ shares is expressly outside the margin lending ban and needs no approval or disclosure, so the obstacle to a funded collar is the derivative legs, not the financing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Examples of prohibited arrangements: a. a put option on variable remuneration;
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The purchased put over plan-sourced shares is the exact structure the policy names as prohibited, so there is no room to argue the ban was not aimed at collars.

bespoke_clauses.topic: forced sale carve-out with a margin lending exception
bespoke_clauses.clause: (lender disposal) a disposal of Company Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, however, this does not extend to disposal under a margin lending agreement if the agreement is prohibited by this policy;
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Enforcement over the shares by a bank under a permitted, non-margin facility can proceed at any time including in a Prohibited Period, but if the facility were later characterised as a margin loan the executive loses that protection and the enforcement sale becomes a policy breach.

bespoke_clauses.topic: 30 day short term test covering derivatives
bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons must not engage in short term or speculative trading in Company Securities or in derivatives or other financial products issued over or in respect of Company Securities. Short term means in less than a 30 day period.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even if the derivatives ban were relaxed, any collar or roll with a tenor under 30 days would independently breach the policy, and 'speculative' is undefined.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A confirmation confirms that the proposed dealing by the Designated Person is within the terms of the Securities Trading Policy but does not otherwise constitute approval or endorsement by the Company or the Notification Officer for the proposed dealing.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The clearance is a compliance check with a 3 business day life, not an endorsement, and a Notification Officer cannot confirm a dealing that paragraph 31 prohibits.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Associates of a Designated Person include ... any trustee of a trust or other fiduciary arrangement under which a Designated Person has, or may be expected to have, investment control or influence, companies in which a Designated Person may control directly or indirectly, nominees ...
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Holding the collared parcel through a trust, nominee or controlled company does not avoid paragraph 31, which binds closely related parties directly.

bespoke_clauses.clause: any extension to a closed period, and any additional period (conditionally or unconditionally), as specified by the Chairman, MD & CEO or CFO of the Company.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Three officers can extend or add Prohibited Periods conditionally at short notice, so any structure requiring a dealing on a fixed future date carries timing risk.

BOQ.summary: A funded collar is not available to a BOQ Designated Person, which includes every Director and member of Key Management Personnel. The obstacle is paragraph 31(b), a standalone prohibition on Designated Persons and their closely related parties dealing at any time in financial products over or in respect of Company Securities, where Financial Products is defined to include derivatives, options, forward contracts, swaps and contracts for difference created by third parties; unlike the remuneration hedging ban in 31(a) it is not limited to unvested or holding-locked shares, and a put option is expressly named as a prohibited arrangement. The financing leg, by contrast, is unusually accommodating: paragraph 26 bans only margin lending, paragraph 27 expressly states that the restriction does not extend to other funding arrangements where Company Securities may be included as security, and Appendix 1 item 6 lets a secured lender enforce at any time, including during a Prohibited Period, provided the facility is not a prohibited margin loan. The only route to a collar would be a written ruling from the General Counsel & Company Secretary that it is a 'type of dealing permitted by law or under this policy' within the closing words of paragraph 31(b), which is a genuine ambiguity but a thin basis for a bank to lend against, and no exemption power exists since the Appendix 2 exceptional circumstances relief reaches only paragraph 24 dealings and disposals. Even then the 30 day short term trading test, which expressly covers derivatives, and the Front Page Test would apply.

DOW.summary: A funded collar is not possible for Directors or Senior/Group Executives under this policy. Section 7.6 imposes an absolute, venue-neutral ban on hedging arrangements, dealing in derivatives, and contracts (including CFDs) intended to secure a profit or avoid a loss from price movements in Downer's securities, applying to all Directors, employees and contractors with no approval route, which squarely catches the OTC put and call legs of a collar. Even if the option legs could somehow be structured around this ban, section 7.7 separately and expressly prohibits Restricted Persons — Directors, Senior Executives, Executives and other notified staff, i.e. the bank's target clientele — from margin lending, securities lending, or granting any security interest, mortgage, charge, lien or encumbrance over Downer securities, barring the secured loan leg outright. Outside these express bans, an ordinary sale requires Company Secretary or Chairman approval outside the 28-day post-AGM/results open windows and is barred in Closed Periods, and a lender's forced close-out sale within six months of acquisition is separately deemed prohibited short-term trading. The Chairman (or Chairman of the Audit and Risk Committee) retains a narrow discretion to exempt a Closed Period dealing in exceptional circumstances, but never while undisclosed price-sensitive information is held, and this offers no relief from the hedging or margin-lending prohibitions. In short, both the derivative legs and the secured-financing leg of a collar are independently and expressly prohibited, with no carve-out for vested shares.

rules.detail: Derivatives are named only once, in the closed period ban, where trading in 'any derivatives created over or in respect of the Company's securities' is prohibited during a closed period. There is no venue limitation, so exchange-traded and OTC puts and calls are both caught. Outside closed periods there is no express derivatives prohibition; a derivative transaction over Company securities is a proposed transaction in the Company's securities requiring prior written advice to, and written permission from, the Chairman.
rules.evidence: it is prohibited, under this policy, that the Company's directors, employees and such of the Company's contractors that the Company shall advise are covered by this provision ("Person") trade in the Company's securities or in any derivatives created over or in respect of the Company's securities.

rules.detail: The policy contains no hedging provision at all: it does not define hedging, does not refer to limiting economic risk, and draws no distinction between vested and unvested securities or between plan and non-plan securities. Nothing in the document prohibits hedging of Company securities as such; a hedge would be regulated only as a trade or derivative under the clearance and closed period rules.

Monetisation, prepaid forwards and similar structures are not named. A monetisation of Company securities is a proposed transaction in the Company's securities and so requires prior written notice to the Chairman and written confirmation that it is permissible; if structured as a derivative it is also caught by the closed period ban. There is no prohibition on monetisation as such.
rules.evidence: it is a requirement that any employee, consultant or Director proposing to trade in Company securities first advise the Chairman (in writing) of the details of such proposed trade and not trade until the Chairman advise that such trade is permissible.

rules.detail: Short selling is not mentioned anywhere in the policy and there is no dealing definition that would sweep it in.
Securities lending and borrowing are not mentioned anywhere in the policy.

CFDs are not named. A CFD over Company securities is a derivative created over or in respect of the Company's securities and so is banned during closed periods and otherwise requires prior written Chairman approval as a proposed trade. A CFD opened and closed within 30 days would also breach the short-term trading ban.
rules.evidence: trade in the Company's securities or in any derivatives created over or in respect of the Company's securities.

rules.detail: Margin loans and margin accounts are not mentioned anywhere in the policy, and there is no provision dealing with forced sales by a lender or with margin calls falling in a closed period.

Granting security, a charge, mortgage, lien or pledge over Company securities is not mentioned, and there is no definition of dealing or trading that would treat the grant of security as a trade requiring clearance.

There is no secured financing provision of any kind: no ban, no notification requirement, no disclosure threshold and no minimum shareholding requirement. The loan leg of a funded collar is simply unregulated by this policy.

Absolute ban on buying and selling the same security within 30 days, extending to securities of any close business associate of the Company (joint venture partner, major supplier, major buyer). No carve-outs are given for plan securities or for exercise of options, and there is no stated basis (LIFO or otherwise) for matching trades.
rules.evidence: It is also a policy of the Company that employees, consultants and Directors not engage in "short-term" trading in securities in the Company or in any close business associate (such as a joint venture partner, major supplier, major buyer etc) of the Company. PDIDB.exemption_authority: The Chairman may, on written application, grant written permission for a Person to sell during a closed period where he is of the opinion that exceptional circumstances (severe financial hardship, court order, enforceable undertaking or other legal or regulatory requirement) exist, for a specified period of time; the Chairman may also refuse any proposed trade at any time on best-interests grounds. Where the obligation applies to the Chairman himself, the Managing Director stands in his place. Any exemption is subject to the insider trading provisions of the Corporations Act and ASX restrictions.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the Chairman will seek to determine if he believes that the Company is in possession of inside information or that such proposed trade is, for any other reason, not in the best interests of the Company.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Clearance for the collar legs, and for any later unwind, roll or physical settlement, rests on an unbounded discretion that can be exercised against a hedging or financing structure purely on optics, so no leg of the trade can be assumed to be approvable.

bespoke_clauses.clause: it is prohibited ... that [a Person] trade in the Company's securities or in any derivatives created over or in respect of the Company's securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Entering, unwinding or settling the put and call is barred from 2 business days before each quarterly, half-year and full-year results announcement, which given quarterly reporting closes the window four times a year.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The policy contains no reference to margin lending, secured financing, charges, pledges, hedging or short selling.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan secured on the collared shares is not prohibited by the policy, so the bank's constraints come from the Corporations Act, ASX disclosure and any plan rules or employment terms rather than from this document; the absence of any forced-sale clause also means the policy is silent on a lender selling into a closed period.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The policy makes no reference to employee equity plans, unvested securities, performance rights or options issued as remuneration.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Nothing in the policy limits a collar to vested shares, but nothing exempts plan securities from the clearance or short-term rules either, so any plan documents must be checked separately for hedging or disposal restrictions.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Short-term trading means buying and selling the same security within 30 days.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar established and unwound inside 30 days, or one whose legs are opened and closed against each other in that period, risks being characterised as short-term trading, so tenor should comfortably exceed 30 days.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Such approval would not constitute a representation that such person would not be in breach of the law in so trading, as it is such person's obligation to make such determination.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Chairman clearance gives the bank no comfort that the director is free of inside information, so the bank must obtain its own representations at each of entry, roll and settlement.

bespoke_clauses.clause: each Director shall promptly (within one business day) report to the Company officer maintaining that register the details of any change in such holdings of such Director.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A change in a Director's holdings caused by physical settlement, share transfer to a security trustee or lender enforcement must be reported within one business day, on top of the Appendix 3Y/3Z regime.

bespoke_clauses.clause: not engage in "short-term" trading in securities in the Company or in any close business associate (such as a joint venture partner, major supplier, major buyer etc) of the Company.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The short-term ban reaches beyond the Company's own securities, so a basket or index hedge containing joint venture partner securities could be caught.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The policy is expressed to apply to 'employees, consultants and Directors' and to 'Persons'; it does not define associates, spouses, dependants or controlled entities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no express extension to family trusts or controlled companies, so the policy's own reach over a collar held through such a vehicle is untested, though the insider trading law and the procuring provisions still apply.

PDIDB.summary: A funded collar is possible under this policy, which is a short 2017 document that is silent on hedging, derivatives generally, margin lending, encumbrances and secured financing. Both derivative legs and the grant of security over the shares would be treated as proposed trades in Company securities requiring prior written notice to the Chairman and his written permission before execution, with written confirmation of the completed transaction back to the Chairman within 3 business days and, for a Director, a holdings report within one business day. The Chairman has an unbounded discretion to refuse any trade that he considers not in the best interests of the Company, so approval of a hedging and financing structure cannot be assumed, and the same clearance is needed for any unwind, roll or settlement. Execution must avoid the closed periods, which run from 2 business days before each quarterly, half-year and full-year results announcement to the announcement itself and expressly extend to derivatives over the Company's securities. Tenor should exceed 30 days to stay clear of the short-term trading ban, and the policy offers the bank no forced-sale protection because it says nothing about lender enforcement in a closed period.

It is confidential: 'Liontown Personnel must not disclose to anyone that an Additional Period is in effect.' Blackout Periods and Additional Periods together are Prohibited Periods; trading in an Additional Period is possible only on exceptional circumstances clearance under section 8.

rules.detail: Company Securities expressly include derivatives of shares, options and performance rights, naming equity swaps, futures, hedges and exchange-traded or over-the-counter options, whether cash settled or otherwise. Restricted Persons must not trade in Company Securities at any time without prior written clearance, so an OTC put or written call requires clearance regardless of whether a Prohibited Period is running.

rules.detail: For Liontown Personnel who are not Restricted Persons there is no blanket clearance requirement; derivatives over Company Securities are Company Securities and so may not be traded during a Blackout Period or Additional Period or while holding Inside Information, and clearance is required only where the policy stipulates it (sections 7, 12, 13 and 14). A collar is a hedging arrangement, so section 12 clearance would in practice apply to this tier too.
rules.evidence: Liontown Personnel, who are not Restricted Persons, must also adhere to the procedures for obtaining prior written clearance outlined in this Clause where stipulated by this Policy.

rules.detail: Absolute ban, with no clearance route, on transactions or arrangements limiting the economic risk of participating in unvested entitlements under any equity based remuneration scheme. This is a separate sentence from the clearance-based rule for hedging security holdings generally, so no Approving Officer can authorise it.
rules.evidence: Liontown Personnel are prohibited from entering into transactions or arrangements which limit the economic risk of participating in unvested entitlements under any equity based remuneration schemes.

rules.detail: Hedging of a vested, unrestricted security holding in the Company is expressly permitted with prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer under the section 8 procedure. The clearance request form has a dedicated field requiring details where section 12 applies, so hedging is contemplated rather than merely tolerated. Clearance may be refused in absolute discretion.
rules.evidence: Liontown Personnel must not enter into transactions or arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk of their security holding in the Company without first obtaining prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer in accordance with the procedure set out in section 8.

rules.detail: Vested securities held under ASX restricted securities rules or voluntary escrow cannot be traded while the escrow runs, so no physically settled hedge, transfer or pledge of those shares is possible. A cash-settled hedge over them is still a section 12 arrangement requiring clearance, and an Approving Officer would need to be satisfied it does not breach the escrow terms.
rules.evidence: Any Liontown Personnel who holds Company Securities subject to binding restrictions on transfer (either as ASX restricted securities or through voluntary escrow arrangements) must comply with the terms of any applicable escrow arrangements and will be unable to trade in those securities during that time.

rules.detail: Monetisation, prepaid forwards and similar structures are not named. A prepaid forward or equivalent is an agreement to dispose of securities and so a trade, and it operates to limit the economic risk of the holding, so it needs section 12 clearance; if it is funded by security over the shares it also needs section 13 clearance.
rules.evidence: To "trade" in securities means, whether as principal or agent, to apply for, acquire or dispose of securities; enter into an agreement to apply for, acquire or dispose of securities.

rules.detail: Short selling is not named anywhere in the policy. It falls within the ban on short term or speculative trading of Company Securities in section 11, which has no clearance route and no stated exceptions.
rules.evidence: The Company wishes to encourage Liontown Personnel to adopt a long-term attitude to investment in Company Securities. Therefore, Liontown Personnel must not engage in short term or speculative trading of Company Securities.

rules.detail: Securities lending and borrowing are not mentioned. The definition of trade covers only applying for, acquiring or disposing of securities and agreements to do so, so a stock loan is caught only to the extent it involves an outright transfer of title, and section 13 addresses secured lending to the person rather than lending of securities by the person.

CFDs are not named but are derivatives of Company shares settled by cash and so are Company Securities; trading them requires clearance for Restricted Persons and is barred in Prohibited Periods for everyone. In practice a CFD would also be caught by the section 11 prohibition on short term or speculative trading.
rules.evidence: derivatives of any of the above (including equity swaps, futures, hedges and exchange-traded or over-the-counter options) whether settled by cash or otherwise

rules.detail: Margin loans in relation to Company Securities are permitted but only with prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer under the section 8 procedure. There is no outright ban, no vesting-state limit and no stated LVR or price trigger guidance. A disposal resulting from the secured lender exercising its rights is excluded from the Blackout Period restrictions by section 9(g).

bespoke_clauses.topic: secured lending is clearance-gated, not banned
bespoke_clauses.clause: Liontown Personnel must not enter into margin loan agreements or other secured lending arrangements in relation to Company Securities without first obtaining prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer in accordance with the procedure set out in section 8.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar is expressly permitted subject to prior written clearance rather than prohibited, which is the single most important difference from policies that ban secured financing outright.

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedging is clearance-gated for vested holdings
bespoke_clauses.clause: Liontown Personnel must not enter into transactions or arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk of their security holding in the Company without first obtaining prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The put and call legs are permissible with clearance over vested unrestricted shares, and the clearance form has a dedicated field for section 12 details, so the structure must be disclosed to the Approving Officer in full.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Liontown Personnel are prohibited from entering into transactions or arrangements which limit the economic risk of participating in unvested entitlements under any equity based remuneration schemes.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The collar must be sized strictly to vested shares; no Approving Officer discretion can cure a hedge that reaches unvested performance rights or options, and over-hedging vested holdings risks being characterised as hedging the unvested tail.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a disposal of Company Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement [is excluded from the restrictions outlined in section 6].
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement sale is expressly excluded from the Blackout Period restrictions, so lender enforcement during a closed period does not itself breach the policy, though section 8's blanket clearance requirement for Restricted Persons is not in terms disapplied and the carve-out does not displace the insider trading law.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Written clearance can be withdrawn by the Approving Officer at any time prior to the order for dealing being lodged or otherwise authorised, if new information comes to light or there is a change in circumstances.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Pricing risk sits with the client: a cleared collar can be pulled before execution, so the bank should not commit hedge or funding until the trade is actually lodged.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any written clearance granted under this policy will be valid for the period of 3 business days from the time which it is given or such other period as may be determined by the Approving Officer. The expiry time of the clearance will be stated in the clearance granted.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The default execution window is only 3 business days, but the form lets the Approving Officer specify a longer bespoke period, which can be requested up front to accommodate documentation and settlement of a collar and loan.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any request for written clearance can be given or refused by the Approving Officer in their absolute discretion. ... Where a waiver is refused, it is final and binding on the Restricted Person and the Restricted Person must keep all information relating to the waiver confidential.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no appeal and no reasons requirement, so the bank cannot assume approval of a collar and the client may be unable to explain a refusal to the bank.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Liontown Personnel must not trade in Company Securities within any period imposed by the Board (or its delegate) from time to time ... Liontown Personnel must not disclose to anyone that an Additional Period is in effect.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Undisclosed Additional Periods can block entry, roll, unwind or physical settlement at any time, and the client is barred from telling the bank why.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any Liontown Personnel who holds Company Securities subject to binding restrictions on transfer (either as ASX restricted securities or through voluntary escrow arrangements) ... will be unable to trade in those securities during that time.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Escrowed shares cannot be delivered to a security trustee or sold on enforcement, so only unrestricted vested shares can serve as collateral for the loan.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Liontown Personnel must not engage in short term or speculative trading of Company Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The prohibition is undefined and qualitative, so a short-dated collar, an early unwind or a cash-settled structure could be characterised as speculative trading in Company Securities, and tenor and settlement mechanics should be raised with the Approving Officer at clearance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where this policy requires a Restricted Person to do an act or thing, the relevant Restricted Person must do that act or thing in respect of the Connected Person.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Holding the collared shares through a family trust, controlled company or spouse does not avoid the clearance requirements for hedging or secured lending.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If before carrying out the trade, the Restricted Person comes into possession of Inside Information or a Prohibited Period commences, that person must not carry out the trade, notwithstanding that it has been approved.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Approval lapses automatically on the onset of inside information or a blackout, so the bank needs a fresh representation at signing and at each subsequent settlement or roll.

bespoke_clauses.clause: written clearance granted under this policy is never an endorsement of the proposed trade or a confirmation regarding the absence of Inside Information.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank cannot rely on the Approving Officer's clearance as diligence and must take its own representations from the client.

LTR.summary: A funded collar is possible under this policy, which is unusually accommodating: section 12 permits hedging arrangements that limit the economic risk of a security holding, and section 13 permits margin loans and other secured lending arrangements in relation to Company Securities, in each case subject to prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer rather than being prohibited. The clearance request form has a dedicated field for section 12 and 13 details, so the whole structure must be disclosed; clearance is at absolute discretion, is valid for 3 business days by default (a longer period may be specified), can be withdrawn before the order is lodged, and lapses if inside information arises or a Prohibited Period starts. The collar must be sized strictly to vested holdings, because hedging arrangements limiting the economic risk of unvested equity scheme entitlements are prohibited outright with no clearance route, and escrowed or ASX restricted shares cannot be traded or delivered. Execution must sit outside the four quarterly Blackout Periods and any confidential Board-imposed Additional Period, and Restricted Persons (KMP, executive employees and their Connected Persons) need clearance for every trade including the derivative legs, since Company Securities expressly include over-the-counter options and equity swaps. A helpful feature for the bank is section 9(g), which excludes a disposal resulting from a secured lender exercising its rights from the blackout restrictions; tenor should be long enough to avoid the undefined ban on short term or speculative trading, and directors must report resulting holdings changes within three business days.

rules.section: Speculative Trading; Which securities does this Policy apply to?
rules.detail: Dealing in derivatives is expressly named as an activity a Restricted Person must not engage in without Written Clearance, and put and call options are given as examples. Megaport Securities expressly include hedging or derivative instruments in relation to Megaport securities, with no venue limitation, so OTC options with a bank are squarely caught. Written Clearance is available only on the exceptional circumstances test in 'When can Written Clearance be given?'.
rules.evidence: In particular you must not engage in the following activities without Written Clearance: engage in hedging arrangements, deal in derivatives or enter into other arrangements which limit the economic risk related to Megaport Securities (including, for example, the use of put and call options, contracts for difference and other contracts intended to secure a profit or avoid a loss based on fluctuations in the price of Megaport Securities)

rules.section: Speculative Trading; Authorised Trading; When can Written Clearance be given?
rules.detail: Hedging arrangements and other arrangements limiting economic risk related to Megaport Securities require Written Clearance. The policy draws no distinction between vested, unvested or holding-locked securities for hedging, and no distinction between plan and non-plan securities. The gate is high: a Restricted Person who wishes to engage in speculative trading 'may apply for permission to trade if exceptional circumstances exist', and Written Clearance can only be given if the trade is not for speculative gain, not likely to be seen as unfair, and exceptional circumstances justify it.
rules.evidence: If you are a Restricted Person or their Relative and wish to trade in Megaport Securities during a Restricted Period or if you are a Restricted Person who wishes to engage in speculative trading or grant security over your Megaport Securities, but cannot do so because of this Policy, you may apply for permission to trade if exceptional circumstances exist. This is called Written Clearance.

rules.detail: Monetisation and prepaid forwards are not named. Any such structure is an 'other arrangement which limits the economic risk related to Megaport Securities' and so falls in the Written Clearance gate; if it is funded by security over the shares the Security Arrangements paragraph applies as well.
rules.evidence: enter into other arrangements which limit the economic risk related to Megaport Securities

rules.detail: Short selling as such is not named, but entering into any arrangement designed to profit from a decrease in the share price is expressly listed as requiring Written Clearance. In practice clearance is unavailable, because it can only be given where the proposed trade is not for speculative gain and exceptional circumstances exist, so a short position is effectively barred.
rules.evidence: enter into any arrangement designed to profit from a decrease in the share price of Megaport Securities.

rules.detail: Securities lending and borrowing are not mentioned. The policy has no definition of 'trade', and the Security Arrangements paragraph is directed at granting security to secure the person's own obligations rather than at lending out securities.

Contracts for difference are named expressly as an example of an arrangement limiting economic risk that requires Written Clearance, subject to the same exceptional circumstances and no-speculative-gain conditions.
rules.evidence: including, for example, the use of put and call options, contracts for difference and other contracts intended to secure a profit or avoid a loss based on fluctuations in the price of Megaport Securities

rules.detail: Margin lenders are named expressly. Granting security over Megaport Securities to a margin lender requires Written Clearance but is not banned. A disposal of Megaport Securities by a secured lender under a loan agreement secured by the Megaport Securities is outside the Policy altogether.
rules.evidence: you must not, unless you have Written Clearance, directly or indirectly, grant any form of security (such as a charge, mortgage or pledge) over any of your Megaport Securities (including those Megaport Securities which are unvested or the subject of a holding lock) to secure your obligations to any third party, including a margin lender.

rules.detail: Granting any form of security, directly or indirectly, over vested unrestricted Megaport Securities to secure obligations to any third party requires Written Clearance. There is no outright ban and no limit on the identity of the secured party.
rules.evidence: you must not, unless you have Written Clearance, directly or indirectly, grant any form of security (such as a charge, mortgage or pledge) over any of your Megaport Securities

rules.detail: The Security Arrangements paragraph is a clearance gate, not a prohibition, and reaches any form of security granted directly or indirectly to secure obligations to any third party, so a bank loan secured on collared shares is caught. rules.evidence: If you are a Restricted Person ... who wishes to engage in speculative trading or grant security over your Megaport Securities, but cannot do so because of this Policy, you may apply for permission to trade if exceptional circumstances exist.

MP1.exemption_authority: Authorised Officers have absolute discretion to give, refuse or withdraw Written Clearance, and their decisions are final. Written Clearance for trading in a Restricted Period, for speculative trading (including hedging and derivatives) and for granting security is available only where exceptional circumstances exist, being at the Authorised Officer's discretion but illustrated by exceptional financial hardship, a court order or enforceable undertaking, or exceptional detriment to family affairs, and only where the trade is not contrary to law, not for speculative gain, not to take advantage of Inside information and not likely to be seen by the public, press, other shareholders or ASX as unfair.

bespoke_clauses.topic: exceptional circumstances gate on hedging and security
bespoke_clauses.clause: If you are a Restricted Person ... who wishes to engage in speculative trading or grant security over your Megaport Securities, but cannot do so because of this Policy, you may apply for permission to trade if exceptional circumstances exist. ... Written Clearance can only be given if ... the proposed trade is not for speculative gain ... and exceptional circumstances exist justifying the issue of the Written Clearance.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is the decisive clause for a funded collar: both the derivative legs and the security over the shares are routed to a clearance that on its face is only available in exceptional circumstances such as financial hardship or a court order, so an ordinary portfolio-diversification collar is very unlikely to be approvable.

bespoke_clauses.topic: security arrangements are gated, not banned
bespoke_clauses.clause: you must not, unless you have Written Clearance, directly or indirectly, grant any form of security (such as a charge, mortgage or pledge) over any of your Megaport Securities (including those Megaport Securities which are unvested or the subject of a holding lock) to secure your obligations to any third party, including a margin lender.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg is not prohibited outright and can even in principle cover unvested or holding-locked shares, but it needs Written Clearance and reaches indirect security, so a security trustee or back-to-back arrangement does not avoid it.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This Policy does not apply to: ... disposal of Megaport Securities by a secured lender under a loan agreement secured by the Megaport Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bank's enforcement sale is entirely outside the Policy, so lender enforcement during a Closed Period or Board-imposed Restricted Period does not breach it, although the Corporations Act insider trading prohibition still applies to the disposal.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Authorisation requirement table (Chair to Chair of the Audit Committee; CEO or a director other than the Chairperson to the Chair; all other Executive Management to the CEO) differs from the Authorised Trading table (Chair to two non-executive directors or a non-executive director and the CEO or CFO; CEO or a director other than the Chair to two directors; any other Restricted Person to the CEO).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A hedging or security arrangement is an Authorised Trading matter, so a director needs sign-off from two directors rather than the Chair alone, which raises the approval bar and lengthens the timetable for documenting a collar.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Unless otherwise specified in the Written Clearance and provided the Written Clearance has not been withdrawn, trades and other dealings in Megaport Securities that have received Written Clearance must be made within 7 days of the date of that Written Clearance.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The collar legs and the security must be executed within 7 days of clearance unless a longer period is written into the clearance, so documentation should be fully negotiated before clearance is sought.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Authorised Officers have absolute discretion to give or refuse Written Clearance and to withdraw Written Clearance if new information comes to light. The Authorised Officer's decisions are final and if you are refused Written Clearance you must keep that refusal confidential.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Clearance can be pulled before execution and a refusal cannot be explained to the bank, so the bank should not commit funding or hedge until the trade is done.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the proposed trade is not for speculative gain, to take advantage of Inside information or likely to be seen by the public, press, other shareholders or ASX as unfair.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An optics test sits alongside the legal tests, and a director monetising a large stake through a bank collar is exactly the kind of transaction that could be judged likely to be seen as unfair.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A Restricted Person who would be prohibited from trading under this Policy must not trade through any member of their family, or through a trust or company over which they have influence or control.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Controlled Entities are themselves Restricted Persons, so holding the collared shares through a family trust or company gains nothing and the same Written Clearance is needed.

bespoke_clauses.clause: All requests to buy or sell Megaport Securities must include: ... the intended volume of securities to be purchased or sold; an estimated time frame for the sale or purchase; and a statement that the person is not in possession of any Inside information.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The Authorised Officer must be given the size and timing of the trade, so the notional, tenor and settlement mechanics of the collar cannot be kept confidential from the Company.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Closed Period ... (a) in respect of Board members and Executive Management ... from 9 June ... from 10 December ... four weeks prior to the conclusion of the annual general meeting; (b) in respect of all other Restricted Persons ... four weeks prior to the announcement ... two weeks prior to the conclusion of the annual general meeting.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Directors and Executive Management face materially longer closed periods, roughly 9 June to the full year result and 10 December to the half year result plus an AGM window, so open windows for entering or unwinding a collar are narrow.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If you trade in Megaport Securities you must notify the Company Secretary of the details of all completed transactions within 14 days after each transaction. This is necessary whether or not authorisation or Written Clearance was required prior to trading.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Every leg, roll and settlement of the collar must be reported to the Company Secretary and recorded on the register, and directors must report within 2 days for Appendix 3Y purposes.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This Policy applies to the securities of other companies if: the other company is a joint venture or collaborative partner of Megaport; ... or Megaport has a substantial interest (5% or more) in the other company.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The clearance and closed period regime extends to securities of certain counterparties, so a basket hedge that includes those names would also be caught.

MP1.summary: A funded collar is theoretically permitted but practically very hard under this policy, because both legs of the structure are routed to the same narrow gate. Dealing in derivatives, hedging arrangements and other arrangements limiting economic risk related to Megaport Securities, including put and call options and CFDs by name, require Written Clearance, and granting any form of security directly or indirectly over Megaport Securities to any third party including a margin lender also requires Written Clearance; neither is banned outright, and unvested and holding-locked securities are expressly within the security gate rather than excluded. The difficulty is that the Authorised Trading paragraph makes Written Clearance for speculative trading and for security arrangements available only where exceptional circumstances exist, illustrated by exceptional financial hardship, a court order or exceptional detriment to family affairs, and only where the trade is not for speculative gain and not likely to be seen by the public, press, other shareholders or ASX as unfair. A director would need sign-off from two directors (two non-executive directors or a non-executive director and the CEO or CFO for the Chair), must disclose volume and timing, must execute within 7 days of clearance, faces long Closed Periods running from 9 June and 10 December plus an AGM window and any Board-imposed Restricted Period, and must notify the Company Secretary within 2 days of each trade. The one clearly favourable feature for a bank is that a disposal of Megaport Securities by a secured lender under a loan agreement secured by those securities falls entirely outside the Policy, so enforcement is not a policy breach.

BFL.ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board controls the windows directly. A Trading Window is opened only by a decision of the Board in consultation with the Company Secretary, and once opened the Company Secretary notifies Restricted Persons by email or intranet and notifies the share registries and brokers. 'A Trading Window may be varied, suspended or withdrawn by the Board at any time', and 'Restricted Persons may not assume that a Trading Window is open, even after the relevant results announcement.' The policy does not say whether a suspension or its reason is confidential.

rules.detail: Derivatives are not the subject of a separate rule, but Securities is defined to include 'warrant contracts and other derivatives relating to shares', with no venue limitation, so an exchange-traded or OTC option over BSP shares is a Company Security and dealing in it requires prior approval and must fall in a Trading Window. In practice almost any derivative a director would want is separately caught: hedging transactions are banned outright by 3.8.2 and forward contracts and short sales by 3.8.1.
rules.evidence: Securities: Shares, debentures, options to subscribe for new shares and options over existing shares, preference shares, warrant contracts and other derivatives relating to shares

rules.detail: A flat, unqualified ban on hedging exposure to Company Securities. There is no clearance or approval route, no distinction between vested, unvested or locked securities, no distinction between plan and non-plan securities, and no exception in clause 3.6. The only conceivable relief is the clause 3.7 waiver, which is available only where the Restricted Person is selling and not buying, so it cannot authorise the purchase of a put.
rules.evidence: A Restricted Person must not engage in transactions designed to hedge their exposure to Company Securities.

rules.detail: Forward contracts are expressly named within the ban on short-term and speculative trading, so a prepaid forward or similar monetisation is prohibited on its face, and any such structure is also a transaction designed to hedge exposure to Company Securities contrary to 3.8.2.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must not trade in Company Securities on a short-term basis or for speculative trading gain, including on-market short-term buying and selling, forward contracts and short-selling.

rules.detail: Short-selling is named expressly within the ban on short-term and speculative trading, with no approval route and no exception.
rules.evidence: including on-market short-term buying and selling, forward contracts and short-selling.

rules.detail: Securities lending and borrowing are not mentioned. There is no definition of 'deal' or 'dealing' that would sweep a stock loan in, and clause 3.8.3 addresses financing taken by the Restricted Person rather than the lending out of securities.

CFDs are not named. A CFD is a derivative relating to shares and so a Company Security, and it falls within the ban on trading for speculative gain and, where used to reduce exposure, within the outright hedging ban. There is no approval route for either prohibition.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must not trade in Company Securities on a short-term basis or for speculative trading gain

rules.detail: Margin lending in respect of Company Securities is permitted with the prior approval of the Chairman (or delegate). Where such approval has been granted, an involuntary disposal resulting from the margin lender exercising its rights is one of the limited dealings permitted outside a Trading Window.
rules.evidence: A Restricted Person must not enter into margin lending or other secured financing arrangements in respect of Company Securities, unless the prior approval of the Chairman (or his or her delegate) has been obtained.

rules.detail: Granting a charge, mortgage, lien or pledge is not separately named. Encumbering Company Securities is regulated only as the security component of a margin lending or other secured financing arrangement under 3.8.3, which requires the prior approval of the Chairman or delegate. An encumbrance unconnected with financing is not addressed and is not caught by any dealing definition.
rules.evidence: A Restricted Person must not enter into margin lending or other secured financing arrangements in respect of Company Securities, unless the prior approval of the Chairman (or his or her delegate) has been obtained.

rules.detail: The prohibition on 'margin lending or other secured financing arrangements in respect of Company Securities' is expressly subject to prior Chairman approval, so a bank loan secured on BSP shares is available in principle. Approval sits with the Chairman (or delegate) for every Restricted Person, unlike the clause 3.11 table which routes ordinary dealing approvals elsewhere. No conditions, LVR limits or price triggers are specified.
