bespoke_clauses.clause: A Restricted Person must not engage in transactions designed to hedge their exposure to Company Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This single sentence defeats a funded collar: the put and call legs are transactions designed to hedge exposure, the ban has no approval or waiver route and no vesting-state carve-out, and it applies to every Restricted Person and their Closely Connected Persons.

bespoke_clauses.topic: financing is approvable but hedging is not
bespoke_clauses.clause: A Restricted Person must not enter into margin lending or other secured financing arrangements in respect of Company Securities, unless the prior approval of the Chairman (or his or her delegate) has been obtained.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg alone is available with Chairman approval, so an unhedged secured loan against BSP shares is possible even though the collar that would normally accompany it is not.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons must not trade in Company Securities on a short-term basis or for speculative trading gain, including on-market short-term buying and selling, forward contracts and short-selling. BSP considers "short-term" to be a period of 6 months or less.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Forward contracts are prohibited by name, closing off prepaid forwards and forward-sale monetisations as an alternative to a collar, and any hedge unwound within 6 months would independently breach the short-term ban.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A waiver will only be granted if ... the Restricted Person is selling not buying Company Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even the exceptional circumstances route cannot authorise buying a put or entering a derivative position, so there is no discretionary path to a collar; the only sanctioned way to raise cash against a holding is an outright sale or an approved secured loan.

bespoke_clauses.clause: All periods that are not Trading Windows are "closed periods" for the purposes of the Listing Rules, during which time Restricted Persons are prohibited from dealing in Company Securities. ... A Trading Window may be varied, suspended or withdrawn by the Board at any time.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Dealing is prohibited by default and permitted only inside four announced windows totalling roughly 70 business days a year, and the Board can suspend a window at any moment, so any transaction timetable is fragile.

bespoke_clauses.topic: no assumption of an open window
bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons may not assume that a Trading Window is open, even after the relevant results announcement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank cannot infer an open window from the results calendar and must see the Company Secretary's written notification before any leg is executed.

bespoke_clauses.topic: five day notice and five day execution
bespoke_clauses.clause: made in writing to the respective persons specified in clause 3.11 at least 5 Business Days prior to the proposed dealing taking place ... If approved, the confirmation must specify a period of time of no more than 5 Business Days within which the dealing must be completed.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Five business days' advance notice plus a maximum five business day execution window means pricing must be arranged in advance and cannot be left to the moment of approval.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Prior notification, its receipt, any acknowledgement of or response to any such notification is not an endorsement, approval or recommendation of the proposed dealing. Restricted Persons remain responsible for their own investment decisions and compliance with applicable laws and this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Chairman or Company Secretary sign-off gives the bank no comfort, so it must take its own representations on inside information and policy compliance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: where a Restricted Person has been granted approval to enter into margin lending or other secured financing arrangements (see clause 3.8.3), an involuntary disposal of securities that results from the margin lender or financier exercising its rights under the arrangement;
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The lender's enforcement sale is permitted outside a Trading Window only if the financing itself was approved in advance, so an unapproved facility leaves the client in breach on enforcement.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Each Restricted Person must ensure that: any dealing by their Closely Connected Persons are undertaken in accordance with this Policy ... Closely Connected Entity: Any family company or family trust that the Restricted Person or their close family member(s) may control or have an interest in.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The hedging ban and financing gate reach family trusts and companies in which the person merely has an interest, so no holding structure escapes them.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Under the Papua New Guinea Capital Market Act 2015, Australian Corporations Act 2001 (Cth), PNGX Listing Rules, ASX Listing Rules, SPX Listing Rules ... Where this Policy is inconsistent with an applicable law, regulation or prudential standard within a relevant jurisdiction, the Policy applies only to the extent applicable.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: BSP is PNG-incorporated and triple listed, so any structure must clear PNG capital markets law and Bank of PNG prudential standards as well as Australian law, and disclosure runs to three exchanges.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons must keep, and make available to the Company Secretary ... on request, a register of dealings by themselves and their Closely Connected Persons, in the form of a record of every dealing, together with supporting material such as contract notes or their equivalent.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Every leg of any structure must be documented and producible to the Company on demand, so nothing about a financing arrangement can be kept private from BSP.

BFL.summary: A funded collar is not possible under this policy. Clause 3.8.2 bans outright any transaction designed to hedge exposure to Company Securities, with no approval route, no vesting-state carve-out and no exception in clause 3.6, and the clause 3.7 waiver cannot help because it is granted only where the Restricted Person is selling and not buying. Clause 3.8.1 independently prohibits forward contracts, short-selling and any trading on a short-term basis, defined as 6 months or less, which closes off prepaid forwards and other monetisation substitutes. The loan leg on its own is achievable: clause 3.8.3 permits margin lending and other secured financing arrangements in respect of Company Securities with the prior approval of the Chairman or delegate, and clause 3.6.1(e) then treats a financier's enforcement sale as a permitted dealing outside a Trading Window, so an unhedged secured facility over BSP shares is the only viable version of the structure. Any such facility must be documented with 5 Business Days' prior written notice to the approver in the clause 3.11 table, executed within a maximum 5 Business Day approval window that must itself fall inside one of the four announced Trading Windows, notified to the Company Secretary on completion, recorded in the person's own register of dealings, and, for directors, disclosed to PNGX, ASX and SPX.

NIC.exemption_authority: The Board (for the Chair) or the Chair of the Board (for other Directors and Senior Executives) may grant a waiver from the blackout or short-term trading rules in exceptional circumstances (rule 6.5), and may give, withhold, condition or withdraw approval to trade under rule 6.6 in its discretion without giving reasons.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This provision includes engaging in hedging or other arrangements that would have the effect of limiting the economic risk in connection with Company Securities including Securities which are unvested, subject to a holding lock or issued pursuant to an equity based remuneration scheme.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The collar's put and call legs need prior written approval from the rule 7 approver even if written over unvested or holding-locked equity award shares, not only fully vested unrestricted stock.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The policy contains no provision addressing margin lending, encumbrance, custodial transfer or any other secured financing arrangement over Company Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A loan secured on the collared shares is not expressly prohibited or made subject to clearance or disclosure, but the bank should obtain the Company's written confirmation, since the broad 'vary economic risk' language in 6.9 could arguably be read by the Company to capture the financing structure as a whole.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If granted, trading consent is only valid for a period of 5 trading days after notification of approval. Trading consent is automatically deemed to be withdrawn if the person becomes aware of inside information prior to trading.

bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The Company can refuse or withdraw clearance for the collar without explanation, and the executive cannot disclose a refusal to the bank, which is a practical execution risk for the transaction timeline.

bespoke_clauses.clause: their associates (as defined in the Corporations Act) including, close family members and trusts and entities controlled by them
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a family trust or controlled entity does not escape the clearance and hedging restrictions that apply to the Restricted Person.

NIC.summary: A funded collar is conditionally possible for a Nickel Industries director or Senior Executive, but only with prior written approval: clause 6.9 expressly names put and call options and CFDs and bans dealing in derivatives or hedging without approval from the Chair (or the Board, for the Chair), and this ban explicitly extends even to unvested or holding-locked shares. Approved trades must fall outside the roughly one-month quarterly blackout window, be executed within 5 trading days of clearance, and lapse automatically if inside information arises. The policy is entirely silent on margin lending, encumbrance and secured financing, so the loan leg secured on the collared shares is not expressly prohibited or regulated, but the bank should seek the Company's written comfort given the breadth of the 'vary economic risk' language. Refusal of approval is confidential and given in the Company's unfettered discretion, and short-term or speculative trading is discouraged, favouring a longer collar tenor.

AUB.ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may determine 'any additional periods' as Blackout Periods from time to time (7.1(d)). The policy is silent on whether such periods are announced or kept confidential, and on who lifts them.

rules.detail: There is no standalone derivatives rule. 'Securities' is defined to include derivatives, structured financial products, swaps and warrants with no venue limitation, and 'Deal' includes purchasing or selling or entering into an agreement to do so. Buying a put or writing a call over Company shares is therefore a Dealing in Company Securities: permitted only outside Blackout Periods, with prior written clearance, and with no Inside Information.
rules.evidence: Securities includes shares, options, rights, debentures, or other securities or derivatives including any structured financial product, swap, futures contract, contract for difference, spread bet, or warrant.

rules.detail: For an AUB Connected Person who is not a Designated Person, no Blackout Period or clearance requirement is imposed; only the absolute insider trading prohibition and (if a plan participant) the 7.7 hedging ban apply.
rules.evidence: Additional restrictions in this policy apply to Designated Persons, including requirements relating to Blackout Periods, clearance to Deal and other specified prohibitions.

rules.tier: Participants in a Company employee incentive plan
rules.detail: Absolute ban, with no clearance or exceptional-circumstances route, on any transaction limiting the economic risk of unvested Company Securities. A collar over unvested plan securities is squarely prohibited.
rules.evidence: Participants in a Company employee incentive plan (which includes Designated Persons) are prohibited from entering into a transaction that limits the economic risk of unvested Company Securities or vested Company Securities that are subject to a restriction on transfer, such as a holding lock.

rules.tier: Participants in a Company employee incentive plan
rules.detail: The ban extends past vesting to vested securities that remain subject to a transfer restriction such as a holding lock, so shares under a disposal restriction period cannot be collared even though they have vested.
rules.evidence: prohibited from entering into a transaction that limits the economic risk of unvested Company Securities or vested Company Securities that are subject to a restriction on transfer, such as a holding lock.

rules.detail: The 7.7 prohibition is limited by its terms to unvested securities and to vested securities still subject to a transfer restriction. Hedging vested, unrestricted shares (whether plan-sourced or bought on market) is not prohibited; it is caught only as a Dealing in derivative Securities requiring prior written clearance outside a Blackout Period.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons must not Deal in Company Securities at any time (including outside a Blackout Period) without prior written clearance

rules.detail: Monetisation, prepaid forwards and collar-plus-loan structures are not named. A prepaid forward or an agreement to sell is an 'agreement to do' a sale and so a Dealing requiring prior written clearance; the derivative legs are themselves Securities. Any loan leg secured on the shares must additionally be run past 7.8.
rules.evidence: Deal includes directly or indirectly applying for, subscribing for, purchasing or selling or entering into an agreement to do any of those things

rules.detail: Flat prohibition on short selling Company Securities, with no clearance route. Written calls settled against shares the person owns are not short sales, but any leg that leaves the person net short would breach.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons must not engage in short term Dealing or short selling in Company Securities.

rules.detail: Securities lending and borrowing are not mentioned anywhere in the policy and are not within the definition of Deal, which is confined to applying for, subscribing for, purchasing, selling and agreements to do those things.

CFDs and spread bets are expressly listed within the definition of Securities, so dealing in one is a Dealing requiring prior written clearance outside a Blackout Period. A short CFD would additionally breach the short selling ban and a CFD closed out inside 12 months the short term dealing ban.
rules.evidence: other securities or derivatives including any structured financial product, swap, futures contract, contract for difference, spread bet, or warrant.

rules.detail: Margin lending is permitted but not by right: prior approval is required, and it must come from the Chair of the Board (or the Chair of the Board Audit & Risk Committee in their absence) rather than the ordinary clearance officer. Approval is expressly required for entering the arrangement, for transferring shares into an existing margin loan account, and for selling shares to satisfy a margin call.
rules.evidence: Approval must be obtained prior to a Designated Person entering into margin lending arrangements in relation to Company Securities.

rules.detail: Granting security, a charge, lien or pledge is not itself within the definition of Deal and no general encumbrance rule exists. The only encumbrance regime is 7.8, and the policy directs anyone uncertain whether an arrangement is a margin lending arrangement to consult the Chief Legal and Risk Officer, so a lender's security over Company Securities should be treated as requiring Chair approval.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons should consult with the Company's Chief Legal and Risk Officer if they are uncertain as to whether an arrangement should be classified as a margin lending arrangement.

rules.detail: There is no blanket ban on secured financing. The policy addresses only 'margin lending arrangements in relation to Company Securities', which is not defined; a bank loan secured on collared shares is on its face such an arrangement, and in any event the uncertainty clause routes it to the Chief Legal and Risk Officer and then to Chair approval. Nothing prohibits the financing outright.
rules.evidence: Approval must be obtained prior to a Designated Person entering into margin lending arrangements in relation to Company Securities.

rules.detail: Short term Dealing is prohibited outright, with a 12 month intention-based benchmark running both ways (buy with a view to resale, or sell with a view to repurchase). The only carve-out is an immediate sale of securities acquired on conversion of another security, such as exercise of a share right.
rules.evidence: In general, the purchase of Company Securities with a view to their resale within a 12 month period, or the sale of Company Securities with a view to their repurchase within a 12 month period, will be considered to be a Dealing of a 'short term' nature.

AUB.exemption_authority: The Chair of the Board, or in the Chair's absence the Chair of the Board Audit & Risk Committee, may permit Dealing during a Blackout Period in exceptional circumstances (7.5) and must approve margin lending arrangements (7.8). The Board may add Blackout Periods (7.1(d)) and approves the policy. The CEO or CFO designate additional Designated Persons. There is no exemption from the hedging prohibition in 7.7 or the short selling and short term dealing prohibitions in 7.9.

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedging ban limited to unvested and locked securities
bespoke_clauses.clause: Participants in a Company employee incentive plan (which includes Designated Persons) are prohibited from entering into a transaction that limits the economic risk of unvested Company Securities or vested Company Securities that are subject to a restriction on transfer, such as a holding lock.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The hedging ban stops at vesting and release of the holding lock, so a collar over vested, unrestricted shares is not caught by it and remains available subject to clearance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Approval must be obtained prior to a Designated Person entering into margin lending arrangements in relation to Company Securities. Such Dealings would cover: (a) entering into a margin lending arrangement in respect of Company Securities; (b) transferring Company Securities into an existing margin loan account; and (c) selling Company Securities to satisfy a call pursuant to a margin loan.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike policies that ban all secured financing, AUB only requires Chair approval, so the loan leg of a funded collar is permissible if the Chair approves it.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons should consult with the Company's Chief Legal and Risk Officer if they are uncertain as to whether an arrangement should be classified as a margin lending arrangement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bank loan secured on collared shares should be put to the Chief Legal and Risk Officer up front, because if it is classified as margin lending the approval must come from the Chair rather than the ordinary clearance officer.

bespoke_clauses.topic: margin call sale is a controlled dealing
bespoke_clauses.clause: Such Dealings would cover ... selling Company Securities to satisfy a call pursuant to a margin loan.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A forced sale or enforcement by the financier is treated as the executive's own Dealing needing prior Chair approval, so a collar loan must not permit the bank to sell shares during a Blackout Period without that approval.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons must not engage in short term Dealing or short selling in Company Securities. In general, the purchase of Company Securities with a view to their resale within a 12 month period, or the sale of Company Securities with a view to their repurchase within a 12 month period, will be considered to be a Dealing of a 'short term' nature.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar tenor of less than 12 months, or one with early unwind or roll features, risks being characterised as short term Dealing, so the structure should be written for at least 12 months.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any clearance granted: (d) will be valid for a period of 7 calendar days from the date of approval; and (e) may be withdrawn at any time prior to the Dealing occurring. Any Dealing must occur within the period of the approval.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Pricing, documentation and execution of the collar and the secured loan must all complete within 7 calendar days of clearance, and the clearance can be pulled at any point before signing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Following any Dealing, the Designated Person must notify the Company Secretary within one business day.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Entry into the collar, and any later unwind, roll or settlement, must be reported to the Company Secretary within one business day, and for Directors it will also feed the Appendix 3Y notifiable interest disclosure.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Securities includes shares, options, rights, debentures, or other securities or derivatives including any structured financial product, swap, futures contract, contract for difference, spread bet, or warrant.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no venue limitation, so the OTC put and call written with a bank are themselves Company Securities and each leg is a Dealing subject to clearance and Blackout Periods.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Associate means ... an entity (including without limitation trusts, companies and nominees) and/or person that the AUB Connected Person controls or may be expected to control or influence.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Booking the collar or the loan through a family trust, company or nominee does not avoid the policy; the AUB Connected Person must take reasonable steps to ensure the Associate complies.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A Designated Person may be permitted to Deal in Company Securities during a Blackout Period where: (a) exceptional circumstances exist ... The Designated Person must demonstrate that the proposed Dealing is the only reasonable course of action available.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is a hardship and legal-obligation escape hatch approved by the Chair, but the 'only reasonable course of action' test means it will rarely support a discretionary collar entry or unwind inside a Blackout Period.

AUB.summary: A funded collar is possible under this policy, which is unusually permissive: there is no blanket prohibition on hedging vested shares and no ban on secured financing. Over vested Company Securities that are no longer subject to a holding lock or other transfer restriction, a Designated Person may buy a put and write a call, since both legs are 'Securities' and each is a Dealing requiring only prior written clearance (Chair of the Board for KMP, the Chair of the Board Audit & Risk Committee for the Chair, the Chief Legal and Risk Officer for others), granted outside the 15 December, 15 June and pre-AGM Blackout Periods, valid for 7 calendar days, revocable before execution, and notified to the Company Secretary within one business day. The loan leg secured on the collared shares is not prohibited but should be treated as a margin lending arrangement, which requires separate prior approval from the Chair of the Board and, importantly, means any enforcement sale by the bank also needs prior Chair approval and cannot simply run during a Blackout Period. The structure must not extend to unvested plan securities or vested securities still subject to a holding lock, where hedging is absolutely prohibited with no exemption, and must not leave the executive net short. Tenor should exceed 12 months so the arrangement is not characterised as short term Dealing under section 7.9.

bespoke_clauses.clause: During any period that is not a trading blackout period under section 4.1, all GQG Personnel must, prior to any proposed dealing, seek approval for the proposed dealing in the Company's securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike a typical open/closed trading window model, GQG Personnel need prior CCO approval for every dealing at any time of year, so a collar's entry, unwind or roll always needs fresh clearance rather than only during closed periods.

bespoke_clauses.topic: no vesting carve-out for hedging or monetisation
bespoke_clauses.clause: GQG Personnel are prohibited from engaging in hedging, monetization transactions or similar arrangements involving Company securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The ban is not limited to unvested or restricted holdings, so even a collar entirely over long-held, unrestricted vested shares is expressly prohibited, with no clearance route at all.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where any approval is required for a dealing under this Policy, approval will not be granted where, in the judgment of the CCO, the dealing would not satisfy the Front Page Test.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even the margin-lending leg, which is otherwise approvable, is subject to a discretionary reputational veto that a bank-structured, security-backed facility could well fail regardless of legal compliance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Company may, at its discretion, make any approval granted in accordance with section 4.5(a) conditional upon such terms and conditions as the Company sees fit (for example, with regard to the circumstances in which the Company's securities may be sold to satisfy a margin call).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If a secured loan were ever approved, GQG can impose its own conditions on when the lender may sell on a margin call, constraining a bank's standard enforcement rights over collared shares.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a disposal of securities of the Company that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A lender's enforcement sale is excluded from the short-term dealing, blackout and preclearance rules, but this does not cure the separate, unconditional ban on entering the hedge itself.

bespoke_clauses.clause: GQG Personnel must take appropriate steps to ensure that their "Connected Persons" only deal in securities in circumstances where the GQG Person to whom they are connected would be permitted to deal under this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Structuring the collar or loan through a family member's account or a related entity does not escape the hedging and derivatives bans.

GQG.summary: A funded collar is not possible under this policy. Section 3.4 imposes an unconditional, blanket ban on 'hedging, monetization transactions or similar arrangements' over Company securities, expressly including any arrangement that limits the economic risk of holding them, with no carve-out for vested or unrestricted shares and no clearance route. Section 3.3 separately bans dealing in any derivative linked to the value of the Company's securities other than those issued under an employee compensation plan, which independently catches an OTC put and call. Even the financing leg alone is constrained: a margin lending arrangement or transfer into a margin account needs prior CCO (and sometimes Board-committee) approval, is subject to a discretionary 'Front Page Test', and every dealing outside a blackout period requires fresh prior clearance regardless of the calendar. There is no exceptional-circumstances relief for entering a hedge (only for a sale in hardship or under court order), so a bank-funded equity collar cannot be implemented under this policy as drafted.

The Board may also derogate the Policy's application to a Personnel member's Associate where there is no conflict of interest, and the ACRMC approves amendments to the Policy itself.

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedging ban scoped to at-risk remuneration
bespoke_clauses.clause: Personnel must not trade in PNI Securities as part of a hedging arrangement aimed at limiting exposure in relation to part of their "at risk" remuneration.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike a blanket hedging ban, this only reaches securities forming part of incentive remuneration; a collar over ordinary vested, unrestricted, non-incentive PNI shares is not caught by the hedging prohibition and only needs standard trade pre-clearance, making a funded collar structurally available.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where there is an existing holding and more PNI Securities are purchased, the holding period is 2 months for all new and existing PNI Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any top-up purchase during the life of a collar (e.g. under a DRP variation, though DRP participation is itself blocked in Fixed Prohibited Periods) would restart the 2-month minimum hold across the whole collared position, delaying a permitted unwind.

bespoke_clauses.clause: PNI discourages the use of leveraged margin lending arrangements and other secured financing arrangements by Personnel in relation to PNI Securities but has not prohibited their use.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bank loan secured on the collared shares is permitted in principle, but is subject to prior disclosure to the Company Secretary/Board, prior written approval, and PNI's discretion to impose its own conditions on the facility, including on forced-sale triggers.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Disclosure of a Director's margin lending or secured financing arrangement will be required to be made to the ASX if there is a change in the Director's interest in Securities or if the Board determines that the existence of such arrangement would have a material effect on the price or value of Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A Director entering a funded collar may need to make a separate ASX disclosure of the financing arrangement itself, beyond the standard Appendix 3Y change-of-interest notice for the derivative legs.

bespoke_clauses.clause: trading wholly initiated by a party independent to the Personnel member (e.g. a margin call related sale of stock initiated by the margin lender)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bank's enforcement sale on default or margin call does not itself require fresh trading approval, giving the lender a clearer path to enforce security over the collared shares.

PNI.summary: A funded collar is achievable under this policy, subject to conditions. The hedging prohibition in section 4 is narrow: it only bans hedging arrangements tied to a Personnel member's "at risk" remuneration, so entering a collar over ordinary vested, unrestricted PNI shares is not itself banned and instead only needs standard prior written approval from the relevant authorising officer (Chair of the ACRMC for the Chair of the Board; Chair of the Board for other Directors/KMP/Company Secretary; Company Secretary for other Personnel), valid for 5 business days, outside the two Fixed Prohibited Periods and while not in possession of Inside Information. The financing leg is expressly permitted, though discouraged: entering a margin loan or other secured financing arrangement, or granting security over the shares, requires prior disclosure to the Company Secretary (who informs the Board) and prior written approval, and PNI may impose its own conditions, including on the circumstances of a margin-call sale; a lender's independently initiated enforcement sale does not itself need approval. Directors' financing arrangements may trigger a separate ASX disclosure obligation if they change the Director's interest or are assessed as material. The main structural constraints are the two Fixed Prohibited Periods, the 2-month minimum holding period (which resets across the whole holding on any new purchase), and PNI's broad discretion to refuse or condition approval and to withdraw it on a change of circumstances.

NWH.summary: A funded collar is not possible for NWH directors or employees under this policy. Clause 10 imposes an absolute, expressly overriding ("notwithstanding any other part of this policy") ban on directors and employees entering into any transaction in associated products that operates to limit the economic risk of their NWH shareholding - a purchased put and written call collar is squarely such a transaction - and there is no clearance route, vesting-state carve-out, or exceptional-circumstances relief available for it; the hardship/court-order relief in clause 7 covers only ordinary and short-term dealing during Restricted Periods, not hedging. The financing leg alone would otherwise be workable: entering a margin loan or otherwise encumbering NWH securities requires only disclosure of the arrangement's terms (number of securities, trigger points, and any unilateral lender sale right) to the Relevant Officers/Company Secretary on entry or variation, not prior approval, and a lender's enforcement sale is expressly excluded from the policy's operation. Because the hedge is banned outright for any director or employee, however, the financing leg cannot be paired with a collar in this structure. Consultants are excluded from both the hedging ban and the disclosure obligation, but this is not a realistic route for a director or executive. This is a 2010 policy and NRW Holdings may since have adopted an updated version that should be checked before relying on this conclusion.

EBO.exemption_authority: The Board of EBOS may approve updates, amendments to, and exemptions to this Policy from time to time. Within the Policy, the CEO (or the Chair for the CEO's, a Director's or the Chair's own trades, or the Chair of the Audit & Risk Committee for the Chair's trades) may grant, in their sole and absolute discretion, prior written consent to trade during a Blackout Period for severe financial hardship or legal/court compulsion; such approval is automatically deemed withdrawn if the person becomes an Information Insider before completing the trade.
jurisdiction_overlays: New Zealand Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 and NZX Listing Rules, applied alongside the Australian Corporations Act 2001 and ASX Listing Rules given EBOS's dual NZX/ASX listing

bespoke_clauses.topic: absolute margin lending / secured financing ban
bespoke_clauses.clause: You must not have margin lending arrangements in relation to EBOS Securities ... Restricted Persons must not enter into or continue with any margin loan arrangements to fund the acquisition of EBOS Securities or in relation to which EBOS Securities may be used as a security against repayment of the loan. This restriction extends to Restricted Persons' Associates.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is an unconditional, no-clearance ban on using EBOS Securities as loan security, so the financing leg of a bank-funded collar cannot be implemented under this policy for any tier, vesting state, or associate structure.

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedging ban scoped to unvested/locked entitlements
bespoke_clauses.clause: Rule 8 No hedging on unvested entitlements: Restricted Persons must not enter into hedging arrangements ... to limit their exposure in relation to unvested entitlements or vested entitlements that remain subject to any holding lock or other trading restriction.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The hedging ban does not reach ordinary vested, unrestricted EBOS shares, so the derivative legs of a collar (put and call) over such shares are not themselves prohibited and can proceed with CEO/Chair consent, unlike the financing leg.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A consent is automatically deemed to be withdrawn if you become aware of Material Information prior to trading and, in that event, you must not trade.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A cleared collar must be executed within the 10-day consent validity and can become unexecutable if Material Information arises before completion, requiring a fresh Request for Consent.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Rule 18 Chief Executive Officer trading ... Rule 19 Director trading ... Where the Chair proposes to make any Trade ... the prior written consent of the Chair of the Audit & Risk Committee shall be required.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: For a collar involving the CEO, a Director or the Chair, the consent chain escalates to a different, more senior approver, which must be factored into execution timelines and confidentiality of the request.

bespoke_clauses.clause: selling EBOS Securities to satisfy a call under a margin loan except where the holder of EBOS Securities has no control over the sale
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even if a secured facility existed in breach of Rule 7, a forced sale the holder has no control over is treated as outside the banned activity, but the underlying margin lending or security arrangement is prohibited from inception regardless.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Trading in EBOS Securities by a Director must be advised to NZX and ASX within 5 trading days ... All Trades in EBOS Securities by a Senior Manager must be disclosed to NZX (and will also be disclosed to ASX) within [5 trading days, or 20 working days for specified acquisitions].
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Entry into, and unwind of, the collar's derivative legs by a Director or Senior Manager each trigger separate NZX and ASX disclosure obligations with different timeframes depending on the trade type.

EBO.summary: A funded collar (a loan secured on the collared shares) is not possible under this policy: Rule 7 imposes an absolute, unconditional ban on margin lending and any arrangement in which EBOS Securities are used as security for a loan, extending to Restricted Persons' Associates, with no consent or clearance route. The unfunded derivative legs are, however, structurally available over vested, unrestricted EBOS shares: Rule 8's hedging ban is expressly confined to unvested entitlements and vested entitlements still subject to a holding lock or trading restriction, so a Restricted Person may enter a put/call collar over ordinary vested unrestricted shares (a derivative over EBOS shares is itself an "EBOS Security" and its acquisition a "Trade") subject to the standing Rule 3 consent regime: prior written CEO approval (Chair approval for the CEO, Directors and the Chair), consent valid for 10 days, refusal kept confidential, and execution outside the two Blackout Periods and the 3-month short-term trading restriction. Consent automatically lapses if Material Information arises before the trade completes, and Directors' and Senior Managers' dealings trigger separate NZX/ASX disclosure within 5 trading days (up to 20 working days for specified acquisition types). In short: the hedge can be structured with consent, but the loan cannot be secured on the shares under this policy as drafted.

FBU.ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Fletcher Building Company Secretary (Deputy Company Secretary if unavailable) holds the discretion: 'the approval to trade is at the discretion of the Fletcher Building Company Secretary' and Schedule II is only a set of 'general guidelines on when approval will not be granted'. The event-driven No Trade Periods for capital structure changes and corporate activity are self-executing and by their nature undisclosed, and refusals are confidential because 'In declining any approval to trade, no reasons need be given.'

rules.detail: Listed derivatives over Fletcher Building securities are within the Policy's definition of both 'trade' and 'securities', so trading them requires prior written notification to and consent from the Company Secretary and is barred during No Trade Periods. There is no express derivatives clause and no outright prohibition.
rules.evidence: 'trade' includes buying or selling listed securities, or agreeing to do so, and trading in derivatives (such as options or warrants) over or which relate to Fletcher Building securities, in each case whether as principal or agent

rules.detail: The definition of 'trade' in 1.1 catches derivatives 'over or which relate to Fletcher Building securities' with no venue limit, so an OTC put and call written with a bank is a trade requiring consent. Paragraph 3.4, which lists the securities covered, is narrower and refers only to 'listed derivatives', but the consent form expressly contemplates an 'off-market trade', so OTC positions must be cleared.
rules.evidence: trading in derivatives (such as options or warrants) over or which relate to Fletcher Building securities, in each case whether as principal or agent, but it does not include subscription for, or the issue of, new securities.

rules.tier: Any employee who is offered participation in equity based incentive remuneration
rules.detail: Absolute ban, with no consent route, on any transaction (derivative or otherwise) limiting the economic risk of participating in equity based incentive remuneration. The stated purpose is that 'the incentive remains at risk until achieved', so the ban bites while awards are unvested or subject to performance hurdles.
rules.evidence: Any employee who is offered participation in equity based incentive remuneration is prohibited from entering into transactions (whether through the use of derivatives or otherwise) which limit the economic risk of participating in the equity based incentive remuneration.

rules.tier: Any employee who is offered participation in equity based incentive remuneration
rules.detail: The Policy does not name a restricted-but-vested state, but Schedule I distinguishes the acquisition of an interest under a scheme from 'the subsequent transfer of the full and unrestricted titles to the shares on the satisfaction of, and at a time fixed by, the terms of the scheme'. Until unrestricted title transfers the incentive is arguably not yet 'achieved', so the clause 6 ban should be treated as still applying.
rules.evidence: This policy also includes a prohibition from entering into transactions which limit the economic risk of participating in equity based incentive remuneration, so that the incentive remains at risk until achieved.

rules.detail: Once full and unrestricted title has passed and the incentive has been achieved, clause 6 is spent; hedging of freely held shares, and of shares never acquired through an incentive plan, is not prohibited. Any such derivative is nonetheless a 'trade' requiring prior written consent from the Company Secretary and cannot be entered during a No Trade Period.
rules.evidence: Before trading the Company's securities, persons covered by this Policy must, in writing: (a) notify the Fletcher Building Limited Company Secretary of their intention to trade in securities, and receive consent to do so

rules.detail: Monetisation, prepaid forwards and similar structures are not named. An agreement to sell is expressly a trade, so a forward sale or collar-plus-loan monetisation of unrestricted shares needs prior written consent, valid 10 trading days, and must be outside a No Trade Period. Monetising equity incentive awards that are still at risk would breach clause 6.
rules.evidence: 'trade' includes buying or selling listed securities, or agreeing to do so

rules.detail: Short selling is not mentioned anywhere in the Policy or its Schedules. A short sale would still be a 'trade' requiring consent, but there is no express prohibition.
Securities lending and borrowing are not mentioned, and the definition of 'trade' (buying, selling, agreeing to do so, and trading in derivatives) does not obviously sweep in a stock loan.

CFDs are not named. A CFD is a derivative which relates to Fletcher Building securities and so is a 'trade' requiring prior written consent. If the underlying exposure is equity incentive remuneration still at risk, clause 6 prohibits it outright.
rules.evidence: trading in derivatives (such as options or warrants) over or which relate to Fletcher Building securities

rules.detail: Margin lending is not mentioned. There is no prohibition, no notification obligation and no guidance on forced sales by a margin lender during a No Trade Period.

Granting a mortgage, charge, lien or pledge over Fletcher Building securities is not mentioned and is not within the definition of 'trade', which is confined to buying, selling, agreeing to do so and trading in derivatives.

Secured financing in respect of Fletcher Building securities is not addressed at all: no prohibition, no clearance requirement, no disclosure trigger. The loan leg of a funded collar is therefore not caught by the Policy, though the security granted must not itself effect a disposal requiring consent.
There is no minimum holding period, no speculative or short-term trading ban and no LIFO or intention test. The only temporal constraint is that a consent lapses 10 trading days after notification.

clearance.approver: Fletcher Building Limited Company Secretary; delegated to the Deputy Company Secretary if the Company Secretary is not available
clearance.post_trade_to: NZX and ASX, by those persons who have been advised that they are required to make securities trading disclosures
clearance.post_trade_deadline: unspecified

clearance.evidence: A consent is only valid for a period of 10 trading days after notification.  A consent is automatically deemed to be withdrawn if the person becomes aware of material information prior to trading.

exceptions.evidence: Any interest in securities in the Company acquired on accepting an offer under a Company employee share scheme, and the subsequent transfer of the full and unrestricted titles to the shares on the satisfaction of, and at a time fixed by, the terms of the scheme.

Any interest in securities in the Company acquired on participating in the Executive Long-Term Share Scheme or similar legacy schemes; any forfeiture of securities on the failure to meet the performance requirements prescribed; and any transfer of full and unrestricted title at the time fixed by the terms of scheme.
Any shares acquired pursuant to the Company's dividend reinvestment plan.

Any pro-rata offer to all eligible shareholders of securities of the Company, whether to acquire by way of a rights or bonus issues or dispose of through a share repurchase/buy back or general share cancellation plan.
Accepting an offer made to all shareholders pursuant to the New Zealand Takeovers Code.

The excluded transactions are the request to convert any capital notes on an interest re-set date into shares of the Company; any shares so issued; and the repurchase or redemption of the capital note for cash if the company so elects not to issue shares.

Fletcher Building Corporate Governance practices, approved by the board annually
Company employee share scheme rules

FBU.exemption_authority: No formal exemption or waiver power. The Company Secretary has an unfettered discretion to grant or refuse consent to trade ('the approval to trade is at the discretion of the Fletcher Building Company Secretary'), and Schedule II is expressed as guidance only, so the Company Secretary can in principle consent during a listed No Trade Period. The clause 6 ban on limiting the economic risk of equity incentive remuneration is absolute and has no waiver route. The Board approves the Policy.
jurisdiction_overlays: New Zealand Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 insider trading regime is the primary legal overlay, not the Corporations Act
Dual listed NZX (FBU) and ASX (FBU); designated persons must make securities trading disclosures to both NZX and ASX
New Zealand Takeovers Code (specific insider trading exemption relied on for the takeover carve-out)
Policy expressly contemplates conduct outside New Zealand: 'even conduct that occurs entirely outside of New Zealand can also be subject to New Zealand's insider trading legislation'

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any employee who is offered participation in equity based incentive remuneration is prohibited from entering into transactions (whether through the use of derivatives or otherwise) which limit the economic risk of participating in the equity based incentive remuneration.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The only absolute prohibition in the Policy; it is drafted around the incentive remuneration itself rather than around a class of securities, so a collar over shares that are traceably incentive awards still at risk is banned outright with no consent route, while a collar over freely held or fully vested shares is not.

bespoke_clauses.clause: so that the incentive remains at risk until achieved
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This purpose statement is the best argument that the clause 6 ban falls away once awards have vested and unrestricted title has transferred, which is the state in which the bank's collar would be written.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Policy contains no reference to margin lending, secured financing, charges, pledges, encumbrances or forced sales anywhere in its eight clauses or two Schedules.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar, secured on the collared shares, is unregulated by this Policy, which is unusually permissive by ASX standards; only the derivative legs need clearance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: To be transacted: On NZX/ASX/off-market trade/other (specify)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The consent form expressly accommodates an off-market trade, confirming that an OTC collar can be described to and consented by the Company Secretary rather than being incapable of clearance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Fletcher Building securities covered by this Policy include shares, capital notes, options and rights ... and any listed derivatives, including futures contracts or warrants listed on an authorised futures exchange, in respect of Fletcher Building securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Paragraph 3.4 arguably confines 'securities' to listed derivatives while the definition of 'trade' in 1.1 has no venue limit; the conservative reading (consent required for an OTC collar) should be applied, and the ambiguity should be resolved with the Company Secretary in writing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A consent is only valid for a period of 10 trading days after notification.  A consent is automatically deemed to be withdrawn if the person becomes aware of material information prior to trading.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The 10 trading day window is generous by ASX standards and allows time to price and document a collar, but the consent self-destructs if the executive learns material information before execution, so a bank should require a bring-down confirmation at signing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Although the approval to trade is at the discretion of the Fletcher Building Company Secretary, Schedule II to this Policy sets out some general guidelines on when approval will not be granted.  In declining any approval to trade, no reasons need be given.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Consent can be refused without reasons for any reason, so neither the executive nor the bank can rely on a collar being renewable, rollable or unwindable at a future date.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any significant acquisition or divestment, having regard to the group as a whole: From day that there is a realistic prospect of a transaction arising until after full public disclosure is generally available to the market.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Undisclosed corporate-activity and capital-raising blackouts can arise at any time and are not calendar-bound, so physical settlement, unwind or roll of the collar may be blocked without warning.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any such person is included with respect to all of their interests in any of the Company's securities, whether direct, indirect, contingent, beneficial or legal.  The nature of an interest should be interpreted widely.  This will extend to interests held through other entities or persons (eg trusts, associates, related parties, spouses, and closely-held companies, etc) where the person has the ability to influence or control that person or entity.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A 'contingent' interest is expressly captured, so a collar or loan documented through a family trust or holding company is within the Policy and cannot be used to sidestep the consent requirement.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Policy contains no minimum holding period, speculative trading ban or intention test.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no tenor constraint on a collar and no risk that a short-dated or early-terminating structure is characterised as prohibited short-term dealing.

FBU.summary: A funded collar over fully vested, unrestricted Fletcher Building shares is achievable, and this is one of the more permissive policies of its kind. The Policy is silent on margin lending, secured financing, charges and forced sales, so the loan leg secured on the collared shares is not prohibited; the put and call legs are caught only as a 'trade' under paragraph 1.1, which expressly includes trading in derivatives over or relating to Fletcher Building securities with no venue limit. The conditions are prior written notification to and consent from the Company Secretary using the prescribed form (which contemplates an off-market trade), execution within the 10 trading day validity, no material information at execution, and timing outside the 1 July and 1 January No Trade Periods and any undisclosed capital-raising or corporate-activity blackout. The decisive constraint is clause 6: any employee offered equity based incentive remuneration is absolutely prohibited, with no consent route, from any transaction limiting the economic risk of that incentive remuneration, so the collar must be confined to shares whose incentive has been 'achieved' - vested with full and unrestricted title transferred - and must not reach awards still subject to performance hurdles or restriction. Consent is discretionary and may be refused without reasons, so neither entry nor any later roll or unwind can be treated as assured.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Employees are prohibited from entering into margin lending and other secured financing arrangements in respect of Spark New Zealand Restricted Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar, secured on the collared shares, is expressly and unconditionally prohibited for all employees regardless of vesting state or tier, with no clearance or exemption route identified anywhere in the policy.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any permission to deal can be given or refused by Spark New Zealand in its discretion, without giving reasons. ... Permission to deal can be withdrawn if new information comes to light or there is a change in circumstances.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even the unfunded derivative legs of a collar are subject to unreasoned, revocable consent, so a cleared trade cannot be relied upon as final until executed within the 10 trading day validity window.

bespoke_clauses.clause: There are no 'safe' periods for dealing in Spark New Zealand Restricted Securities. You may never deal in Spark New Zealand Restricted Securities if you have Inside Information.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Collar entry, unwind, roll or settlement must always be individually checked against Inside Information status; there is no blanket open window that removes that check.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A consent is automatically deemed to be withdrawn if the person becomes aware of Inside Information prior to dealing.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A cleared collar must be priced and executed within the 10 trading day validity and becomes unexecutable if Inside Information arises before signing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: All dealing involving: 1. Spark New Zealand Directors; or 2. Greater than 100,000 shares/options, must be approved by the Chairman of the Spark New Zealand Board.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar of institutional size (or entered by a director) escalates approval to the Chairman rather than the Company Secretary alone, adding a decision-maker to the bank's execution timetable.

bespoke_clauses.clause: You cannot avoid the insider trading laws by dealing in Spark New Zealand Restricted Securities through companies or trusts you control.

SPK.summary: A funded collar is not possible under this policy, although the unfunded hedge legs could be. Restricted Persons (directors, the Managing Director, Leadership Team and other designated staff) may enter a purchased put and written call over vested, unrestricted shares as a dealing requiring prior notification and consent from the Company Secretary (Chairman of the Board if the person is a Director or the size exceeds 100,000 shares/options), executed within 10 trading days, outside the half-year and full-year black-out periods, and only while not in possession of Inside Information; the express hedging ban applies only to unvested 'at-risk' remuneration. However, the policy separately and unconditionally prohibits employees from 'entering into margin lending and other secured financing arrangements' in respect of Spark New Zealand Restricted Securities, with no tier carve-out, security-state distinction or exemption authority, so the loan leg secured on the collared shares cannot be put in place. Consent for the derivative legs is discretionary, may be refused without reasons, and lapses automatically if Inside Information arises before execution. General employees outside the Restricted Persons/Directors tiers face no consent regime at all beyond the fundamental Inside Information prohibition, but are equally bound by the secured financing ban.

bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If a secured facility were ever put in place, the lender's enforcement sale is excluded from the closed-period/notification regime (though still subject to the insider trading ban), so enforcement is not itself a breach.

NHF.summary: A funded collar is not possible under this policy for Key Management Personnel or their Associates. Paragraph 4.1 imposes an absolute, carve-out-free ban on dealing 'at any time' in options, warrants, futures or other financial products issued over NHF Securities by third parties such as banks, which catches both the purchased put and written call legs of an OTC collar; paragraph 4.2 separately names 'a put option on incentive remuneration' as a prohibited hedging arrangement and more broadly bans transactions limiting the economic risk of a KMP's security holding. The loan leg is not entirely closed off: margin loans over NHF Securities are prohibited outright, but 'other secured financial arrangements' over NHF Securities are expressly permitted subject to Board approval, so a loan secured on the shares could in principle be approved on its own. A secured lender's enforcement sale, if it ever occurred, is a Schedule 4 excluded dealing outside the Closed Period/notification regime, though always subject to the insider trading ban. Because the option components have no approval or exceptional-circumstances route anywhere in the policy, the collar as a whole cannot be implemented notwithstanding the more permissive secured-financing provision.

L1G.summary: A funded collar's option legs are prohibited under this policy: section C(d) bars Covered Persons from entering into transactions in derivative instruments or other products associated with L1G Securities that operate to limit the economic risk of their holding, which squarely catches a purchased put and written call regardless of vesting state, and there is no clearance or exemption route for this prohibition (the Company Secretary's discretionary exemption applies only to breaches of the Closed Trading Period and short-term trading rules). bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The ban does not reach ordinary on-market vested shares, or plan shares once vesting and any holding lock have ended, so a collar over such shares is not prohibited by this clause.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and members of the GLT who finance acquisitions of Securities by margin call loans must advise the Company Secretary of these arrangements

bespoke_clauses.clause: a disposal of Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If the bank ever enforces its security and sells the collared shares, that sale is excluded from the short-term dealing, Closed Period and outside-period rules, though it remains subject to the insider trading law generally.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Approver may request more information from the applicant, grant the request, refuse the request or impose conditions on the dealing. ... If a request is not approved or an approval is revoked, that fact must be kept confidential.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even where a dealing does require approval (e.g. a collar entered while shares remain locked, or during a prohibited period), the Approver can impose bespoke conditions on the collar's terms and can revoke a granted approval at any time without reason.

MTS.summary: A funded collar over fully vested, unrestricted Metcash shares appears largely unrestricted by this policy: 'Securities' is defined narrowly as Metcash's own shares, options, notes, performance rights and debentures, so a bank-written OTC put and call are not 'Securities' and fall outside the Closed Period, approval and short-term dealing rules; the only hedging/derivative prohibition (section 6.1) is expressly confined to Securities that are unvested or still subject to a holding lock under an incentive plan. The loan leg is also workable: Directors and GLT members who finance acquisitions of Securities by margin call loans need only advise the Company Secretary for a register (with the Chair told of any lender intention to sell) rather than seek approval, though it is unclear whether this notification duty extends to a loan secured on already-vested shares rather than financing a purchase, and it does not extend to Specified Management at all. If the shares remain subject to a holding lock, or dealing occurs within a Closed Period (1 October to half-year results; 1 April to full-year results) or another Board-specified restricted period, prior written approval from the Chair (or the Group CEO for Specified Managers) is required, and is discretionary, conditional and revocable without reason. A secured lender's enforcement sale is expressly excluded from the short-term dealing and Closed Period rules. Overall, once shares are vested and unrestricted, this policy permits a funded collar with only light-touch disclosure, making it comparatively more accommodating than policies with a broader dealing/derivatives definition.

ZIP.summary: A funded collar over vested Zip shares is structurally available but fully discretionary. Both the derivative legs (put and call, caught as a hedging arrangement under clause 8.1) and the secured loan (clause 8.2) require prior written approval from an Approving Officer (the Chairperson for Directors/Officers/GET, or the Company Secretary/CFO/Executive Director for other Zip Personnel), executed outside the four annual Prohibited Periods and any confidential Board-imposed blackout, and while the executive holds no inside information. Hedging of unvested entitlements under an equity-based remuneration scheme is absolutely prohibited by clause 7.1 with no approval route, so the collar must be confined to shares that have already vested. Approval, once granted, is valid for only 7 business days and may be refused or revoked at the Approving Officer's absolute and unreviewable discretion, kept confidential if declined, so timing and durability are real execution risks. Family trusts or entities controlled by the executive do not escape these requirements, as they are themselves defined as Zip Personnel.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Company Personnel who are not in possession of Inside Information may also apply for and be given written approval to encumber Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar can be secured on the shares even inside a Closed Period, subject to a case-by-case approval, which is unusually permissive compared with policies that ban secured financing outright.

bespoke_clauses.topic: lender enforcement excluded from Closed Period ban
bespoke_clauses.clause: A disposal of Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement [is Excluded Trading, completed] without seeking prior approval.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement sale on default or margin call is not itself a Policy breach and needs no fresh clearance, even during a Closed Period, reducing the bank's execution risk on default.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any prior written approval to trade in Securities ... is automatically deemed: (a) to be withdrawn if the person becomes aware of any Inside Information ... (b) suspended upon the start of any Closed Period ... (c) to lapse upon expiration of any time limit for which the approval to trade applies.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A cleared collar trade must be executed within its stated time limit and before any Closed Period or inside information arises, or fresh approval is required.

bespoke_clauses.topic: Canadian SEDI reporting of related financial instruments
bespoke_clauses.clause: a Reporting Insider is required to disclose any change in any interest in, or right or obligation associated with, a related financial instrument. Reporting Insiders must file an insider report electronically through ... 'SEDI', usually within five days after the trade occurs.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: As a Canadian-incorporated, dual-listed issuer, a collar entered by a Reporting Insider is likely a 'related financial instrument' requiring its own SEDI filing within about 5 days, additional to and separate from the ASX-side approval and reporting process.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Policy contains no reference to unvested entitlements, holding locks or equity incentive scheme vesting.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no distinct restriction (or exemption) tailored to unvested shares; the collar analysis turns entirely on the general trading-approval and encumbrance-approval provisions regardless of how the shares were acquired.

SX2.summary: A funded collar appears achievable under this Policy, which is unusually permissive: there is no hedging-specific prohibition at all, and both encumbering the shares (the loan leg) and entering the derivative legs as ordinary 'trading' are approvable with prior written approval, even inside a Closed Period in exceptional circumstances (hardship, court order or Board discretion) for the encumbrance. Outside Closed Periods, standard prior written approval from the Chair, CEO or Managing Director (or the Audit Committee Chair if the applicant is the Chair) is required, automatically lapses if the person acquires Inside Information or a Closed Period begins, and must be exercised within its stated time limit, so execution should be timed to an open window. A secured lender's enforcement sale on default or margin call is expressly excluded from the Closed Period ban and needs no fresh approval, which reduces the bank's counterparty risk on enforcement. As a Canadian-incorporated dual-listed entity, a Reporting Insider entering the collar will likely also need to file a SEDI report on the resulting 'related financial instrument' within about five days, a disclosure duty separate from the ASX-side clearance process. Directors additionally must report the transaction to the Corporate Secretary within 2 business days for onward 5-business-day ASX disclosure.

Independently of the Policy's clearance procedure, a Director must notify ASX (via the Company Secretary) within 5 business days of any change in interests in a contract that confers a right to call for or deliver Company shares - language that squarely covers an OTC put/call collar.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Company Securities... includes any shares in the Company, debentures (including convertible notes) issued by the Company, units of shares in the Company and options to acquire or subscribe for shares in the Company... to 'deal' in Company Securities includes subscribing for, purchasing or selling Company Securities or entering into an agreement to do any of those things.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A third-party OTC put/call collar is arguably neither a 'Company Security' nor itself a 'deal', so its creation may fall outside this Policy's clearance and Blackout Period regime entirely, though this interpretation carries risk and should be confirmed with the Company Secretary before relying on it.

bespoke_clauses.topic: Director ASX disclosure of option-like contracts
bespoke_clauses.clause: a director of the Company must notify ASX within 5 business days after any change in ... interests in contracts to which the director is a party or under which the director is entitled to a benefit, and that confer a right to call for or deliver shares in or debentures of the Company
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even if the internal clearance process does not reach the collar, a Director must still notify ASX (Appendix-3Y-style) within 5 business days of entering it, and must tell the Company Secretary promptly so that filing can be made.

bespoke_clauses.topic: margin lending expressly excluded from broker-credit ban
bespoke_clauses.clause: not utilise broker credit ... Such prohibition does not extend to normal documented margin lending or loan facilities offered to the general public by brokers, banks or other lending institutions.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar is not banned outright, though the 'offered to the general public' qualifier creates doubt as to whether a bespoke bilateral facility for one executive squarely fits the carve-out.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the purchase of Company Securities with a view to resale within a 12 month period and the sale of Company Securities with a view to repurchase within a 12 month period would be considered to be transactions of a "short term" nature
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If the collar's settlement disposes of shares within 12 months of their acquisition and any repurchase intention is present, it risks being characterised as prohibited short-term trading; a straightforward one-way exit is less likely to be caught.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A "Blackout Period" operates in respect of ... the close of business on 31 December and 30 June ... and ... the last Trading Day of each month up to the ... Monthly Net Tangible Asset per Share announcement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike policies granting the Board a general discretion to declare extra confidential blackouts, MFF's Blackout Periods are limited to fixed, predictable reporting dates, making collar timing more certain.

MFF.summary: A funded collar is plausibly achievable, and on unusually favourable terms if the narrow definitions are read literally. 'Company Securities' and 'deal' are defined narrowly (the Company's own shares/debentures/options, and subscribing, purchasing, selling or agreeing to do so), so the OTC put and call legs of a collar with a bank may not themselves be caught by the Policy's Company Secretary approval process or Blackout Periods at all, though this reading should be confirmed given the general principles in clause 6.1. The loan leg is expressly not banned: normal documented margin lending or loan facilities from banks or lending institutions are carved out of the broker-credit prohibition, though the 'offered to the general public' qualifier leaves some doubt for a bespoke bilateral facility. Directors must separately notify ASX within 5 business days of entering any contract conferring a right to call for or deliver Company shares, which squarely covers an option-based collar, and within 14 days of any change in relevant interest. Any actual sale or transfer of the underlying shares (e.g. on settlement) is a 'deal' requiring prior notification to, and subsequent written confirmation with, the Company Secretary, must avoid the fixed half-year and monthly NTA Blackout Periods (absent exceptional-circumstances consent), and should not be structured to look like short-term trading within 12 months of acquisition.

RWC.exemption_authority: No exemption exists from the hedging ban (6.3) or the margin lending ban (6.2) - neither has an exceptions process anywhere in the Policy. For blackout-period dealing (5.3) and short-term dealing (6.1), the CEO (Senior Executives/Nominated Employees/Employees), the Chair of the Board (Directors), or the Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee (the Chair) may approve in their sole discretion where exceptional circumstances (severe financial hardship or court order) are evidenced.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Under this Policy, hedging of the Company's securities is not permitted.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A put-and-call collar is a textbook hedge of holding risk; it is banned outright for every tier with no exceptional-circumstances or Board-discretion route anywhere in the Policy, unlike blackout dealing and short-term dealing which do have hardship/court-order routes.

bespoke_clauses.topic: absolute margin lending ban, broadly worded
bespoke_clauses.clause: Employees, directors, and Connected Persons must not engage in any dealing in the Company's securities in connection with a margin lending arrangement. ... entering into a margin lending arrangement ... transferring securities ... into an existing margin loan account ... selling securities ... to satisfy a call.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The funded loan leg, if it functions as a share-secured facility with margin-call-style triggers, is likely to be treated the same as a margin loan and banned outright with no approval route at any stage of the arrangement.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Company will take a substance over form approach and will have regard to the intent and spirit of this Policy when applying and enforcing it.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Labelling the loan something other than a 'margin loan' is unlikely to escape the 6.2 prohibition if it is secured against, and enforceable by reference to the value of, the shares.

bespoke_clauses.topic: lender enforcement carve-out does not legitimise the loan
bespoke_clauses.clause: a disposal of securities of the Company that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement [is excluded from sections 5.1, 5.2, 5.4 and 6.1].
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even though a genuine secured lender's own enforcement sale is excused from blackout/window/approval rules, this exclusion is about the disposal only - it does not cure the underlying prohibition on the executive entering into the arrangement in the first place.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Sections 5.1, 5.2, 5.4 and 6.1 of this Policy do not apply to ... participation in an employee, executive or director equity plan operated by the Company.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The equity-plan exclusion only lifts the blackout/window/approval and short-term dealing rules for plan participation itself - it does not touch the hedging ban (6.3) or the margin lending ban (6.2), both of which apply with full force to vested plan shares once collar structuring is contemplated.

RWC.summary: A funded collar is not possible under this Policy for any tier. Hedging of the Company's securities - which a purchased put and written call over vested shares squarely constitutes - is banned outright by clause 6.3 with no exceptions process anywhere in the Policy. Separately, clause 6.2 bans any dealing connected with a margin lending arrangement, including entering the arrangement, transferring shares into it, and selling to meet a call, again with no approval route, and the Company's stated substance-over-form approach (section 10) means a differently-labelled but functionally equivalent share-secured loan is unlikely to escape that ban. The only relief mechanisms in the Policy - the exceptional-circumstances approval for blackout-period dealing and for short-term dealing, and the equity-plan/DRP/takeover/non-discretionary-plan exclusions - apply to different, unrelated restrictions (windows, short-term trading) and do not extend to either the hedging or the margin lending prohibition. A secured lender's own enforcement sale on default is excused from blackout and approval requirements, but that does not make entry into the loan itself lawful under the Policy.
