bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons are prohibited from entering into hedging arrangements to limit their exposure in relation to "at-risk" remuneration (meaning any unvested shares, options or rights issued or acquired under any future Chorus employee incentive schemes where performance hurdles have not yet been achieved or other conditions have not yet been met).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar over already-vested, unrestricted shares is not caught by the only hedging-specific prohibition in the Policy; it is treated as an ordinary dealing requiring consent (for Restricted Persons) or nothing beyond the Inside Information rule (for other Chorus Personnel).

bespoke_clauses.clause: "Chorus Restricted Securities" means any Chorus shares, options, derivatives and debt securities. ... any options, derivatives or other financial products issued or created over or in respect of any securities of Chorus.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no interpretive gap: entering an OTC put/call collar is unambiguously a dealing in a Chorus Restricted Security, so the consent process (for Restricted Persons) applies directly rather than by analogy.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Policy contains no reference to margin lending, secured financing, or encumbering securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar is neither banned nor expressly permitted; the Bank should confirm with the General Counsel and Company Secretary whether pledging or transferring the shares to a collateral agent needs consent as an 'otherwise deal[ing]' in Chorus shares, by analogy with the express 'transferring shares to a trust' example.

bespoke_clauses.topic: double approval for Directors and large trades
bespoke_clauses.clause: all dealings involving (i) Chorus Directors or (ii) greater than 100,000 shares/options must be approved by the Chairman of the Board.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A Director's collar, or any Restricted Person's collar exceeding 100,000 shares/options, needs both General Counsel and Company Secretary consent and separate Chairman approval.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A consent is only valid for a period of 10 trading days after notification ... A consent is automatically deemed to be withdrawn if the Restricted Person becomes aware of Inside Information prior to dealing.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Pricing and execution of the collar must occur within 10 trading days of consent, and any inside information arising before execution voids the consent.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This policy applies whether the dealing is to be done in New Zealand or overseas and whether or not the dealing relates to Chorus' New Zealand or foreign securities
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An offshore-booked OTC collar with an international bank is still squarely within scope of the Policy and its consent/black-out requirements.

CNU.summary: A funded collar over vested, unrestricted Chorus shares appears achievable. The Policy's only hedging-specific prohibition is expressly limited to unvested 'at-risk' remuneration, so hedging vested shares is treated as an ordinary dealing in a Chorus Restricted Security (a category that expressly includes derivatives): for a Restricted Person this needs prior written consent from the General Counsel and Company Secretary (plus Chairman approval if the person is a Director or the trade exceeds 100,000 shares/options), consent lasting 10 trading days and lapsing automatically if Inside Information arises, executed outside the two annual results black-out periods (or any ad hoc GC&CS-declared period) absent severe hardship or a court order; for other Chorus Personnel, only the fundamental no-dealing-on-Inside-Information rule applies, with no consent process at all. The Policy is entirely silent on margin lending, secured financing and encumbrance, so the loan leg of the collar is not expressly addressed either way, and the Bank should confirm whether pledging the shares or transferring them to a collateral agent is treated as 'dealing' requiring the same consent, given the Policy's example that transferring shares to a trust does require consent. As a dual NZX/ASX-listed issuer, the Policy applies to dealings anywhere in the world, so an offshore-booked collar is not outside its scope.

LSF.exemption_authority: The Board may agree to a Restricted Person dealing during a blackout period (5.4: "unless otherwise agreed to by the Board"), and the Chairperson may grant a sale-only hardship clearance under 5.8. No exemption exists from the absolute hedging ban in 5.10.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Company does not have employees and most activities are outsourced, including investment management.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no unvested/vested distinction to navigate; any collar would be over ordinary shares held outright by a director or officer, so the analysis turns entirely on the hedging ban and margin loan consent regime rather than plan-security carve-outs.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A Restricted Person must not enter into hedging arrangements with respect to securities in the Company (including any shares, options and rights).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike the margin loan regime, there is no consent or clearance mechanism for hedging at all; a collar's put and call legs are squarely 'transactions in financial products that operate to limit the economic risk' of the shareholding and are banned outright with no route to permission.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Company may, at its discretion, make any clearance granted in accordance with this Clause 5.11 conditional upon such terms and conditions as the Company sees fit (for example, in regards to the circumstances in which the securities in the Company may be sold to satisfy a margin call).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even though the loan leg of a collar (a secured financing/margin-type arrangement) is not banned outright, the Company's consent is required up front and can be conditioned on when and how the lender may force a sale, which a bank counterparty would need to accommodate contractually.

bespoke_clauses.topic: no closed-period carve-out for margin calls
bespoke_clauses.clause: The Restricted Persons are to be subject to restrictions on trading in the Company's shares at certain times of the year.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The policy does not state that a lender's forced sale to meet a margin call is excluded from the blackout periods, so enforcement of the loan or unwind of the collar during a closed period is not clearly protected and would likely need Board agreement or advance structuring around windows.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Board has an absolute discretion to place an embargo on Restricted Persons and/or their respective associated parties trading in the Company's shares at any time.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An unscheduled, discretionary trading embargo (confidentiality not addressed) can override any planned collar entry, unwind or hedge adjustment at short notice.

LSF.summary: A funded collar is not possible in the form the bank typically offers, because clause 5.10 imposes an absolute, clearance-free ban on any 'hedging arrangement' or transaction in financial products that limits the economic risk of holding L1 Long Short Fund shares, which squarely catches an OTC purchased put and written call; there is no exemption authority for this ban. The financing leg is more workable: margin lending or similar secured financing is not prohibited but requires the Company's prior written consent (via the Chairperson and Company Secretary), and the Company can impose conditions, including on when a lender may sell to meet a margin call. Even if the derivative ban were somehow structured around, ordinary share dealing (including any sale on unwind) requires prior notification to the Company Secretary and is barred during the four annual blackout periods (5 business days around dividend/capital management announcements, half-year results, full-year results and the AGM) and during any Board-imposed embargo, with only a narrow sale-only hardship exception available from the Chairperson. Because there is no employee equity incentive scheme, there is no unvested/vested distinction; the shares in question would be ordinary vested holdings throughout. Overall, the bank could not lawfully write the derivative legs of a collar for a Restricted Person or their associates under this policy as currently drafted.

RSG.exemption_authority: The Approving Officer may grant a sale-only clearance during a Closed Period in Exceptional Circumstances (severe financial hardship, court order, or other overriding legal/regulatory requirement), limited to the number of shares needed and subject to no Inside Information and compliance with Article 19 of UK MAR; described as unlikely to be granted except in rare cases. No exemption exists from the PDMR's absolute, permanent prohibition on financial products/hedge arrangements or margin lending/similar secured arrangements in section 5.

FCA notification requirements for PDMRs and PCAs

bespoke_clauses.topic: PDMR absolute derivatives and secured-financing ban
bespoke_clauses.clause: PDMRs are prohibited at all times from Dealing in financial products issued or created over or in respect of the Company's Securities (including, but not limited to, hedge arrangements). ... PDMRs are prohibited at all times from entering into margin lending or similar arrangements in respect to Company Securities they hold or in which they have a Relevant Interest.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Both legs of a funded collar with a bank (the OTC put/call and the secured loan) are banned outright for any PDMR at all times, with no clearance mechanism, no vesting distinction and no listed exception route in Schedule 1 or 2 (those only cover ordinary share sales in Exceptional Circumstances).

bespoke_clauses.clause: For the avoidance of doubt this prohibition in relation to financial products does not apply to an option over unissued capital granted by the Company.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Confirms the ban targets third-party/market derivatives like a bank collar, not the Company's own incentive option grants; it gives no comfort for a bank-written structure.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Sections 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11 and 14 also apply to PCAs of PDMRs ... Section 5 (the absolute hedging/margin-lending ban) is not among the sections listed as extending to PCAs.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: On a literal reading, a PDMR's family trust or spouse (a PCA) is not directly bound by the absolute section 5 ban, only by the general clearance/notification regime; however the PDMR's own overriding duty to 'ensure that their PCAs do not breach this Policy' makes routing a collar through a PCA a live legal risk rather than a clean workaround.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Deal ... includes: ... using Company Securities as security for a loan or other obligation.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: For senior employees who are not PDMRs, both the derivative legs and the secured loan of a collar are only 'Dealings' requiring ordinary prior clearance and post-trade notification, not an absolute ban, making a funded collar structurally possible for that population subject to Closed Periods and Approving Officer discretion.

bespoke_clauses.clause: from 1 January of each year until publication of the Company's annual financial report ... from 1 July of each year until publication of the Company's half-year financial report ... from first day of each Quarter until the publication of the Company's quarterly report
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Because RSG reports quarterly, half-yearly and annually, and each Closed Period runs from the start of the period to publication (with a 30-day minimum for annual/half-year), open trading windows for entering or unwinding a collar are narrow and must be checked quarter by quarter.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The status of Trading Plans and Investment Programmes under the UK Market Abuse Regulation and, more particularly the ability of a member of Personnel to carry out transactions under a Trading Plan or an Investment Programme during Closed Periods, remains uncertain.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even for non-PDMR Personnel, the Company treats derivative or plan-based structures executing during a Closed Period as legally uncertain under UK MAR and takes a conservative approach, so a bank should expect execution to be confined to open windows.

RSG.summary: For a PDMR (director or senior executive with regular access to Inside Information), a funded collar with a bank is not possible: section 5 imposes an absolute, permanent, clearance-free prohibition on Dealing in any financial product created over or in respect of Company Securities (expressly including hedge arrangements) and on margin lending or similar secured arrangements, with no exception in Schedules 1 or 2. For other Personnel, both legs are only 'Dealings' under the broad definitions (which expressly cover derivatives, agreements to deal, and using shares as security for a loan), so a collar is structurally possible subject to prior written clearance from the Approving Officer (5 Business Day validity, 3 Business Day response), post-trade notification to the Company Secretary within 1 Business Day, and execution outside the frequent Closed Periods (which run from the start of each quarter/half-year/year until results are published, plus event-driven blackouts). Routing a PDMR's collar through a family member or trust (a PCA) is legally uncertain, since the absolute section 5 ban is not among the sections expressly extended to PCAs, but the PDMR's overriding duty to prevent PCA breaches makes this an unreliable workaround rather than a safe structuring route. No exemption authority exists for the section 5 ban; the only discretionary relief (Exceptional Circumstances) is limited to a sale-only clearance during a Closed Period and would not authorise a collar's derivative or loan legs in any event.

MSB.exemption_authority: None. There is no hardship, court-order or other discretionary waiver from the black-out periods or the derivatives ban; only the fixed exceptions in clause 3.6 (managed portfolios, dividend reinvestment plans, option exercise) apply, and the Board's power under 3.5(c) is only to add further blackout periods, not to grant relief from them.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Mesoblast Personnel must not trade in the Company's derivatives.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This one-line, undefined and unconditional prohibition applies to every director, officer, employee, contractor and consultant (and their Connected Persons) at all times, with no clearance mechanism and no vesting distinction, and on a natural reading blocks the purchased put and written call legs of a bank collar outright.

bespoke_clauses.clause: No provision of the policy refers to margin lending, security, charges, pledges or any other secured financing arrangement in respect of Company securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar (secured on the collared shares) is not expressly prohibited or regulated by this policy at all, so absent the derivatives ban it would not itself be a policy obstacle; however, since the derivative legs are banned, the financing leg cannot be isolated into a compliant transaction.

bespoke_clauses.topic: trust/company structuring does not avoid insider trading
bespoke_clauses.clause: the definition of "procure" can include a director or employee who acquires Company securities through a trust or company while in possession of "inside information" may contravene these insider trading provisions and this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Structuring the collar or loan through a personal trust or holding company does not avoid personal liability if the individual is in possession of inside information at the time, and Connected Persons (including such trusts and controlled companies) are independently bound by the clause 3 rules including the derivatives ban.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This policy was adopted by the Mesoblast Board of Directors on 28 August 2013.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The document provided is dated 2013 with no amendment history or next-review date recorded; a bank should confirm this remains Mesoblast's current, in-force Share Trading Policy before relying on its terms.

MSB.summary: A funded collar is not possible under this policy for any Mesoblast Personnel or their Connected Persons. Clause 3.3 imposes an absolute, unconditional and undefined ban on trading in 'the Company's derivatives', with no clearance mechanism, no exception in clause 3.6, no vesting distinction, and no discretionary waiver authority anywhere in the document, so the purchased put and written call legs of an OTC collar are prohibited outright regardless of whether the shares are vested. This ban extends to a Designated Person's spouse, minor children, nominee or investment manager, family trust, or family-controlled company, so routing the derivative through an associate does not avoid it. By contrast, the loan leg is entirely unaddressed: the policy contains no provision on margin lending, encumbrance or secured financing, so a standalone secured loan (without the derivative overlay) would not itself breach this policy. Because the collar's option legs are banned, the structure as a whole cannot be implemented, and any attempt to acquire the securities or deal via a trust or company while in possession of inside information would separately risk an insider trading contravention. The document is dated 2013 with no evidence of subsequent amendment, so its current force should be confirmed before relying on it.

OBM.exemption_authority: The Authorising Officer has absolute, case-by-case discretion under 4.3 to approve Dealings during a Blackout Period, or other Dealings otherwise prohibited by the Policy but not prohibited by law, for severe financial hardship or a court order/enforceable undertaking. Whether this discretion can extend to override the separate 'at any time' bans on protection arrangements and security-granting/margin lending over unvested or holding-locked securities (3.5(a), 3.6(a)) is untested, since those bans are not framed as prohibitions on 'Dealing' (the defined term used in 4.3).

bespoke_clauses.clause: OBM Persons must not ... enter into any type of "protection arrangements" ... (a) in respect of any OBM Shares or Incentive Plan Securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock – at any time; and (b) otherwise – without approval under section 5.1.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The prohibition on hedging/protection arrangements (and the parallel prohibition on granting security/margin lending in 3.6) is tied to vesting status, not to tier: it is an absolute, clearance-free bar while shares are unvested or subject to a holding lock, but becomes merely approval-gated once the shares vest and any holding lock lifts. A funded collar is therefore only conceivable over shares that have fully vested and are no longer holding-locked.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A disposal of OBM Shares or Incentive Plan Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights under a loan or security agreement, subject to the grant of security having been granted with approval under section 5.1 [is not regulated by this Policy and may be undertaken ... at any time].
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike most peer policies, OBM expressly exempts a bank's enforcement sale on default from the Policy altogether, including during a Blackout Period, so long as the original grant of security over the shares was itself approved. This directly de-risks the lender's ability to enforce the collar loan's security without the borrower being put in breach.

bespoke_clauses.clause: grant any form of security (whether by way of charge, mortgage, pledge or otherwise) over any OBM Shares or Incentive Plan Securities ... to secure any obligation of that person or any third party.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The security-granting prohibition/approval regime is not limited to bank margin loans; it expressly covers any charge, mortgage or pledge securing any obligation (even a third party's), so the collar loan's security interest is squarely within scope and needs 5.1 approval once shares are vested and unrestricted.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any written approval granted under this Policy will be valid for the period of 5 trading days ... Written approval ... may be withdrawn by the Authorising Officer in writing, in person or by email at any time during the approval period.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A cleared collar (derivative legs and/or security grant) must be executed within 5 trading days, and the Authorising Officer can revoke the approval at any point before execution, so timing and re-clearance risk should be built into the transaction schedule.

bespoke_clauses.clause: In exceptional circumstances an Authorising Officer has discretion to approve under section 5.1: (a) Dealings in OBM Shares during a Blackout Period; or (b) other Dealings, that would otherwise be prohibited by this Policy but are not prohibited by law.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: It is unclear whether this hardship/court-order override (framed around 'Dealings') can reach the separately-worded absolute bans on protection arrangements and security-granting over unvested/holding-locked shares, since those bans are not expressed as prohibitions on 'Dealing'; the bank should not assume this route can unlock a collar before full vesting.

OBM.summary: A funded collar is workable under this policy, but only once the underlying OBM shares have fully vested and any holding lock has lifted: over unvested or holding-locked shares, both the derivative legs (a 'protection arrangement' under 3.5, expressly including hedging and short selling) and the loan's security (3.6) are banned at any time with no exception. Once the shares are vested and unrestricted, both legs become merely approval-gated: an OBM Person or their Connected Person may enter into the protection arrangement and grant security over the shares (to secure their own or even a third party's obligation, covering the bank loan) with prior written approval from the Authorising Officer (5 trading days' validity, revocable, refusal confidential but not final in the sense that a fresh request can always be made). Execution must also avoid the quarterly, half-year and full-year Blackout Periods (and any additional period set by the Board or Managing Director) unless the Authorising Officer grants an exceptional-circumstances approval for hardship or a court order. Distinctively, OBM's policy expressly carves out a secured lender's enforcement sale on default from the Policy altogether, including during a Blackout Period, provided the original security grant was itself approved, which meaningfully de-risks the bank's enforcement rights. Key Management Personnel must separately notify the Company Secretary of every Dealing, including exempt ones, within two business days for ASIC/ASX reporting.

ILU.exemption_authority: Under 2.4, the Chairman of the Audit and Risk Committee, the Chairman, or the Company Secretary (per the 2.5 approval chain) may grant a sale-only clearance during a Closed Period for severe financial hardship, a court order or enforceable undertaking, or another overriding legal or regulatory requirement, on sufficient evidence. The Section 4 exclusions and the 2.4 exceptional-circumstances process apply only to Sections 2.3 (Closed Period), 2.5 (clearance) and 3.1 (short-term trading); no exemption authority is provided anywhere from the Section 3.2 bans on economic-risk-limiting transactions over unvested/holding-locked securities or on KMP using securities as collateral.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and employees must not at any time enter into a transaction (e.g. a derivative) that operates or is intended to operate to limit the economic risk of holdings of unvested Company securities or vested Company securities which are subject to a holding lock.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The put/call legs of a collar are absolutely banned, with no clearance route, only while the underlying shares are unvested or holding-locked. Once vested and unrestricted, the same transaction is merely an ordinary 'dealing' in a security (since the Securities definition expressly includes derivatives and CFDs) requiring prior written clearance for Directors and Restricted Employees.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Key Management Personnel (KMP) must not at any time enter into a transaction that involves using Company securities as collateral in any financial transaction, including margin lending arrangements.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: For a KMP, the secured loan leg of a funded collar is banned permanently and unconditionally, regardless of vesting status, with no clearance route and no exclusion under Section 4 (which only carves out Sections 2.3, 2.5 and 3.1, not 3.2). This blocks a funded collar for KMP even over long-vested, unrestricted shares.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Section 3.2(b) applies only to Key Management Personnel; no equivalent express provision restricts non-KMP Directors or employees from granting security over their Company securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: For a Director or employee who is not KMP, the secured loan leg of a collar is not expressly prohibited by this Policy, and pledging shares (without a change of beneficial ownership) may fall outside the 'deal' definition altogether, making a funded collar structurally more feasible for that population, subject to legal confirmation.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a disposal of securities of the Company that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement [is excluded from the operation of Sections 2.3, 2.5 and 3.1].
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bank's enforcement sale on default is expressly excluded from the Closed Period ban, the clearance requirement and the 12-month short-term trading rule, which materially de-risks the bank's ability to enforce security over a non-KMP borrower's shares.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and Restricted Employees must not disclose to anyone that an Additional Closed Period is in effect.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An undisclosed, Board-imposed blackout can arise at any time and cannot be revealed even to a transacting counterparty, adding execution-timing risk to entering, adjusting or unwinding a collar.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors or Restricted Employees given clearance to trade must trade no more than two (2) business days from clearance being received, otherwise the approval is no longer effective and fresh approval must be sought.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Collar execution must occur within 2 business days of clearance, and the approver may revoke clearance at any time beforehand without giving reasons, so timing needs to be tightly coordinated with the bank counterparty.

ILU.summary: For Key Management Personnel, a funded collar is not possible: section 3.2(b) permanently and unconditionally bans using Company securities as collateral in any financial transaction (including margin lending), with no vesting distinction, no clearance route and no exclusion, so the secured loan leg cannot be implemented even though the derivative legs would become clearance-gated once the shares vest and any holding lock lifts. For Directors and Restricted Employees who are not KMP, the position is more favourable: the section 3.2(a) ban on risk-limiting transactions applies only while the shares are unvested or holding-locked, and once vested and unrestricted, both a put and a call are simply 'securities' (the definition expressly includes derivatives and contracts for difference) requiring ordinary prior written clearance, to be executed within 2 business days and outside Closed Periods. Secured financing is not expressly regulated for non-KMP personnel at all, and a lender's enforcement sale on default is expressly excluded from the Closed Period, clearance and short-term trading rules, which supports the bank's ability to rely on its security. Ordinary employees who are neither Directors, Restricted Employees nor KMP face only the general insider-trading prohibition and the unvested/holding-locked derivatives ban, with no formal clearance system for other dealings. Overall, a funded collar over fully vested, unrestricted shares held by a non-KMP Director or employee appears structurally achievable subject to timely clearance and window management, but is squarely blocked for any KMP.

SUL.summary: A funded collar over vested, unrestricted shares appears workable for Designated Persons (directors, ELT, the Company Secretary and other notified persons) subject to prior written approval from the applicable Approval Officer, confined to an open Trading Window, and executed within 5 business days of approval. Hedging is only expressly banned while shares are unvested or subject to a plan holding lock; once vested and unrestricted, entering into the put/call is an ordinary dealing requiring clearance rather than being prohibited outright. The Policy's only financing restriction bans 'margin lending arrangements' and transfers into an 'existing margin loan account', which is narrower than a full secured-financing ban, so a bespoke pledge-secured loan not structured as a margin loan is not expressly caught, though this should be confirmed given the Policy's substance-over-form approach. Usefully, a disposal resulting from a secured lender exercising its rights is an Excluded Dealing, exempt from both the short-term dealing ban and the Trading Window restriction, so the bank's enforcement sale is not blocked by a closed window. Residual risks are the ban on 'other short term dealings (for example, forward contracts)', which could catch a short-tenor collar, and the Approval Officer's unfettered, confidential discretion to refuse or revoke clearance under the Front Page Test.

The Company will determine whether the arrangement requires disclosure to the market.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike many peer policies, MND does not prohibit margin lending or other secured financing over its securities; a bank loan secured on the collared shares only triggers a notification duty, with the Company deciding whether market disclosure is needed.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a disposal of Securities of MND that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example (where permitted), under a margin lending arrangement
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An enforcement sale by the bank as secured lender falls outside the Policy entirely, so it is not blocked by a closed period or the need for Chairman approval.

bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: OTC put/call derivatives referencing MND shares are expressly 'Securities', so the collar legs are subject to the same trading-window and notification regime as ordinary share dealings, rather than falling outside the Policy altogether.

bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Within an open trading window there is no discretionary approval gate to negotiate -- only a pre-trade no-inside-information declaration -- so collar execution timing is largely within the executive's control once a window is open.

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedging ban limited to Corporations Act scope
bespoke_clauses.clause: Key Management Personnel and their closely related parties are prohibited from entering into hedging arrangements with respect of any part of their remuneration that has not vested, or that has vested but is subject to a holding lock.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Once incentive securities vest and any holding lock lifts, hedging is no longer expressly banned, opening the door to a funded collar over vested, unrestricted shares.

MND.summary: A funded collar over vested, unrestricted MND shares is workable for both Key Management Personnel and Other Employees. The Corporations Act-based hedging ban applies only to remuneration that is unvested or still subject to a holding lock; once vested and unrestricted, entering the put/call is treated as an ordinary Dealing (Securities expressly include third-party derivatives over MND shares) requiring only a pre-trade self-declaration to the Company Secretary of no inside information, executed within an open trading period (24 hours to 30 working days after results or the AGM, or as the Board otherwise permits). Critically, MND does not prohibit margin lending or other secured financing over its securities at all -- entering such an arrangement, including a pledge securing the funding leg of a collar, only triggers a notification to the Company Secretary, who decides whether market disclosure is required. A forced sale by the bank as secured lender exercising its rights is expressly excluded from the Policy altogether, so it is not blocked by a closed period. The main constraints are that collar entry, unwind or roll must fall within an open trading period or receive the Chairman's discretionary, confidential and revocable approval for exceptional circumstances, and post-trade details must be notified to the Company Secretary within 2 working days.

bespoke_clauses.topic: Associated Product ban scoped to unvested entitlement
bespoke_clauses.clause: Where Genesis Energy Persons are entitled to participate in any equity-based remuneration scheme, they must not enter into any transaction for any 'Associated Product'. An Associated Product is any product which has the effect of limiting the economic risk of participating in any entitlement a Genesis Energy Person is eligible for under the remuneration scheme.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This anti-hedging rule is framed around the unvested incentive entitlement, not shares already vested and held outright; on its literal wording a collar over vested, unrestricted shares is not caught, though this reading should be confirmed with the General Counsel and Company Secretary.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Policy contains no reference to margin lending, secured financing, encumbrance, charges, pledges or a secured lender's enforcement rights.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar is neither prohibited nor subject to any notification or disclosure duty under this Policy, unlike most ASX peer policies; that silence, and any separate NZ financial markets law overlay, should be checked before relying on it.

bespoke_clauses.topic: pre-approval required for every trade by Restricted Persons
bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons must seek pre-approval for any Trading in Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Every leg of a collar (entry, roll, unwind) by a director or senior manager needs prior written consent valid for only 10 trading days (2 trading days if granted during a Blackout Period), and lapses automatically if Material Information arises before execution.

bespoke_clauses.clause: You cannot avoid "Key Rule 1" by Trading in Securities through companies or trusts you control. If the companies or trusts that you control, Trade in Securities while you have Material Information, you will be deemed to have traded in the Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Routing the collar or a related hedge through a controlled trust or company does not avoid the insider trading prohibition or the Restricted Person pre-approval requirement.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Securities means Ordinary shares of Genesis Energy which are quoted on the NZX Main Board and Australian Stock Exchange, Genesis Energy capital bonds quoted on the NZDX market, and NZ electricity futures contracts that are traded on ASX.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Both NZX and ASX disclosure regimes (and the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013) can be triggered by a collar over Genesis Energy shares, in addition to this Policy's own approval and notification requirements.

GNE.summary: A funded collar over vested, unrestricted Genesis Energy shares appears achievable for Restricted Persons (directors, the Chief Executive and senior managers), subject to obtaining written pre-approval for the transaction -- from the Chief Executive, or the Chairman of the Board for Director/Chief Executive requests -- valid for 10 trading days (2 trading days if granted during a Blackout Period) and automatically withdrawn if Material Information comes to light. The Policy's only anti-hedging rule (the 'Associated Product' restriction) is framed around a person's unvested entitlement under an equity-based remuneration scheme, not securities already vested and held, so hedging of vested shares is not expressly banned on its wording, though this should be confirmed. Notably, the Policy contains no provision at all on margin lending, secured financing, encumbrance or a secured lender's enforcement rights, so the loan leg of the collar is neither prohibited nor subject to any notification duty under this document, though the silence and any NZ financial markets law overlay should be checked separately. Both the put/call derivatives and any monetisation fall within 'Securities'/'Trading' by definition (Securities expressly include options and derivatives), so they are subject to the same pre-approval and Blackout Period restrictions as an ordinary share trade, with post-trade details reported to the General Counsel and Company Secretary. The main residual constraints are the short-term trading discouragement (buying and selling within 3 months needs prior approval) and the Blackout Periods around each set of results and any prospectus, during which dealing needs exceptional-circumstances approval.

BWP.exemption_authority: The Authorising Officer (Managing Director and/or Chief Executive Officer, or the Chair/independent chair of the Audit and Risk Committee as applicable) may waive the Blackout Period restriction, but not any Prohibited Dealing under 7.2, in exceptional circumstances such as severe financial hardship or compulsion by court order; clearance can be given or refused without reasons, is final and binding, may be withdrawn on new information, and the Authorising Officer may refer the matter to the Board for approval.

bespoke_clauses.clause: (security or margin interests) creating a security interest or other financial interest, or entering into a margin loan, in respect of Securities ... Board approval cannot be granted for proposed Dealings that are prohibited Dealings.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar -- any security interest over the shares, not just a margin loan -- is an absolute, Board-unwaivable prohibition for Designated Persons (the Chair, all directors including the MD/CEO, and their direct reports), so the structure cannot be cleared under any circumstances for this tier.

bespoke_clauses.topic: remuneration hedging ban tied to disposal restriction, not vesting
bespoke_clauses.clause: entering into a hedging or similar arrangement (with anyone) if the arrangement would have the effect of limiting the exposure of a Designated Person to risk relating to an element of the Designated Person's remuneration that remains subject to restrictions on disposal.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This ban follows the disposal restriction rather than the vesting date -- shares that have vested but remain subject to a holding lock cannot be collared -- and it is also an unwaivable prohibited Dealing.

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedge and security interest expressly named as Dealings
bespoke_clauses.clause: creating a hedge, security interest, margin loan or other financial interest over or in relation to the Securities
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Both legs of a collar (the hedge/derivative and the secured loan) are expressly named as Dealings, removing any argument that a bespoke OTC structure falls outside the Policy.

bespoke_clauses.clause: [The excluded dealings in section 9 do not include a disposal resulting from a secured lender exercising its rights.]
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Because Designated Persons cannot create a security interest at all, the Policy provides no carve-out for a lender's enforcement sale; secured financing is simply unavailable for this tier rather than merely restricted.

bespoke_clauses.topic: off-market authorisation lapses in 5 business days
bespoke_clauses.clause: is taken to be withdrawn in respect of any off-market Dealing not completed within five business days, or in respect of any on-market Dealing where the relevant trade has not been entered into within ten business days.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An OTC collar is an off-market Dealing, so any authorisation to enter it (for the non-prohibited, vested-unrestricted hedge leg) lapses after 5 business days and must be re-sought if not executed in time.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Dealings that would not satisfy The Front Page Test should not occur, even where the Dealing may not strictly be prohibited under the Policy or otherwise at law.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even the permitted hedge-only leg for a Designated Person could be discouraged or refused on reputational grounds beyond the strict legal analysis.

BWP.summary: A funded collar is not available to Designated Persons (the Chair, all directors including the Managing Director/CEO, and the MD/CEO's direct reports) under this Policy: creating any security interest or other financial interest, or entering a margin loan, over BWP securities is an express, unwaivable 'Prohibited Dealing' for which 'Board approval cannot be granted', and hedging any element of remuneration still subject to disposal restrictions is separately and equally unwaivable. Once shares vest and any disposal restriction lifts, hedging is not itself banned and, together with an OTC put/call and any monetisation, is an ordinary Dealing (hedges and derivatives are expressly named) requiring prior written authorisation from the Managing Director/CEO (or the Chair for the MD/CEO's own dealing, or the independent chair of the Audit and Risk Committee for the Chair's own dealing), confined outside Blackout Periods and lapsing after 5 business days for an off-market transaction. For BWP Personnel who are not Designated Persons, none of the 7.2 prohibitions apply -- margin loans, security interests and hedges are all merely Dealings subject only to the insider trading rules and the Front Page Test, so a funded collar would in principle be workable for that group, though they are unlikely to be the bank's target clients. Because the security-interest ban is absolute for Designated Persons, the Policy provides no secured-lender enforcement carve-out and no financing disclosure regime for that tier. Overall, the funded collar as a whole is blocked for the directors and executives the bank is targeting, and only an unfunded, hedge-only structure could be contemplated for them, subject to authorisation.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Employees and Designated Officers are not permitted to enter into transactions (includes, but is not limited to, hedging arrangements, margin loans and / or share lending arrangements) in Company Securities (or any derivative thereof) which operate to limit the economic risk of holding any security in the Company or any vested or unvested entitlements to securities in the Company under any equity based remuneration schemes offered by the Company (or any member of the Group).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This single clause bans both legs of a funded collar outright -- the hedge (put and call) and any margin loan or other risk-limiting financing -- for all Employees and Designated Officers, across vested and unvested holdings, with no clearance or exemption route referenced anywhere in the Policy.

bespoke_clauses.clause: transactions (includes, but is not limited to, hedging arrangements, margin loans and / or share lending arrangements)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The 'not limited to' wording means a bespoke secured loan or novel collar structure cannot be argued to fall outside the ban merely because it is not called a margin loan or hedge by name.

bespoke_clauses.clause: which operate to limit the economic risk of holding any security in the Company or any vested or unvested entitlements to securities in the Company under any equity based remuneration schemes offered by the Company
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The prohibition is not confined to incentive-plan securities -- it extends to 'any security in the Company', so open-market purchased shares held by a director or executive are equally covered.

bespoke_clauses.clause: I acknowledge that this approval to trade is value for only fourteen (14) days from the date indicated below, unless otherwise revoked earlier by notice in writing.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even for the narrow set of dealings not caught by clause 14 (e.g. an outright sale of vested shares outside a window), a Designated Officer's clearance to trade lapses after 14 days.

bespoke_clauses.clause: [The Policy does not state that a refusal of clearance must be kept confidential, nor that the Approving Officer may impose conditions on a clearance.]
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike most peer policies, there is no express confidentiality protection around a refused clearance request and no explicit power to attach conditions; clearance here is effectively binary.

SRL.summary: A funded collar is not available under this Policy for any Employee or Designated Officer, at any vesting stage: clause 14 imposes a blanket, unconditional ban on entering into transactions -- expressly including hedging arrangements, margin loans and share lending arrangements, and by its 'includes, but is not limited to' wording likely any other risk-limiting or secured financing arrangement -- that operate to limit the economic risk of holding any Company security or any vested or unvested equity-remuneration entitlement. No clearance, exemption or exceptional-circumstances route in the Policy reaches this prohibition; the exceptional-circumstances discretion in clause 10 only relieves the Blackout Period and Executive Trading Window timing restrictions on ordinary dealing, not the clause 14 ban. Outside of a collar structure, an outright sale or purchase of vested shares by a Designated Officer requires prior written clearance from the Approving Officer (the Managing Director/CEO, or the chairperson of the Audit Committee for other directors), valid for only 14 days, and is barred altogether during quarterly Blackout Periods and while in possession of inside information; ordinary Employees face no clearance requirement but the same Blackout Period and insider trading restrictions apply. Because margin loans and share lending are outright prohibitions rather than merely regulated activities, the Policy contains no secured-lender enforcement carve-out and no financing disclosure regime. In short, the bank's funded collar cannot be offered to directors or executives of this company under the current Policy.

exceptions.approver: Authorising Officer, within the Board's absolute discretion
exceptions.evidence: the Authorising Officer has discretion to approve dealings in GYG securities during a Blackout Period, or other dealings that would otherwise be prohibited by this policy ... may include, without limitation, severe financial hardship

GYG.exemption_authority: The Board has absolute discretion to decide what counts as 'exceptional circumstances' (e.g. severe financial hardship or a court order/enforceable undertaking); the Authorising Officer may then approve, by email, dealings otherwise prohibited (including in a Blackout Period), on confirmation the person holds no Inside Information.

bespoke_clauses.clause: GYG Persons and other GYG employees may at any time: ... a disposal of GYG securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights under a loan or security agreement
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike policies that treat a lender's enforcement sale as a breach, GYG expressly permits it 'at any time', including in a Blackout Period, so the bank could enforce against the collared shares on default without putting the executive in breach (subject to post-event notification to the Authorising Officer).

bespoke_clauses.clause: Section 6 states it 'applies to Directors and Senior Management only', yet its Authorising Officer table (6.1(c)) includes a row for 'Any other GYG Person or other GYG employee', and sections 9.2(b)/9.3(b) (which apply to all GYG Persons and employees) cross-refer to 'consent under paragraph 6.1'.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: For a non-Director/Senior-Management participant the availability of a clearance route for the collar's derivative and security legs is not free of doubt; the conservative reading (and the one supported by the 6.1(c) table) is that Company Secretary/General Counsel consent is still required.

bespoke_clauses.clause: entering into protection arrangements includes entering into transactions which ... operate to limit the economic risk of any GYG Person's security holding ... or otherwise enable a GYG Person to profit from a decrease in the market price of securities
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The definition is not limited by venue or instrument type, so an OTC put and written call over vested shares squarely falls within 'protection arrangements' and needs consent even though derivatives, hedging and monetisation are not separately named.

bespoke_clauses.clause: not addressed
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no floor on retained holdings, so a collar sized against the full vested position would not itself breach a shareholding guideline.

GYG.summary: A funded OTC collar is workable once the GYG shares have vested and are free of any holding lock: both the put/call structure (a 'protection arrangement' under 9.2, since it limits economic risk and could profit from a price fall) and the loan secured on the shares (9.3) are permitted with prior consent from the Authorising Officer, taken outside Blackout Periods and while not in possession of Inside Information. Both legs are prohibited outright, with no consent route, while the shares remain unvested or subject to a holding lock. Consent is granted by the Chair of the Board or Audit & Risk Committee chair for directors and senior KMP, and by the Company Secretary or General Counsel for other staff, though the policy's own section headings leave some doubt as to whether non-Director/Senior-Management participants can access this route. A useful feature for the bank is the express carve-out permitting a secured lender's enforcement sale 'at any time', including during a Blackout Period, so default enforcement against the collared shares would not itself breach the policy. There is no minimum shareholding requirement and no defined short-term holding period beyond a general, undated ban on short-term or speculative trading, and the only exemption authority is the Board's case-by-case discretion for hardship or court orders.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and senior executives must obtain approval in accordance with the procedure set out in paragraph 3.3 for any proposed dealing in the Company's securities in connection with a margin lending arrangement, irrespective of any trading window.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar always needs prior written approval for this tier, never just the lighter open-window notification, and the secured-lender forced-sale exclusion is itself expressed as 'subject to paragraph 3.4', so enforcement sales are not an automatic safe harbour from approval.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where a Relevant Person enters into a hedging arrangement in respect of Company securities, the Company may, where appropriate, disclose the fact and nature of the hedge (eg in its annual report or to ASX).

bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The Company can constrain the loan's margin-call/enforcement mechanics as a condition of approval, which the bank's standard facility terms would need to accommodate.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Connected Person means, in relation to an Employee ... a company or any other entity which the Employee has an ability to control.

LOV.summary: A funded OTC collar is achievable over vested, unrestricted Lovisa shares: hedging is banned outright before vesting and while subject to a holding lock, but hedging vested, unrestricted shares is expressly permitted once processed as an ordinary dealing under clause 3.3. For directors and senior executives that means 48-hour advance notice during the four-week trading windows or prior written approval from the Chair/CEO outside them, executed within 2 business days and confirmed to the Company Secretary; for other Relevant Persons it is simply notified to the Company Secretary within 2 business days after dealing. The loan leg is only addressed as a 'margin lending arrangement', but directors and senior executives must obtain approval for it 'irrespective of any trading window', and the Company may condition that approval, including around margin-call sale triggers; a secured lender's enforcement sale is excluded from the ordinary dealing rules only 'subject to' that approval requirement. Entry, renewal or close-out cannot occur while the executive holds inside information, must avoid a 3-month short-term dealing pattern, and the Company may publicly disclose the fact and nature of the hedge. Overall the collar and its financing are workable, subject to vesting, tier-appropriate prior clearance, timing outside blackout periods, and the Company's discretion to condition or disclose the arrangement.

bespoke_clauses.topic: margin lending approval scope and recent amendment
bespoke_clauses.clause: This update introduces a formal approval process for any margin lending arrangements involving Company Securities by Key Management Personnel (KMP) ... These changes provide flexibility that will enable the Founders to hold their Tasmea shares given their confidence in the unique business model ... and potentially deal with the consequences of the proposed taxation changes to Superannuation Laws.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The August 2025 amendment was adopted specifically to let KMP/Founders borrow against their shares, evidencing Board willingness to approve secured financing (the loan leg of a funded collar) for KMP, subject to the tiered approval procedure.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where approval is given for entry into a margin lending arrangement, the Company may, where appropriate or required by law, disclose to the ASX the fact and nature of the margin lending arrangement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank and executive should expect the secured loan (and by extension a funded collar) to potentially be publicly disclosed.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Derivatives may, subject to the approval of the Chairperson ... be used in relation to vested positions which are not subject to disposal restrictions.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike sections 3-5, section 6.2 is not expressly limited to Designated Persons, while non-Designated employees/consultants/contractors are otherwise free to deal absent Inside Information (3.3); conservatively, Chairperson approval for the derivative leg should be sought regardless of tier.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Buy or sell orders for Company Securities which are placed but not completed outside of a Black-out Period are subject to the following restrictions once the Black-out Period commences: the order must be completed within five trading days otherwise it will lapse; and the order cannot be varied.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Relevant to timing the unwind, roll or physical settlement of a collar leg that straddles the start of a Black-out Period.

TEA.summary: A funded OTC collar is achievable under Tasmea's policy: its own definition of 'Derivatives' expressly includes 'collars', and while use of Derivatives is banned outright over unvested equity and vested securities still subject to a Holding Lock, it is expressly permitted over vested, unrestricted holdings with the prior written approval of the Chairperson (or the Board, if the Chairperson is the trader). The loan leg is separately regulated as a 'margin lending arrangement' (a term defined broadly enough to cover any borrowing secured on existing shares) and, for Key Management Personnel, requires tiered written approval; the Board only introduced this KMP margin-lending approval regime in August 2025 specifically to give the Founders financing flexibility. Both approvals must be obtained outside Black-out Periods, require the person not to hold Inside Information, and the Company may disclose the arrangement to the ASX. It is unclear whether the section 6.2 derivatives-approval requirement extends to employees, consultants or contractors who are not Designated Persons, since that section (unlike the surrounding ones) is not expressly limited to Designated Persons; the conservative reading is that Chairperson approval should be sought regardless of tier. There is no minimum shareholding requirement and no short-term dealing restriction, and a margin-call sale during a Black-out Period still requires the same prior written approval rather than being automatically excluded.

ALK.summary: A funded OTC collar is achievable for a Restricted Person once the relevant shares have vested: hedging that limits the economic risk of unvested equity-based remuneration is banned outright, but hedging of a vested holding, and the margin loan or other secured lending arrangement financing it, are each expressly permitted with prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer (Managing Director, Chair, or Chair of the Audit Committee, per the section 7 hierarchy), obtained while not in possession of Inside Information and, if within a Prohibited Period, only in exceptional circumstances such as severe financial hardship or a court order. Clearance is valid for 5 business days (or another period the Approving Officer sets), and any dealing under it must be notified to the Company Secretary within 2 business days, with all clearances reported to the Board. Company Securities are defined to expressly include over-the-counter options and other derivatives, so a bank collar falls squarely within scope, and while a secured lender's enforcement sale on default is excluded from the Blackout Period trading ban, the underlying loan itself must first be cleared under section 11. For ordinary (non-restricted) Employees, hedging and secured financing are not addressed by the policy and only need clearance if undertaken during a Prohibited Period or structured as short-term trading, which is separately banned (purchase and sale within 3 months) subject to Board exemption in exceptional circumstances.

SMR.summary: A funded OTC collar is achievable for a Restricted Person once the relevant shares have vested and are free of any restriction arrangement (including a holding lock): margin lending, hedging, derivative and secured financing arrangements are each expressly grouped as 'Funding Arrangements' requiring the Board's prior approval, with the Board to be given the lender's unilateral sale rights and any trigger events. Funding Arrangements that would limit risk exposure on remuneration that is unvested, or vested but still restricted, are banned outright, so the collar and its loan can only reference fully vested, unrestricted shares. Once approved, a lender's enforcement sale under the arrangement is an Excluded Dealing not subject to Blackout Period restrictions, but that protection depends on the Funding Arrangement having been properly Board-approved beforehand; the Restricted Person must also keep the Company Secretary informed of relevant changes in circumstances, and market disclosure of key terms is required if the arrangement covers 5% or more of the Company's securities. Short selling is banned outright for everyone, and any sale within 120 days of acquisition (relevant to an early unwind) needs prior Clearance to Deal under the ordinary section 2.5 process even outside a Blackout Period. Ordinary Dealing by Restricted Persons outside the Funding Arrangements regime still needs a separate Clearance to Deal from the applicable Clearance Officer, valid for 5 business days, with completion notified to the Company Secretary within 3 business days.

bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Because only 'margin lending arrangements' are banned, a bank loan secured on vested shares that does not itself compel a forced sale during a closed period appears permitted in principle, though it must be cleared with the Company Secretary as not being a margin loan in substance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Deal at any time in financial products associated with the Company’s securities, except for a type of dealing permitted by law or a permitted dealing under this policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is a standalone, unconditional prohibition, not a clearance gate, on entering OTC derivatives such as a purchased put or written call; none of the section 7 permitted-dealing carve-outs covers a bank collar, so the derivative legs cannot proceed under any clearance route.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a disposal of Company’s securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights. However, this does not extend to disposal under any margin lending agreements, where such agreements are prohibited by this policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If the loan leg were structured as a non-margin secured facility, the lender's enforcement sale on default would be a Permitted Dealing available at any time, including in a closed period, without prior notification or clearance, subject only to the general insider trading prohibition.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Financial products include derivatives, options, warrants, futures, forward contracts, swaps and contracts for difference issued or created over or associated with the Company’s securities by third parties.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The definition is venue-neutral and covers third-party-issued instruments, so an OTC put/call written by a bank falls squarely within the banned category regardless of being off-exchange.

DDR.summary: A funded collar is not possible under this policy for Designated Persons. Section 8.3(b) imposes a standalone, unconditional ban on dealing 'at any time' in financial products associated with the Company's securities (expressly including derivatives and CFDs), subject only to permitted dealings in section 7, none of which covers entering an OTC put and call with a bank; this is an outright prohibition rather than a clearance gate, and it applies regardless of vesting state. The loan leg is more favourable: only 'margin lending arrangements' are banned (8.1), and the policy expressly states this does not extend to other secured funding arrangements over the Company's securities, with a secured lender's enforcement sale carved out as a Permitted Dealing available at any time. However, because the derivative overlay is banned outright, the favourable treatment of the secured loan is moot, and a funded collar cannot be implemented while this policy stands.

RGN.summary: A funded collar is achievable for a Designated Person over fully vested, unrestricted REIT Units, subject to conditions. The put and call legs are a 'Derivative' (the Policy expressly names collars as an example) and are permitted for Designated Persons only with prior written notification to and approval from the Chairman, valid for five business days, outside the closed periods, and only while not in possession of Inside Information; derivatives over unvested or still-restricted (holding-locked) units are banned outright. The loan leg cannot be a 'margin lending arrangement' (banned for Designated Persons), but other secured loan arrangements over REIT Units are expressly permitted provided the Designated Person first notifies the Chairman of the intention and discloses the loan's terms. A secured (non-margin) lender's enforcement sale on default is excluded from the blackout-period restriction, supporting the bank's ability to enforce outside a trading window, but this carve-out does not extend to margin lending arrangements, so the facility should be documented and characterised as a non-margin secured loan. Overall, execution is possible but is gated by vesting state, trading-window timing, Chairman approval/notification, and careful avoidance of margin-lending characterisation.

bespoke_clauses.topic: blanket security/margin ban with no carve-out
bespoke_clauses.clause: must not grant security or enter into margin lending arrangements against Company securities held
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike many peer policies, there is no carve-out for non-margin secured financing; granting any security interest over the shares (the loan leg of a funded collar) is banned outright for Directors, staff and their associates, with no clearance or exceptional-circumstances route available for this restriction.

bespoke_clauses.topic: no general preclearance outside closed periods
bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors (other than the Chairman) and staff may seek prior written permission to deal in the Company’s securities during the Closed Periods from the Chairman, but only in exceptional circumstances
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Outside Closed Periods there is no general preclearance or notification-before-trading requirement (only the post-trade disclosure duty in section F), so dealing in the derivative legs of a collar outside a Closed Period, absent material non-public information, is not gated by a formal approval process under this policy.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and staff must not deal in the Company’s securities in the following circumstances: ... For short term trading or speculative purposes and must not grant security or enter into margin lending arrangements against Company securities held.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The policy never mentions derivatives, options, swaps, CFDs or hedging, so whether entering an OTC put/call is a 'dealing' subject to the Closed Period and inside-information prohibitions is untested; this should be confirmed with the Company Secretary before relying on the policy's silence.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If their trading activity materially conflicts with the Company’s trading activity.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: As a listed investment company, AUI's own trading book could create a distinct conflict-of-interest constraint if the collar counterparty bank trades the same securities AUI holds.

AUI.summary: The loan leg of a funded collar is fatal under this policy: section B.3 imposes a blanket, unconditional ban on granting security or entering margin lending arrangements against Company securities held, with no carve-out for non-margin secured financing and no exceptional-circumstances relief available for this restriction, so a bank loan secured on the collared shares cannot be implemented. The policy is silent on derivatives, options and hedging altogether, so the put and call legs alone are not expressly regulated beyond the general prohibitions on dealing while possessing material non-public information, dealing during the two annual Closed Periods (unless the Chairman, or the Lead Independent Director for the Chairman, grants exceptional-circumstances approval), and dealing for short-term or speculative purposes. Outside a Closed Period there is no general preclearance requirement, only a post-trade notification duty to the Company Secretary. Because the funded structure inherently requires pledging the shares as collateral, a funded collar with a bank is not possible under this policy regardless of vesting state or timing; an unfunded collar (derivatives only, no security granted) would face no express bar but its treatment as a 'dealing' is untested and should be confirmed with the Company Secretary.

bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If the collar's financing were treated as a margin loan, the executive would need to certify quarterly that a margin call during a blackout period would not force liquidation, effectively requiring a cash or collateral buffer beyond the collared shares.

bespoke_clauses.topic: MFG Board approval gates margin loans
bespoke_clauses.clause: Margin lending of MFG Securities by Access Persons or Directors is prohibited except in exceptional circumstances that are acceptable to and have been approved by the MFG Board.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar, if treated as margin lending, requires the MFG Board itself (not just the CCO) to approve it as an exceptional circumstance before the CCO can consent to the associated Trade.

MFG.summary: A funded collar faces two layered obstacles under this policy. Entering the put and call is expressly prohibited by section 3.3's ban on derivative transactions that limit the economic risk of an MFG Securities holding, and can only proceed with the CCO's written consent, which is generally reserved for financial hardship or a court order and is never given while the person may hold Inside Information. The loan leg, if treated as margin lending, is separately prohibited unless the MFG Board itself approves it as an exceptional circumstance, and even then the executive must certify quarterly that a margin call during a Blackout Period would not force a sale of the shares. Both legs, and any monetisation alternative structured as a Trade, are additionally subject to the standard pre-clearance regime, the Blackout Period (from the first trading day after a reporting period end until the day after results release), and the three-month short-term trading ban. A funded collar is therefore only achievable with dual CCO and MFG Board sign-off, executed outside blackout periods and while the executive holds no Inside Information, rather than as a matter of right.

DBI.exemption_authority: The Chair of the Board (for the CEO or other Directors), the Chair of the Finance and Audit Committee (for the Chair of the Board), or the CEO (for all other Employees) may grant approval to deal during a blackout period only in exceptional circumstances (severe financial hardship or compulsion by court order) accompanied by sufficient evidence that the dealing is the most reasonable course of action; the approver need not give reasons and may revoke approval at any time, and a refusal or revocation must be kept confidential.

bespoke_clauses.clause: DBI will take a substance over form approach and will have regard to the intent and spirit of this Policy when applying and enforcing it.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A funded collar structured to avoid the words 'hedging' or 'margin lending' will still be assessed on its economic substance, so documentation choices are unlikely to avoid the express restrictions.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The approver is not obliged to provide reasons for any aspect of their decision, and may revoke their approval at any time. If a request is not approved or an approval is revoked, that fact must be kept confidential.

bespoke_clauses.topic: margin lending ban with no carve-out
bespoke_clauses.clause: Employees are prohibited from entering into a margin lending arrangement in respect of DBI securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike some peer policies, there is no Board approval process or exceptional-circumstances carve-out for margin lending, and non-margin secured financing is not separately addressed, so the loan leg sits in an unaddressed grey zone that the Company Secretary should confirm is not caught by this ban before proceeding.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Hedging includes entering into any arrangements that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding DBI securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This definition is broad enough to catch a collar's combined put/call position regardless of how it is documented, so the vesting-state restrictions in 3.6 govern the derivative legs directly.

DBI.summary: Over fully vested, unrestricted DBI securities, the put and call legs of a collar are 'hedging' (broadly defined to include any arrangement limiting economic risk) and are not banned outright; they may proceed with prior written approval under the ordinary section 4 process (Chair of the Board, Chair of the Finance and Audit Committee, or the CEO depending on the Employee's role), outside blackout periods and without Inside Information. Hedging of unvested plan securities, or vested securities still subject to a holding lock, is banned absolutely with no exception. The loan leg is more difficult: margin lending arrangements in respect of DBI securities are prohibited outright with no Board or hardship exception anywhere in the policy, and the policy does not separately address non-margin secured financing, leaving a bank loan secured on the collared shares in an unaddressed grey area that would need confirmation from the Company Secretary. Approval to deal, once granted, must be exercised within 3 business days, can be revoked at any time without reasons, and any refusal or revocation must be kept confidential. Overall, the derivative legs look achievable case-by-case on vested, unrestricted shares, but the funded loan leg is either prohibited (if characterised as margin lending) or unaddressed, so bespoke sign-off from DBI would be needed before a funded collar could proceed.

NEU.exemption_authority: In exceptional circumstances, the Chairperson may permit a Designated Person to deal during a Prohibited Period; the nature of the exceptional circumstances and the justification must be evidenced in writing (3.4). No waiver mechanism is stated for the separate, absolute ban on trading in the Company's derivatives.

bespoke_clauses.topic: derivatives ban has no clearance route
bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons must not trade in the Company's derivatives.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike ordinary share dealing (which can be cleared by the Chairperson), this clause is a standalone, unqualified prohibition with no approval mechanism, so an OTC put and call collar cannot be cleared under this policy at all.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Before any Designated Person deals in securities of the Company (at any time), they must first obtain approval from the Chairperson. ... This obligation operates at all times.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even outside the annual closed period, any purchase, sale, unwind or physical settlement of a collar's share leg needs fresh Chairperson approval and a written no-inside-information statement each time.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The policy contains no reference to margin lending, secured financing, encumbrance or minimum shareholding requirements.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar is not expressly banned, but granting security over the shares to the bank is not addressed either, leaving real uncertainty over whether it would be treated as a 'dealing' requiring Chairperson approval and, if effected during the annual closed period, a breach.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If approval is given, the Designated Person may ordinarily trade within five business days after receiving the approval. ... A further application will need to be made if no dealing takes place within the five business days.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any cleared step of a collar (e.g. entry or unwind, to the extent not itself blocked by the derivatives ban) must be executed within a short window or re-cleared, complicating multi-leg execution with a bank counterparty.

NEU.summary: A funded collar with a bank is not achievable under this policy. Section 3.3 imposes an absolute, unqualified ban on Designated Persons trading in 'the Company's derivatives' - broad enough to catch an OTC purchased put and written call over vested Neuren shares - and, unlike ordinary share dealing, no Chairperson clearance or exceptional-circumstances waiver is provided for that specific rule. Even setting aside the derivatives ban, any change in beneficial interest in the shares (including any sale to unwind or settle a collar) requires prior written Chairperson approval at all times, not only during the annual closed period running from 1 January until release of the Appendix 4E preliminary final report, and must occur within five business days of approval (two-day notification for directors). The policy is silent on margin lending, secured financing and encumbrance, so the loan and share-charge leg has no express prohibition but also no defined clearance pathway, leaving its treatment as a 'dealing' uncertain. Overall, the standalone derivatives ban is the binding obstacle to a funded collar structure.
