bespoke_clauses.clause: This procedure applies even if the request for consent is made during a trading window.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar, if it looks like a margin loan capable of triggering a forced sale, cannot simply be timed into an open trading window; it needs the separate exceptional-circumstances consent that is rarely granted.

bespoke_clauses.topic: risk limiting products sweep unvested and locked shares
bespoke_clauses.clause: designated personnel must not engage in transactions or arrangements in risk limiting products which operate to limit the economic risk of unvested entitlements to EVENT securities ... or vested EVENT securities that are subject to a holding lock or other disposal restriction.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar can only be considered over vested, unrestricted EVT shares; performance rights, unvested options and plan shares still subject to a holding lock cannot be collared at all, with no consent override.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated personnel must not conduct any dealings or enter into transactions during a trading window until acknowledgement has been received for the notification.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even within an open window, the derivative legs of a collar cannot be executed until written acknowledgement of the notification is received, adding a timing dependency to any bank execution schedule.

bespoke_clauses.topic: no defined secured financing concept beyond margin loans
bespoke_clauses.clause: The policy prohibits margin loan arrangements which could result in a forced sale of EVENT securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Because only margin lending (not secured financing generally) is named, a loan structured to avoid the specific features of a 'margin loan' resulting in forced sale may arguably sit outside this restriction, though it would likely still be treated as such in substance by the Company Secretary.

EVT.summary: A funded collar is not clearly available, and turns heavily on vesting status and how the loan is characterised. The put and call themselves are 'risk limiting products'/financial products caught by the securities definition: if written over vested, unrestricted EVT shares they can be dealt within a trading window (or, outside one, only with rarely-granted exceptional-circumstances consent) subject to prior written notification and acknowledgement from the Chairman, Lead Independent Director, CEO or Company Secretary depending on tier; hedging of unvested entitlements or vested but holding-locked shares is absolutely prohibited with no consent route at all. The loan, if it functions as a margin lending arrangement capable of producing a forced sale, needs prior written consent that 'will not usually be given' and is considered only in exceptional circumstances, even if sought inside a trading window - this is the most likely blocking point for a bank-secured funded collar. Refusal of any consent is final, confidential, and cannot be challenged, and there is no minimum shareholding carve-out or disclosure regime for secured financing. Overall, the derivative legs could plausibly clear on vested, unrestricted shares within a window, but the secured loan leg faces a strong practical veto.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Margin Loan means any lending or similar arrangement allowing a person to borrow money to invest in securities using existing investments as security.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Combined with the outright ban on using Company Securities as security for 'a Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement' (6.3(b)), this generic definition extends beyond broker margin loans to catch any bank loan secured against the collared shares, so the funded leg of a collar is banned outright with no clearance path.

bespoke_clauses.clause: derivatives within the meaning given in section 761D of the Corporations Act (such as options, forward contracts, swaps, futures, warrants, caps and collars)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The policy expressly contemplates 'collars' as a derivative instrument, confirming a purchased put/written call structure is squarely within scope of the derivatives/hedging restrictions rather than an interpretive stretch.

bespoke_clauses.clause: an Employee may seek written approval from the Chair (Approval Officer) to dispose of or transfer (but not acquire or otherwise Deal with) Company Securities during a Black-out Period (Disposal Consent).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even the hardship/court-order exception route only ever permits a sale or transfer during a Black-out Period, not entry into a new derivative or financing arrangement, so a collar cannot be established, and its loan cannot be secured, under this exception.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A consultant or contractor (who is not an Employee) may, at any time, Deal in Company Securities if he or she does not have information that he or she knows, or ought reasonably to know, is Inside Information.

BGL.summary: A funded collar is not achievable under this policy. The derivative legs (a purchased put and written call are expressly contemplated as 'collars' within the Derivatives definition) are banned outright over unvested equity instruments and vested shares subject to a Holding Lock or other disposal restriction, with no consent route; once shares are vested and unrestricted, derivatives may be used only with prior written approval (Executive Director/CEO, or the Chair for Directors), outside the 15-trading-day pre-results/24-hour post-results Black-out Periods and any ad hoc black-out, and absent Inside Information. The loan leg is fatal regardless of vesting state: section 6.3 bans both borrowing to acquire Company Securities and using Company Securities as security for 'a Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement', a term broadly defined to cover any lending arrangement secured by existing investments, with no clearance or hardship exception available - the only hardship/court-order exception permits disposal or transfer, not encumbrance or new financing. Consultants and contractors who are not 'Employees' escape the Black-out Period, approval and margin loan restrictions, but this narrow population is unlikely to include a director or senior executive holding vested equity for a collar. Overall, the derivative legs might clear on vested, unrestricted shares with prior approval, but the secured loan is expressly and absolutely prohibited, so a bank-funded collar cannot be implemented.

FLT.summary: A funded collar is achievable once the underlying Flight Centre shares are vested and no longer subject to a holding lock, but is completely blocked before then for Directors, Senior Executives and their Closely Connected Persons. On unvested or vested-but-locked remuneration, margin loans, hedging and any other risk-limiting arrangement are absolutely prohibited with no consent route. Once vested and unrestricted, both the derivative legs and the secured loan (captured under margin lending / encumbrance) can be entered within an open 30-day Trading Window (following half-year results, full-year results, AGM results or profit guidance) without needing prior approval, provided the person holds no inside information; the only additional requirement is immediate notification to the Company Secretary, who informs the Board, once the shares involved reach 5% of Flight Centre's issued capital. Dealing outside a Trading Window is otherwise barred unless the Company Secretary grants a 7-day exceptional-circumstances approval. Overall, both legs of a funded collar can proceed on vested, unrestricted shares timed to an open window, subject only to a disclosure trigger at the 5% threshold, with no veto right reserved to the Company in the policy itself.

bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bank's enforcement sale under a properly consented loan is excused from the Blackout Period ban; but if the loan itself was never cleared under section 8.1, the forced-sale exception is unavailable and the enforcement sale would breach the policy - so obtaining upfront consent for the loan is essential to preserve the bank's enforcement rights.

bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement mechanics for a funded collar could be pre-negotiated and built into the consent itself, giving more structuring flexibility than a blanket-ban policy would allow.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any Employee who holds HMC Capital Group Securities subject to binding restrictions on transfer (either as ASX restricted securities or through voluntary escrow arrangements) must comply with the terms of any applicable escrow arrangements and will be unable to Trade in the relevant HMC Capital Group Securities during that time.

bespoke_clauses.topic: pre-approval required at all times, not just in closed periods
bespoke_clauses.clause: When permitted to Trade in accordance with this Policy, or where Trading is proposed during a Blackout Period, all Directors and Employees must give a prior written request for pre-approval to the Group Chief Executive Officer and the Group Company Secretary of any proposed Trading
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike open-window-only policies, every leg of a collar (entry, unwind, or roll) needs individual case-by-case pre-approval regardless of the Blackout Period calendar, adding execution friction and a 5-trading-day validity window to each step.

HDN.summary: A funded collar is achievable for Directors and Senior Executives under this policy, but only once the HDN units are vested and free of any holding lock, dealing restriction or ASX/voluntary escrow, and only with layered consent. The put and call legs, expressly caught as 'Financial Products' operating to limit economic risk, are absolutely prohibited over unvested units or units still subject to a holding lock, with no waiver; once vested and unrestricted they require prior written pre-approval from the Group CEO and Group Company Secretary (Chair and Company Secretary for a Director), certifying no inside information, executed within 5 trading days of approval and generally outside the Blackout Periods (1 January to 1 business day after half-year results; 1 July to 1 business day after annual results). The loan leg is directly addressed: including the units in a margin loan portfolio, transferring them into a margin loan account, or otherwise trading under a margin lending arrangement all require the same CEO/Company Secretary (or Chair) consent, which may be made conditional on the circumstances in which units can be sold to satisfy a margin call, and a lender's forced sale during a Blackout Period is excused from breach only if that consent was obtained beforehand. Directors and Senior Executives must also notify the Company Secretary of every trade within 2 business days, and any dealing on behalf of an associate needs the same pre-approval. Overall, a funded collar can be implemented on vested, unrestricted, non-escrowed units once the requisite consents for both the derivatives and the secured financing are obtained in advance, with the bank's enforcement rights preserved only if the loan was cleared upfront.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and Employees are only permitted to buy a derivative position ... however not a contract to sell a put or a call option.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The written-call leg of any collar cannot be granted by the executive under this Policy, which permits only long derivative positions; only the purchased-put leg is capable of being structured.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The intention of this Policy is that it only permits hedging arrangements which are within the control of the Director or Employee rather than conferring control of any purchase or sale decision to a third party.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even a compliant long put must leave exercise/pricing decisions with the executive, not the bank counterparty, which may constrain how the bank structures settlement mechanics.

bespoke_clauses.topic: no equity plan or vesting provisions
bespoke_clauses.clause: The Policy contains no reference to unvested securities, performance hurdles, employee equity incentive schemes or a minimum shareholding requirement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no vesting-based restriction on the shares to be collared, so the analysis turns entirely on the general dealing, hedging and short-term trading rules rather than any plan-specific lock-up.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Board of Directors will decide whether disclosure is required in relation to margin loans taken by Director/s. ... in certain circumstances the existence of 'margin loans' or similar arrangements financing securities holdings may constitute material price sensitive information.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A Director-level loan secured on the collared shares may trigger a Board assessment of whether the financing itself must be announced to the ASX.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If such a sale occurs during a Trading Blackout period, the Chairman will consider whether a breach of this policy has been made after considering all circumstances.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Enforcement of the bank's security over the collared shares during a blackout is not automatically excused; it is reviewed case by case for breach, creating execution uncertainty for the lender.

CQR.summary: A funded collar is only partially possible: Directors and Employees may buy (go long) a derivative position such as a put option under section 3.4, but the Policy expressly permits buying and not selling a put or call option, so the executive cannot write the call leg that funds the structure. Margin loans and 'similar arrangements' secured over Securities are not prohibited for Directors, who need only inform the Chairman and/or Company Secretary after the fact, with the Board deciding whether the financing itself must be disclosed to the ASX; the Policy is silent on secured financing by other Employees. Any dealing, including entering the put (and, if structured, the loan), must occur outside the four designated Trading Blackouts and any ad hoc blackout, with prior notification and consent from the Chairman/executive director/Company Secretary and no possession of Inside Information, and must not be short-term (held under four weeks) absent hardship or entitlement-offer circumstances. Enforcement of the bank's security through a forced sale during a blackout is not automatically permitted and is reviewed by the Chairman for breach. Overall, the loan and put-purchase legs are workable with notification, but the written-call leg as conventionally structured is not permitted under the express hedging clause.

bespoke_clauses.clause: dispose of securities of the Company resulting from a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement ... a sale that occurs under that mortgage or charge as a consequence of default would not breach insider trading laws.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement sale of the collared shares on default is an express, automatic exception, available at any time including in a Closed Period, without needing separate clearance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Key Management Personnel are prohibited from entering into Margin Lending arrangements whereby lenders are provided with rights over their interests in the company's securities unless Board approval is obtained, such approval not to be withheld unreasonably.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of the collar, secured over the collared shares, needs upfront Board approval, but the Board cannot unreasonably refuse it, giving a workable (if not guaranteed) path.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the management of the sale of any significant volume of Company securities (ie a volume that would represent a volume in excess of 10% of the total securities held by the seller prior to the sale, or a volume to be sold that would be in excess of 10% of the average daily traded volume ... for the preceding 20 trading days) ... needs to be discussed with the Board and the Company's legal advisers prior to the execution of any sale.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If the collared shares (or the call exercise/put exercise settlement) exceed these thresholds, the unwind must be pre-discussed with the Board and legal advisers and documented before execution, adding a process step beyond ordinary approval.

bespoke_clauses.clause: it is not permissible to provide the exercise price of options by selling the shares acquired on the exercise of these options unless the sale of those shares occurs outside the periods specified in paragraph 4.1.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If the shares to be collared are being funded via a cashless option exercise, that funding sale must occur outside Closed Periods, which can constrain timing of when the collared parcel becomes available.

PYC.summary: A funded collar is achievable in substance but requires two layers of Board-level consent. The put and call legs are 'financial products issued or created over or in respect of the Company's securities' under section 4.3, so they may only be traded within an open Trading Window and require the prior written approval of the Chairman (or the Board, for the Chairman) under section 5.1, with post-trade notification to the Company Secretary within five business days. The loan secured on the collared shares falls within the section 4.3 restriction on arrangements giving a lender rights over the KMP's interest in Company securities, so it needs prior Board approval, though that approval must not be withheld unreasonably. Critically, a subsequent forced sale by the secured lender on default, including during a Closed Period, is expressly carved out as a permitted exception and confirmed not to breach the insider trading rules, giving the bank comfort on enforcement. Unwind or settlement volumes above 10% of the executive's holding or 10% of 20-day average traded volume must additionally be discussed with the Board and legal advisers before execution.

PPT.summary: A funded collar is not possible under this policy. Rule 1(c) bans any hedging arrangement aimed at limiting the economic risk of holding Perpetual Securities or at-risk remuneration, which squarely catches both the purchased put and written call, and Rule 2 separately and absolutely bans entering into or facilitating margin loans over Perpetual Securities, catching the secured loan leg. Neither prohibition carries a Board-approval, clearance or hardship exemption; the Section 5 'Exceptional Circumstances' process only allows selling (not acquiring) securities during a Prohibited Period, and does not lift Rules 1 or 2. A structure engineered to achieve the same economic outcome by another label would still breach the Section 7 anti-circumvention clause, which prohibits structuring arrangements or using third parties to circumvent the policy. Combined with the outright short-selling ban and 12-month minimum holding period, there is no pathway under this policy for the bank to offer this executive a funded OTC equity collar.

It is a narrow internal conduct policy for RE Services staff administering schemes like MXT, requiring written same-day pre-approval of trading (from the Business Unit Head, or from the General Manager, Managed Fund Services for the Business Unit Head), a maintained personal trading register, avoidance of two calendar non-trading periods tied to financial statement releases, event-driven non-trading periods while a disclosing event or scheme amendment is unresolved, and a three-month minimum hold before redemption. bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is an internal tension: margin lending may be approved for Designated Persons, but granting security over the shares - which a margin loan or the bank's loan would typically require - is separately and absolutely banned with no stated exception, so it is unclear how any approved loan could actually be secured on the shares.

VGN.summary: A funded collar is not possible under this policy. Section 8.2 expressly and absolutely prohibits entering into transactions that limit the economic risk of a Company Securities holding or that enable a person to profit from a price decrease, and the Securities definition itself names 'caps and collars' as exactly this kind of derivative, so both the purchased put and the overall collar structure are banned outright with no clearance or hardship exception. Granting any form of security over the shares is separately and absolutely prohibited, which would block the bank's loan from being secured on the collared parcel, notwithstanding that margin lending itself carries a conditional prior-approval pathway for Designated Persons. Any dealing that were nonetheless attempted would still need to fall within a four-week Trading Window following half-year results, full-year results or the AGM (or be approved as a hardship/exceptional-circumstances sale only) and, for Designated Persons, would separately require prior written Authorising Officer approval at all times. Given the explicit bans on collar-type derivatives, profit-from-decrease arrangements and share encumbrances, this policy leaves no pathway for a director or executive to enter a funded OTC equity collar.

EOS.exemption_authority: The Chair (or CEO where the Chair is involved) may determine 'other exceptional circumstances' warranting a confirmation to deal during a Prohibited Period, in addition to severe financial hardship and court orders; the Notification Officer retains discretion to grant confirmation for other circumstances it considers warrant one, exercised with caution.

bespoke_clauses.topic: margin lending vs other secured funding

bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bank loan secured on the collared shares is not a 'margin lending arrangement' and is expressly carved out of the only financing prohibition in the policy, but the executive should have the Company Secretary confirm the classification before entering the facility.

bespoke_clauses.topic: financial products dealing restricted to permitted types
bespoke_clauses.clause: deal at any time in Financial Products associated with the Company’s Securities, except for the type of dealing permitted by law or under this policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The put and call legs of the collar are Financial Products, so they can only be entered as a dealing that fits the standard notification/confirmation process or a Part 5 exception, not as an unrestricted OTC trade even outside a Prohibited Period.

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedging ban extends to holding-locked vested shares
bespoke_clauses.clause: has vested but remains subject to a holding lock
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Shares that have technically vested but remain under a holding lock are treated the same as unvested shares for hedging purposes, narrowing the pool of shares eligible for the collar to fully unrestricted vested holdings.

bespoke_clauses.topic: lender enforcement carve-out excludes margin loans
bespoke_clauses.clause: a disposal of the Company’s Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, however, this does not extend to disposal under a margin lending agreement where such agreements are prohibited by this policy
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If the bank enforces its security and force-sells the collared shares, that disposal is an excluded dealing outside the confirmation process only because the facility is not classified as margin lending; correct structuring of the loan is therefore load-bearing for exit mechanics.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A confirmation ... expires five days from its date, unless it specifies a different expiry date.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Collar execution and documentation with the bank must be completed within the five business day clearance window (or a longer window if the Notification Officer specifies one), or fresh clearance must be sought.

EOS.summary: A funded collar is achievable in principle but only over vested Company Securities that are no longer subject to a holding lock, since 6.3(a) bans any arrangement limiting economic risk on unvested or holding-locked remuneration securities outright. Over eligible vested shares, the put and call legs are Financial Products dealings that require prior written notification to, and confirmation from, the applicable Notification Officer (the specific officer depending on whether the individual is the Chair, another Director, the CEO, or another Designated Person), executed within the confirmation's five-day validity, outside the periodic and ad hoc Prohibited Periods and without Inside Information. The loan leg secured on the collared shares is not a prohibited margin lending arrangement; 6.1 expressly permits other funding arrangements using the shares as security, though the Company Secretary should confirm this classification before the facility is entered. A lender's enforcement sale is an excluded dealing outside the confirmation process, but only because it is not a margin loan; short-term or speculative trading (under six months) and short selling are separately and absolutely prohibited, so collar tenor should be set with that floor in mind.

bespoke_clauses.topic: dealing definition sweeps in derivatives, hedging, security interests and lending
bespoke_clauses.clause: granting or receiving interests in securities may include but is not limited to directly or indirectly granting, allowing the grant of or becoming entitled to a security interest in or over securities. Lending securities is a form of dealing in securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Both the OTC put/call legs and the grant of security over the collared shares are 'dealing' requiring notice and Company Secretary confirmation like an ordinary share trade, but none of these instruments is separately banned outside the unvested-hedging rule.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons are not permitted to enter transactions with securities (or any derivative thereof) in associated products which limit the economic risk of any unvested entitlements under any equity-based remuneration schemes offered by the Company.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar over already-vested shares falls outside the express anti-hedging ban, so vested holdings are eligible subject only to the general clearance and Trading Window regime.

bespoke_clauses.topic: forced sale carve-out names margin lending
bespoke_clauses.clause: a disposal of securities of the Company that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Enforcement of the bank's security by force-selling the collared shares is expressly excluded from the Trading Window and approval restrictions, giving the bank a clean enforcement path even during a Closed Period.

bespoke_clauses.clause: you are authorised to deal in Company Securities for the 5 business days following the approval date of the Managing Director and/or CEO
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Collar documentation and execution with the bank must be completed within the 5-business-day clearance window unless a longer period is specified.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons should ensure that any securities trading which is prohibited by this Policy is not undertaken by their ... a company or trust over which the Restricted Person has influence or control (regardless of who is the beneficiary)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a family trust or controlled company does not escape the clearance obligation or the anti-hedging ban on unvested entitlements.

EQR.summary: A funded collar appears achievable under this policy. The anti-hedging ban in clause 14.1 applies only to unvested equity-based remuneration entitlements, so a collar written over vested, unrestricted Company Securities is not itself an express breach. Because 'trading' is defined broadly to include derivatives, hedging transactions and the grant of a security interest over securities, both the put/call legs and the bank's security over the collared shares are Dealings requiring prior notice to, and confirmation from, the Chair (generally via the Company Secretary) or the Board (for the Chair), to be executed within the 5-business-day clearance window and only inside an open Trading Window or under an exceptional-circumstances approval. A lender's forced sale on enforcement, including under a margin lending arrangement, is expressly excluded from the trading restrictions, so the bank's enforcement rights are not blocked by a Closed Period. The executive must notify the Company Secretary of the completed trade within two business days; no minimum shareholding requirement or specific secured-financing disclosure obligation is addressed.

PRN.exemption_authority: The relevant Approving Officer (Perenti Chair, Audit & Risk Committee Chair, or Chief Corporate Services Officer/Board delegate, as applicable) may grant clearance to deal during a blackout period in exceptional circumstances such as severe financial hardship or compulsion by court order, only with sufficient evidence that the dealing is the most reasonable course of action, and after consulting management or the Board where appropriate; no person may approve their own request or one relating to their own Connected Persons.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where any approval is required for a dealing under this Policy, approval will not be granted where the dealing would not satisfy the Front Page Test.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even a collar structure that literally complies with every rule can still be refused clearance if the Approving Officer judges it would look bad publicly, adding a discretionary reputational filter on top of the mechanical requirements.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Perenti may, at its discretion, make any approval granted in accordance with Section 6.2(a) conditional upon such terms and conditions as Perenti sees fit (for example, with regard to the circumstances in which Perenti securities may be sold to satisfy a margin call).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Perenti can constrain when and how the bank may force-sell the collared shares on a margin call or collar trigger, so the loan facility's default/enforcement terms may need Perenti's sign-off, not just the initial financing approval.

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedging of vested unrestricted shares expressly permitted
bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons and their Connected Persons are permitted to hedge their vested and unrestricted Perenti securities provided that the hedge transaction is treated as a dealing in Perenti securities for the purposes of this Policy, and the relevant approvals and notifications required under Section 5 are made on that basis.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is an unusually explicit endorsement of hedging (including, by extension, a collar) once shares are vested and unrestricted, provided it goes through the ordinary approval and notification process like any other trade.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a disposal of Perenti securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement (where that arrangement has been entered into in accordance with this Policy)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: For the bank's enforcement sale to be excluded from blackout-period restrictions, the underlying loan facility must itself have been approved under Section 6.2/Section 5 when it was entered into; an unapproved financing arrangement would not benefit from this carve-out.

bespoke_clauses.clause: if clearance to deal is refused, the Restricted Persons seeking the clearance must keep that information confidential and not disclose it to anyone (other than its Connected Persons where relevant, and the Restricted Persons must ensure that the information is kept confidential).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If the collar clearance is refused, the executive cannot tell the bank or advisers why, which may complicate renegotiating deal timing or terms.

PRN.summary: A funded collar is achievable under this policy, but only over vested and unrestricted Perenti securities; hedging vested, unrestricted holdings is expressly permitted under Section 6.3(d), provided the hedge is treated as a dealing and cleared through the ordinary Section 5 process (Perenti Chair for directors and Group Executive Committee members, the Audit & Risk Committee Chair for the Perenti Chair, and the CCSO or a Board delegate for other Restricted Persons), each clearance valid for five clear trading days and unavailable while holding Inside Information. Hedging is banned outright over securities that have not yet vested or remain subject to a holding lock. The loan leg is a dealing via the 'security interest ... or other financial interest' limb of the dealing definition and specifically as a margin lending arrangement under Section 6.2, both requiring Section 5 approval to enter into, with Perenti able to impose conditions on how and when the collared shares may be sold to meet a call or on enforcement. A secured lender's enforcement sale on default is excluded from blackout-period restrictions provided the financing arrangement itself was approved when it was entered into, but approval for any leg can still be refused under the discretionary 'Front Page Test' even where the letter of the policy is satisfied.

LLC.summary: A funded collar faces material constraints under this dated (2010) policy. Hedging of vested entitlements is permitted for Directors, Designated Executives and Employees, but only with prior notification to the General Counsel or Company Secretary and only when entered into during the narrow prescribed trading windows (a 6-week window after results/AGM for Directors and Designated Executives, or the equivalent period for Employees); hedging of unvested entitlements is banned outright. The loan leg is problematic for Directors and Designated Executives because margin loan arrangements in respect of Lend Lease securities are prohibited outright with no exemption route, and it is unclear whether a bespoke bank loan secured on the collared shares would be treated as falling within that ban; the policy does not address non-margin-loan secured financing at all, and is silent on margin lending for other Employees. There is no exception permitting a secured lender to force-sell shares outside a trading window, which increases enforcement risk. Given the ambiguity around the margin loan ban's scope and the absence of a formal clearance/approval architecture for ordinary trades, structuring a funded collar for a Director or Designated Executive would require bespoke legal advice on characterisation of the financing, while the position for other Employees is comparatively more open but still governed by narrow timing windows.

TAH.summary: A funded collar is not achievable for Directors or Restricted Employees under this policy, even though the derivative legs alone would be approvable. The put and call are 'dealings' under the broad definition (creating a hedge or other financial interest) and so require prior written approval from the Chairman (Directors) or the Company Secretary/MD & CEO (Restricted Employees), execution within five business days of approval, and avoidance of the half-year, full-year, AGM and any ad hoc Blackout Periods and of inside information. The loan leg fails outright: the policy separately and unconditionally prohibits Directors and Restricted Employees (and their associates) from granting a lender any rights over their Tabcorp securities, a ban that is not limited to acquisition financing and has no exemption authority or clearance route. Only unvested performance rights/options and restricted plan shares are absolutely barred from any hedge or derivative; vested, unrestricted shares are otherwise only subject to the general dealing/approval regime. General 'team members' outside these two tiers face no approval regime and no secured-financing ban, but they also have no unvested equity incentives typically at stake and are an unlikely collar counterparty. Refusals of approval are confidential and approval can also be refused for non-compliance with the separate Minimum Shareholding Policies.

WLE.summary: A funded collar is not achievable for Restricted Persons (the Board, subsidiary directors/company secretary, equity-incentive participants, Executives and the Company Secretary) under this policy. Section 1.10 imposes an absolute, unconditional ban on 'hedging arrangements', defined to include any transaction in financial products that limits the economic risk of holding Company securities, which squarely captures a purchased put or a full collar, and unlike the margin loan provision there is no consent, clearance or exemption mechanism available for it. The loan leg is only conditionally restricted: a margin loan or other margin lending arrangement secured on Company shares requires the Company's prior consent, which may be granted subject to conditions such as forced-sale triggers, but that permission cannot cure the outright prohibition on the derivative legs. Outside prohibited periods (5 business days before a dividend or capital management announcement, or a Board-imposed embargo) and while not holding inside information, an ordinary sale otherwise requires prior written notification to the Company Secretary and the Chairperson, and only a sale (never a purchase) can be cleared in exceptional circumstances (hardship, court order, or other Chairperson-approved cause) during a prohibited period. Restricted Persons' associated parties (spouse, dependants, family trust or company) are bound by the same hedging ban and margin loan consent requirement, so the structure cannot be routed around the policy through them.

4DX.summary: A funded collar is effectively blocked for Restricted Persons (Directors, other KMP, and notified employees) of 4DMedical. Section 6.11 imposes an absolute ban on 'transactions designed to hedge their exposure to Company Securities', squarely covering a purchased put or a collar, and the exceptional-circumstances waiver in section 6.9 applies only to the blackout-period rule and the short-term dealing rule, not to the hedging ban, so no waiver mechanism is available for it at all. The loan leg is only conditionally restricted: a margin loan or other secured financing arrangement over Company Securities requires the Chairman's (or delegate's) prior approval, or the Board's if the Restricted Person is the Chairman, and once approved, a lender's subsequent enforcement sale is expressly excepted from the blackout-period restriction. Even setting the hedging ban aside, any derivative dealing (Securities is defined to include options and other derivatives) needs prior notification and Company Secretary/Chairman confirmation, cannot occur during the annual or half-year blackout periods, and is discouraged if the position is held six months or less. Closely Connected Persons (spouse, minor children, family trust or company) are bound by the same restrictions, so the structure cannot be routed around the hedging ban through them. Overall, the secured loan could in principle be approved but the put and call legs cannot, making a funded collar with a bank unavailable to Restricted Persons as drafted.

The exercise (but not the sale on exercise) of an option or a right under an equity based executive or employee incentive plan, or the conversion of a convertible security, where the final date for exercise or conversion of the security, falls during a prohibited period and Beach has been in an exceptionally long prohibited period and the person could not reasonably have been expected to exercise it at time when he or she is free to do so.

BPT.exemption_authority: The Chairman (for a director applicant) or the Company Secretary in consultation with the CEO (for any other Beach Person) may give prior written permission, with such conditions as are relevant, to deal during a Closed Period or other prohibited period, on evidence of severe financial hardship or other exceptional circumstances, provided the applicant does not possess inside information.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The policy contains no reference anywhere to margin lending, security interests, charges, liens or other secured financing arrangements.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar secured against Beach shares is not addressed at all by this Share Trading Policy, so it is neither prohibited nor conditioned by it, though general law and any separate corporate policy could still apply.

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedging ban covers holding-locked vested entitlements
bespoke_clauses.clause: Entering into transactions which limit the economic risk of participating in unvested entitlements, such as unvested options or vested entitlements that remain subject to a holding lock, under a Beach equity based executive or employee incentive plan.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The hedging ban extends beyond unvested awards to vested shares still subject to a holding lock, so a collar can only be written once shares are both vested and released from any holding lock.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where the dealing would be regarded as 'short term dealing';
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: No holding period or months threshold is defined, creating uncertainty over how soon after vesting a multi-month collar (or its unwind) could be entered without being characterised as short-term dealing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The prohibition may not be generally advised to Beach People to protect confidentiality so a Beach Person wanting to deal in Beach securities may not be told why or for how long the prohibition will last.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An undisclosed CEO-imposed blackout could block entry, unwind or settlement of a collar at any time without warning or explanation.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any dealing in Beach securities must occur within five business days after notification (or permission being granted for a Designated Person) and must be consistent with the notification.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Both collar legs must be priced and executed within five business days of notification or approval, a tight window for arranging bank documentation.

BPT.summary: A funded collar over vested, unrestricted Beach shares is structurally possible for Designated Persons (directors, the CEO, executives and their direct reports), because 'dealing' is expressly defined to include 'creating a derivative over securities' and the express hedging ban applies only to unvested entitlements or vested entitlements still subject to a holding lock. The derivative legs require prior written approval from the Chairman and Company Secretary (or the CEO and Company Secretary if the dealer is the Chairman), execution within five business days of approval, and must avoid the half-year, full-year and quarterly Closed Periods, any undisclosed CEO-imposed prohibition, short-term dealing (an undefined term), and inside information. Strikingly, the policy contains no provision at all on margin lending, security interests or secured financing, so the loan leg secured against the collared shares is not addressed, restricted or conditioned by this Share Trading Policy. Non-Designated Beach People face a lighter regime of manager notification rather than approval for the same dealings. Overall, the derivative legs are approvable once shares are vested and unlocked and the loan is simply outside this policy's scope, but the undefined short-term dealing prohibition and the confidential ad hoc blackout power both create execution-timing risk for the bank.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Reporting Insiders and Designated Insiders shall not in respect of Company Securities engage in transactions in derivatives in respect of Company Securities (such as put and call options), or any other hedging or equity monetization transaction in which the individual's economic interest and risk exposure in Company Securities is changed (such as collars or forward sales contracts).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is an outright, unconditional ban on the exact structure proposed — a collar is named verbatim — with no exceptional-circumstances or approval route available anywhere in the policy, unlike blackout-period trading, margin lending or short-term dealing, each of which can be approved.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Reporting Insiders and Designated Insiders must not engage in any margin lending or other secured financing arrangements in respect of Company Securities without prior approval of the General Counsel and Corporate Secretary and the Executive Chairman.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan secured on the collared shares could in principle be approved, but this approval cannot cure the absolute ban on the derivative legs, so the funded collar as a package cannot proceed even though its financing component is only conditionally restricted.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the General Counsel and Corporate Secretary and the Executive Chairman may provide written clearance to a Reporting Insider or Designated Insider to trade in Company Securities during a regular blackout period
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This waiver mechanism is expressly limited to trading during a blackout period; it has no application to the Anti-Hedging Restrictions, confirming there is no back door for a collar even in hardship or court-ordered circumstances.

bespoke_clauses.clause: any other instrument, agreement or understanding that affects, directly or indirectly, a person's economic interest in a security of the Company
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The definition is broad enough to capture almost any synthetic or economic-exposure structure, reinforcing that a funded collar cannot be engineered around the express derivatives/hedging ban by re-labelling it.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If the Executive Chairman wishes to engage in any margin lending or other secured financing arrangements in respect of Company Securities, he must first submit a pre-clearing request to the General Counsel and Corporate Secretary and the Lead Director.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If the collar's loan leg were sought by the Executive Chairman specifically, approval routes to the Lead Director instead of the Executive Chairman approving himself.

CIA.summary: A funded collar is not achievable for Reporting Insiders or Designated Insiders (directors, KMP, and other designated officers/employees, together with their designated family members and closely connected persons) under this policy. The Anti-Hedging Restrictions impose an absolute, unconditional ban on 'transactions in derivatives in respect of Company Securities (such as put and call options), or any other hedging or equity monetization transaction ... (such as collars or forward sales contracts)' — collars are named verbatim — and unlike every other restriction in the policy (blackout-period trading, margin lending, short-term dealing/short selling), there is no approval, pre-clearance or exceptional-circumstances route that can lift it. The loan leg is only conditionally restricted: a margin loan or other secured financing arrangement over Company Securities requires prior approval of the General Counsel and Corporate Secretary and the Executive Chairman (or, for the Executive Chairman himself, the Lead Director), but this approval cannot cure the absolute ban on the derivative legs. Reporting Insiders and Designated Insiders may otherwise trade only within the open window beginning the third business day after quarterly, half-yearly or annual results and ending at the close of the following financial quarter, subject to written pre-clearance valid for five trading days and any discretionary blackout period imposed by the General Counsel and Corporate Secretary. Directors, officers and employees outside these two tiers face only the general insider trading prohibition, but they are also the population unlikely to hold the vested incentive equity a collar would be written over.

TBN.exemption_authority: The Authorising Officer, in the Board's absolute discretion, may approve dealing during a Blackout Period or other otherwise-prohibited dealing in 'exceptional circumstances' such as severe financial hardship or a court order/enforceable undertaking; approval must be given by email and notification requirements still apply.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The entering into of all types of "protection arrangements" for any Tamboran securities (or Tamboran products in the derivatives markets) ... includes ... operate to limit the economic risk of any Tamboran Person's security holding (e.g. hedging arrangements) ... or otherwise enable a Tamboran Person to profit from a decrease in the market price of securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An OTC put and call over vested, unrestricted shares squarely falls within 'protection arrangements' and is permitted only with prior consent under 1.6; over unvested or holding-locked shares it is banned outright.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a disposal of Tamboran securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights under a loan or security agreement
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement sale of collared shares under the loan security is an exempted dealing that Tamboran Persons may make at any time, including during a Blackout Period, subject only to advising the Authorising Officer per 1.12(b) — a clean lender remedy.

bespoke_clauses.topic: granting security ban on unvested/locked shares
bespoke_clauses.clause: Tamboran Persons may not at any time, directly or indirectly, grant any form of security ... over any Tamboran securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock, to secure any obligation of that Tamboran Person or any third party or enter into any margin lending arrangement involving Tamboran securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank's loan cannot be secured on shares before vesting or while subject to a holding lock, so the funded collar can only be structured over vested, unrestricted shares.

bespoke_clauses.topic: consent for security/margin over vested shares
bespoke_clauses.clause: Unless paragraph (a) applies, Tamboran Persons may, directly or indirectly, grant any form of security ... or enter into any margin lending arrangement involving Tamboran securities, with consent under paragraph 1.6.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of the collar, secured on vested unrestricted shares, is permitted but needs prior written consent from the relevant Authorising Officer, the same as the derivative legs.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The policy uses 'buy or sell', 'trade' and 'deal in' without one omnibus defined term for 'Dealing' (contrast a typical Attachment-style definition).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Activities are expressly and separately named (protection arrangements at 1.10, security/margin lending at 1.11) rather than swept in by a broad dealing definition, which reduces ambiguity about whether a bespoke OTC collar or its financing leg is caught — both are caught expressly.

bespoke_clauses.clause: for the purposes of section (d) only, a spouse (including a de facto spouse), child ... a person financially dependent on or acting in concert with any of the persons referred to in sub-paragraph (i)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The associate extension is literally limited to 'section (d)' (the Directors and Senior Management definition); a bank should not rely on this apparent gap to route a collar or loan through an associate's account, as the Company would likely treat it as caught regardless.

bespoke_clauses.clause: In exceptional circumstances the Authorising Officer, has discretion to approve dealings in Tamboran securities during a Blackout Period, or other dealings that would otherwise be prohibited by this policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Entry into or unwind of a collar during a Blackout Period is not a right but could be approved case-by-case for hardship or court order, via email, at the Board's absolute discretion.

TBN.summary: A funded collar is not possible over unvested or holding-locked Tamboran shares: protection arrangements (which expressly include hedging and short-selling-type instruments) and any grant of security or margin lending over such shares are banned outright under 1.10(a) and 1.11(a). Over vested, unrestricted shares, both the derivative legs (as a 'protection arrangement') and the secured loan leg (as a grant of security or margin lending arrangement) are permitted, but each requires prior written-style consent from the applicable Authorising Officer (chair of the Audit and Risk Committee for the Board chair; the Board chair for other directors, Company Secretary and KMP; the Company Secretary or CEO for others), confirmation of no inside information, a post-trade transaction confirmation, and must sit outside Blackout Periods unless the Board exercises its narrow 'exceptional circumstances' discretion. The document usefully exempts a secured lender's forced sale on default from the Blackout/dealing restrictions, so the bank's enforcement remedy is not itself blocked, though the executive must still notify the Authorising Officer. Tenor and structuring should avoid characterisation as 'short-term or speculative trading', which is banned outright with no defined holding period. Overall: workable over vested unrestricted shares with prior consent at each stage, but entirely blocked while shares remain unvested or holding-locked.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Secured Lending Arrangement means any arrangement involving the use of Company Securities as collateral or security for any indebtedness or other obligation, including without limitation a margin lending or other secured arrangement.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Global Leadership Team and Finance Team members are expected to have sufficient resources to meet a margin call by any means other than the sale of Company Securities ... they must take immediate steps to rearrange their affairs to prevent this from occurring.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The Company expects the loan (and by extension the collar's financing leg) to be structured with enough headroom that a margin call never forces a sale of the collared shares, which should inform the LVR/put strike chosen.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Company may publicly disclose the terms and nature of any margin loan or Secured Lending Arrangement to which a Company director is a party, and the terms and circumstances of any call made or likely to be made under those arrangements.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A director's funded collar could be publicly disclosed by the Company at its own discretion, including its loan-to-value ratio and any margin call, independent of the director's own ASX notification obligations.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Persons to whom this policy applies must not sell more than 2% of the total issued share capital worth of securities in any 6 month period without obtaining approval from the Chairman ... as to the form and timing of the sale and the management of its public disclosure.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unwind or settlement of a large collar involving delivery/sale of more than 2% of issued capital in a 6-month window needs separate Chairman/Board sign-off on timing and disclosure, on top of ordinary Trading Window and Secured Lending clearance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any approval given may be revoked in writing, prior to the Dealing taking place, if ... new information comes to light in relation to the Secured Lending Arrangement ... or any other relevant event or circumstance, as determined by the Board.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If a person comes into possession of Inside Information after receiving an approval to Deal, they must not Deal despite having received the approval.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Execution of a cleared collar (or its unwind) must be re-checked against Inside Information at the moment of trade, not just at the time approval was granted.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Approval will only be given under exceptional circumstances where the Dealing would occur in the period between 30 June and the announcement to ASX of final results for the year and between 31 December and the announcement to ASX of the interim results for the half-year.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Collar entry, unwind or roll timed in the weeks immediately before annual or half-year results faces a materially harder approval bar than an ordinary Closed Period dealing.

DMP.summary: A funded collar over vested, unrestricted shares is workable but multi-gated: the derivative legs are a Dealing in Company Securities (which expressly include third-party-created derivatives) and, if within a Trading Window, need only no Inside Information and no short-term/speculative purpose (plus Designated Person pre-notification); outside a Trading Window they need Chairman or Company Secretary approval, harder to obtain in the weeks before results. The loan leg is a Secured Lending Arrangement, permitted with the Responsible Person's (Chairman/ARC Chairman) prior written approval at any time for Global Leadership Team and Finance Team members, or via the same clause 7 route for other covered persons dealing under one, and carries ongoing disclosure of loan size, LVR and trigger points; that approval is revocable before completion and any approved terms may be publicly disclosed by the Company. A lender's forced sale on a margin call is an exempt dealing not requiring fresh clearance, but the Company expects GLT/Finance Team members to avoid needing one at all. Hedging of unvested equity incentive holdings needs separate Chairman consent under clause 6.8, and unwinding a large enough position (over 2% of issued capital in six months) needs additional Chairman/Board approval on timing and disclosure. Overall, a funded collar is achievable over vested, unrestricted shares with layered board-level clearances at entry, and it must be re-cleared if the executive later holds Inside Information.

MI6.exemption_authority: The Chair (Approval Officer) may, acting with caution, grant a Disposal Consent to a Designated Person to dispose of or transfer (not acquire) Company Securities during a Black-out Period for severe financial hardship or a court order/legal requirement, subject to written application and supporting documentation, and only if the person has no Inside Information; the consent may carry conditions including its duration and the Board is notified of any consent granted.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Derivatives include: (a) derivatives within the meaning given in section 761D of the Corporations Act (such as options, forward contracts, swaps, futures, warrants, caps and collars); and (b) any other transaction in financial products which operate to limit (in any way) the economic risk associated with holding the relevant securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The policy's own definition of Derivatives expressly names 'collars', so a funded equity collar's put and call legs are squarely and expressly caught, not merely swept in by inference.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons may not: (a) enter into a Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement to acquire any Company Securities; or (b) use Company Securities as security for a Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no clearance route, vesting-state carve-out, or exemption for this ban - the loan leg of a bank-funded collar cannot be implemented for any Designated Person, regardless of whether the shares are vested and unrestricted.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Company prohibits the use of Derivatives in relation to unvested equity instruments ... Derivatives may be used in relation to vested positions which are not subject to disposal restrictions subject to compliance with the law and the other provisions of this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The put/call legs of a collar could in principle be executed over vested, unrestricted shares with standard clearance, even though the financing leg cannot be implemented at all - the two legs face fundamentally different treatment.

bespoke_clauses.clause: In exceptional circumstances a Designated Person may seek written approval from the Chair (Approval Officer) to dispose of or transfer (but not acquire or otherwise Deal with) Company Securities during a Black-out Period (Disposal Consent).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even the Black-out Period override is limited to disposals/transfers for hardship or court order, so it could permit unwinding an existing collar position during a black-out but not entering into new derivative legs or a financing arrangement.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Buy or sell orders for Company Securities which are placed but not completed outside of a Black-out Period ... the order must be completed within five trading days otherwise it will lapse; and the order cannot be varied.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Execution of a collar's derivative legs straddling the start of a Black-out Period is time-limited and cannot be adjusted once the black-out commences.

bespoke_clauses.clause: An employee, consultant or contractor (who is not a Designated Person) may, at any time, Deal in Company Securities if he or she does not have information that he or she knows, or ought reasonably to know, is Inside Information.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Black-out Periods, the clause 5 approval regime, and the clause 6.3 margin loan ban are all expressed to apply only to Designated Persons; the policy is silent on secured financing by a non-Designated employee, though this is an unlikely profile for a bank collar counterparty.

MI6.summary: A funded collar is not possible under this policy for any Designated Person: clause 6.3 imposes an absolute, unconditional ban on entering a Margin Loan or 'similar funding arrangement' or using Company Securities as security for one, with no vesting-state carve-out, approval route or exemption authority. The derivative legs fare better - the Derivatives definition expressly names 'collars' as a captured instrument, and their use is banned outright only over unvested or holding-locked shares (6.2(a)); over vested, unrestricted shares, derivatives are expressly permitted (6.2(b)) subject to the standard prior written approval of the relevant Approving Officer, a 5 business day clearance validity, avoidance of Black-out Periods, and post-trade notification to the Company Secretary within 5 business days. Because the financing leg is categorically prohibited with no clearance mechanism, a bank cannot lawfully take security over a Designated Person's Company Securities to fund the structure, even though the put and call could otherwise be cleared. The only partial relief is a narrow, Chair-approved Disposal Consent for disposals/transfers (not acquisitions or financing) during a Black-out Period in cases of genuine hardship or court order.

external_documents: Director's disclosure deed (Listing Rule 3.19B)
MGH.exemption_authority: The Chairman (or the Chosen Director/CEO for the Chairman's own Trades) may grant written approval for a Management Team member to Trade in exceptional circumstances - financial hardship (excluding tax liability), a court order/enforceable undertaking, or where delay would cause greater hardship, family detriment, or breach a court order - provided the Trade is lawful, not for short-term/speculative gain, does not exploit Inside Information, and would not appear unfair; the approval must state its period and lasts 7 days.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Securities include securities of any kind including ordinary shares, preference shares, debentures, convertible notes, options and hedging mechanisms or derivative instruments.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An OTC put and call sold by a bank are expressly 'Securities' under this definition, so the collar's derivative legs are directly and expressly regulated by the Policy, not merely inferred.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors must obtain the Board's approval before entering into a margin loan or similar arrangements concerning Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A director may enter the collar's loan leg (secured on the collared shares) with prior Board approval - there is no outright prohibition, unlike some peer policies, but the process is Board-level, not a single officer's sign-off.

bespoke_clauses.clause: for more than $50,000 worth of Securities to any party if written approval from the Chairman is not obtained, covering the form of and timing of the sale, and the management of its public disclosure, before entering into discussions for the potential sale of those Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any collar-sized position (almost certainly over $50,000) triggers a separate Chairman approval covering timing, form and public disclosure management, before even entering into sale discussions - relevant to structuring the written call and any unwind.

bespoke_clauses.topic: Management Team can never trade freely
bespoke_clauses.clause: A member of the Management Team may not Trade at any time, including during a Trading Window, unless they obtain prior written approval from ... the Chairman
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A likely collar counterparty (director, CEO or CFO) needs the Chairman's prior written approval for every trade, including inside a Trading Window, so entry, adjustment and unwind of both collar legs each require individual sign-off.

bespoke_clauses.topic: public disclosure of margin loan terms
bespoke_clauses.clause: Where a Director has entered into margin loan or similar funding arrangements for a material number of Securities, the Company may need to disclose the key terms of the arrangements, including the number of Securities involved, the trigger points, the right of the lender to sell unilaterally and any other material details.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If the collar's financing leg is material, the Company may be required to publicly disclose its size, trigger points and the bank's unilateral sale rights.

bespoke_clauses.clause: disposals by a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under an approved margin lending arrangement
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement sale on default is an Excluded Trade, so it is not blocked by a Prohibited Period and needs no fresh Chairman/Board approval - a clean lender remedy, provided the original margin loan was itself approved.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The policy makes no reference anywhere to 'unvested', 'vesting' or a 'holding lock'.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike several peer policies, MGH does not separately restrict hedging, derivatives or margin loans over unvested equity incentives; the general Trade/Trading Window/Management Team approval regime is the only gate, aside from the Excluded Trading carve-out (f) that blocks selling securities obtained on exercise until the relevant exercise date has passed.

MGH.summary: A funded collar is achievable for a Director under this policy, but with layered approvals. The derivative legs are expressly 'Securities' (hedging mechanisms or derivative instruments); a non-Management Restricted Person could trade them during a Trading Window with only post-trade notification, but a Management Team member (the likely counterparty) needs the Chairman's prior written approval for every trade, in or out of a Trading Window. The loan leg is a margin loan or similar funding arrangement concerning Securities, permitted for Directors with the Board's prior approval, and if material the Company may need to publicly disclose its size, trigger points and the bank's unilateral sale right. Any trade over $50,000 additionally needs Chairman approval covering timing, form and disclosure before discussions even begin, which will almost always apply to a collar-sized position. A lender's forced sale on default is an Excluded Trade requiring no fresh approval. Overall: workable with Board approval for the financing leg and Chairman approval for each derivative leg and any large unwind, and there is no vesting-state carve-out to navigate.

REG.title: Policy for dealing in securities

REG.ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may specify any other blackout period from time to time (clause 3.2(a)); the Policy does not state whether such additional periods are kept confidential.

rules.detail: Securities is defined to extend to financial products issued or created over or in respect of Company securities, whether created by the Company or third parties, with no venue limitation, so an OTC put/call is caught. Derivatives (exchange-traded options, CFDs, other derivatives) are expressly named as prohibited during blackout periods; outside blackout periods they are a 'dealing' requiring approval under 3.3.
rules.evidence: For the avoidance of doubt, during the above periods Relevant Persons must not deal in financial products issued or created over or in respect of the Company's securities (for example, exchange-traded options, contracts for differences and other derivatives).

rules.detail: Absolute ban on hedging unvested equity held under any employee, executive or director equity plan; no clearance route.
rules.evidence: Company securities must never be hedged prior to the vesting of those Company securities. In particular, Relevant Persons are prohibited from entering into any hedge transaction involving unvested equity held pursuant to any employee, executive or director equity plan operated by the Company.

rules.detail: Absolute ban on hedging vested Company securities that remain subject to a plan holding lock or dealing restriction; no clearance route.
rules.evidence: Company securities must never be hedged while they are subject to a holding lock or restriction on dealing under the terms of any employee, executive or director equity plan operated by the Company.

rules.detail: Monetisation structures (e.g. prepaid forward sale) are not named. 'Securities' extends to financial products created over Company securities and 'dealing' includes agreements to buy or sell, so a monetisation transaction is a dealing requiring approval under 3.3 and is barred in blackout periods and while holding inside information.
rules.evidence: the term 'securities' also extends to financial products issued or created over or in respect of securities issued by the Company (for example, warrants and other derivative products), whether or not the financial products are created by the Company or by third parties.

rules.detail: Short selling is not named anywhere in the Policy or Attachment 1, and is not listed as an example of prohibited or short-term dealing.
Securities lending is not mentioned anywhere in the Policy.

Contracts for differences are expressly named as an example of financial products caught by the blackout prohibition; outside blackout periods a CFD is a dealing requiring approval and would also be caught by the short-term/speculative dealing restriction if opened and closed within 3 months.
rules.evidence: during the above periods Relevant Persons must not deal in financial products issued or created over or in respect of the Company's securities (for example, exchange-traded options, contracts for differences and other derivatives).

rules.detail: Blanket ban on dealing in Company securities pursuant to a margin lending arrangement, with no security-state or approval carve-out.

rules.detail: Granting a charge, lien or pledge over Company securities is not named outside the specific margin lending prohibition in 3.4, and the dealing definition does not expressly mention encumbrance.

The Policy only names 'margin lending arrangements' as prohibited; it does not use a broader term such as 'secured financing arrangement'. bespoke_clauses.clause: Relevant Persons may not deal in the Company's securities pursuant to a margin lending arrangement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar is banned if characterised as a 'margin lending arrangement'; the term is undefined, so whether a bespoke bilateral loan secured on the collared shares escapes the ban is untested and should be cleared with the Chair/CEO before proceeding.

bespoke_clauses.clause: subject to paragraph 3.4, a disposal of securities of the Company that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This exclusion removes a lender's enforcement sale from the blackout and approval requirements in 3.2 and 3.3, but only 'subject to paragraph 3.4', so it does not rescue a financing arrangement that is itself a prohibited margin loan.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Hedging includes entering into transactions in financial products that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding Company securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A purchased put and written call collar squarely fits this definition; it is permitted with clearance only over vested and unrestricted shares, and never over unvested or holding-locked vested shares.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If a waiver is granted... the duration of the waiver to deal in securities will be 2 business days.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar entered under an exceptional-circumstances waiver during a blackout period must be fully executed within 2 business days, a tight window for documenting a bank collar and loan.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If the market was aware of all the current circumstances, could my proposed transaction be perceived by the market as me (or my Connected Persons) taking advantage of my position in an inappropriate way?
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even a formally compliant collar must be self-assessed for negative market perception, and any concerns must be flagged in the approval request, giving the approver discretion to refuse or condition clearance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where a Relevant Person enters into a hedging arrangement in respect of Company securities, the Company may, where appropriate, disclose the fact and nature of the hedge (eg in its annual report or to ASX).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank and executive should expect the collar's existence and terms could be publicly disclosed by the Company in its annual report or to ASX.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a company or any other entity which the Employee has an ability to control.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Routing the loan or collar through a controlled entity or trust does not avoid the Policy's approval requirements or the margin lending ban, since Connected Persons' dealings are treated as the Employee's own.

REG.summary: A funded collar is workable only over vested and unrestricted Regis shares: unvested shares and vested shares still under a plan holding lock can never be hedged, and even permitted hedges of vested unrestricted shares are treated as a 'dealing' requiring prior approval (Board/ARCC Chair for the Chair; Chair of the Board for other directors; CEO for senior executives and other employees), execution within 2 business days of approval, and avoidance of blackout periods (30 June and 31 December to results release) and any period the person holds inside information. The loan leg is the key obstacle: clause 3.4 bans 'margin lending arrangements' using Company securities as security, and while a bespoke bank loan secured on the collared shares may not be a literal margin loan, the Policy's forced-sale exclusion (available only 'subject to paragraph 3.4') suggests secured lending over Company securities generally is not intended to be permitted, so structuring and approval risk falls on the loan. No minimum shareholding requirement or standing financing-disclosure obligation is stated, but the Company may separately disclose the hedge's existence in its annual report or to ASX, and each dealing must be confirmed to the Company Secretary within 2 business days. Tenor should exceed three months given the short-term dealing prohibition. Overall verdict: the derivative legs are achievable with clearance on vested, unrestricted shares in an open window, but the secured-loan leg needs an explicit, favourable ruling from the Chair of the Board or CEO that it is not a prohibited 'margin lending arrangement'.

PMV.summary: A funded collar over Premier shares faces a comparatively light regime: this Policy has no hedging, margin lending or secured financing prohibition, and clause 4.1(f) expressly contemplates a secured lender exercising rights under a loan agreement, so the loan leg secured on vested shares is not itself restricted. The put/call derivative legs are 'securities'/'dealing' under the broad definitions (any derivatives, including options, and any agreement to acquire or dispose) and so require only a written pre-dealing notice to the Company Secretary (or, for the CEO, initial notice to the Chairman), completion within 14 days of the notice being received, and execution within a window period (six weeks after half-year or full-year results, or a rights trading period) or under a Designated Officer's exceptional-circumstances approval, never while holding inside information. A standard representation on the dealing forms states an intention not to sell newly purchased securities within 6 months, but this does not constrain hedging or encumbering already-held vested shares. If the bank needs to force a sale on default and that falls within a Closed Period, the Board must exercise its clause 4.1(f) discretion to permit it. Overall verdict: a funded collar is achievable with routine notice-based clearance in a window period, and the loan leg is not itself prohibited, making this one of the more collar-friendly policies, subject to checking the executive's own employee share plan or shareholder agreement for a stricter overriding term.
