where a Restricted Person is a trustee, trading in the Company's Securities by that trust provided the Restricted Person is not a beneficiary of the trust and any decision to trade during a Closed Period is taken by the other trustees or by the investment managers independently of the Restricted Person
undertakings to accept, or the acceptance of, a takeover offer for the Company

exceptions.approver: the Board
exceptions.evidence: accepting an offer or invitation made by the Company to all or most of its security holders, such as a rights issue, a security purchase plan, a dividend or distribution reinvestment plan and an equal access buy-back, where the plan that determines the timing and structure of the offer has been approved by the Board

a disposal of the Company's Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement (note the rules applicable to Restricted Persons entering into arrangements that provide lenders with rights over their interests in the Company's Securities in paragraph 9 of this policy)

the exercise (but not the sale of the Company's Securities following exercise) of an option or a right under an employee incentive scheme, or such similar scheme or plan, or the conversion of a convertible security, where the final date for the exercise of the option or right, or the conversion of the security, falls during a Closed Period

trading under a non-discretionary trading plan for which Prior Written Clearance has been provided in accordance with paragraph 5 and where: (i) the Restricted Person did not enter into the plan or amend the plan during a Closed Period; (ii) the trading plan does not permit the Restricted Person to exercise any influence or discretion over how, when, or whether to trade
a Dealing which results in no change in the beneficial interest in the Company's Securities.

financing_disclosure: Restricted Persons: trigger = inception (before entering into any Dealing or arrangement giving a lender rights over their interests in Company Securities); to whom = the Designated Officer; deadline = prior written consent must be obtained before entering into the arrangement (clause 9).

ASB.exemption_authority: The Designated Officer (the Chairman for all Restricted Persons other than the Chairman; the Company Secretary where the Chairman is the Applicant) may grant Prior Written Clearance to sell or otherwise dispose of Securities during a Closed Period for severe financial hardship or other exceptional circumstances (a court order, enforceable undertaking, other overriding legal or regulatory requirement, or any circumstance the Designated Officer is satisfied is the only reasonable course of action), responding within 14 days of a written Application lodged at least 21 days beforehand; approval may be conditioned in the Designated Officer's absolute discretion, and rejection (given without reasons) is final.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Without limiting any other provision of this policy, a Restricted Person must not enter into any Dealing or arrangement that provides lenders with rights over their interests in the Company's Securities without first obtaining the prior written consent of the Designated Officer.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is the operative gate for the funded collar's loan leg: granting the bank security over the collared shares is expressly permitted, but only with the Designated Officer's (the Chairman's, or the Company Secretary's if the executive is the Chairman) prior written consent -- there is no blanket ban on secured financing as seen in many peer policies.

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedging and scrip lending are express Dealings
bespoke_clauses.clause: Deal or Dealing means buying or selling a Security holding in the Company or entering into a margin loan, scrip lending or hedging arrangement which involves a Security holding in the Company.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar (a hedging arrangement) and a margin loan are both expressly named as Dealings, so the put/call legs and the loan leg both sit within the ordinary clearance and Closed Period framework rather than a separate prohibition.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a Restricted Person must not Deal in the Company's Securities: (a) where the Dealing is of a short-term nature
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike policies with a fixed 3- or 6-month rule, 'short-term nature' is undefined, leaving the Chairman/Designated Officer discretion to treat an early unwind or short-dated collar as prohibited; a longer-dated structure reduces this risk.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a disposal of the Company's Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement (note the rules applicable to Restricted Persons entering into arrangements that provide lenders with rights over their interests in the Company's Securities in paragraph 9 of this policy)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bank's enforcement sale on default can proceed during a Closed Period as an Excluded Dealing, but only after a 7-business-day Excluded Dealing Notice to the Designated Officer, who can block it without giving reasons.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons are: (a) All Directors and their spouses and any Related Party; (b) The Chief Executive Officer, the Chief Operating Officers, the Chief Financial Officers of Group Companies; and (c) All Key Management Personnel ... not otherwise mentioned.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The Policy has no unvested/vested-locked distinction and no equity-plan hedging carve-out, so the same clearance and Closed Period rules apply uniformly to any vested shareholding used to fund a collar.

ASB.summary: A funded collar over Austal shares is comparatively achievable: 'Dealing' is expressly defined to include entering into a margin loan, scrip lending or hedging arrangement, so the put/call legs and the loan leg are Dealings governed by the ordinary clearance regime rather than being separately banned. Outside Closed Periods (broadly, within four months of a half-yearly or preliminary final results release, minus the 24 hours after any ASX announcement), a Restricted Person need only notify the Chairman or Company Secretary in writing, confirm no Inside Information, and be advised there is no known reason to preclude the deal, then notify again within two business days after dealing. Critically for the loan leg, clause 9 requires the Designated Officer's (the Chairman's, or the Company Secretary's if the executive is the Chairman) prior written consent before granting a lender rights over the collared shares -- an express gate, not a prohibition. A lender's enforcement sale during a Closed Period is possible as an Excluded Dealing but needs a 7-business-day advance notice and the Designated Officer's non-objection, which can be refused without reasons. Overall verdict: workable subject to the Designated Officer's consent to the security interest and timing within an open window or an Excluded Dealing/exceptional-circumstances process, with the undefined 'short-term nature' prohibition counselling a longer-dated structure.

ORA.exemption_authority: For Designated Persons, the Company Secretary (or the Chairman of the Board, or the Chairman of the Audit & Compliance Committee where the Chairman is the applicant) may approve trading to dispose of Orora Securities during a Blackout Period or ad hoc restriction period only for severe financial hardship, a court order requiring transfer or sale, or a circumstance deemed exceptional by the Chairman (or the Chair of the Audit & Compliance Committee if the Chairman is the applicant), provided the person is not in possession of inside information and the proposed trading is the only reasonable course of action; the decision is in the approver's sole discretion, is final and binding, may be withdrawn if circumstances change, and a withheld approval must be kept confidential. bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons must not engage in margin lending or other secured financing arrangements over Orora Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is a blanket, unconditional ban on the loan leg of a funded collar for Designated Persons (Directors, Senior Executives, all KMP and their Associates), with no clearance route and no carve-out for vested shares.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A disposal of Orora Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This exclusion contemplates a secured lender existing, yet Designated Persons are separately and absolutely banned from entering into any secured financing arrangement in the first place; it may only be relevant to non-Designated Orora Persons or legacy arrangements, and should not be read as reviving the loan leg for Designated Persons.

bespoke_clauses.clause: 'Derivatives' ... includes the following if they relate to or derive value from Orora Securities: ... contracts for difference, spread bets and caps and collars.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The Policy expressly anticipates a collar structure and treats it as a Derivative/Security, so the put/call legs are squarely Trading requiring notification (Designated Persons) and compliance with Blackout Periods, quite separate from the outright ban on the financing leg.

bespoke_clauses.clause: any hedging over vested Orora Securities must comply with this Policy and, if applicable to that Orora Person, Orora's Minimum Shareholding Policy
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar over vested shares subject to an MSR may be restricted or reduced in permitted size by the separate Minimum Shareholding Policy, which is not in this document and must be independently reviewed.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This prohibition against insider trading applies to all Orora Persons at all times, including outside of Blackout Periods and other ad hoc restriction periods, and overrides all other provisions of this Policy, including any consent or approval to trade which may be granted under this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even a Company Secretary/Chairman-approved collar trade cannot proceed, and any purported approval is void, if the executive possesses inside information at the time of execution.

bespoke_clauses.clause: it is unlikely that details of the ad hoc restriction will be communicated to all Orora Persons ... Any such communication is to be treated as confidential.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An undisclosed ad hoc restriction can silently block execution or unwind of a collar even outside the scheduled Blackout Periods.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Following the end of each financial year, all Directors and Senior Executives must certify to the Company Secretary that they and their Associates are in compliance with this Policy (or advise of any breaches of this Policy).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar or loan arrangement inconsistent with the Policy would need to be disclosed (or falsely certified) at each annual compliance certification, so any secured financing question should be resolved with the Company Secretary well before that certification falls due.

ORA.summary: A funded collar over vested Orora shares faces a hard block on the loan leg: Designated Persons (Directors, Senior Executives, all KMP, and their Associates) 'must not engage in margin lending or other secured financing arrangements over Orora Securities', an unconditional ban with no clearance route. The derivative legs are, by contrast, expressly contemplated: 'Derivatives' is defined to include 'caps and collars' and other OTC instruments, and hedging of vested Orora Securities is permitted subject to compliance with the Policy (pre-trade notification for Designated Persons -- to the Chairman of the Board, the Chairman of the Audit & Compliance Committee, or the MD&CEO, as applicable, with a copy to the Company Secretary) and, if applicable, Orora's separate Minimum Shareholding Policy; hedging unvested securities under an employee plan is absolutely prohibited. Any dealing must also avoid the two annual Blackout Periods (31 December to half-year results; 30 June to full-year results) and any confidential ad hoc restriction, and can never proceed while the person holds inside information, which overrides any approval already granted. Outside those windows, only an exceptional-circumstances approval from the Company Secretary or Chairman (for severe hardship, a court order, or a circumstance the Chairman or Audit & Compliance Chair deems exceptional) permits a disposal during a Blackout Period. Overall verdict: the put/call collar structure itself is workable with notification outside Blackout Periods, but the bank's loan secured on the collared shares is expressly and unconditionally prohibited for Designated Persons, making a standard funded collar not achievable without restructuring the financing so that no security is taken over Orora shares.

CIP.exemption_authority: Chairman of the Board or CEO has sole discretion to judge whether exceptional circumstances (e.g. severe financial hardship) justify approving a sale or disposal during a blackout period, including on conditions; the Company Secretary communicates the outcome.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Centuria Securities: securities of any class, notes, options bonds or any related derivatives issued by the Group.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Because only Group-issued derivatives are 'Centuria Securities', an OTC put/call written by a bank over an executive's existing vested shares is not itself within the defined dealing universe, so entry into the collar is not expressly regulated.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The policy contains no reference to margin lending, other secured financing, encumbrance, hedging, short selling, stock lending or CFDs.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A loan secured on the collared shares is not prohibited by this policy, but the complete silence also means there is no bank-facing disclosure or consent carve-out to rely on if a dispute arises; general insider-trading and blackout principles would still govern any resulting sale or transfer of the shares.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Procedures for Directors reporting on trading in Centuria Securities ... Directors must immediately report any trades ... The consent requirement in paragraph 12 is addressed only to 'Employees'.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A Director entering or unwinding a collar outside a blackout period may not need prior Company Secretary/CEO consent at all under this policy, only post-trade notification, easing execution timing (subject to the separate blackout and inside-information bans).

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and Employees are not permitted to buy, sell or otherwise trade in Centuria Securities during a "blackout period".
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Entering a cash-settled OTC derivative that does not itself involve buying or selling the underlying shares may fall outside the blackout ban, though delivery, exercise or a forced sale of the physical shares would not.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the sale or disposal of the Centuria Securities is the most reasonable method available to alleviate the exceptional circumstances
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The only blackout carve-out is framed around a sale/disposal for hardship reasons, so it would not obviously extend to establishing a collar or granting security for a loan during a blackout period.

CIP.summary: CIP's trading policy (Centuria Capital Group's Directors' & Employees' Securities Trading Policy) is a bare-bones insider-trading and blackout-period policy that never mentions derivatives, hedging, monetisation, short selling, stock lending, CFDs, margin lending, encumbrance or secured financing, so none of these is expressly prohibited or made subject to clearance. A funded OTC equity collar over vested shares, and a loan secured on those shares, therefore sit outside the policy's express dealing restrictions, which are limited to buying, selling or otherwise trading 'Centuria Securities' (a term that excludes third-party derivatives not issued by the Group). Employees must obtain Company Secretary (or CEO) consent before dealing and may need to provide trading confirmations; Directors face no equivalent pre-clearance gate but must report trades immediately for ASX Listing Rule 3.19A purposes. The overriding bans on dealing while in possession of inside information and on buying/selling during a blackout period still apply to any actual sale, delivery, or forced sale of the physical shares under the collar or loan, and the only blackout carve-out (severe hardship) is framed around a sale, not derivative entry. Overall, a funded collar appears structurally available under this policy, subject to ordinary insider-trading and blackout timing discipline rather than any specific financing or hedging prohibition.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors may enter into hedging transactions in respect of the Company securities held by them outside any equity based performance plan or once the securities have been vested.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors, employees and contractors must not at any time engage in short-term trading in securities of the Company.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: With no stated holding period, a short-dated or early-unwound collar risks being characterised as short-term trading; tenor and structuring should avoid any appearance of short-term speculation.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The prohibition extends to dealings by anyone, including Directors' and employees' nominees, agents or other associates, such as family members, family trusts and family companies.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Structuring the collar or loan through a related trust or entity does not avoid the approval process or black-out timing restrictions.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and executives are also excluded from dealing in securities within the period from receipt of the Board Pack and the Directors' Meeting.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This recurring short blackout window (in addition to the 14-day results and AGM windows) further narrows the calendar available to enter, unwind or roll the collar.

DVP.summary: A funded OTC equity collar over vested shares looks achievable under this policy for Directors and employees, since 'Securities' expressly includes derivatives related to the Company's shares 'whether issued by the company or not', bringing an OTC put/call squarely within the ordinary approval process (self-certification of no inside information plus Chairman/Managing Director notification) rather than any outright ban. The hedging prohibition is confined to unvested equity-incentive entitlements; Directors are expressly permitted to hedge shares held outside a performance plan or once vested, provided this occurs outside black-out periods (14 days before results/AGM, and the Board Pack-to-Board Meeting window) and complies with the policy generally. The loan leg secured on the collared shares is not addressed anywhere in the policy, so it is neither prohibited nor subject to any disclosure or forced-sale carve-out, leaving the bank without policy-based protection if enforcement is needed during a black-out period. An undefined, absolute ban on short-term trading counsels a longer-dated structure, and any dealing must still avoid periods when the individual holds undisclosed price-sensitive information. Overall: permitted with Chairman clearance and black-out timing discipline for vested shares; unvested plan entitlements cannot be collared at all.

bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The policy names 'collars' specifically as a banned derivative product over Company securities, so a bank-written funded collar (purchased put and written call) is expressly and unconditionally prohibited for Employees and, via the 'additional restrictions' overlay, for Key Management Personnel, with no clearance route available.

bespoke_clauses.clause: not enter into arrangements ... where the lender is granted a right to sell or compel the sale of the securities at a time that this policy prohibits the employee dealing in the securities [Employees item 4] versus a disposal of securities ... that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights ... is specifically excluded from the application of this policy [Scope of the Policy].
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The policy discourages granting a lender forced-sale rights exercisable during a prohibited dealing period, yet separately excludes the lender's actual exercise of such rights from the policy altogether; a bank relying on enforcement should seek company comfort given this internal tension, though it is moot for a collar structure because the hedge leg is independently and absolutely banned.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Will the transaction take place on the ASX (circle): YES/NO. If the transaction is not to take place on the ASX, advise details of the transaction.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The Key Management Personnel clearance application contemplates off-market/OTC transactions generally, showing the policy anticipates non-exchange dealings, but this administrative accommodation does not override the standalone, unconditional ban on derivative products.

bespoke_clauses.clause: take all reasonable steps to prevent the trading by their spouse, partner, child or other immediate family member, or trust or other entity controlled by them or an investment adviser on behalf of them intends dealing in Imdex securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a family trust or related entity does not avoid the derivatives ban, since employees must take reasonable steps to prevent associated persons from dealing on their behalf.

IMD.summary: A funded OTC equity collar is expressly prohibited under this policy: the Employees section bans the use of 'derivatives such as caps, collars, warrants or similar products' in relation to any Imdex securities held by employees, with no qualification by vesting status, venue or clearance, and this ban extends to Key Management Personnel (including Directors) as an 'additional restriction' layered on top of the ordinary Employee rules. Even disregarding the derivatives ban, Key Management Personnel could not deal without prior written Chairman approval (valid only 14 days, subject to conditions), and never during the half-year, year-end or AGM Closed Periods or a Board-declared Prohibited Period. The financing leg is only conditionally restricted: pledging Company securities as collateral requires 'care' and must not grant a lender a forced-sale right exercisable during a prohibited dealing time, though a secured lender's actual exercise of enforcement rights is separately excluded from the policy altogether. Because the derivatives prohibition is absolute and names 'collars' specifically, no tier or holding period can support a funded collar under this policy; at most, an unhedged secured loan carefully timed outside closed/prohibited periods might be considered, but the collar itself cannot be structured.

bespoke_clauses.topic: Front Page Test as approval gate
bespoke_clauses.clause: Where any approval is required for a dealing under this Policy, approval will not be granted where the dealing would not satisfy the Front Page Test.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Beyond the formal rules, a bank-funded collar could still be refused clearance if it would be perceived as the executive exploiting their position, an additional discretionary hurdle beyond the express criteria.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons must take appropriate steps to ensure that their Connected Persons only deal in securities in circumstances where the Restricted Person to whom they are connected would be permitted to deal under this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a family member or a controlled entity does not avoid the Policy; the Restricted Person remains responsible for ensuring the same clearance and timing rules are met.

RDX.summary: A funded OTC equity collar is achievable under this policy once the underlying shares are vested and free of any plan holding lock: hedging (defined broadly as 'any arrangements that operate to limit the economic risk' of holding the securities) is permitted for Restricted Persons with prior written approval (Chair of the Board for Directors, Managing Director for Senior Executives/Nominated Employees), outside blackout periods, subject to the Front Page Test and no Inside Information, and is unrestricted for Employees who are not Restricted Persons. Hedging of unvested securities, or vested securities still subject to a plan holding lock, is an absolute, unconditional ban for every tier, so the collar cannot attach to those shares. The loan leg is treated the same way as a margin lending arrangement: Restricted Persons need prior Company approval to enter it or to transfer shares into a margin loan account, which the Company may condition (including as to margin-call sale terms), while a secured lender's enforcement sale on default is expressly excluded from the short-term dealing ban, blackout periods and the approval requirement altogether. The substance-over-form clause means the Company can look through the collar's structure to its economic effect when assessing compliance, and any collar entry, unwind or settlement must still avoid blackout periods (or obtain exceptional-circumstances approval) and pass the Front Page Test. Overall: workable for vested, unrestricted holdings with the required clearances and timing discipline; unavailable for unvested or holding-locked plan securities.

Entering such a transaction to limit the direct economic risk of a holding is prohibited by default; a written consent application may be made under 6.2.5, but the Company Secretary 'will generally withhold' consent unless special circumstances (e.g. financial hardship, court order) exist and the Chair agrees, so this is not a routine clearance path for a wealth-management-motivated collar.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Derivatives ... includes the following if they relate to or derive their value from Company Securities: put or call options, forward contracts, futures, warrants, depositary receipts, structured financial products, swaps, contracts for difference, spread bets, caps and collars, and any other hedging or investment arrangement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The definition of 'Derivatives' expressly names 'caps and collars' among the instruments caught by the ban on transactions that limit the direct economic risk of a holding, so a bank-written funded collar is squarely and specifically targeted, not merely swept in generically.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Company Secretary (or their delegate) will generally withhold prior written consent unless special circumstances exist (such as financial hardship or a court order requiring the sale of securities) and the Chair has agreed to the granting of consent.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The only route to clearance for a collar or margin loan uses the same high bar as hardship sales; an ordinary wealth-management-motivated collar is unlikely to be approved even though the Policy formally permits an application.

bespoke_clauses.topic: forced-sale exclusion conditioned on prior consent
bespoke_clauses.clause: A disposal of Company Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement which has been conducted with the prior written consent of the Company Secretary (or their delegate), after consultation with the Chair.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The forced-sale carve-out only protects a margin lending arrangement that itself had prior written consent; an unconsented loan gets no such protection, so the bank should confirm consent was obtained for the financing leg before relying on an unencumbered enforcement path.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Associate means someone that a Restricted Person (the Principal) can be regarded as having investment control or influence over. Such person might include: a family member ...; a nominee ... (including an investment manager managing funds on the Principal's behalf); a trust ...; a person in partnership ...; and a company that the Principal controls.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Investment control/influence tests catch nominees, investment managers acting for the Principal, and controlled trusts/companies, so routing the collar or loan through a related vehicle does not escape the Policy.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Each trading window opens one hour after the Company announces to the ASX its estimated Net Tangible Assets and closes at the end of the last Trading Day before the day on which the Company announces its next estimated Net Tangible Asset value.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Because NTA is announced weekly and monthly, the default 'open' trading window is narrow and recurring; even if consent for a collar were obtained, execution timing would still need to fit within these short windows and outside the separate results/DRP/buy-back Blackout Periods.

PGF.summary: A funded OTC equity collar is not realistically available under this policy: the definition of 'Derivatives' expressly names 'caps and collars' among the instruments banned from limiting the direct economic risk of a Restricted Person's (or Associate's) holding in Company Securities, and while a written consent application can formally be made under clause 6.2.5, the Company Secretary 'will generally withhold' consent unless special circumstances such as financial hardship or a court order exist and the Chair agrees, a bar aimed at forced sales rather than routine hedging or financing transactions. The loan leg fares only slightly better: margin lending of Company Securities is similarly prohibited unless the Company Secretary gives prior written consent after consulting the Chair under the same narrow standard, though once validly consented a secured lender's later enforcement sale is excluded from the Policy altogether, including during a Blackout Period. Any permitted dealing must in any event occur within the narrow, recurring trading window (opening an hour after each NTA announcement and closing before the next) and outside the results/dividend, DRP and buy-back Blackout Periods, and never while Inside Information is held. As a listed investment company, the Policy has no employee equity-vesting concept, so there is no vested/unvested distinction to exploit. Overall: the collar's derivative legs are expressly and specifically prohibited in the ordinary course, and even the financing leg needs a rarely-granted consent, so a funded collar cannot practically be structured under this policy.

bespoke_clauses.clause: No person shall purchase or sell or otherwise monetize securities of the Company while in possession of Undisclosed Material Information.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is the only clause that plainly reaches an OTC collar (naming 'monetize'), but it only bars entry while the individual holds undisclosed material information; the separate quarterly blackout provision is worded narrower ('purchasing or selling') and does not on its face use the word 'monetize', creating a textual gap for collar entry during the blackout window if no MNPI is held.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Policy imposes no requirement to seek clearance or give notice before dealing, other than the Chief Executive Officer's written consent needed to deal during a blackout period.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Outside the quarterly blackout and while free of undisclosed material information, a director or executive can enter, unwind or roll a collar without company approval, which simplifies timing but leaves the bank with no company sign-off trail confirming the trade is compliant.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This Policy covers all written or oral communications and applies to any director, officer or employee of the Company. It also applies to any consultant or contractor (a 'Representative').
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Spouses, trusts and controlled entities are not mentioned, so routing the collar or its security through a related vehicle is not addressed or restricted by the document.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the Company complies with its timely disclosure obligations as required under applicable Canadian securities laws, including the Securities Act (British Columbia)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The Policy is drafted for a TSX-listed, BCSC-regulated issuer with no reference to ASX Listing Rules or the Australian insider trading regime, so an Australian bank should confirm which regime actually governs the executive's holding before relying on this document alone.

bespoke_clauses.topic: silence on secured financing and derivatives
bespoke_clauses.clause: (No provision addresses margin loans, pledges, encumbrances, derivatives, hedging, short selling, stock lending or CFDs.)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: None of the structural elements of a funded collar (the put, the call, or the loan secured on the shares) is expressly prohibited, permitted or made subject to clearance, so the transaction is not blocked by the Policy but also receives no express safe harbour.

ORE.summary: This Policy is a disclosure and insider trading policy, not a comprehensive securities dealing policy, and it is silent on derivatives, hedging, margin lending, encumbrance, secured financing, short selling, stock lending, CFDs and short-term dealing. A funded collar is therefore not expressly prohibited, but the only operative restrictions are: (i) no director, officer, employee or Representative may purchase, sell or 'otherwise monetize' Company securities while in possession of Undisclosed Material Information; and (ii) individuals privy to material financial information (including the Board) may not purchase or sell during the ten-trading-day pre-results blackout (extending to first full trading day after filing) without the Chief Executive Officer's prior written consent, granted only for hardship or tax-timing reasons. There is no pre-clearance system for ordinary dealing outside the blackout, no minimum shareholding requirement, and no restriction tied to vesting status. A funded collar over vested shares could proceed provided the executive holds no undisclosed material information at signing, is outside any applicable blackout (or obtains CEO consent), and the transaction and its governing law are confirmed against the Company's actual Canadian/TSX regulatory obligations rather than assumed ASX norms.

bespoke_clauses.topic: outright hedging ban on held securities
bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors, key management personnel and any other designated Restricted Persons covered under this policy are also prohibited from entering into any transaction to hedge securities held in the Company.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is an absolute, non-waivable ban with no clearance route; a purchased put and written call are squarely a hedge of securities held, so a funded collar cannot be structured for directors, KMP or any other designated Restricted Person even with company consent.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors, officers and employees of the Company are prohibited from entering into arrangements for the hedging, or otherwise limiting their exposure to risk in relation to unvested shares, options or rights issued or acquired under the Company's employee equity scheme.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Closes off a collar over unvested equity incentives for the entire workforce, not just Restricted Persons, so vesting must complete before any collar discussion.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a disposal of securities that is a result of a secured lender exercising its rights, for example, under a margin loan arrangement [is excluded from the operation of the share trading policy].
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Suggests the loan/security leg of a structure is not itself barred by the trading policy (only the derivative hedge legs are), though enforcement remains subject to general insider trading law and could occur while the executive holds inside information.

bespoke_clauses.clause: clearance may be given for a Restricted Person to sell (but not to purchase) securities when they would otherwise be prohibited from doing so
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even where a closed-period exception is granted for hardship or court order, it only ever permits a sale, so collar legs (a purchased put and a written call) could not be entered under this route during a Closed Period.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the Board has an absolute discretion to place an embargo on Restricted Persons and/or employees and/or their respective associated parties trading in Company securities at any time.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An unscheduled, discretionary embargo could freeze collar entry, unwind or roll at any time, with no stated notice period or confidentiality treatment.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Each Restricted Person has a personal responsibility to ensure that their 'associated parties' ... complies with the same respective restrictions as apply to Restricted Persons
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Routing the collar or its security through a spouse, family company or trust does not avoid the hedging ban or Closed Period restrictions.

CYL.summary: A funded collar is not possible for directors, key management personnel or any other designated Restricted Person under this policy: section 'Securities issued under equity-based remuneration scheme' imposes an outright, non-waivable ban on any transaction to hedge securities held in the Company, which squarely catches a purchased put and written call, and there is no clearance or exemption route for it. The ban on hedging or otherwise limiting economic risk in unvested plan securities applies even more broadly to all directors, officers and employees. By contrast, secured financing itself is not directly prohibited -- a forced sale by a secured lender exercising its rights (margin loan given only as an example) is expressly excluded from the operation of the trading policy -- but that carve-out only covers the lender's disposal, not the collar's derivative legs, so the funded structure as a whole cannot proceed. Ordinary trading exceptions (closed-period hardship or court-order clearance) are sale-only and would not permit entering a collar. Associated parties (spouse, family company or trust) are bound by the same restrictions, so the ban cannot be avoided by routing the structure through a related entity.

GLF.summary: A funded collar is not banned outright under this policy but is doubly gated by clearance: both the hedging arrangement (the purchased put and written call) and the secured loan (margin lending or any arrangement granting security over the Units) are expressly named as requiring prior written clearance from the Company Secretary under the Trading Request Procedure, each valid for only five business days once granted and revocable or refusable without reasons given. There is no employee equity plan under this policy (it governs listed trust Units generally), so there is no unvested/vested distinction -- the clearance and Black-out Period rules apply uniformly to whatever Units are held. Entry, unwind or roll of the collar must fall outside the several Black-out Periods (around NTA/NAV releases, PDS/prospectus lodgement, unitholder meetings, and buy-backs) and while the individual holds no Inside Information, and must not amount to trading in or out of Units within three months of acquisition absent separate clearance. Family trusts or related entities (Connected Persons) cannot apply independently and must route any clearance request through the sponsoring EQT Person, LIT Person or LIT Partner. Directors of the Responsible Entity additionally face a two-business-day post-trade disclosure duty to the Company Secretary for ASX reporting purposes.

DTL.summary: A funded collar over vested shares appears achievable for a Data#3 Restricted Person, subject to timing and disclosure conditions. Financial products created over or in respect of DTL securities -- which expressly includes an OTC put or call -- are only barred during the two annual Closed Periods (1 January to half-year results, 1 July to full-year results) or any Board-resolved Prohibited Period, or while the person holds Inside Information; outside those windows no clearance is required. The loan secured on the collared shares is not prohibited but is a 'Security Arrangement' requiring immediate written disclosure to the Chairman (or alternate), with possible ASX notification if material, and any margin call forcing a sale must also be notified immediately, though the resulting forced sale itself is expressly permitted at any time including in a Closed Period. The collar must not be entered with an intention to sell the underlying shares within 12 months of their acquisition, given the absolute short-term trading ban, and if timed within a Prohibited Period would need written permission from the Chairman and Company Secretary (or alternate) on hardship or court-order grounds only, which would not extend to voluntary collar entry.

GNP.exemption_authority: The Authorising Officer (Chair of ARC/an Independent Director for the Chair of the Board; the Chair of the Board/Chair of ARC for other directors, Company Secretary and KMP; the Company Secretary/Managing Director for any other GPG Person) may, in absolute discretion and without giving reasons, approve dealing during a Blackout Period or otherwise-prohibited dealing in 'exceptional circumstances' (severe financial hardship or a court order/enforceable undertaking). The decision is final and binding, can be withdrawn if new information emerges, and must be kept strictly confidential.

bespoke_clauses.clause: GPG Persons may at any time ... dispose of GPG securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights under a loan or security agreement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike policies that treat a lender's enforcement sale as a breach, this exemption lets a bank liquidate collateral shares at any time, including during a Blackout Period, provided the underlying secured financing was itself validly entered into (i.e. over vested, unlocked shares with consent).

bespoke_clauses.clause: for the purposes of clause 3 only, a spouse (including a de facto spouse), child ... a close relative, a person financially dependent on or acting in concert with any of the persons referred to in clause 1(b)(i)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Natural-person associates (spouse, children, dependants) are only brought within clause 3 (Blackout Periods/notification); the express clause 4 bans on protection arrangements and secured financing/margin lending apply only to the GPG Person and entities they control, so a collar or loan booked in a spouse's own name arguably sits outside clause 4's literal wording, though general insider trading law and the acting-in-concert language would still need to be checked case by case.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a company or trust controlled by any of the persons referred to in clause 1(b)(i) above
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike natural-person associates, a company or trust the executive controls is included in the GPG Person definition without limitation, so routing the collar/loan through a family trust or investment vehicle does not escape clause 4's bans.

bespoke_clauses.clause: GPG may impose, without notice and in its sole and absolute discretion, additional restrictions on trading ... even where the proposed trade would otherwise take place outside a Blackout Period ... must be kept strictly confidential.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A scheduled collar entry, roll or unwind date can be blocked by an undisclosed ad hoc restriction with no advance warning and no stated end date.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If an GPG Person comes into possession of Inside Information after receiving a clearance to trade, they must not trade despite having received the clearance.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A cleared collar or financing transaction can become unexecutable if inside information arises between clearance and signing, with no stated re-clearance mechanism.

bespoke_clauses.clause: In exceptional circumstances the Authorising Officer has discretion to approve dealings in GPG securities during a Blackout Period ... may include, without limitation, severe financial hardship, or a requirement to comply with a court order.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Offers a narrow, wholly discretionary and unreviewable route to execute, unwind or settle a collar during a closed period, but cannot be relied upon as a matter of right.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If an GPG Person undertakes any of the actions described in paragraph 5(a), that GPG Person must advise the relevant Authorising Officer.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even exempt dealings (e.g. a secured lender's enforcement sale) must still be reported to the Authorising Officer after the event, creating an ongoing disclosure trail for any financing arrangement.

bespoke_clauses.clause: (not addressed anywhere in the policy)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no minimum shareholding requirement to preserve, simplifying sizing of the collar and loan against the full vested, unlocked holding.

GNP.summary: A funded collar over vested, unrestricted GenusPlus shares is achievable but only once the shares are both vested and free of any holding lock, and only with prior consent under clause 3.3: the put and call together are a 'protection arrangement' under clause 4.2, and the loan secured on those shares is a 'grant of security'/margin lending arrangement under clause 4.3, each independently banned outright while the shares remain unvested or holding-locked, with no exemption authority for that state. Once vested and unlocked, both legs require consent from the Authorising Officer (varying by seniority: Chair of ARC/Independent Director, the Chair of the Board, or the Company Secretary/Managing Director), execution must avoid the three annual Blackout Periods and any confidential ad hoc restriction, and any clearance lapses if inside information later arises. Usefully, a secured lender's enforcement sale on default is expressly carved out as a permitted dealing 'at any time', so the bank's ability to liquidate collateral is not blocked by a subsequent closed period. Natural-person associates (as opposed to controlled companies or trusts) are, on the policy's literal wording, only caught by the Blackout Period/notification regime and not by clause 4's substantive bans, which may be relevant to structuring but should not be relied on without further analysis. There is no minimum shareholding requirement and no fixed short-term holding period beyond a general speculative-trading ban.

bespoke_clauses.topic: margin lending ban is KMP-only and margin-loan-specific
bespoke_clauses.clause: directors, officers and other “Key Management Personnel” ... of the Group are prohibited from using his or her holding in any of the Group's securities as collateral for any margin lending.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The express prohibition is confined to KMP and to 'margin lending'; other employees and contractors face no express bar on pledging shares, and even for KMP whether a bank's collar-secured loan counts as 'margin lending' (rather than another form of secured financing) is undefined and would need to be tested.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A Key Management Person with security over his or her holding ... in connection with margin lending which is in existence prior to 1 March 2016 will not be in breach ... provided that the Key Management Person notifies the Chairman ... within five business days of becoming aware that his or her margin loan facility ... is subject to a margin call, in material breach, or reaches 90% or above of any applicable loan-to-value ratio.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any new collar-secured loan post-dates 1 March 2016 and so cannot rely on this grandfathering; it confirms the general rule is a forward-looking ban on new KMP margin/secured lending against Group shares.

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedging ban tied to vesting/restriction status only
bespoke_clauses.clause: must not enter into a transaction if the transaction effectively operates to hedge or limit the economic risk of securities allocated under the Group's employee incentive plans during the period those securities remain unvested or subject to restrictions under the terms of the plan.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Once plan securities vest and restrictions lapse, hedging is no longer expressly banned and only ordinary Dealing clearance and Closed Period rules apply, so the collar's put/call legs over vested unrestricted shares are structurally available subject to clearance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Dealing in securities is a broad concept and covers more than simply buying or selling securities. It extends to exercising options over securities and entering agreements to buy or sell securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Granting a charge or lien is not listed as a form of Dealing, so outside the KMP margin lending clause, pledging shares to secure a loan is not independently regulated by this policy.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A Relevant Person must notify the Company Secretary: before, or immediately after, any buying or selling by them ... of Group securities at any time.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Entry into, unwind of, or settlement under a collar (to the extent treated as buying or selling) must be notified to the Company Secretary regardless of Closed Period status, creating an ongoing disclosure trail for the bank's structure.

GOZ.summary: A funded collar is workable in part but faces a real gap on the financing leg. The put and call over vested, unrestricted shares would be a Dealing requiring prior clearance (Chairman for directors; Managing Director or Company Secretary for employees; Company Secretary or Managing Director for other Relevant Persons), executed outside the two annual Closed Periods and not while short-term (within 3 months of acquisition) or while holding inside information, with notification to the Company Secretary before or immediately after dealing. Hedging is only expressly banned while the plan securities remain unvested or restriction-locked, so hedging vested unrestricted shares is permitted with clearance. However, for directors, officers and other Key Management Personnel, using their Group securities as collateral for margin lending is expressly prohibited (subject only to a narrow pre-1 March 2016 grandfather), and it is unclear whether a bank collar loan secured on shares with margin-call features would be characterised as 'margin lending' and caught by this ban; for other employees and contractors there is no equivalent express prohibition. Structuring the loan leg to avoid the 'margin lending' label, or restricting the funded collar to non-KMP employees, would materially improve feasibility, but KMP participation carries real prohibition risk absent a policy carve-out.
